src: abhyavakīrṇānāṃ ca tatra yāni bodhisatvānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi patitāni, tāni dharaṇitale pratiṣṭhitāni / yāni punar mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi patitāni, tāni tatraiva sthitāni na bhūmau patitāni /
tgt: When the flowers fell on the bodies of the bodhisattvas, they fell off on the floor, but when they fell on the bodies of the great disciples, they stuck to them and did not fall.

src: tatas te mahāśrāvakā ṛddhiprātihāryaiḥ tāni puṣpāṇy utsṛjanti, na ca patanti /
tgt: The great disciples shook the flowers and even tried to use their magical powers, but still the flowers would not shake off.

src: atha sā devatāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha kiṃ bhadantaśāriputra,
tgt: Then, the goddess said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, why do you shake these flowers?”

src: etāni puṣpāṇy utsṛjasi / āha akalpikāni devate etāni puṣpāṇi / tasmād aham etāni puṣpāṇy apanayāmi /
tgt: Śāriputra replied, “Goddess, these flowers are not proper for religious persons and so we are trying to shake them off.”

src: devatāha mā bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ vocaḥ /
tgt: The goddess said, “Do not say that, reverend Śāriputra.

src: etāni hi puṣpāṇi kalpikāni /
tgt: These flowers are proper indeed!

src: tathā hy etāni puṣpāṇi na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti /
tgt: Such flowers have neither constructual thought nor discrimination.

src: sthaviraḥ punaḥ śāriputraḥ kalpayati vikalpayati ca /
tgt: But the elder Śāriputra has both constructual thought and discrimination.

src: ye bhadantaśāriputra svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāṃ kalpayanti vikalpayanti ca, te 'kalpikāḥ / sthaviras tu kalpayati vikalpayati ca /
tgt: “Reverend Śāriputra, impropriety for one who has renounced the world for the discipline of the rightly taught Dharma consists of constructual thought and discrimination, yet the elders are full of such thoughts.

src: ye punar na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti, te kalpikāḥ /
tgt: One who is without such thoughts is always proper.

src: paśya bhadantaśāriputra eṣāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi na śliṣyanti /
tgt: “Reverend Śāriputra, see how these flowers do not stick to the bodies of these great spiritual heroes, the bodhisattvas!

src: yathāpi nāma sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇatvāt /
tgt: This is because they have eliminated constructual thoughts and discriminations.

src: tadyathāpi nāma bhīrukajātīyasya puruṣasyāmanuṣyā avatāraṃ Iabhante / evam eva saṃsārabhayabhītānāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāny avatāraṃ labhante / ye punaḥ sarvasaṃsārakleśabhayavigatāḥ,
tgt: “In the same way that evil spirits have power over fearful men but cannot disturb the fearless, those intimidated by fear of the world are in the power of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures, which do not disturb those who are free from fear of the passions inherent in the constructive world.

src: kiṃ teṣāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni kariṣyanti / yeṣāṃ vāsanāprahīṇā, teṣāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi śliṣyanti /
tgt: Thus, these flowers stick to the bodies of those who have not eliminated their instincts for the passions and do not stick to the bodies of those who have eliminated their instincts.

src: tasmāt sarvavāsanāprahīṇānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi na śliṣyanti /
tgt: Therefore, the flowers do not stick to the bodies of these bodhisattvas, who have abandoned all instincts.”

src: atha khalv āyuṣmāñ śāriputras tāṃ devatām etad avocat kiyacciraniviṣṭā punas tvaṃ devate iha gṛhe /
tgt: Then the venerable Śāriputra said to the goddess, “Goddess, how long have you been in this house?”

src: āha yāvacciraniviṣṭā sthavirasyāryā vimuktiḥ /
tgt: The goddess replied, “I have been here as long as the elder has been in liberation.”

src: āha na cirasthitā tvaṃ devate iha gṛhe / āha kiyacciraniviṣṭā punaḥ sthavirasyāryā vimuktiḥ /
tgt: The goddess said, “Has the elder been in liberation for quite some time?”

src: tataḥ sthaviras tūṣṇīm abhūt /
tgt: At that, the elder Śāriputra fell silent.

src: āha kim idānīṃ mahāprajñānām agryaḥ sthaviras tūṣṇīm abhūt /
tgt: The goddess continued, “Elder, you are ‘foremost of the wise!’ Why do you not speak?

src: prāptakālaṃ praśnaṃ na visarjayati /
tgt: Now, when it is your turn, you do not answer the question.”

src: āha apravyāhārā hi devate vimuktiḥ / tan na jāne kiṃ vyāharāmīti /
tgt: Since liberation is inexpressible, goddess, I do not know what to say. Goddess

src: sarvāṇy etāny akṣarāṇi vimuktilakṣaṇāni /
tgt: All the syllables pronounced by the elder have the nature of liberation.

src: yā hi sā vimuktiḥ, sā nādhyātmaṃ na bahir nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate / evam akṣarāṇy api /
tgt: Liberation is neither internal nor external, nor can it be apprehended apart from them. Likewise, syllables are neither internal nor external, nor can they be apprehended anywhere else.

src: tasmāt tarhi bhadantaśāriputra mā akṣarāpanayena vimuktiṃ nirdiśa /
tgt: Therefore, reverend Śāriputra, do not point to liberation by abandoning speech! Why?

src: sarvadharmasamatā hi vimuktiḥ /
tgt: The holy liberation is the equality of all things!

src: āha nanu devate rāgadoṣamohavigamād vimuktiḥ /
tgt: Goddess, is not liberation the freedom from desire, hatred, and folly?

src: devatāha abhimānikānām eṣa nirdeṣo rāgadoṣamohavigamād vimuktir iti / ye nirabhimānikāḥ, teṣāṃ rāgadoṣamohaprakṛtir eva vimuktiḥ /
tgt: “Liberation is freedom from desire, hatred, and folly”that is the teaching for the excessively proud. But those free of pride are taught that the very nature of desire, hatred, and folly is itself liberation.

src: atha khalv āyuṣmāñ śāriputras tāṃ devatām etad avocat
tgt: Śāriputra

src: sādhu sādhu devate kiṃ tvayā prāptaṃ kiṃ vā sākṣātkṛtam, yasyās ta īdṛśaṃ pratibhānam /
tgt: Excellent! Excellent, goddess! Pray, what have you attained, what have you realized, that you have such eloquence? Goddess

src: āha na mayā bhadantaśāriputra kiṃcit prāptaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ vā /
tgt: I have attained nothing, reverend Śāriputra. I have no realization.

src: tena ma īdṛśaṃ pratibhānam /
tgt: Therefore I have such eloquence.

src: yeṣām evaṃ bhavaty asmābhiḥ prāptaṃ vā sākṣātkṛtaṃ ceti,
tgt: Whoever thinks, “I have attained!

src: te svākhyāte dharmavinaya ābhimānikā ity ucyante /
tgt: I have realized!” is overly proud in the discipline of the well taught Dharma.

src: āha kiṃ tvaṃ devate śrāvakayānikā pratyekabuddhayānikā mahāyānikā vā /
tgt: Goddess, do you belong to the Disciple Vehicle, to the Solitary Sage Vehicle, or to the Great Vehicle? Goddess

src: āha śrāvakāyānikāsmi śrāvakayānasūcanatayā,
tgt: I belong to the Disciple Vehicle when I teach it to those who need it.

src: pratyekabuddhayānikāsmi pratītyadharmāvatāreṇa, mahāyānikāsmi mahākaruṇānutsṛjanatayā /
tgt: And, since I never abandon the great compassion, I belong to the Great Vehicle, as all need that teaching to attain ultimate liberation.

src: api tu khalu punar bhadantaśāriputra na campakavanaṃ praviṣṭā eraṇḍagandhaṃ jighranti / campakavanaṃ tu praviṣṭāś campakagandham eva jighranti / evam eva bhadantaśāriputra neha gṛhe buddhadharmaguṇagandhike vasantaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhagandhaiḥ jighranti /
tgt: Nevertheless, reverend Śāriputra, just as one cannot smell the castor plant in a magnolia wood, but only the magnolia flowers, so, reverend Śāriputra, living in this house, which is redolent with the perfume of the virtues of the buddha qualities, one does not smell the perfume of the disciples and the solitary sages.

src: ye 'pi bhadantaśāriputra śakrabrahmalokapālā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā idaṃ gṛhaṃ praviśanti, te 'py asya satpuruṣasya dharmaśravaṇena buddhadharmaguṇagandhenotpāditabodhicittā niṣkrāmanti /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, the Śakras, the Brahmās, the Lokapālas, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas who live in this house hear the Dharma from the mouth of this holy man and, enticed by the perfume of the virtues of the buddha qualities, proceed to conceive the spirit of enlightenment.

src: dvādaśavarṣāṇy upādāya bhadantaśāriputra prativasantyā me na jātu śrāvakapratyekabuddhasaṃprayuktā kathā śrutapūrvā, nānyatra mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāpratisaṃyuktaivācintyadharmapratisaṃyuktaiva /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, I have been in this house for twelve years, and I have heard no discourses concerning the disciples and solitary sages but have heard only those concerning the great love, the great compassion, and the inconceivable qualities of the Buddha.

src: iha bhadantaśāriputra gṛhe 'ṣṭāv āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ satatasamitaṃ saṃdṛśyante /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, eight strange and wonderful things manifest themselves constantly in this house.

src: katame 'ṣṭau /
tgt: What are these eight?

src: neha rātrir vā divaso vā prajñāyate sadāvabhāsitam idaṃ gṛhaṃ suvarṇavarṇayā prabhayā / neha sūryācandramasau prajñāyete, na bhrājete /
tgt: A light of golden hue shines here constantly, so bright that it is hard to distinguish day and night, and neither the moon nor the sun shines here distinctly.

src: ayaṃ prathama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the first wonder of this house.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra ye praviśantīdaṃ gṛham, teṣāṃ samanantarapraviṣṭānāṃ sarvakleśā na bādhante /
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, whoever enters this house is no longer troubled by his afflictions from the moment he is within.

src: ayaṃ dvitīya āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the second strange and wonderful thing.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra idaṃ gṛham avirahitaṃ śakrabrahmalokapālair anyabuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitaiś ca bodhisatvaiḥ /
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, this house is never forsaken by Śakra, Brahmā, the Lokapālas, and the bodhisattvas from all the other buddhafields.

src: ayaṃ tṛtīya āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the third strange and wonderful thing.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra idaṃ gṛhaṃ satatasamitam avirahitaṃ dharmaśravaṇena ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktayā kathayāvivartyadharmakathayā ca
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, this house is never empty of the sounds of the Dharma, the discourse on the six transcendences, and the discourses of the irreversible wheel of the Dharma.

src: ayaṃ caturtha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the fourth strange and wonderful thing.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe yās tūryasaṃgītayo divyamānuṣyakāṇi vā vādyāni vādyante, tebhyas tūryebhyo 'pramāṇo dharmaśabdanirhāro niścarati sārvakālikaḥ /
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, in this house one always hears the rhythms, songs, and music of gods and men, and from this music constantly resounds the sound of the infinite Dharma of the Buddha.

src: ayaṃ pañcama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the fifth strange and wonderful thing.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe catvāri mahānidhānāni sarvaratnaparipūrṇāny akṣayāṇi yato niṣyandaṃ sarvadaridrakṛpaṇā ādāya prakrāmanti, na ca kṣīyante /
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, in this house there are always four inexhaustible treasures, replete with all kinds of jewels, which never decrease, although all the poor and wretched may partake of them to their satisfaction.

src: ayaṃ ṣaṣṭha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the sixth strange and wonderful thing.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe śākyamunis tathāgato 'mitābho 'kṣobhyo ratnaśrī ratnārcī ratnacandro ratnavyūho duḥprasahaḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ prabhūtaratnaḥ siṃhanādanādī siṃhaghoṣas tathāgata evaṃ pramukhā daśasu dikṣv apramāṇās tathāgatā ye 'sya satpuruṣasya cintitamātreṇāgacchanti / āgatya ca tathāgataguhyaṃ nāma dharmamukhapraveśaṃ deśayitvā prakrāmanti /
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, at the wish of this good man, to this house come the innumerable tathāgatas of the ten directions, such as the Tathāgatas Śākyamuni, Amitābha, Akṣobhya, Ratnaśrī‌, Ratnārcis, Ratnacandra, Ratnavyūha, Duḥprasāha, Sarvārtha­siddha, Prabhūtaratna, Siṃhanādanādī, Siṃhaghoṣa, and so forth, and when they come they teach the door of Dharma called The Secrets of the Tathāgatas, and then depart.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe sarvadevabhavanavyūhāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāś ca saṃdṛśyante /
tgt: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, all the splendors of the abodes of the gods and all the splendors of the fields of the buddhas shine forth in this house.

src: ayam aṣṭama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
tgt: That is the eighth strange and wonderful thing.

src: ime bhadantaśāriputra aṣṭāv āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ satatasamitam iha gṛhe saṃdṛśyante /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, these eight strange and wonderful things are seen in this house.

src: ka imām acintyadharmatāṃ paśyañ śrāvakadharmatāyai spṛhayet /
tgt: Who then, seeing such inconceivable things, would believe the teaching of the disciples?

src: āha kiṃ tvaṃ devate strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasi /
tgt: Goddess, what prevents you from transforming yourself out of your female state?

src: āha paripūrṇāni me dvādaśavarṣāṇy upādāya strībhāvaṃ paryeṣamāṇāyā na cainaṃ labhe /
tgt: Although I have sought my “female state” for these twelve years, I have not yet found it.

src: api ca bhadantaśāriputra yā māyākāreṇa strīnirmitā yas tām evaṃ vadet kiṃ tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasīti, sa kiṃ vadet /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, if a magician were to incarnate a woman by magic, would you ask her, “What prevents you from transforming yourself out of your female state?”

src: āha na tasyāḥ kācit bhūtā pariniṣpattiḥ /
tgt: Such a woman would not really exist, so what would there be to transform?

src: āha evam eva bhadantaśāriputra apariniṣpanneṣu sarvadharmeṣu māyānirmitasvabhāveṣu kutas tavaivaṃ bhavati kiṃ tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasīti /
tgt: Just so, reverend Śāriputra, all things do not really exist. Now, would you think, “What prevents one whose nature is that of a magical incarnation from transforming herself out of her female state?”

src: atha sā devatā tādṛśam adhiṣṭhānam adhitiṣṭhati sma / yathā sthaviraḥ śāriputro yādṛśī sā devatā tādṛśaḥ saṃdṛśyate,
tgt: Thereupon, the goddess employed her magical power to cause the elder Śāriputra to appear in her form and to cause herself to appear in his form.

src: atha sā devatā śāriputrarūpā śāriputraṃ devatārūpadhāriṇam apṛcchat kiṃ bhadantaśāriputra strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasi / śāriputro devatārūpy āha
tgt: Then the goddess, transformed into Śāriputra, said to Śāriputra, transformed into a goddess, “Reverend Śāriputra, what prevents you from transforming yourself out of your female state?”

src: na jāne kiṃ vinivartayāmīti /
tgt: I do not know what to transform!”

src: āha yadi sthaviraḥ śakṣyati strībhāvaṃ vinivartayitum, tataḥ sarvāḥ striyo 'pi strībhāvaṃ vinivartayiṣyanti /
tgt: The goddess continued, “If the elder could again change out of the female state, then all women could also change out of their female states.

src: yathā sthaviro na strī strīva saṃdṛśyate, evaṃ sarvastrīṇām api strīrūpaṃ na ca striyaḥ strīrūpāś ca saṃdṛśyante /
tgt: All women appear in the form of women in just the same way as the elder appears in the form of a woman. While they are not women in reality, they appear in the form of women.

src: idaṃ saṃdhāya bhagavān āha ḥsarvadharmā na strī na puruṣaḥ iti /
tgt: With this in mind, the Buddha said, ‘In all things, there is neither male nor female.’ ”

src: atha sā devatā tad adhiṣṭhānam avāsṛjat /
tgt: Then, the goddess released her magical power and each returned to their ordinary form.

src: atha sā devatāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha kva nu te bhadantaśāriputra strīrūpaṃ kṛtaṃ gatam /
tgt: She then said to him, “Reverend Śāriputra, what have you done with your female form?” Śāriputra

src: āha na tat kṛtaṃ na vikṛtam /
tgt: I neither made it nor did I change it.

src: āha evam eva sarvadharmā na kṛtā na vikṛtāḥ / yatra ca na kṛtir na vikṛtis tad buddhavacanam /
tgt: Just so, all things are neither made nor changed, and that they are not made and not changed, that is the teaching of the Buddha.

src: āha itas tvaṃ devate cyutā kutropapatsyase /
tgt: Goddess, where will you be born when you transmigrate after death?

src: āha yatraiva tathāgatanirmita upapatsyate, tatraivāham upapatsye /
tgt: I will be born where all the magical incarnations of the Tathāgata are born.

src: āha tathāgatanirmitasya na cyutir nopapattiḥ /
tgt: But the emanated incarnations of the Tathāgata do not transmigrate nor are they born.

src: āha evam eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ na cyutir nopapattiḥ /
tgt: All things and living beings are just the same they do not transmigrate nor are they born!

src: āha kiyaccireṇa punar devate bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase /
tgt: Goddess, how soon will you attain the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood?

src: āha yadā sthaviraḥ pṛthagjanadharmasamanvāgato bhaviṣyati, tadāhaṃ bodhim abhisaṃbhotsye /
tgt: At such time as you, elder, become endowed once more with the qualities of an ordinary individual, then will I attain the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood.

src: āha asthānam etad devate yad ahaṃ pṛthagjanadharmasamanvāgataḥ syām /
tgt: Goddess, it is impossible that I should become endowed once more with the qualities of an ordinary individual.

src: āha evam eva bhadantaśāriputra asthānam etad yad ahaṃ bodhim abhisaṃbhotsye /
tgt: Just so, reverend Śāriputra, it is impossible that I should attain the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood!

src: asthānasthitaiva hi bodhiḥ /
tgt: Because perfect enlightenment stands upon the impossible.

src: tasmād asthānaṃ na kaścid abhisaṃbhotsyate /
tgt: Because it is impossible, no one attains the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood.

src: sthavira āha
tgt: Śāriputra

src: uktaṃ devate tathāgatena ḥgaṅgānadīvālikāsamās tathāgatā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante 'bhisaṃbhotsyante caḥ /
tgt: But the Tathāgata has declared “The tathāgatas, who are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have attained perfect buddhahood, are attaining perfect buddhahood, and will go on attaining perfect buddhahood.”

src: devatāha akṣaragaṇanāsaṃketādhivacanam etad bhadantaśāriputra atītānāgatapratyutpannā buddhā iti /
tgt: Goddess Reverend Śāriputra, the expression “the buddhas of the past, present, and future” is a conventional expression made up of a certain number of syllables.

src: na punar buddhā atītā vānāgatā vā vartamānā vā /
tgt: The buddhas are neither past, nor present, nor future.

src: tryadhvasamatikrāntā hi bodhiḥ /
tgt: Their enlightenment transcends the three times!

src: api ca prāptaṃ sthavireṇārhatvam /
tgt: But tell me, elder, have you attained the state of arhat?

src: āha prāptam asaṃprāptikāraṇena /
tgt: It is attained, because there is no attainment.

src: āha evam evābhisaṃbodhir anabhisaṃbodhikāraṇena /
tgt: Just so, there is perfect enlightenment because there is no attainment of perfect enlightenment.

src: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha dvānavatibuddhakoṭīparyupāsitā bhadantaśāriputra eṣā devatābhijñājñānavikrīḍitā praṇidhānasamucchritā
tgt: Then the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the venerable elder Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, this goddess has already served ninetytwo million billion buddhas. She plays with the superknowledges. She has truly succeeded in all her vows.

src: kṣāntipratilabdhāvaivartikasamavasaraṇā praṇidhānavaśena yathecchati tathā tiṣṭhati satvaparipākāya // //
tgt: She has gained the tolerance of the birthlessness of things. She has actually attained irreversibility. She can live wherever she wishes on the strength of her vow to develop living beings.”

src: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim evam āha kathaṃ kulaputra bodhisatvo gatiṃgato bhavati buddhadharmeṣu /
tgt: Then, the crown prince Mañjuśrī asked the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, “‌Noble sir, how does the bodhisattva follow the way to attain the qualities of the Buddha?”

src: āha yadā mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvo 'gatigamanaṃ gacchati, tadā bodhisatvo gatiṃgato bhavati buddhadharmeṣu /
tgt: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, when the bodhisattva follows the wrong way, he follows the way to attain the qualities of the Buddha.”

src: āha katamac ca bodhisatvasyāgatigamanam /
tgt: Mañjuśrī continued, “How does the bodhisattva follow the wrong way?”

src: āha yadā pañcānantaryagatiṃ ca gacchati, na ca vyāpādavihiṃsāpraduṣṭo bhavati /
tgt: Vimalakīrti replied, “Even should he enact the five deadly sins, he feels no malice, violence, or hate.

src: nirayagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvarajaḥkleśavigataś ca bhavati /
tgt: Even should he go into the hells, he remains free of all taint of afflictions.

src: durjayo yoganando 'yaṃ sthite vararucāvataḥ / āśraye vaitasīṃ vṛttiṃ kālaṃ tāvatpratīkṣitum // iti saṃcintya sa prājñaḥ śakaṭālo madicchayā / akarodrājakāryāṇi punaḥ saṃprāpya mantritām //
tgt: Now the discreet Śakatāla made up his mind that it would be difficult to overthrow Yogananda as long as I was in office, and that he had accordingly better imitate the cane which bends with the current, and watch a favourable moment for vengeance, so at my request he resumed the office of minister and managed the king’s affairs.

src: kadācidyoganando 'tha nirgato nagarādvahiḥ / śliṣyatpañcāṅguliṃ hastaṃ gaṅgāmadhye vyalokayat //
tgt: Once on a time Yogananda went outside the city, and beheld in the middle of the Ganges a hand, the five fingers of which were closely pressed together.

src: kimetaditi papraccha māmāhūya sa tatkṣaṇam / ahaṃ ca dve nijāṅgulyau diśi tasyāmadarśayam //
tgt: That moment he summoned me and said: “What does this mean?” But I displayed two of my fingers in the direction of the hand.

src: tena tasmiṃstirobhūte haste rājātivismayāt / bhūyo 'pi tadapṛcchanmāṃ tataścāhaṃ tamabravam // pañcabhirmilitaiḥ kiṃ yajjagatīha na sādhyate / ityuktavānasau hastaḥ śvāṅgulīḥ pañca darśayan // tato 'sya rājan naṅgulyāv ete dve darśite mayā / aikacitye dvayoreva kimasādhyaṃ bhavediti // ityukte gūḍhavijñāne samatuṣyattato nṛpaḥ / śakaṭālo vyaṣīdacca madbuddhiṃ vīkṣya durjayām //
tgt: Thereupon that hand disappeared, and the king, exceedingly astonished, again asked me what this meant, and I answered him: “That hand meant to say, by showing its five fingers: ‘What cannot five men united effect in this world?’ Then I, king, showed it these two fingers, wishing to indicate that nothing is impossible when even two men are of one mind.” When I uttered this solution of the riddle the king was delighted, and Śakatāla was despondent, seeing that my intellect would be difficult to circumvent.[1] One day Yogananda saw his queen leaning out of the window and asking questions of a Brāhman guest that was looking up.

src: tanmātrādeva kupito rājā viprasa tasya saḥ / ādiśadbadhamīrṣyā hi vivekaparipanthinī //
tgt: That trivial circumstance threw the king into a passion, and he gave orders that the Brāhman should be put to death for jealousy interferes with discernment.

src: hantuṃ vadhyabhuvaṃ tasmin nīyamāne dvije tadā / ahasadgatajīvo 'pi matsyo vipaṇimadhyagaḥ //
tgt: Then as that Brāhman was being led off to the place of execution in order that he might be put to death, a fish in the market laughed aloud, though it was dead.

src: tadaiva rājā tadbuddhvā vadhaṃ tasya nyavārayat / viprasya māmapṛcchacca matsyahāsasya kāraṇam //
tgt: [also see notes on the motif of laughter] The king hearing it immediately prohibited for the present the execution of that Brāhman, and asked me the reason why the fish laughed.

src: nirūpya kathayāmyetadityuktvā nirgataṃ ca mām / cintitopasthitaikānte sarasvatyevamabravīt // asya tālataroḥ pṛṣṭhe tiṣṭha rātrābalakṣitaḥ / atra śroṣyasi matsyasya hāsahetum asaṃśayam // tacchrutvā niśi tatrāhaṃ gatvā tālopari sthitaḥ / apaśyaṃ rākṣasīṃ ghorāṃ bālaiḥ putraiḥ sahāgatam //
tgt: and after I had gone out Sarasvatī came to me secretly on my thinking of her and gave me this advice: “Take up a position on the top of this palm-tree at night so as not to be observed, and thou shalt without doubt hear the reason why the fish laughed.” Hearing this I went at night to that very place, and ensconced myself on the top of the palm-tree, and saw a terrible female Rākṣasa[2] coming past with her children;

src: sā bhakṣyaṃ yācamānāṃstānavādītpratipālyatām / prātarvo vipramāṃsāni dāsyāmyadya hato na saḥ //
tgt: when they asked her for food, she said: “Wait, and I will give you to-morrow morning the flesh of a Brāhman;

src: kasmātsa na hato 'dyeti pṛṣṭā tairabravītpunaḥ / taṃ hi dṛṣṭva mṛto 'pīha matsyo hasitavāniti // hasitaṃ kimu teneti pṛṣṭā bhūyaḥ sutaiśca sā / avocadrākṣasī rājñaḥ sarvā rājño 'pi viplutāḥ // sarvatrāntaḥpure hyatra strīrūpāḥ puruṣāḥ sthitāḥ / hanyate 'naparādhas tu vipra ity ahasat timiḥ //
tgt: he was not killed to-day.”[3] They said to their mother: “Why was he not killed today?” Then she replied: “He was not executed because a fish in the town, though dead, laughed when it saw him.” The sons said: “Why did the fish laugh?” She continued: “The fish, of course, said to himself: ‘All the king’s wives are dissolute, for in every part of this harem there are men dressed up as women, and nevertheless while these escape an innocent Brāhman is to be put todeath,’ and this tickled the fish so that he laughed.

src: bhūtānāṃ pārthivātyarthanirvivekatvahāsinām / sarvāntaścāriṇāṃ hyetā bhavantyeva ca vikriyāḥ // etattasyā vacaḥ śrutvā tato 'pakrāntavāhanam / prāptaśca matsyahāsasya hetuṃ rājñe nyavedayam //
tgt: For demons assume these disguises, insinuating themselves into everything, and laughing at the exceeding want of discernment of kings.” After I had heard that speech of the female Rākṣasa I went away from thence, and in the morning I informed the king why the fish laughed.

src: prāpya cāntaḥpurebhyas tān strīrūpān puruṣāṃs tataḥ / bahv amanyata māṃ rājā vadhādvipraṃ ca muktavān //
tgt: The king, after detecting in the harem those men clothed as women, looked upon me with great respect, and released that Brāhman from the sentence of death.

src: ityādi ceṣṭitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya rājño viśṛṅkhalam / khinne mayi kadācicca tatrāgāccitrakṛnnavaḥ //
tgt: I was disgusted by seeing this and other lawless proceedings on the part of the king, and while I was in this frame of mind there came to the Court a new painter.

src: alikhat sa mahādevīṃ yoganandaṃ ca taṃ paṭe / sajīvam iva taccitraṃ vākceṣṭārahitaṃ tv abhūt //
tgt: He painted on a sheet of canvas the principal queen and Yogananda, and that picture of his looked as if it were alive; it only lacked speech and motion.

src: taṃ ca citrakaraṃ rājā tuṣṭo vittairapūrayat / taṃ ca vāsagṛhe citrapaṭaṃ bhittāvakārayat //
tgt: And the king, being delighted, loaded that painter with wealth, and had the painting set up on a wall in his private apartments.

src: ekadā ca praviṣṭasya vāsake tatra sā mama / saṃpūrṇalakṣaṇā devī pratibhāti sma citragā //
tgt: Now one day when I entered into the king’s private apartments it occurred to me that the painting of the queen did not represent all her auspicious marks;

src: lakṣaṇāntarasaṃbandhādabhyūhya pratibhāvaśāt / athākārṣamahaṃ tasyāstilakaṃ mekhalāpade //
tgt: from the arrangement of the other marks I conjectured by means of my acuteness that there ought to be a spot where the girdle comes, and I painted one there.

src: saṃpūrṇalakṣaṇāṃ tena kṛtvaināṃ gatavānaham / praviṣṭo yoganando 'tha tilakaṃ taṃ vyalokayat //
tgt: Then I departed after thus giving the queen all her lucky marks. Then Yogananda entered and saw that spot, and asked his chamberlains who had painted it.

src: kenāyaṃ racito 'treti so 'pṛcchacca mahattarān / te ca nyavedayaṃstasmai kartāraṃ tilakasya mām //
tgt: And they indicated me as the person who had painted it.

src: devyā guptapradeśasthamimaṃ nānyo mayā vinā / vetti tajjñātavānevamasau vararuciḥ katham // channaḥ kṛto 'munā nūnaṃ mamāntaḥpuraviplavaḥ / dṛṣṭavānata evāyaṃ strīrūpāṃstatra tānnarān // iti saṃcintayāmāsa yoganandaḥ krudhā jvalan / jāyante bata mūḍhānāṃ saṃvāda api tādṛśāḥ // tataḥ svairaṃ samāhūya śakaṭālaṃ samādiśat / tvayā vararucirvadhyo devīvidhvaṃsanāditi // yathā jñāpayasītyuktvā śakaṭālo 'gamadbahiḥ / acintayacca śaktiḥ syāddhantuṃ vararuciṃ na me //
tgt: Yogananda thus reflected while burning with anger: “No one except myself knows of that spot, which is in a part of the queen’s body usually concealed, then how can this Vararuci have come thus to know it?[4] No doubt he has secretly corrupted my harem, and this is how he came to see there those men disguised as women.” Foolish men often find such coincidences.[5] Then of his own motion he summoned Śakatāla, and gave him the following order:— “You must put Vararuci to death for seducing the queen.” Śakatāla said: “Your Majesty’s orders shall be executed,” and went out of the palace, reflecting: “I should not have power to put Vararuci to death, for he possesses god-like force of intellect;

src: divyabuddhiprabhāvo 'sābuddhartā ca mamāpadaḥ / viprasya tadvaraṃ guptaṃ saṃprati svīkaromi tam //
tgt: and he delivered me from calamity; moreover he is a Brāhman;

src: iti niścitya so 'bhyetya rājñaḥ kopamakāraṇam / vadhāntaṃ kathayitvā me śakaṭālo 'bravīttataḥ // anyaṃ kaṃcitpravādāya hanmyahaṃ tvaṃ ca madgṛhe / pracchannas tiṣṭha mām asmād rakṣituṃ kopanān nṛpāt // iti tadvacanāc channas tadgṛhe 'vasthito 'bhavam / sa cānyaṃ hatavān kaṃcin madvadhākhyātaye niśi // evaṃ prayuktanītiṃ taṃ prītyāvocamahaṃ tadā / eko mantrī bhavānyena hantuṃ māṃ na kṛtā matiḥ //
tgt: therefore I had better hide him and win him over to my side.” Having formed this resolution, he came and told me of the king’s causeless wrath which had ended in his ordering my execution, and thus concluded: “I will have someone else put to death in order that the news may get abroad, and do you remain hidden in my house to protect me from this passionate king.” In accordance with this proposal of his, I remained concealed in his house, and he had someone else put to death at night, in order that the report of my death might be spread.[6] When he had in this way displayed his statecraft, I said to him out of affection: “You have shown yourself an unrivalled minister in that you did not attempt to put me to death;

src: nahi hantumahaṃ śakyo rākṣaso mittramasti me / dhyātamātrāgato viśvaṃ grasate sa madicchayā //
tgt: for I cannot be slain, since I have a Rākṣasa to friend, and he will come, on being only thought of, and at my request will devour the whole world.

src: rājā tvihendradattākhyaḥ sakhā vadhyo na me dvijaḥ / tacchrutvā so 'bravīnmantrī rakṣo me darśyatāmiti //
tgt: As for this king, he is a friend of mine, being a Brāhman named Indradatta, and he ought not to be slain.” Hearing this, that minister said: “Show me the Rākṣasa.” Then I showed him that Rākṣasa who came with a thought;

src: tato dhyātāgataṃ tasmi tadrakṣo 'hamadarśayam / taddarśanācca vitrasto vismitaśca vabhūva saḥ //
tgt: and on beholding him Śakatāla was astonished and terrified.

src: rakṣasyantarhite tasmiñ śakaṭālaḥ sa māṃ punaḥ / kathaṃ te rākṣaso mittraṃ saṃjāta iti pṛṣṭavān // tato 'hamavadaṃ pūrvaṃ rakṣārthaṃ nagare bhraman / rātrau rātrau kṣayaṃ prāpadekaiko nagarādhipaḥ //
tgt: And when the Rākṣasa had disappeared Śakatāla again asked me: “How did the Rākṣasa become your friend?” Then I said: “Long ago the heads of the police, as they went through the city night after night on inspecting duty, perished one by one.

src: tacchrutvā yoganando māmakaronnagarādhipam / bhramaṃścāpaśyamatrāhaṃ bhramantaṃ rākṣasaṃ niśi // sa ca māmavadadbrūhi vidyate nagare 'tra kā / surūpā strīti tacchrutvā vihasyāhaṃ tamabravam // yā yasyābhimatā mūrkha surūpā tasya sā bhavet / tacchrutvaiva tvayaikena jito 'smītyavadatsa mām //
tgt: On hearing that, Yogananda made me head of the police, and as I was on my rounds at night I saw a Rākṣasa roaming about, and he said to me: ‘Tell me, who is considered the best-looking woman in this city?’ When I heard that I burst out laughing, and said: ‘You fool, any woman is good-looking to the man who admires her.’ Hearing my answer, he said: ‘You are the only man that has beaten me.’ And now that I had escaped death by solving his riddle,[7] he again said to me: ‘I am pleased with you;

src: praśnamokṣādvadhottirṇaṃ māṃ punaścābravīdasau / tuṣṭo 'smīti suhṛnme tvaṃ saṃnidhāsye ca te smṛtaḥ //
tgt: henceforth you are my friend, and I will appear to you when you call me to mind.’ Thus he spoke and disappeared, and I returned by the way that I came.

src: ityuktvāntarhite tasminyathāgatamagāmaham / evam āpatsahāyo me rākṣaso mittratāṃ gataḥ // ityuktavānahaṃ bhūyaḥ śakaṭālena cārthitaḥ / gaṅgāmadarśayaṃ tasmai mūrtāṃ dhyānādupasthitām //
tgt: Thus the Rākṣasa has become my friend, and my ally in trouble.” When I had said this, Śakatāla made a second request to me, and I showed him the goddess of the Ganges in human form who came when I thought of her.

src: stutibhistoṣitā sā ca mayā devī tirodadhe / babhūva śakaṭālaśca sahāyaḥ praṇato mayi //
tgt: And that goddess disappeared when she had been gratified by me with hymns of praise. But Śakatāla became from henceforth my obedient ally.

src: ekadā ca sa mantrī māṃ guptasthaṃ khinnamabravīt / sarvajñenāpi khedāya kimātmā dīyate tvayā // kiṃ na jānāsi yadrājñāmavicāraratā dhiyaḥ / acirācca bhavecchuddhistathā cātra kathaṃ śṛṇu // ādityavarmanāmātra babhūva nṛpatiḥ purā / śivavarmābhidhāno 'sya mantrī cābhūnmahāmatiḥ //
tgt: Now once on a time that minister said to me when my state of concealment weighed upon my spirits: “Why do you, although you know all things, abandon yourself to despondency? Do you not know that the minds of kings are most undiscerning, and in a short time you will be cleared from all imputations?[8] In proof of which listen to the following tale:— There reigned here long ago a king named Ādityavarman, and he had a very wise minister, named Śivavarman.

src: rājñastasyaikadā caikā rājñī garbhamadhārayat / tadbuddhvā sa nṛpo 'pṛcchadityantaḥ purarakṣiṇaḥ // varṣadvayaṃ praviṣṭasya vartate 'ntaḥpure 'tra me / tadeṣā garbhasaṃbhūtiḥ kutaḥ saṃprati kathyatām // athocuste praveśo 'tra puṃso 'nyasyāsti na prabho / śivavarmā tu te mantrī praviśatyanivāritaḥ // tacchrutvācintayadrājā nūnaṃ drohī sa eva me / prakāśaṃ ca hate tasminnapavādo bhavenmama // ityālocya sa taṃ yuktyā śivavarmāṇamīśvaraḥ / sāmantasyāntikaṃ sakhyuḥ prāhiṇodbhogavarmaṇaḥ //
tgt: Now it came to pass that one of that king’s queens became pregnant, and when he found it out, the king said to the guards of the harem: “It is now two years since I entered this place, then how has this queen become pregnant? Tell me.” Then they said: “No man except your minister Śivavarman is allowed to enter here, but he enters without any restriction.” When he heard that, the king thought: “Surely he is guilty of treason against me, and yet if I put him to death publicly I shall incur reproach.” Thus reflecting, that king sent that Śivavarman on some pretext to Bhogavarman, a neighbouring chief,[9] who was an ally of his, and immediately afterwards the king secretly sent off a messenger to the same chief, bearing a letter by which he was ordered to put the minister to death.[10] When a week had elapsed after the minister’s departure, that queen tried to escape out of fear, and was taken by the guards with a man in woman’s attire.

src: ādityavarmā tadbuddhvā sānutāpo 'bhavattadā / kiṃ mayā tādṛśo mantrī ghātito 'kāraṇāditi //
tgt: Then Ādityavarman when he heard of it was filled with remorse, and asked himself why he had causelessly brought about the death of so excellent a minister.

src: atrāntare sa ca prāpa nikaṭaṃ bhogavarmaṇaḥ / śivavarmā sa copāgāllekhamādāya pūruṣaḥ // vācayitvā ca taṃ lekhamekānte śivavarmaṇe / śaśaṃsa vadhanirdeśaṃ bhogavarmā vidhervaśāt //
tgt: In the meanwhile Śivavarman reached the Court of Bhogavarman, and that messenger came bringing the letter; and fate would have it so that after Bhogavarman had read the letter he told to Śivavarman in secret the order he had received to put him to death.

src: śivavarmāpy avocat taṃ sāmantaṃ mantrisattamaḥ / tvaṃ vyāpādaya māṃ no cen nihanmyātmānam ātmanā // tacchrutvā vismayāviṣṭo bhogavarmā jagāda tam / kimetadbrūhi me vipra śāpito 'si na vakṣi cet //
tgt: The excellent minister Śivavarman in his turn said to that chief: “Put me to death; if you do not, I will slay myself with my own hand.” When he heard that, Bhogavarman was filled with wonder, and said to him: “What does all this mean? Tell me, Brāhman;

src: atha vakti sma taṃ mantrī hanyeyaṃ yatra bhūpate / tatra dvādaśa varṣāṇi deśe devo na varṣati // tacchrutvā mantribhiḥ sārdhaṃ bhogavarmā vyacintayat / duṣṭaḥ sa rājā deśasya nāśamasmākamicchati // kiṃ hi tatra na santyeva vadhakā guptagāminaḥ / tasmānmantrī na vadhyo 'sau rakṣyaḥ svātmavadhādapi //
tgt: if you do not, you will lie under my curse.” Then the minister said to him: “King, in whatever land I am slain, on that land God will not send rain for twelve years.” When he heard that, Bhogavarman debated with his minister: “That wicked king desires the destruction of our land, for could he not have employed secret assassins to kill his minister? So we must not put this minister to death.

src: iti saṃmantrya dattvā ca rakṣakān bhogavarmaṇā / śivavarmā tato deśāt preṣito 'bhūt tataḥ kṣaṇāt //
tgt: Moreover, we must prevent him from laying violent hands on himself.” Having thus deliberated and appointed him guards, Bhogavarman sent Śivavarman out of his country that moment;

src: evaṃ pratyāyayau jīvansa mantrī prajñayā svayā / śuddhiścāsyānyato jātā nahi dharmo 'nyathā bhavet //
tgt: so that minister by means of his wisdom returned alive, and his innocence was established from another quarter, for righteousness cannot be undone.

src: itthaṃ tavāpi śuddhiḥ syāttiṣṭha tāvadgṛhe mama / kātyāyana nṛpo 'pyeṣa sānutāpo bhaviṣyati //
tgt: In the same way your innocence will be made clear, Kātyāyana[11]; remain for a while in my house; this king too will repent of what he has done.

src: ityuktaḥ śakaṭālena cchanno 'haṃ tasya veśmani / pratīkṣamāṇo 'vasaraṃ tānyahānyatyavāhayam //
tgt: When Śakatāla said this to me, I spent those days concealed in his house.

src: tasyātha yoganandasya kāṇabhūteḥ kadācana / putro hiraṇyaguptākhyo mṛgayāyai gato 'bhavat // aśvavegātprayātasya kathaṃciddūramantaram / ekākino vane tasya vāsaraḥ paryahīyata //
tgt: Then it came to pass that one day, O Kāṇabhūti, a son of that Yogananda named Hiraṇyagupta went out hunting, and when he had somehow or other been carried to a great distance by the speed of his horse, while he was alone in the wood, the day came to an end;

src: tataśca tāṃ niśāṃ netuṃ vṛkṣamārohati sma saḥ / kṣaṇāttatraiva cārohadṛkṣaḥ siṃhena bhīṣitaḥ //
tgt: and then he ascended a tree to pass the night. Immediately afterwards a bear, which had been terrified by a lion, ascended the same tree;

src: sa dṛṣṭvā rājaputraṃ taṃ bhītaṃ mānuṣabhāṣayā / mā bhaiṣīrmama mittraṃ tvamityuktvā nirbhayaṃ vyadhāt //
tgt: he seeing the prince frightened, said to him with a human voice: “Fear not, thou art my friend,” and thus promised him immunity from harm.

src: visrambhādṛkṣavākyena rājaputro 'tha suptavān / ṛkṣastu jāgradevāsīdadhaḥ siṃho 'tha so 'bravīt //
tgt: Then the prince, confiding in the bear’s promise, went to sleep, while the bear remained awake.

src: ṛkṣaṃ mānuṣametaṃ me kṣipa yāvadvrajāmyaham / ṛkṣastato 'bravītpāpa na mitraṃ ghātayāmyaham // kramādṛkṣe prasupte ca rājaputre ca jāgrati / punaḥ siṃho 'bravīdetamṛkṣaṃ me kṣipa mānuṣa // tacchrutvātmabhayāttena siṃhasyārādhanāya saḥ / kṣipto 'pi nāpataccitramṛkṣo daivaprabodhitaḥ //
tgt: Then the lion below said to the bear: “Bear, throw me down this man and I will go away.” Then the bear said: “Villain, I will not cause the death of a friend.” When in course of time the bear went to sleep while the prince was awake, the lion said again: “Man, throw me down the bear.” When he heard that, the prince, who through fear for his own safety wished to propitiate the lion, tried to throw down the bear, but, wonderful to say, it did not fall, since fate caused it to awake.

src: mittradrohin bhavonmatta iti śāpam adāc ca saḥ / tasya rājasutasyaitadvṛttāntāvagamāvadhim //
tgt: And then that bear said to the prince: “Become insane, thou betrayer of thy friend,”[12] laying upon him a curse destined not to end until a third person guessed the whole transaction.

src: prāpyaiva svagṛhaṃ prātarunmatto 'bhūnnṛpātmajaḥ / yoganandaśca taddṛṣṭvā viṣādaṃ sahasāgamat //
tgt: Accordingly the prince, when he reached his palace in the morning, went out of his mind, and Yogananda seeing it was immediately plunged in despondency, and said;

src: abravīcca sa kāle 'smiñ jīved vararucir yadi / idaṃ jñāyeta tatsarvaṃ dhiṅ me tadvadhapāṭavam //
tgt: “If Vararuci were alive at this moment all this matter would be known;

src: tacchrutvā vacanaṃ rājñaḥ śakaṭālo vyacintayat / hanta kātyāyanasyāyaṃ labdhaḥ kālaḥ prakāśane // na so 'tra mānī tiṣṭheca rājā mayi ca viśvaset / ityālocya sa rājānamabravīdyācitābhayaḥ //
tgt: curse on my readiness to have him put to death!” Śakatāla, when he heard this exclamation of the king’s, thought to himself: “Ha! here is an opportunity obtained for bringing Kātyāyana out of concealment, and he, being a proud man, will not remain here, and the king will repose confidence in me.” After reflecting thus, he implored pardon, and said to the king: “O King, cease from despondency;

src: rājannalaṃ viṣādena jīvanvararuciḥ sthitaḥ / yoganandastato 'vādīddrutamānīyatāmiti // athāhaṃ śakaṭālena yoganandāntikaṃ haṭhāt / ānītas taṃ tathābhūtaṃ rājaputraṃ vyalokayam //
tgt: Vararuci remains alive.” Then Yogananda said: “Let him be brought quickly.” Then I was suddenly brought by Śakatāla into the presence of Yogananda and beheld the prince in that state;

src: mittradrohaḥ kṛto 'nena devetyuktvā tathaiva saḥ / sarasvatīprasādena vṛttāntaḥ kathito mayā // tatastacchāpamuktena stuto 'haṃ rājasūnunā / tvayā kathamidaṃ jñātamityapṛcchatsa bhūpatiḥ //
tgt: and by the favour of Sarasvatl I was enabled to reveal the whole occurrence; and I said: “King, he has proved a traitor to his friend.” Then I was praised by that prince who was delivered from his curse; and the king asked me how I had managed to find out what had taken place.

src: athāham avadaṃ rājaṃl lakṣaṇair anumānataḥ / pratibhātaśca paśyanti sarvaṃ prajñāvatāṃ dhiyaḥ //
tgt: Then I said: “King, the minds of the wise see everything by inference from signs, and by acuteness of intellect.

src: tadyathā tilako jñātastathā sarvamidaṃ mayā / iti madvacanātso 'bhūdrājā lajjānutāpavān //
tgt: So I found out all this in the same way as I found out that mole.” When I had said this, that king was afflicted with shame.

src: athānādṛtasatkāraḥ pariśuddhyaiva lābhavān / svagṛhaṃ gatavānasmi śīlaṃ hi viduṣāṃ dhanam //
tgt: Then, without accepting his munificence, considering myself to have gained all I desired by the clearing of my reputation, I went home; for to the wise character is wealth.

src: prāptasyaiva ca tatratyo jano 'rodītpuro mama / abhyetya māṃ samudbhrāntamupavarṣo 'bravīttataḥ // rājā hataṃ niśamya tvāmupakośāgnisādvapuḥ / akarodatha mātuste śucā hṛdayamasphuṭat // tac chrutvābhinavodbhūtaśokāvegavicetanaḥ / sadyo 'ham apataṃ bhūmau vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ //
tgt: And the moment I arrived the servants of my house wept before me, and when I was distressed at it Upavarṣa came to me and said: “Upakośā, when she heard that the king had put you to death, committed her body to the flames,[13] and then your mother’s heart broke with grief.” Hearing that, senseless with the distraction produced by recently aroused grief, I suddenly fell on the ground like a tree broken by the wind; and in a moment I tasted the relief of loud lamentations.

src: kṣaṇācca gatavānasmi pralāpānāṃ rasajñatām / priyabandhuvināśotthaḥ śokāgniḥ kaṃ na tāpayet // ā saṃsāraṃ jagatyasminnekā nityā hyanityatā / tadetāmaiśvarīṃ māyāṃ kiṃ jānannapi muhyasi // ityādibhir upāgatya varṣeṇa vacanair aham / bodhito 'tha yathātattvaṃ kathaṃciddhṛtimāptavān //
tgt: Whom will not the fire of grief, produced by the loss of dear relations, scorch? Varṣa came and gave me sound advice in such words as these: “The only thing that is stable in this ever-changeful world is instability; then why are you distracted though you know this delusion of the Creator?” By the help of these and similar exhortations I at length, though with difficulty, regained my equanimity;

src: tato viraktahṛdayastyaktvā sarvaṃ nibandhanam / praśamaikasahāyo 'haṃ tapovanamaśiśriyam //
tgt: then, with heart disgusted with the world, I flung aside all earthly lords and, choosing self-restraint for my only companion, I went to a grove where asceticism was practised.

src: divaseṣvatha gacchatsu tattapovanamekadā / ayodhyāta upāgacchadvipra eko mayi sthite //
tgt: Then, as days went by, once on a time a Brāhman from Ayodhyā came to that ascetic grove while I was there.

src: sa mayā yoganandasya rājyavārtām apṛcchyata / pratyabhijñāya māṃ so 'tha saśokamidamabravīt // śṛṇu nandasya yadvṛttaṃ tatsakāśādgate tvayi / labdhvāvakāśas tatrābhūc chakaṭālaś cireṇa saḥ //
tgt: I asked him for tidings about Yogananda’s government, and he recognising me told me in sorrowful accents the following story:— “Hear what happened to Nanda after you had left him. Śakatāla, after waiting for it a long time, found that he had now obtained an opportunity of injuring him.

src: sa cintayanvadhopāyaṃ yoganandasya yuktitaḥ / kṣitiṃ khanantamadrākṣīccāṇakyākhyaṃ dvijaṃ pathi //
tgt: While thinking how he might by some device get Yogananda killed, he happened to see a Brāhman named Cāṇakya digging up the earth in his path.

src: kiṃ bhuvaṃ khanasītyukte tena vipro 'tha so 'bravīt / darbhamunmūlayāmyatra pādo hyetena me kṣataḥ // tacchrutvā sahasā mantrī kopanaṃ krūraniścayam / taṃ vipraṃ yoganandasya vadhopāyamamanyata // nāma pṛṣṭvābravīttaṃ ca he brahmandāpayāmi te / ahaṃ trayodaśīśrāddhaṃ gṛhe nandasya bhūpateḥ //
tgt: He said to him: ‘Why are you digging up the earth?’ The Brāhman whom he had asked said: ‘I am rooting up a plant of darbha grass here because it has pricked my foot.[14] When he heard that, the minister thought that Brāhman who formed such stern resolves out of anger would be the best instrument to destroy Nanda with.’ After asking his name he said to him: ‘Brāhman, I assign to you the duty of presiding at a śrāddha [also see notes on śrāddha] on the thirteenth day of the lunar fortnight, in the house of King Nanda;

src: dakṣiṇātaḥ suvarṇasya lakṣaṃ tava bhaviṣyati / bhokṣyase dhuri cānyeṣāmehi tāvadgṛhaṃ mama //
tgt: you shall have one hundred thousand gold pieces by way of fee, and you shall sit at the board above all others;

src: ityuktvā śakaṭālastaṃ cāṇakyamanayadgṛham / śrāddhāhe 'darśayattaṃ ca rājñe sa śraddadhe ca tam //
tgt: in the meanwhile come to my house.’ Saying this, Śakatāla took that Brāhman to his house, and on the day of the śrāddha he showed the Brāhman to the king, and he approved of him.

src: tataḥ sa gatvā cāṇakyo dhuri śrāddha upāviśat / subandhunāmā vipraśca tāmaicchaddhuramātmanaḥ //
tgt: Then Cāṇakya went and sat at the head of the table during the śrāddha, but a Brāhman named Subandhu desired that post of honour for himself.

src: tadgatvā śakaṭālena vijñapto nandabhūpatiḥ / avādīnnāparo yogyaḥ subandhurdhuri tiṣṭhatu // āgatyaitāṃ ca rājājñāṃ śakaṭālo bhayānataḥ / na me 'parādha ityuktvā cāṇakyāya nyavedayat // so 'tha kopena cāṇakyo jvalanniva samantataḥ / nijāṃ muktvā śikhāṃ tatra pratijñāmakarodimām // avaśyaṃ hanta nando 'yaṃ saptabhirdivasairmayā / vināśyo bandhanīyā ca tato nirbhanyunā śikhā //
tgt: Then Śakatāla went and referred the matter to King Nanda, who answered: ‘Let Subandhu sit at the head of the table; no one else deserves the place.’ Then Śakatāla went and, humbly bowing through fear, communicated that order of the king’s to Cāṇakya, adding: ‘It is not my fault.’ Then that Cāṇakya, being, as it were, inflamed all over with wrath, undoing the lock of hair on the crown of his head, made this solemn vow: ‘Surely this Nanda must be destroyed by me within seven days, and then my anger being appeased I will bind up my lock.’[15] When he had said this, Yogananda was enraged;

src: ityuktavantaṃ kupite yoganande palāyitam / alakṣitaṃ svagehe taṃ śakaṭālo nyaveśayat //
tgt: so Cāṇakya escaped unobserved and Śakatāla gave him refuge in his house.

src: tatropakaraṇe datte guptaṃ tenaiva mantriṇā / sa cāṇakyo dvijaḥ kvāpi gatvā kṛtyāmasādhayat //
tgt: Then, being supplied by Śakatāla with the necessary instruments, that Brāhman Cāṇakya went somewhere and performed a magic rite;

src: tadvaśādyoganando 'tha dāhajvaramavāpya saḥ / saptame divase prāpte pañcatvaṃ samupāgamat //
tgt: in consequence of this rite Yogananda caught a burning fever, and died when the seventh day arrived;

src: hatvā hiraṇyaguptaṃ ca śakaṭālena tatsutam / pūrvanandasute lakṣmīścandragupte niveśitā //
tgt: and Śakatāla, having slain Nanda’s son Hiraṇyagupta, bestowed the royal dignity upon Candragupta, a son of the previous Nanda.

src: mantritve tasya cābhyarthya bṛhaspatisamaṃ dhiyā / cāṇakyaṃ sthāpayitvā taṃ sa mantrī kṛtakṛtyatām // manvāno yoganandasya kṛtavairapratikriyaḥ / putraśokena nirviṇṇaḥ praviveśa mahadvanam // iti tasya mukhācchrutvā viprasya sutarāmaham / kāṇabhūte gataḥ khedaṃ sarvamālokya cañcalam //
tgt: And after he had requested Cāṇakya, equal in ability to Bṛhaspati,[16] to be Candragupta’s prime minister and established him in the office, that minister, considering that all his objects had been accomplished, as he had wreaked his vengeance on Yogananda, despondent through sorrow for the death of his sons, retired to the forest.”[17] After I had heard this, O Kāṇabhūti, from the mouth of that Brāhman, I became exceedingly afflicted, seeing that all things are unstable;

src: khedāc cāham imāṃ draṣṭum āgato vindhyavāsinīm / tatprasādena dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ smṛtā jātirmayā sakhe //
tgt: and on account of my affliction I came to visit this shrine of Durgā, and through her favour having beheld you, O my friend, I have remembered my former birth.

src: prāptaṃ divyaṃ ca vijñānaṃ mayoktā te mahākathā / idānīṃ kṣīṇaśāpo 'haṃ yatiṣye dehamujjhitum //
tgt: And having obtained divine discernment I have told you the great tale. Now, as my curse has spent its strength, I will strive to leave the body;

src: tvaṃ ca saṃprati tiṣṭheha yāvadāyāti te 'ntikam / śiṣyayukto guṇāḍhyākhyastyaktabhāṣātrayo dvijaḥ // so 'pi hyahamiva krodhāddevyā śapto gaṇottamaḥ / mālyavānnāma matpakṣapātī martyatvamāgataḥ //
tgt: and do you remain here for the present, until there comes to you a Brāhman named Guṇāḍhya, who has forsaken the use of three languages,[18] surrounded with his pupils, for he like myself was cursed by the goddess in anger, being an excellent Gaṇa, Mālyavān by name, who for taking my part has become a mortal.

src: tasmai maheśvaroktaiṣā kathanīyā mahākathā / tataste śāpanirmuktistasya cāpi bhaviṣyati //
tgt: To him you must tell this tale originally told by Śiva, then you shall be delivered from your curse, and so shall he.

src: evaṃ vararucistatra kāṇabhūternivedya saḥ / pratasthe dehamokṣāya puṇyaṃ badarikāśramam //
tgt: [M] (main story line continued) Having said all this to Kāṇabhūti, that Vararuci set forth for the holy hermitage of Badarikā in order to put off his body.

src: gacchandadarśa gaṅgāyāṃ so 'tha śākāśinaṃ munim / tatsamakṣaṃ ca tasyarṣeḥ kuśenābhūtkarakṣatiḥ //
tgt: As he was going along he beheld on the banks of the Ganges a vegetable-eating[19] hermit, and while he was looking on, that hermit’s hand was pricked with kuśa grass.

src: tato 'sya rudhiraṃ niryattena śākarasīkṛtam / ahaṃkāraparīkṣārthaṃ kautukātsvaprabhāvataḥ //
tgt: Then Vararuci turned his blood, as it flowed out, into sap[20] through his magic power, out of curiosity, in order to test his egotism;

src: taddṛṣṭvā hanta siddho 'smītyagāddarpamasau muniḥ / tato vararuciḥ kiṃcidvihasyeva jagāda tam //
tgt: on beholding that, the hermit exclaimed: “Ha! I have attained perfection”; and so he became puffed up with pride.

src: jijñāsanāya raktaṃ te mayā śākarasīkṛtam / yāvannādyāpyahaṃkāraḥ parityaktastvayā mune //
tgt: Then Vararuci laughed a little and said to him: “I turned your blood into sap in order to test you, because even now, O hermit, you have not abandoned egotism.

src: jñānamārge hyahaṃkāraḥ parigho duratikramaḥ / jñānaṃ vinā ca nāstyeva mokṣo vrataśatairapi //
tgt: Egotism is in truth an obstacle in the road to knowledge hard to overcome, and without knowledge liberation cannot be attained even by a hundred vows.

src: svargastu na mumukṣūṇāṃ kṣayī cittaṃ vilobhayet / tasmādahaṃkṛtityāgājjñāne yatnaṃ mune kuru //
tgt: But the perishable joys of Svarga cannot attract the hearts of those who long for liberation;

src: vinīyaivaṃ muniṃ tena praṇatena kṛtastutiḥ / taṃ badaryāśramoddeśaṃ śāntaṃ vararuciryayau // atha sa nibiḍabhaktyā tatra devīṃ śaraṇyāṃ śaraṇamupagato 'sau martyabhāvaṃ mumukṣuḥ / prakaṭitanijamūrtiḥ sāpi tasmai śaśaṃsa svayamanalasamutthāṃ dhāraṇāṃ dehamuktyai // dagdhvā śarīramatha dhāraṇayā tayā taddivyāṃ gatiṃ vararuciḥ sa nijāṃ prapede / vindhyāṭavībhuvi tataḥ sa ca kāṇabhūtir āsīdabhīpsitaguṇāḍhyasamāgamotkaḥ //
tgt: therefore, O hermit, endeavour to acquire knowledge by forsaking egotism.” Having thus read that hermit a lesson, and having been praised by him prostrate in adoration, Vararuci went to the tranquil site of the hermitage of Badarī.[21] There he, desirous of putting off his mortal condition, resorted for protection with intense devotion to that goddess who only can protect, and she, manifesting her real form to him, told him the secret of that meditation which arises from fire, to help him to put off the body. Then Vararuci, having consumed his body by that form of meditation, reached his own heavenly home;

src: iti mahākaviśrīsomadevabhaṭṭaviracite kathāsaritsāgare kathāpīṭhalambake pañcamas taraṅgaḥ / ṣaṣṭhas taraṅgaḥ / tataḥ sa martyavapuṣā mālyavānvicaranvane / nāmnā guṇāḍhaḥ sevitvā sātavāhanabhūpatim // saṃskṛtādyāstadagre ca bhāṣāstisraḥ pratijñayā / tyaktvā khinnamanā draṣṭumāyayau vindhyavāsinīm //
tgt: and henceforth that Kāṇabhūti remained in the Vindhya forest, eager for his desired meeting with Guṇāḍhya. [M] (main story line continued) THEN that Mālyavān wandering about in the wood in human form, passing under the name of Guṇāḍhya, having served the King Sātavāhana, and having, in accordance with a vow, abandoned in his presence the use of Sanskrit and two other languages, with sorrowful mind came to pay a visit to Durgā, the dweller in the Vindhya hills;

src: tadādeśena gatvā ca kāṇabhūtiṃ dadarśa saḥ / tato jātiṃ nijāṃ smṛtvā prabuddhaḥ sahasābhavat //
tgt: and by her orders he went and beheld Kāṇabhūti. Then he remembered his origin and suddenly, as it were, awoke from sleep;

src: āśritya bhāṣāṃ paiśācīṃ bhāṣātrayavilakṣaṇām / śrāvayitvā nijaṃ nāma kāṇabhūtiṃ ca so 'bravīt // puṣpadantācchrutāṃ divyāṃ śīghraṃ kathaya me kathām / yena śāpaṃ tariṣyāvas tvaṃ cāhaṃ ca samaṃ sakhe // tacchrutvā praṇato hṛṣṭaḥ kāṇabhūtiruvāca tam / kathayāmi kathāṃ kiṃ tu kautukaṃ me mahatprabho //
tgt: and making use of the Paiśācha language, which was different from the three languages he had sworn to forsake, he said to Kāṇabhūti, after telling him his own name: “Quickly tell me that tale which you heard from Puṣpadanta, in order that you and I together, my friend, may escape from our curse.” Hearing that, Kāṇabhūti bowed before him, and said to him in joyful mood: “I will tell you the story, but great curiosity possesses me, my lord;

src: jarāsudhālepasite śarīrāntaḥpurāntare / aśaktirārtirāpacca tiṣṭhanti sukhamaṅganāḥ //
tgt: Again as the white wash of old age whitens the outer body, so debility, diseases and dangers become its inmates in the inner typo apartment.

src: abhāvo'gresarī yatra jarā jayati jantuṣu / kastatreha samāśvāso mama mandamatermune //
tgt: It is the extinction of being that is preceded by old age; therefore I as a man of little understanding, can have no reliance in old age (though extolled by some){GL_NOTE:73106:}

src: kiṃ tena durjīvitadurgraheṇa jarāgatenāpi hi jīvyate yat / jarājagatyāmajitā janānāṃ sarvaiṣaṇāstāta tiraskaroti //
tgt: What then is the good of this miserable life, which lives under the subjection of old age? Senility is irresistable in this world, and defies all efforts to avoid or overcome it.

src: śrīrāma uvāca / vikalpakalpanānalpajalpitairalpabuddhibhiḥ / bhedairuddhuratāṃ nītaḥ saṃsārakuhare bhramaḥ //
tgt: Men of little understandings are found to fall into grave errors in this pit of the world, by their much idle talk, ever doubting scepticism, and schisms.

src: satāṃ kathamivāstheha jāyate jālapañjare / bālā evāttumicchanti phalaṃ mukurabimbitam //
tgt: Good people can have no more confidence in the net work of their ribs, than little children may have a liking for fruits reflected in a mirror.

src: ihāpi vidyate yeṣāṃ pelavā sukhabhāvanā / ākhustantumivāśeṣaṃ kālastāmapi kṛntati //
tgt: Time is a rat that cuts off the threads of all thoughts (prospects), which men may entertain here about the contemptible pleasures of this world.

src: na tadastīha yadayaṃ kālaḥ sakalaghasmaraḥ / grasate tajjagajjātaṃ protthābdhimiva vāḍavaḥ //
tgt: There is nothing in this world which the all-devouring time will spare. He devours all things as the submarine fire consumes the over-flowing sea.

src: samastasāmānyatayā bhīmaḥ kālo maheśvaraḥ / dṛśyasattāmimāṃ sarvāṃ kavalīkartumudyataḥ //
tgt: Time is the sovran lord of all, and equally terrible to all things. He is ever ready to devour all visible beings.

src: mahatāmapi no devaḥ pratipālayati kṣaṇam / kālaḥ kavalitānantaviśvo viśvātmatāṃ gataḥ //
tgt: Time as master of all, spares not even the greatest of us for a moment. He swallows the universe within himself, whence he is known as the universal soul.

src: yugavatsarakalpākhyaiḥ kiṃcitprakaṭatāṃ gataḥ / rūpairalakṣyarūpātmā sarvamākramya tiṣṭhati //
tgt: Time pervades all things, but has no perceptible feature of his own, except that he is imperfectly known by the names of years, ages and kalpas.

src: ye ramyā ye śubhārambhāḥ sumeruguravo'pi ye / kālena vinigīrṇāste garuḍeneva pannagāḥ //
tgt: All that was fair and good, and as great as the mount of Meru, have gone down in the womb of eternity, as the snakes are gorged by the greedy Garuda.

src: nirdayaḥ kaṭhinaḥ krūraḥ karkaśaḥ kṛpaṇo'dhamaḥ / na tadasti yadadyāpi na kālo nigiratyayam //
tgt: There was no one ever so unkind, hard-hearted, cruel, harsh or miserly, whom time has not devoured.

src: kālaḥ kavalanaikāntamatiratti girannapi / anantairapi lokaughairnāyaṃ tṛpto mahāśanaḥ //
tgt: Time is ever greedy although he should devour the mountains. This great gourmand is not satiated with gorging every thing in all the worlds.

src: haratyayaṃ nāśayati karotyatti nihanti ca / kālaḥ saṃsāranṛttaṃ hi nānārūpaṃ yathā naṭaḥ //
tgt: Time like an actor plays many parts on the stage of the world. He abstracts and kills, produces and devours and at last destroys every thing.

src: bhinatti pravibhāgasthabhūtabījānyanāratam / jagatyasattayā bandhāddāḍimāni yathā śukaḥ //
tgt: Time is incessantly picking up the seeds of all the four kinds of living beings from this unreal world, as a parrot picks up the seeds from under the cracked shell of a pomegranate.

src: śubhāśubhaviṣāṇāgravilūnajanapallavaḥ / sphūrjati sphītajanatājīvarājīvanīgajaḥ //
tgt: Time like a wild elephant uproots all proud living beings in this world, as the other pulls up the trees of the forest with their tusks.

src: viriñcimūlabrahmāṇḍabṛhaddevaphaladrumam / brahmakānanamābhogi paramāvṛtya tiṣṭhati //
tgt: This creation of God is like a forest, having Brahma for its foundation and its trees full of the great fruits of gods. Time commands it throughout its length and breadth.

src: yāminī bhramarāpūrṇā racayandinamañjarīḥ / varṣakalpakalāvallīrna kadācana khidyate //
tgt: Time glides along incessantly as a creeping plant, composed of years and ages as its parts, and the sable nights as black bees chasing after them.

src: bhidyate nāvabhagno'pi dagdho'pi hi na dahyate / dṛśyate nāpi dṛśyo'pi dhūrtacūḍāmaṇirmune //
tgt: Time, O sage, is the subtlest of all things. It is divided though indivisible, it is consumed though incombustible, it is perceived though imperceptible in its nature.

src: ekenaiva nimeṣeṇa kiṃcidutthāpayatyalam / kiṃcidvināśayatyuccairmanorājyavadātataḥ //
tgt: Time like the mind is strong enough to create and demolish any thing in a trice, and its province is equally extensive with it.

src: durvilāsavilāsinyā ceṣṭayā kaṣṭaṣuṣṭayā / dravyaikarūpakṛdrūpaṃ janamāvartayansthitaḥ //
tgt: Time is a whirlpool to men; and being accompanied with desire his insatiable and ungovernable mistress and delighting in illicit enjoyments, he makes them do and undo the same thing over and over again.

src: tṛṇaṃ pāṃsuṃ mahendraṃ ca sumeruṃ parṇamarṇavam / ātmaṃbharitayā sarvamātmasātkartumudyataḥ //
tgt: Time is prompted by his rapacity to appropriate every thing to himself, from the meanest straw, dust, leaves and worms, to the greatest Indra and the mount Meru itself.

src: krauryamatraiva paryāptaṃ lubdhatātraiva saṃsthitā / sarvadaurbhāgyamatraiva cāpalaṃ vāpi duḥsaham //
tgt: Time is the source of all malice and greediness, and the spring of all misfortunes, and intolerable fluctuations of our states.

src: preraya~llīlayārkendū krīḍatīva nabhastale / nikṣiptalīlāyugalo nije bāla ivāṅgaṇe //
tgt: As boys with their balls play about their play-ground, so does time in his arena of the sky, play with his two balls of the sun and moon.

src: sarvabhūtāsthimālābhirāpādavalitākṛtiḥ / vilasatyeva kalpānte kālaḥ kalitakalpanaḥ //
tgt: Time at the expiration of the kalpa age, will dance about with a long chain of the bones of the dead hanging from his neck to the feet.

src: asyoḍḍāmaravṛttasya kalpānte'ṅgavinirgataiḥ / prasphuratyambare merurbhūrjatvagiva vāyubhiḥ //
tgt: The gale of desolation rising from the body of this desolator of the world at the end of a kalpa age, causes the fragments of mount Meru to fly about in the air like the rinds of the bhoja-petera tree.

src: rudro bhūtvā bhavatyeṣa mahendro'tha pitāmahaḥ / śakro vaiśravaṇaścāpi punareva na kiṃcana //
tgt: Time then assumes his terrific form of fire ([Sanskrit: pralayagni]), to dissolve the world in empty space, when the gods Brahma and Indra and all others cease to exist.

src: dhatte'jasrotthitoddhvastānsargānamitabhāsvarān / anyāndadhaddivānaktaṃ vīcīrabdhirivātmani //
tgt: As the sea shows himself in a continued series of waves rising and falling one after another, so it is time that creates and dissolves the world, and appears to rise and fall in the rotation of days and nights.

src: mahākalpābhidhānebhyo vṛkṣebhyaḥ pariśātayan / devāsuragaṇānpakvānphalabhārāniva sthitaḥ //
tgt: Time plucks the gods and demigods as ripe fruits, from their great arbor of existence, at the end of the world,

src: kālo'yaṃ bhūtamaśakaghuṃghumānāṃ prapātinām / brahmāṇḍodumbaraughānāṃ bṛhatpādapatāṃ gataḥ //
tgt: Time resembles a large fig tree (Ficus religiosa), studded with all the worlds as its fruits, and resonant with the noise of living beings like the hissing of gnats about them.

src: sattāmātrakumudvatyā cijjyotsnāpariphullayā / vapurvinodayatyekaṃ kriyāpriyatamānvitaḥ //
tgt: Time accompanied by Action as his mate, regales himself in the garden of the world, blossoming with the moon-beams of the Divine Spirit.

src: anantāpāraparyantabaddhapīṭhaṃ nijaṃ vapuḥ / mahāśailavaduttuṅgamavalambya vyavasthitaḥ //
tgt: As the high and huge rock supports its body upon the basis of the earth, so does time rest itself in endless and interminable eternity.

src: kvacicchayāmatamaḥśyāmaṃ kvacitkāntiyutaṃ tatam / dvayenāpi kvacidriktaṃ svabhāvaṃ bhāvayan sthitaḥ //
tgt: Time assumes to himself various hues of black, white and red (at night, day and midday) which serve for his vestures.

src: saṃlīnāsaṃkhyasaṃsārasārayā svātmasattayā / urvyeva bhāraghanayā nibaddhapadatāṃ gataḥ //
tgt: As the earth is the great support of hills which are fixed upon it, so is time the support of all the innumerable ponderous worlds that constitute the universe.

src: na khidyate nādriyate nāyāti na ca gacchati / nāstameti na codeti mahākalpaśatairapi //
tgt: Hundreds of great kalpa ages (of the creation and dissolution of the world) may pass away, yet there is nothing that can move eternity to pity or concern, or stop or expedite his course. It neither sets nor rises.

src: kevalaṃ jagadārambhalīlayā ghanahelayā / pālayatyātmanātmānamanahaṃkāramātatam //
tgt: Time is never proud to think, that it is he who without the least sense of pain and labor, brings this world into play and makes it to exist.

src: yāminīpaṅkakalitāṃ dinakokanadāvalīm / meghabhramarikāmātmasarasyāropayansthitaḥ //
tgt: Time is like a reservoir in which the nights are as mud, the days as lotuses, and the clouds as bees.

src: gṛhītvā kṛpaṇaḥ kṛṣṇāṃ rajanīṃ jīrṇamārjanīm / ālokakanakakṣodānāharatyabhito girim //
tgt: As a covetous man, with worn out broom sticks in hand, sweeps over a mountain to gather the particles of gold strewn over it, so does time with his sweeping course of days and nights, collect in one mass of the dead all living beings in the world.

src: saṃcārayankriyāṅgulyā koṇakeṣvarkadīpikām / jagatsadmani kārpaṇyātkva kimastīti vīkṣate //
tgt: As a miserly man trims and lights a lamp with his own fingers, to look into his stores at each corner of the room; so does time light the lamps of the sun and moon to look into the living beings in every nook and corner of the world.

src: prekṣyāharvinimeṣeṇa sūryākṣṇā pākavantyalam / lokapālaphalānyatti jagajjīrṇavanādayam //
tgt: As one ripens the raw fruits in sun and fire in order to devour them, so does time ripen men by their sun and fire worship, to bring them under his jaws at last.

src: jagajjīrṇakuṭīkīrṇānarpayatyugrakoṭare / krameṇa guṇavallokamaṇīnmṛtyusamudgake //
tgt: The world is a dilapidated cottage and men of parts are rare gems in it. Time hides them in the casket of his belly, as a miser keeps his treasure in a coffer.

src: guṇairāpūryate yaiva lokaratnāvalī bhṛśam / bhūṣārthamiva tāmaṅge kṛtvā bhūyo nikṛntati //
tgt: Good men are like a chaplet of gems, which time puts on his head for a time with fondness, and then tears and tramples it down.

src: dinahaṃsānusṛtayā niśendīvaramālayā / tārakesarayājasraṃ capalo valayatyalam //
tgt: Strings of days, nights and stars, resembling beads and bracelets of white and black lotuses, are continually turning round the arm of time.

src: śailārṇadyudharāśṛṅgajagadūrṇāyusaunikaḥ / pratyahaṃ pibate prekṣya tārāraktakaṇānapi //
tgt: Time (as a vulture) looks upon the world as (the carcase of) a ram, with its mountains, seas, sky and earth as its four horns, and the stars as its drops of blood which it drinks day by day.

src: tāruṇyanalinīsoma āyurmātaṅgakesarī / na tadasti na yasyāyaṃ tucchātucchasya taskaraḥ //
tgt: Time destroys youth as the moon shuts the petals of the lotus. It destroys life as the lion kills the elephant: there is nothing however insignificant that time steals not away.

src: kalpakelivilāsena piṣṭapātitajantunā / abhāvo bhāvabhāsena ramate svātmanātmani //
tgt: Time after sporting for a Kalpa period in the act of killing and crushing of all living beings, comes to lose its own existence and becomes extinct in the eternity of the Spirit of spirits.

src: kartā bhoktātha saṃhartā smartā sarvapadaṃ gataḥ //
tgt: Time after a short rest and respite reappears as the creator, preserver, destroyer and remembrancer of all. He shows the shapes of all things whether good or bad, keeping his own nature beyond the knowledge of all. Thus doth time expand and preserve and finally dissolve all things by way of sport.

src: sakalamapyakalākalitāntaraṃ subhagadurbhagarūpadharaṃ vapuḥ / prakaṭayansahasaiva ca gopayan vilasatīha hi kālabalaṃ nṛṣu //
tgt: ?missing text?

src: śrīrāma uvāca / asyoḍḍāmaralīlasya dūrāstasakalāpadaḥ / saṃsāre rājaputrasya kālasyākalitaujasaḥ //
tgt: Rama rejoined:—Time is a self-willed sportsman as a prince, who is inaccessible to dangers and whose powers are unlimited.

src: asyaivācarato dīnairmugdhairbhūtamṛgabrajaiḥ / ākheṭakaṃ jarjarite jagajjaṅgalajālake //
tgt: This world is as it were a forest and sporting ground of time, wherein the poor deluded worldlings are caught in his snare like bodies of wounded stags.

src: ekadeśollasaccāruvaḍavānalapaṅkajā / krīḍāpuṣkariṇī ramyā kalpakālamahārṇavaḥ //
tgt: The ocean of universal deluge is a pleasure-pond of time, and the submarine fires bursting therein as lotus flowers.

src: kaṭutiktāmlabhūtādyaiḥ sadadhikṣīrasāgaraiḥ / taireva taiḥ paryuṣitairjagadbhiḥ kalvavartanam //
tgt: Time makes his breakfast of this vapid and stale earth, flavoured with the milk and curd of the seas of those names.

src: caṇḍī caturasaṃcārā sarvamātṛgaṇānvitā / saṃsāravanavinyastā vyāghrī bhūtaughaghātinī //
tgt: His wife Chandi (Hecate) with her train of Matris (furies), ranges all about this wide world as a ferocious tigress.

src: jñadhvī karatale jñathvī pānapātrī rasānvitā / kamalotpalakahlāralolajālakamālitā //
tgt: The earth with her waters is like a bowl of wine in the hand of time, dressed and flavoured with all sorts of lilies and lotuses.

src: virāvī vikaṭāsphoṭo nṛsiṃho bhujapañjare / saṭāvikaṭapīnāṃsaḥ kṛtaḥ krīḍāśakuntakaḥ //
tgt: The lion with his huge body and startling mane, his loud roaring and tremendous groans, seems as a caged bird of sport in the hand of time.

src: alābuvīṇāmadhuraḥ śaradvyomalasacchaviḥ / devaḥ kila mahākālo līlākokilabālakaḥ //
tgt: The Mahakala like a playful young Kokila (cuckoo), appears in the figure of the blue autumnal sky, and warbling as sweet as the notes of a lute of gourd.

src: ajasrasphūrjitākāro vāntaduḥkhaśarāvaliḥ / abhāvanāmakodaṇḍaḥ parisphurati sarvataḥ //
tgt: The restless bow of death is found flinging its woeful arrows (darts of death) with ceaseless thunder claps on all sides.

src: anuttamastvadhikavilāsapaṇḍito bhramaccalanparivilasanvidārayan / jarajjagajjanitavilolamarkaṭaḥ parisphuradvapuriha kāla īhate //
tgt: This world is like a forest, wherein sorrows are ranging about as playful apes, and time like a sportive prince in this forest, is now roving, now walking, now playing and now killing his game.

src: śrīrāma uvāca atraiva durvilāsānāṃ cūḍamaṇirihāparaḥ / karotyattīti loke'smindaivaṃ kālaśca kathyate //
tgt: Time stands the foremost of all deceitful players in this world. He acts the double parts of creation and destruction, and of action and fate.

src: kriyāmātrādṛte yasya svaparispandarūpiṇaḥ / nānyadālakṣyate rūpaṃ na karma na samīhitam //
tgt: Time has no other character but those of action and motion by which his existence is known to us, and which bind all beings.

src: teneyamakhilā bhūtasaṃtatiḥ paripelavā / tāpena himamāleva nītā vidhuratāṃ bhṛśam //
tgt: Fate is that which frustrates (the necessary consequences of) the acts of all created beings, as the solar heat serves to dissolve the conglomeration of snows.

src: yadidaṃ dṛśyate kiṃcijjagadābhogi maṇḍalam / tattasya nartanāgāramihāsāvatinṛtyati //
tgt: This wide world is the stage wherein the giddy mob dance about.

src: tṛtīyaṃ ca kṛtānteti nāma bibhratsudāruṇam / kāpālikavapurmattaṃ daivaṃ jagati nṛtyati //
tgt: Time has a third name of a terrifying nature known as Kritantah (Fate), who in the form of a Kapalika (one holding human skulls in his hand), dances about in the world.

src: nṛtyato hi kṛtāntasya nitāntamiva rāgiṇaḥ / nityaṃ niyatikāntāyāṃ mune paramakāmitā //
tgt: This dancing and loving Kritantah (Fate), is accompanied by his consort called Destiny to whom he is greatly attached.

src: śeṣaḥ śaśikalāśubhro gaṅgāvāhaśca tau tridhā / upavīte avīte ca ubhau saṃsāravakṣasi //
tgt: Time (as Siva), wears on his bosom of the world, the triplicate white and holy thread composed of the serpent named Ananta and the stream of Ganges, and the digit of the moon on his forehead.

src: candrārkamaṇḍale hemakaṭakau karamūlayoḥ / līlāsarasijaṃ haste brahmanbrahmāṇḍakarṇikā //
tgt: The sun and the moon are the golden armlets of time, who holds in his palm the mundane world as the paltry plaything of a nosegay.

src: tārābinducitaṃ lolapuṣkarāvartapallavam / ekārṇavapayodhau tamekamambaramambaram //
tgt: The firmament with its stars appears like a garment with coloured spots in it; the clouds called Pushkara and Avarta are as the skirts of that garment, which are washed by Time in the waters of the universal deluge.

src: evaṃrūpasya tasyāgre niyatirnityakāminī / anastamitasaṃrambhamārambhaiḥ parinṛtyati //
tgt: Before him, dances his beloved Destiny with all her arts for ever, to beguile the living that are fond of worldly enjoyments.

src: tasyā nartanalolāyā jaganmaṇḍapakoṭare / aruddhaspandarūpāyā āgamāpāyacañcure //
tgt: People hurry up and down to witness the dance of Destiny, whose unrestrained motion keeps them at work, and causes their repeated births and deaths.

src: cārubhūṣaṇamaṅgeṣu devalokāntarāvalī / āpātālaṃ nabholambaṃ kabarīmaṇḍalaṃ bṛhat //
tgt: The people of all the worlds are studded about her person as her ornaments, and the sky stretching from the heaven of gods to the infernal regions, serves for the veil on her head.

src: narakālī ca mañjīramālā kalakalojjvalā / protā duṣkṛtasūtreṇa pātālacaraṇe sthitā //
tgt: Her feet are planted in the infernal regions, and the hell-pits ring at her feet like trinkets, tied by the string of evil deeds or sins.

src: kastūrikātilakakaṃ kriyāsaṃkhyopakalpitam / citritaṃ citraguptena yame vadanapaṭṭake //
tgt: She is painted all over from head to foot by the god Chitra Gupta with ornamental marks prepared by her attendants (the deeds of men), and perfumed with the essence of those deeds.

src: kālāsyaṃ samupādāya kalpānteṣu kilākulā / nṛtyatyeṣā punardevī sphuṭacchailaghanāravam //
tgt: She dances and reels at the nod of her husband at the end of the Kalpas, and makes the mountains crack and crash at her foot-falls.

src: paścātprālambavibhrāntakaumārabhṛtabarhibhiḥ / netratrayavṛhadrandhrabhūribhāṅkārabhīṣaṇaiḥ //
tgt: Behind her dance the peacocks of the god Kumara; and Kala the god of death staring with his three wide open eyes, utters his hideous cries.

src: lambalolajaṭācandravikīrṇaharamūrdhabhiḥ / uccaraccārumandāragaurīkabaracāmaraiḥ //
tgt: Death dances about in the form of the five headed Hara, with the loosened braids of hair upon him; while Destiny in the form of Gauri, and her locks adorned with Mandara flowers keeps her pace with him.

src: uttāṇḍavācalākārabhairavodaratumbakaiḥ / raṇatsaśatarandhrendradehabhikṣākapālakaiḥ //
tgt: This Destiny in her war-dance, bears a capacious gourd representing her big belly, and her body is adorned with hundreds of hollow human skulls jingling like the alms-pots of the Kapali mendicants.

src: śuṣkaśārīrakhaṭvāṅgabharairāpūritāmbaram / bhīṣayatyātmanātmānaṃ sarvasaṃhārakāriṇī //
tgt: She has filled (reached) the sky with the emaciated skeleton of her body, and gets terrified at her all destructive figure.

src: viśvarūpaśiraścakracārupuṣkaramālayā / tāṇḍaveṣu vivalgantyā mahākalpeṣu rājate //
tgt: The skulls of the dead of various shapes adorn her body like a beautiful garland of lotuses, which keep hanging to and fro during her dance at the end of a Kalpa age.

src: pramattapuṣkarāvartaḍamaroḍḍāmarāravaiḥ / tasyāḥ kila palāyante kalpānte tumburādayaḥ //
tgt: The horrible roaring of the giddy clouds Pushkara and Avarta at the end of the Kalpa, serves to represent the beating of her Damaru drum, and put to flight the heavenly choir of Tumburu.

src: nṛtyato'ntaḥ kṛtāntasya candramaṇḍalabhāsinaḥ / tārakācandrikācāruvyomapicchāvacūlinaḥ //
tgt: As death dances along, the moon appears like his ear-ring, and the moon-beams and stars appear like his crest made of peacocks' feathers.

src: ekasmiñchravaṇe dīptā himavānasthimudrikā / apare ca mahāmeruḥ kāntā kāñcanakarṇikā //
tgt: The snow-capt Himalaya, appears like a circlet of bones in the upper loop of his right ear, and the mount Meru as a golden areola in that of the left.

src: atraiva kuṇḍale lole candrārkau gaṇḍamaṇḍale / lokālokācalaśreṇī sarvataḥ kaṭimekhalā //
tgt: Under their lobes are suspended the moon and the sun, as pendant ear-rings glittering over his cheeks. The mountain ranges called the lokaloka are fastened like chains around his waist.

src: itaścetaśca gacchantī vidyudvalayakarṇikā / anilāndolitā bhāti nīradāṃśukapaṭṭikā //
tgt: The lightnings are the bracelets and armlets of Destiny, which move to and fro as she dances along. The clouds are her wrappers that fly about her in the air.

src: musalaiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ prāsaiḥ śūlaistomaramudgaraiḥ / tīkṣṇaiḥ kṣīṇajagadvāntakṛtāntairiva saṃbhṛtaiḥ //
tgt: Death is furnished with many weapons, as clubs, axes, missiles, spears, shovels, mallets and sharp swords, all of which are sure weapons of destruction.

src: saṃsārabandhanādīrghe pāśe kālakaracyute / śeṣabhogamahāsūtraprote mālāsya śobhate //
tgt: Mundane enjoyments are no other than long ropes dropped down by the hand of death, and keeping all mankind fast bound to the world; while the great thread of infinity (ananta) is worn by him as his wreath of flowers.

src: jīvollasanmakarikāratnatejobhirujjvalā / saptābdhikaṅkaṇaśreṇī bhujayorasya bhūṣaṇam //
tgt: The belts of the seven oceans are worn about the arms of Death as his bracelets resplendent with the living sea-animals, and the bright gems contained in their depths.

src: vyavahāramahāvartā sukhaduḥkhaparamparā / rajaḥpūrṇatamaḥśyāmā romālī tasya rājate //
tgt: The great vortices of customs, the successions of joy and grief, the excess of pride and the darkness of passions, form the streaks of hair on his body.

src: evaṃprāyaḥ sa kalpānte kṛtāntastāṇḍavodbhavām / upasaṃhṛtya nṛtyehāṃ sṛṣṭvā saha maheśvaram //
tgt: After the end of the world, he ceases to dance, and creates anew all things from the lowest animal that lives in the earth, to the highest Brahma and Siva.

src: punarlāsyamayīṃ nṛtyalīlāṃ sargasvarūpiṇīm / tanotīmāṃ jarāśokaduḥkhābhibhavabhūṣitām //
tgt: Destiny as an actress, acts by turns her parts of creation and destruction, diversified by scenes of old age, sorrow and misery.

src: bhūyaḥ karoti bhuvanāni vanāntarāṇi lokāntarāṇi janajālakakalpanāṃ ca / ācāracārukalanāmacalāṃ calāṃ ca paṅkādyathārbhakajano racanāmakhinnaḥ //
tgt: Time repeatedly creates the worlds and their woods, with the different abodes and localities teeming with population. He forms the moveable and immovable substances, establishes customs and again dissolves them, as boys make their dolls of clay and break them soon afterwards.

src: śrīrāma uvāca / vṛtte'sminnevameteṣāṃ kālādīnāṃ mahāmune / saṃsāranāmni kaivāsthā mādṛśānāṃ vadatviha //
tgt: Rama said:—Such being the all destructive conduct of time and others (as already described), what confidence, O great sage, can men like me, have upon them?

src: vikrītā iva tiṣṭhāma etairdaivādibhirvayam / mune prapañcaracanairmugdhā vanamṛgā iva //
tgt: We all remain here, O sage! as slaves sold to Fate and Destiny, and are deceived by their allurements as beasts of the forest.

src: eṣo'nāryasamāmnāyaḥ kālaḥ kavalanonmukhaḥ / jagatyavirataṃ lokaṃ pātayatyāpadarṇave //
tgt: This Fate whose conduct is so very inhuman, is always up to devour all beings, and is incessantly throwing men into the sea of troubles.

src: dahatyantardurāśābhirdevo dāruṇaceṣṭayā / lokamuṣṇaprakāśābhijvālābhirdahano yathā //
tgt: He is led by his malicious attempts to inflame the mind with inordinary desires, as the fire raises its flames to burn down a habitation.

src: dhṛtiṃ vidhurayatyeṣā maryādārūpavallabhā / strītvātsvabhāvacapalā niyatirniyatonmukhī //
tgt: Destiny the faithful and obedient wife of Fate, is naturally fickle on account of her being a female, and is always bent on mischief and disturbing the patience.

src: grasate'virataṃ bhūtajālaṃ sarpa ivānilam / kṛtāntaḥ karkaśācāro jarāṃ nītvā'jaraṃ vapuḥ //
