tgt: As the heinous serpent feeds upon the air, so does cruel Death ever swallow the living. He ripens the body with old age to create his zest, and then devours all animals warm with life.

src: yamo nirghṛṇarājendro nārtaṃ nāmānukampate / sarvabhūtadayodāro jano durlabhatāṃ gataḥ //
tgt: Death is called a relentless tyrant, having no pity even for the sick and weak; nor any regard for any one in any state of life.

src: sarvā eva mune phalguvibhavā bhūtajātayaḥ / duḥkhāyaiva durantāya dāruṇā bhogabhūmayaḥ //
tgt: Every one in this world is fond of affluence and pleasures, not knowing that these are only calculated to lead him to his ruin.

src: āyuratyantacapalaṃ mṛtyurekāntaniṣṭhuraḥ / tāruṇyaṃ cātitaralaṃ bālyaṃ jaḍatayā hṛtam //
tgt: Life is very unsteady. Death is very cruel. Youth is very frail and fickle, and boyhood is full of dullness and insensibility.

src: kalākalaṅkito loko bandhavo bhavabandhanam / bhogā bhavamahārogāstṛṣṇāśca mṛgatṛṣṇikāḥ //
tgt: Man is defiled by his worldliness, his friends are ties to the world, his enjoyments are the greatest of his diseases in life, and his avarice and ambition are the mirage that always allures him.

src: śatravaścendriyāṇyeva satyaṃ yātamasatyatām / praharatyātmanaivātmā manasaiva mano ripuḥ //
tgt: Our very senses are our enemies, before which even truth appears as falsehood; the mind is the enemy of the mind and self is the enemy of self.

src: ahaṃkāraḥ kalaṅkāya buddhayaḥ paripelavāḥ / kriyā duṣphaladāyinyo līlāḥ strīniṣṭhatāṃ gatāḥ //
tgt: Self-esteem is stained (with the name of selfishness), intelligence is blamed for its fallaciousness, our actions are attended with bad results, and our pleasures tend only to effeminacy.

src: vāñchāviṣayaśālinyaḥ saccamatkṛtayaḥ kṣatāḥ / nāryo doṣapatākinyo rasā nīrasatāṃ gatāḥ //
tgt: All our desires are directed to enjoyments; our love of truth is lost; our women are the ensigns of vice, and all that were once so sweet, have become tasteless and vapid.

src: vastvavastutayā jñātaṃ dattaṃ cittamahaṃkṛtau / abhāvavedhitā bhāvā bhāvānto nādhigamyate //
tgt: Things that are not real, are believed as real, and have become the cause of our pride, by hardening us in untruth, and keeping us from the light of truth.

src: tapyate kevalaṃ sādho matirākulitāntarā / rāgarogo vilasati virāgo nopagacchati //
tgt: My mind is at a loss to think what to do; it regrets at its increased appetite for pleasure, and for want of that self-denial.

src: rajoguṇahatā dṛṣṭistamaḥ saṃparivardhate / na cādhigamyate sattvaṃ tattvamatyantadūrataḥ //
tgt: My sight is dimmed by the dust of sensuality: the darkness of self-esteem prevails upon me: the purity of mind is never reached to, and truth is far off from me.

src: sthitirasthiratāṃ yātā mṛtirāgamanonmukhī / dhṛtirvaidhuryamāyātā ratirnityamavastuni //
tgt: Life is become uncertain and death is always advancing nigh; my patience is disturbed, and there is an increased appetite for whatever is false.

src: matirmāndyena malinā pātaikaparamaṃ vapuḥ / jvalatīva jarā dehe pratisphurati duṣkṛtam //
tgt: The mind is soiled by dullness, and the body is cloyed with surfeit and ready to fall; old age exults over the body, and sins are conspicuous at every step.

src: yatnena yāti yuvatā dūre sajjanasaṃgatiḥ / gatirna vidyate kācitkvacinnodeti satyatā //
tgt: Youth flies fast away with all our care to preserve it; the company of the good is at a distance; the light of truth shines from no where;and I can have recourse to nothing in this world.

src: mano vimuhyatīvāntarmuditā dūratāṃ gatā / nojjvalā karuṇodeti dūrādāyāti nīcatā //
tgt: The mind is stupified within itself, and its contentment has fled from it: there is no rise of enlightened sentiments in it, and meanness makes its advance to it from a distance.

src: dhīratā'dhīratāmeti pātotpātaparo janaḥ / sulabho durjanāśleṣo durlabhaḥ satsamāgamaḥ //
tgt: Patience is converted into impatience; man is liable to the states of birth and death; good company is rare, but bad company is ever within the reach of every body.

src: āgamāpāyino bhāvā bhāvanā bhavabandhanī / nīyate kevalaṃ kvāpi nityaṃ bhūtaparamparā //
tgt: All individual existences are liable to appear and disappear; all desires are chains to the world, and all worldly beings are ever seen to be led away per force where no body can tell.

src: diśo'pi hi na dṛśyante deśo'pyanyāpadeśabhāk / śailā api viśīryante kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on human life, when the points of the compass become indistinct and undiscernible; when the countries and places change their positions and names, and when mountains even are liable to be dilapidated?

src: adyate sattayāpi dyaurbhu'vana cāpi ūyate / dharāpi yāti vaidhuryaṃ kevāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on man, when the heavens are swallowed in infinity, when this world is absorbed in nothingness, and the very earth loses her stability?

src: śuṣyantyapi samudrāśca śīryante tārakā api / siddhā api vinaśyanti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on men like ourselves, when the very seas are liable to be dried up, when the stars are doomed to fade away and disappear, and when the most perfect of beings are liable to dissolution?

src: dānavā api dīryante dhruvo'pyadhruvajīvitaḥ / amarā api māryante kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on men like us, when even the demigods are liable to destruction, when the polar star is known to change its place, and when the immortal gods are doomed to mortality?

src: śakro'pyākramyate vakrairyamo'pi hi niyamyate / vāyurapyetyavāyutvaṃ kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on men like us, when Indra is doomed to be defeated by demons; when even death is hindered from his aim, and when the current air ceases to breathe?

src: somo'pi vyomatāṃ yāti mārtaṇḍo'pyeti khaṇḍatām / magnatāmagnirapyeti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the very moon is to vanish with the sky, when the very sun is to be split into pieces, and when fire itself is to become frigid and cold?

src: parameṣṭhyapi niṣṭhāvānhriyate hīrarapyajaḥ / bhavo'pyabhāvamāyāti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the very Hari and Brahma are to be absorbed into the Great One, and when Siva himself is to be no more.

src: kālaḥ saṃkālyate yena niyatiścāpi nīyate / khamapyālīyate'nantaṃ kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
tgt: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the duration of time comes to be counted, when Destiny is destined to her final destiny, and when all vacuity loses itself in infinity?

src: aśrāvyāvācyadurdarśatattvenājñātamūrtinā / bhuvanāni viḍambyante kenacidbhramadāyinā //
tgt: That which is inaudible, unspeakable, invisible, and unknowable in his real form, displays to us these wondrous worlds by some fallacy.

src: ahaṃkārakalāmetya sarvatrāntaravāsinā / na so'sti triṣu lokeṣu yasteneha na bādhyate //
tgt: No one conscious of himself (his egoism), can disown his subjection to that Being, that dwells in the hearts of every one.

src: śilāśailakavapreṣu sāśvabhūto divākaraḥ / vanapāṣāṇavannityamavaśaḥ paricodyate //
tgt: This sun said:—the lord of worlds, is impelled (by that power) to run over hills, rocks and fields, like an inert piece of stone, hurled down from a mountain and borne away by a current stream.

src: dharāgolakamantasthasurāsuragaṇāspadam / veṣṭyate dhiṣṇyacakreṇa pakvākṣoṭamiva tvacā //
tgt: This globe of earth, the seat of all the Suras and Asuras, and surrounded by the luminous sphere in the manner of a walnut covered by its hard crust, subsists under His command.

src: divi devā bhuvi narāḥ pātāleṣu ca bhoginaḥ / kalpitāḥ kalpamātreṇa nīyante jarjarāṃ daśām //
tgt: The Gods in the heavens, the men on earth and the serpents in the nether world, are brought into existence and led to decay by His will only.

src: kāmaśca jagadīśānaraṇalabdhaparākramaḥ / akrameṇaiva vikrānto lokamākramya valgati //
tgt: Kama (Cupid) that is arbitrarily powerful, and has forcibly overpowered on all the living world, has derived his unconquerable might from the Lord of worlds.

src: vasanto mattamātaṅgo madaiḥ kusumavarṣaṇaiḥ / āmoditakakupcakraśceto nayati cāpalam //
tgt: As the heated elephant regales the air with his spirituous exudation, so does the spring perfume the air with his profusion of flowers, unsettling the minds of men.

src: anuraktāṅganālolalocanālokitākṛti / svasthīkartuṃ manaḥ śakto na viveko mahānapi //
tgt: So are the loose glances of loving damsels directed to inflict deep wounds in the heart of man, which his best reason is unable to heal.

src: paropakārakāriṇyā parārtiparitaptayā / buddha eva sukhī manye svātmaśītalayā dhiyā //
tgt: One whose best endeavour is always to do good to others, and who feels for others' woes, is really intelligent and happy under the influence of his cool judgement.

src: utpannadhvaṃsinaḥ kālavaḍavānalapātinaḥ / saṃkhyātuṃ kena śakyante kallolā jīvitāmbudhau //
tgt: Who can count the number of beings resembling the waves of the ocean, and on whom death has been darting the submarine fire of destruction.

src: sarva eva narā mohāddurāśāpāśapāśinaḥ / doṣagulmakasāraṅgā viśīrṇā janmajaṅgale / saṃkṣīyate jagati janmaparamparāsu lokasya tairiha kukarmabhirāyuretat //
tgt: All mankind are deluded to entrap themselves in the snare of avarice, and to be afflicted with all evils in life, as the deer entangled in the thickets of a jungle.

src: ākāśapādapalatākṛtapāśakalpaṃ yeṣāṃ phalaṃ nahi vicāravido'pi vidmaḥ //
tgt: The term of human life in this world, is decreased in each generation in proportion to (the increase of their wicked acts). The desire of fruition is as vain as the expectation of reaping fruits from a creeper growing in the sky: yet I know not why men of reason would not understand this truth.

src: adyotsavo'yamṛtureṣa tatheha yātrā te bandhavaḥ sukhamidaṃ saviśeṣabhogam / itthaṃ mudhaiva kalayansuvikalpajālamālolapelavamatirgalatīha lokaḥ //
tgt: This is a day of festivity, a season of joy and a time of procession. Here are our friends, here the pleasures and here the variety of our entertainments. Thus do men of vacant minds amuse themselves with weaving the web of their desires, until they become extinct.

src: śrīrāma uvāca / anyacca tātā'titarāmaramye manorame ceha jagatsvarūpe / na kiṃcidāyāti tadarthajātaṃ yenātiviśrāntimupaiti cetaḥ //
tgt: Rama said:—O sage! this seemingly pleasing but actually unpleasant world, has nothing in it that is productive of such a thing as can afford tranquility to the soul.

src: bālye gate kalpitakelilole manomṛge dāradarīṣu jīrṇe / śarīrake jarjaratāṃ prayāte vidūyate kevalameva lokaḥ //
tgt: After the playful boyhood is over, the mind wastes itself in the society of women like the deer fallen in a cavern, then the body bends down under old age, and the man has only to grieve.

src: jarātuṣārābhihatāṃ śarīrasarojinīṃ dūratare vimucya / kṣaṇādgate jīvitacañcarīke janasya saṃsārasaro'vaśuṣkam //
tgt: As the body is stricken with the frost of old age, its beauty flies afar from it like the bloom of the fading lotus, and then the fountain of man's worldliness is at once dried up.

src: yadā yadā pākamupaiti nūnaṃ tadā tadeyaṃ ratimātanoti / jarābharā'nalpanavaprasūnā vijarjarā kāyalatā narāṇām //
tgt: As the body gets towards its decline, so much doth death rejoice in it. The body grows lean with grey hairs upon the head, just as a creeper fades away with the flowers upon it.

src: tṛṣṇānadī sāratarapravāhagrastākhilānantapadārthajātā / taṭasthasaṃtoṣasuvṛkṣamūlanikāṣadakṣā vahatīha loke //
tgt: All living creatures are borne away by the stream of avarice, which upsets the tree of contentment growing on the bank and flows on for ever in this world.

src: śārīranauścarmanibandhabaddhā bhavāmbudhāvālulitā bhramantī / praloḍyate pañcabhirindriyākhyairadhobhavantī makarairadhīrā //
tgt: Human body is like a vessel covered with skin; and glides over the ocean of the world (without its helmsman of reason). It is tossed about by sensual pleasures, and goes down under the water by the pressure of its whale-like passions.

src: tṛṣṇālatākānanacāriṇo'mī śākhāśataṃ kāmamahīruheṣu / paribhramantaḥ kṣapayanti kālaṃ manomṛgā no phalamāpnuvanti //
tgt: The world is a wilderness abounding in creepers of avarice and trees of sensuality, with hundreds of desires as their branches. Our minds like monkeys pass their time in roving about this forest without getting the fruits.

src: kṛcchreṣu dūrāstaviṣādamohāḥ svāsthyeṣu notsiktamanobhirāmāḥ / sudurlabhāḥ saṃprati sundarībhiḥ ranāhatāntaḥkaraṇā mahāntaḥ //
tgt: Those that do not yield to grief in troubles, that are not elated with prosperity, nor smitten at heart by women, are rare in this world.

src: taranti mātaṅgaghaṭātaraṅgaṃ raṇāmbudhiṃ ye mayi te na śūrāḥ / śūrāsta eveha manastaraṅgaṃ dehendriyāmbhodhimimaṃ taranti //
tgt: Those who fight boldly in the battle fields and withstand the war-elephants, are not so very brave in my opinion, as those who withstand the surges of the mind amidst the streams of carnal appetites.

src: akliṣṭaparyantaphalābhirāmā na dṛśyate kasyacideva kācit / kriyādurāśāhatacittavṛttiryāmetya viśrāntimupaiti lokaḥ //
tgt: I see no such deeds in the world which endure to the last (or final emancipation) of men. Actions proceeding from a desire of fruition in fools, serve only for their restlessness on earth.

src: kīrtyā jagaddikkuharaṃ pratāpaiḥ śriyā gṛhaṃ sattvabalena lakṣmīm / ye pūrayantyakṣatadhairyabandhā na te jagatyāṃ sulabhā mahāntaḥ //
tgt: Such men are rare in the world, that have filled the corners of the world with their fame and valour, who have filled their houses with true riches acquired by honest means and an unwavering patience.

src: apyantarasthaṃ giriśailabhittervajrālayābhyantarasaṃsthitaṃ vā / sarvaṃ samāyānti sasiddhivegāḥ sarvāḥ śriyaḥ santatamāpadaśca //
tgt: Good and bad fortune always overtake a man, even if he were living in an aperture of the rock or within the walls of mountains, or even if he were enclosed within an iron built closet.

src: putrāśca dārāśca dhanaṃ ca buddhyā prakalpyate tāta rasāyanābham / sarvaṃ tu tannopakarotyathānte yatrātiramyā viṣamūrcchanaiva //
tgt: Our sons and riches are mere objects of delight to us. It is as erroneous to suppose them to be of any good to us at the end, as to expect any benefit from the decoction of poison.

src: viṣādayukto viṣamāmavasthā mupāgataḥ kāyavayovasāne / bhāvānsmaransvāniha dharmariktān janturjarāvāniha dahyate'ntaḥ //
tgt: Old people being reduced to calamitous circumstances at the pitiable state of the decay of their bodies and decline of life, have greatly to be tormented at the thoughts of the impious deeds.

src: kāmārthadharmāptikṛtāntarābhiḥ kriyābhirādau divasāni nītvā / cetaścaladbarhiṇapicchalolaṃ viśrāntimāgacchatu kena puṃsaḥ //
tgt: Men having passed their early days in the gratification of their desires and other worldly pursuits at the expense of the acts of virtue and piety, are as much troubled with anxieties at the end, that their minds are seized with a tremor like that of the plumage of a peacock shaken by the breeze. How then can a man attain to tranquility at any time?

src: purogatairapyanavāptarūpaistaraṅgiṇītuṅgataraṅgakalpaiḥ / kriyāphalairdaivavaśādupetairviḍambyate bhinnarucirhi lokaḥ //
tgt: Wealth whether forthcoming or unattainable, whether got by labour or given by fortune, is all as deceitful to the worldly minded, as the high waters of rivers.

src: imānyamūnīhi vibhāvitāni kāryāṇyaparyantamanoramāṇi / janasya jāyājanarañjanena javājjarāntaṃ jarayanti cetaḥ //
tgt: That such and such desirable acts are to be done, are the constant thoughts of men, who desire to please their sons and wives, until they are worn out with age and become crazy in their minds.

src: parṇāni jīrṇāni yathā tarūṇāṃ sametya janmāśu layaṃ prayānti / tathaiva lokāḥ svavivekahīnāḥ sametya gacchanti kuto'pyahobhiḥ //
tgt: Like leaves on trees that grow to fall, and falling make room for others to shoot forth, are those men who devoid of reason, die away daily to be born again.

src: itastato dūrataraṃ vihṛtya praviśya gehaṃ divasāvasāne / vivekilokāśrayasādhukarma rikte'hni rātrau ka upaiti nidrām //
tgt: Men having travelled here and there and far and near, return to their homes at the end of the day; but none of them can have rest by day or night, except the virtuous few that live by honest dealings.

src: vidrāvite śatrujane samaste samāgatāyāmabhitaśca lakṣmyām / sevyanta etāni sukhāni yāvattāvatsamāyāti kuto'pi mṛtyuḥ //
tgt: After quelling his enemies and getting enough of riches in his clutches, the rich man just sits down to enjoy his gains; when death comes upon him, and interrupts his joy.

src: kuto'pi saṃvardhitatuccharūpairbhāvairamībhiḥ kṣaṇanaṣṭadṛṣṭaiḥ / viloḍyamānā janatā jagatyāṃ navetyupāyātamaho na pātam //
tgt: Seeing the vile trash of worldly gains earned and accumulated by the basest means to be but transitory, the infatuated mob do not perceive their approaching dissolution.

src: priyāsubhiḥ kālamukhaṃ kriyante janaiḍakāste hatakarmabaddhāḥ / yaiḥ pīnatāmeva balādupetya śarīrabādhena na te bhavanti //
tgt: Men loving their own lives, and making mouths at the demise of others, are like a herd of sheep bound to the stake, and staring at the slaughter of their fellows, yet feeding themselves to fall as fattened victims to death.

src: agninā rayim aśnavat poṣam eva dive dive yaśasam vīravat tamam
tgt: Through Agni man obtaineth wealth, yea, plenty waxing day by day, Most rich in heroes, glorious.

src: agne yam yajñam adhvaram viśvataḥ pari bhūḥ asi saḥ it deveṣu gacchati
tgt: Agni, the perfect sacrifice which thou encompassest about Verily goeth to the Gods.

src: agniḥ hotā kavi kratuḥ satyaḥ citraśravaḥ tamaḥ devaḥ devebhiḥ ā gamat
tgt: May Agni, sapient-minded Priest, truthful, most gloriously great, The God, come hither with the Gods.

src: yat aṅga dāśuṣe tvam agne bhadram kariṣyasi tava it tat satyam aṅgiraḥ
tgt: Whatever blessing, Agni, thou wilt grant unto thy worshipper, That, Angiras, is indeed thy truth.

src: upa tvā agne dive dive doṣāvastaḥ dhiyā vayam namaḥ bharantaḥ ā imasi
tgt: To thee, dispeller of the night, O Agni, day by day with prayer Bringing thee reverence, we come

src: rājantam adhvarāṇām gopām r̥tasya dīdivim vardhamānam sve dame
tgt: Ruler of sacrifices, guard of Law eternal, radiant One, Increasing in thine own abode.

src: saḥ naḥ pitāiva sūnave agne su upāyanaḥ bhava sacasva naḥ svastaye
tgt: Be to us easy of approach, even as a father to his son: Agni, be with us for our weal.

src: vāyo iti ā yāhi darśata ime somāḥ araṁ kr̥tāḥ teṣām pāhi śrudhi havam
tgt: BEAUTIFUL Vâyu, come, for thee these Soma drops have been prepared: Drink of them, hearken to our call.

src: vāyo iti ukthebhiḥ jarante tvām accha jaritāraḥ suta somāḥ ahaḥ vidaḥ
tgt: Knowing the days, with Soma juice poured forth, the singers glorify Thee, Vâyu, with their hymns of praise.

src: vāyo iti tava pra pr̥ñcatī dhenā jigāti dāśuṣe urūcī soma pītaye
tgt: Vâyu, thy penetrating stream goes forth unto the worshipper, Far-spreading for the Soma draught.

src: indravāyūiti ime sutāḥ upa prayaḥ bhiḥ ā gatam indavaḥ vām uśanti hi
tgt: These, Indra-Vâyu, have been shed; come for our offered dainties' sake: The drops are yearning for you both.

src: vāyo iti indraḥ ca cetathaḥ sutānām vājinīvasūitivājinī vasū tau ā yātam upa dravat
tgt: Well do ye mark libations, ye Vâyu and Indra, rich in spoil So come ye swiftly hitherward.

src: vāyo iti indraḥ ca sunvataḥ ā yātam upa niḥ kr̥tam makṣu itthā dhiyā narā
tgt: Vâyu and Indra, come to what the Soma. presser hath prepared: Soon, Heroes, thus I make my prayer.

src: mitram huve pūta dakṣam varuṇam ca riśādasam dhiyam ghr̥tācīm sādhantā
tgt: Mitra, of holy strength, I call, and foe-destroying Varuṇa, Who make the oil-fed rite complete.

src: r̥tena mitrāvaruṇau r̥tāvr̥dhau r̥ta spr̥śā kratum br̥hantam āśātheiti
tgt: Mitra and Varuṇa, through Law, lovers and cherishers of Law, Have ye obtained your might power

src: kavī iti naḥ mitrāvaruṇā tuvi jātau uru kṣayā dakṣam dadhāteiti apasam
tgt: Our Sages, Mitra-Varuṇa, wide dominion, strong by birth, Vouchsafe us strength that worketh well.

src: aśvinā yajvarīḥ iṣaḥ dravatpāṇī itidravat pāṇī śubhaḥ patī iti puru bhujā canasyatam
tgt: YE Aṣvins, rich in treasure, Lords of splendour, having nimble hands, Accept the sacrificial food.

src: aśvinā puru daṁsasā narā śavīrayā dhiyā dhiṣṇyā vanatam giraḥ
tgt: Ye Aṣvins, rich in wondrous deeds, ye heroes worthy of our praise, Accept our songs with mighty thought.

src: dasrā yuvākavaḥ sutāḥ nāsatyā vr̥kta barhiṣaḥ ā yātam rudravartanī itirudra vartanī
tgt: Nisatyas, wonder-workers, yours arc these libations with clipt grass: Come ye whose paths are red with flame.

src: indra ā yāhi citrabhāno iticitra bhāno sutāḥ ime tvāyavaḥ aṇvībhiḥ tanā pūtāsaḥ
tgt: O Indra marvellously bright, come, these libations long for thee, Thus by fine fingers purified.

src: indra ā yāhi dhiyā iṣitaḥ vipra jūtaḥ suta vataḥ upa brahmāṇi vāghataḥ
tgt: Urged by the holy singer, sped by song, come, Indra, to the prayers, Of the libation-pouring priest.

src: indra ā yāhi tūtujānaḥ upa brahmāṇi hari vaḥ sute dadhiṣva naḥ canaḥ
tgt: Approach, O Indra, hasting thee, Lord of Bay Horses, to the prayers. In our libation take delight.

src: omāsaḥ carṣaṇi dhr̥taḥ viśve devāsaḥ ā gata dāśvāṁsaḥ dāśuṣaḥ sutam
tgt: Ye Viṣvedevas, who protect, reward, and cherish men, approach Your worshipper's drink-offering.

src: viśve devāsaḥ ap turaḥ sutam ā ganta tūrṇayaḥ usrāḥ iva svasarāṇi
tgt: Ye Viṣvedevas, swift at work, come hither quickly to the draught, As milch-kine hasten to their stalls.

src: viśve devāsaḥ asridhaḥ ehi māyāsaḥ adruhaḥ medham juṣanta vahnayaḥ
tgt: The Viṣvedevas, changing shape like serpents, fearless, void of guile, Bearers, accept the sacred draught

src: pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī vājebhiḥ vājinī vatī yajñam vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ
tgt: Wealthy in spoil, enriched with hymns, may bright Sarsavad desire, With eager love, our sacrifice.

src: codayitrī sūnr̥tānām cetantī su matīnām yajñam dadhe sarasvatī
tgt: Inciter of all pleasant songs, inspirer o all gracious thought, Sarasvatî accept our rite

src: mahaḥ arṇaḥ sarasvatī pra cetayati ketunā dhiyaḥ viśvāḥ vi rājati
tgt: Sarasvatî, the mighty flood,– she with be light illuminates, She brightens every pious thought.

src: surūpa kr̥tnum ūtaye sudughām iva go duhe juhūmasi dyavi dyavi
tgt: As a good cow to him who milks, we call the doer of fair deeds, To our assistance day by day.

src: upa naḥ savanā ā gahi somasya soma pāḥ piba go dāḥ it revataḥ madaḥ
tgt: Come thou to our libations, drink of Soma; Soma-drinker thou! The rich One's rapture giveth kine.

src: atha te antamānām vidyāma su matīnām mā naḥ ati khyaḥ ā gahi
tgt: So may we be acquainted with thine innermost benevolence: Neglect us not, come hitherward.

src: parā ihi vigram astr̥tam indram pr̥ccha vipaḥ citam yaḥ te sakhi bhyaḥ ā varam
tgt: Go to the wise unconquered One, ask thou of Indra, skilled in song, Him who is better than thy friends.

src: uta bruvantu naḥ nidaḥ niḥ anyataḥ cit ārata dadhānāḥ indre it duvaḥ
tgt: Whether the men who mock us say, Depart unto another place, Ye who serve Indra and none else;

src: uta naḥ subhagān ariḥ voceyuḥ dasma kr̥ṣṭayaḥ syāma it indrasya śarmaṇi
tgt: Or whether, God of wondrous deeds, all our true people call us blest, Still may we dwell in Indra's care.

src: ā īm āśum āśave bhara yajña śriyam nr̥ mādanam patayat mandayat sakham
tgt: Unto the swift One bring the swift, man-cheering, grace of sacrifice, That to the Friend gives wings and joy.

src: asya pītvā śatakrato itiśata krato ghanaḥ vr̥trāṇām abhavaḥ pra āvaḥ vājeṣu vājinam
tgt: Thou, Ṣatakratu, drankest this and wast the Vr̥itras' slayer; thou Helpest the warrior in the fray.

src: tam tvā vājeṣu vājinam vājayāmaḥ śatakrato itiśata krato dhanānām indra sātaye
tgt: We strengthen, Ṣatakratu, thee, yea, thee the powerful in fight, That, Indra, we may win us wealth.

src: yaḥ rāyaḥ avaniḥ mahān su pāraḥ sunvataḥ sakhā tasmai indrāya gāyata
tgt: To him the mighty stream of wealth, prompt friend ot'him who pours the juice, yea, to this Indra sing your song.

src: ā tu ā ita ni sīdata indram abhi pra gāyata sakhāyaḥ stoma vāhasaḥ
tgt: O COME ye hither, sit ye down: to Indra sing ye forth, your song, companions, bringing hymns of praise.

src: puru tamam purūṇām īśānam vāryāṇam indram some sacā sute
tgt: To him the richest of the rich, the Lord of treasures excellent, Indra, wi th Soma juice outpoured.

src: saḥ gha naḥ yoge ā bhuvat saḥ rāye saḥ puram dhyām gamat vājebhiḥ ā saḥ naḥ
tgt: May he stand by us in our need and in abundance for our wealth: May he come nigh us with his strength.

src: yasya sam sthe na vr̥ṇvate harī iti samat su śatravaḥ tasmai indrāya gāyata
tgt: Whose pair of tawny horses yoked in battles foemen challenge not: To him, to Indra sing your song.

src: suta pāvne sutāḥ ime śucayaḥ yanti vītaye somāsaḥ dadhi āśiraḥ
tgt: Nigh to the Soma-drinker come, for his enjoyment, these pure drops, The Somas mingled with the curd.

src: tvam sutasya pītaye sadyaḥ vr̥ddhaḥ ajāyathāḥ indra jyaiṣṭhyāya sukrato itisu krato
tgt: Thou, grown at once to perfect strength, wast born to drink the Soma juice, Strong Indra, for preeminence.

src: ā tvā viśantu āśavaḥ somāsaḥ indra girvaṇaḥ śam te santu pra cetase
tgt: O Indra, lover of the song, may these quick Somas enter thee: May they bring bliss to thee the Sage.

src: tvām stomāḥ avīvr̥dhan tvām ukthā śatakrato itiśata krato tvām vardhantu naḥ giraḥ
tgt: Our chants of praise have strengthened thee, O Ṣatakratu, and our lauds So strengthen thee the songs we sing.

src: akṣita ūtiḥ sanet imam vājam indraḥ sahasriṇam yasmin viśvāni paiṁsyā
tgt: Indra, whose succour never fails, accept these viands thousandfold, Wherein all manly powers abide.

src: mā naḥ martāḥ abhi druhan tanūnām indra girvaṇaḥ īśānaḥ yavaya vadham
tgt: O Indra, thou who lovest song, let no man hurt our bodies, keep Slaughter far from us, for thou canst.

src: yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam carantam pari tasthuṣaḥ rocante rocanā divi
tgt: They who stand round him as he moves harness the bright, the ruddy Steed The lights are shining in the sky.

src: yuñjanti asya kāmyā harī iti vipakṣasā rathe śoṇā dhr̥ṣṇū iti nr̥ vāhasā
tgt: On both sides to the car they yoke the two bay coursers dear to him, Bold, tawny, bearers of the Chief.

src: ketum kr̥ṇvan aketave peśaḥ maryāḥ apeśase sam uṣat bhiḥ ajāyathāḥ
tgt: Thou, making light where no light was, and form, O men: where form was not, Wast born together with the Dawns.

src: āt aha svadhām anu punaḥ garbha tvam āīrire dadhānāḥ nāma yajñiyam
tgt: Thereafter they, as is their wont, threw off the state of' babes unborn, Assuming sacrificial names.

src: vīl̥u cit ārujatnu bhiḥ guhā cit indra vahni bhiḥ avindaḥ usriyāḥ anu
tgt: Thou, Indra, with the Tempest-Gods, the breakers down of what is firm ' Foundest the kine even in the cave.

src: deva yantaḥ yathā matim accha vidat vasum giraḥ mahām anūṣata śrutam
tgt: Worshipping even as they list, singers laud him who findeth wealth, The far-renowned, the mighty One.

src: indreṇa sam hi dr̥kṣase sam jagmānaḥ abibhyuṣā mandū iti samāna varcasā
tgt: Mayest thou verily be seen coming by fearless Indra's side: Both joyous, equal in your sheen.

src: anavadyaiḥ abhidyu bhiḥ makhaḥ sahasvat arcati gaṇaiḥ indrasya kāmyaiḥ
tgt: With Indra's well beloved hosts, the blameless, hastening to heaven, The sacrificer cries aloud.

src: ataḥ parijman ā gahi divaḥ vā rocanāt adhi sam asmin r̥ñjate giraḥ
tgt: Come from this place, O Wanderer, or downward from the light of heaven: Our songs of praise all yearn for this.

src: itaḥ vā sātim īmahe diva vā pārthivāt adhi indram mahaḥ vā rajasaḥ
tgt: Indra we seek to give us help, from here, from heaven above the earth, Or from the spacious firmament.

src: indram it gāthinaḥ br̥hat indram arkebhiḥ arkiṇaḥ indram vāṇīḥ anūṣata
tgt: INDRA the singers with high praise, Indra reciters with their lauds, Indra the choirs have glorified.

src: indraḥ it haryoḥ sacā sam miślaḥ ā vacaḥ yujā indraḥ vajrī hiraṇyayaḥ
tgt: Indra hath ever close to him his two bay steeds and word-yoked car, Indra the golden, thunder-armed.

src: indraḥ dīrghāya cakṣase ā sūryam rohayat divi vi gobhiḥ adrim airayat
tgt: Indra hath raised the Sun on high in heaven, that he may see afar: He burst the mountain for the kine.

src: indraḥ vājeṣu naḥ ava sahasra pradhaneṣu ca ugraḥ ugrābhiḥ ūti bhiḥ
tgt: Help us, O Indra, in the frays, yea, frays, where thousand spoils are gained, With awful aids, O awful One.

src: indram vayam mahādhane indram arbhe havāmahe yujam vr̥treṣu vajriṇam
tgt: In mighty battle we invoke Indra, Indra in lesser fight, The Friend who bends his bolt at fiends.

src: saḥ naḥ vr̥ṣan amum carum satrādāvan apa vr̥dhi asmabhyam aprati skutaḥ
tgt: Unclose, our manly Hero, thou for ever bounteous, yonder cloud, For us, thou irresistible.

src: tuñje tuñje ye ut tare stomāḥ indrasya vajriṇaḥ na vindhe asya su stutim
tgt: Still higher, at each strain of mine, thunder-armed Indra's praises rise: I find no laud worthy of him.

src: vr̥ṣā yūthāiva vaṁsagaḥ kr̥ṣṭīḥ iyarti ojasā īśānaḥ aprati skutaḥ
tgt: Even as the bull drives on the herds, he drives the people with his might, The Ruler irresistible:

src: yaḥ ekaḥ carṣaṇīnām vasūnām irajyati indraḥ pañca kṣitīnām
tgt: Indra who rules with single sway men, riches, and the fivefold race Of those who dwell upon the earth.

src: indram vaḥ viśvataḥ pari havāmahe janebhyaḥ asmākam astu kevalaḥ
tgt: For your sake from each side we call Indra away from other men: Ours, and none others', may he be.

src: ā indra sānasim rayim sa jitvānam sadāsaham varṣiṣṭham ūtaye bhara
tgt: INDRA, bring wealth that gives delight, the victor's ever-conquering wealth, Most excellent, to be our aid;

src: ni yena muṣṭi hatyayā ni vr̥trā ruṇadhāmahai tvāūtāsaḥ ni arvatā
tgt: By means of which we may repel our foes in battle hand to hand, By thee assisted with the car.

src: indra tvāūtāsaḥ ā vayam vajram ghanā dadīmahi jayema sam yudhi spr̥dhaḥ
tgt: Aided by thee, the thunder-armed, Indra, may we lift up the bolt, And conquer all our foes in fight.

src: vayam śūrebhiḥ astr̥ bhiḥ indra tvayā yujā vayam sāsahyāmapr̥tanyataḥ
tgt: With thee, O India, for ally with missile-darting heroes, may We conquer our embattled foes.

src: mahān indraḥ paraḥ ca nu mahi tvam astu vajriṇe dyauḥ na prathinā śavaḥ
tgt: Mighty is Indra, yea supreme; greatness be his, the Thunderer: Wide as the heaven extends his power

src: sam ohe vā ye āśata naraḥ tokasya sanitau viprāsaḥ vā dhiyāyavaḥ
tgt: Which aideth those to win them sons, who come as heroes to the fight, Or singers loving holy thoughts.

src: yaḥ kukṣiḥ soma pātamaḥ samudraḥ iva pinvate urvīḥ āpaḥ na kākudaḥ
tgt: His belly, drinking deepest draughts of Soma, like an ocean swells, Like wide streams from the cope of heaven.

src: eva hi asya sūnr̥tā vi rapśī go matī mahī pakvā śākhā na dāśuṣe
tgt: So also is his excellence, great, vigorous, rich in cattle, like A ripe branch to the worshipper.

src: eva hi te vi bhūtayaḥ ūtayaḥ indra māvate sadyaḥ cit santi dāśuṣe
tgt: For verily thy mighty powers, Indra, are saving helps at once Unto a worshipper like me.

src: eva hi asya kāmyā stomaḥ uktham ca śaṁsyā indrāya soma pītaye
tgt: So are his lovely gifts; let lauds and praises be to Indra sung, That he may drink the Soma juice.

src: indra ā ihi matsi andhasaḥ viśvebhiḥ somaparva bhiḥ mahān abhiṣṭiḥ ojasā
tgt: COME, Indra, and delight thee with the juice at all the Soma feasts, Protector, mighty in thy strength.

src: ā īm enam sr̥jata sute mandim indrāya mandine cakrim viśvāni cakraye
tgt: To Indra pour ye forth thejuice, the active gladdening juice to him Ile gladdening, oinnific God.

src: matsva su śipra mandi bhiḥ stomebhiḥ viśva carṣaṇe sacā eṣu savaneṣu ā
tgt: O Lord of all men, fair of cheek, rejoice thee in the gladdening lauds, Present at these drink-offerings.

src: asr̥gram indra te giraḥ prati tvām ud ahāsata ajoṣāḥ vr̥ṣabham patim
tgt: Songs have outpoured themselves to thee, Indra, the strong, the guardian Lord, And raised themselves unsatisfied.

src: sam codaya citram arvāk rādhaḥ indra vareṇyam asat it te vi bhu pra bhu
tgt: Send to us bounty manifold, O Indra, worthy of' our wish, For power supreme is only thine.

src: asmān su tatra codaya indra rāye rabhasvataḥ tuvi dyumna yaśasvataḥ
tgt: O Indra, stimulate thereto us emulously fain for wealth, And glorious, O most splendid One.

src: uddhanvānā rajo ghoraṃ tāṭakā rāghavāvubhau| rajomeghena mahatā muhūrtaṃ sā vyamohayat||
tgt: And raising thick clouds of dust, Tāțakā instantly bewildered both the descendants of Raghu.

src: tato māyāṃ samāṃsthāya śilāvarṣeṇa rāghavau| avākirat sumahatāṃ tataścakrodha rāghavaḥ||
tgt: And then by help of illusion, she began to pour upon them a mighty shower of crags. And thereat Raghu's descendant was wroth.

src: śilāvarṣaṃ mahat tasyāḥ śaravarṣeṇa rāghavaḥ| prativāryopadhāvantyāḥ karau ciccheda patribhiḥ||
tgt: And resisting that mighty shower of crags by vollies of shafts, Rāghava with arrows cut off her hands.

src: tataśchinnabhujāṃ śrāntāmabhyāśe parigarjatīm| saumitrirakarot krodhāddhatakarṇāgranāsikām||
tgt: And with the fore-parts of her arms lopped off, as she was roaring before them, Sumitra's son waxing wroth deprived her of her ears and nose.

src: kāmarūpadharā sā tu kṛtvā rūpāṇyanekaśaḥ| antardhānaṃ gatā yakṣī mohayantī svamāyayā||
tgt: Thereupon that one capable of assuming forms at will, began to assume various shapes; and to vanish from sight, bewildering her antagonists with her illusory displays.

src: aśmavarṣaṃ vimuñcantī bhairavaṃ vicacāra sā| tatastāvaśmavarṣeṇa kīryamāṇau samantataḥ|| dṛṣṭvā gādhisutaḥ śrīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt| alaṃ te ghṛṇayā rāma pāpaiṣā duṣṭvāriṇī|| yajñavighnakarī yakṣī purā vardheta māyayā| vadhyatāṃ tāvadevaiṣā purā saṃdhyā pravartate|| rakṣāṃsi saṃdhyākāle tu durdharṣāṇi bhavanti hi|
tgt: Terribly ranging the field, the Yakṣī showered crags upon her antagonists. And beholding them enveloped on all sides by that craggy downpour, the auspicious son of Gadhi spoke these words-O Rāma, renounce your antipathy. This one of wicked ways is exceedingly impious. And this sacrifice-disturbing Yakși will, by virtue of her power of illusion, come to increase more and more in energy. Do you, therefore, against the arrival of dusk, slay her! The Rākṣasas are incapable of being controlled when evening sets in.

src: ityuktaḥ sa tu tāṃ yakṣīmaśmavṛṣṭayābhivarṣiṇīm || darśayaśabdavedhitvaṃ tāṃ rurodha sa sāyakaiḥ|
tgt: Thus addressed, Rāma, displaying his skill in aiming by sounds, enveloped with arrows that Yakṣī showering crags.

src: sā ruddhā bāṇajālena māyābalasamanvitā|| abhidudrāva kākutsthaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca vineduṣī| tāmāpatantī vegena vikrāntāmaśanīmiva || śareṇorasi vivyādha sā papāta mamāra ca|
tgt: Being thus hemmed in with a network of shafts, she possessed of the powers of illusion, rushed against Kākutstha and Lakşmaņa, uttering terrible roars. And as that Yaksi, in prowess like to a thunder-bolt, was rushing on, Rāma pierced her chest with arrows, and thereat she dropped down and died.

src: tāṃ hatāṃ bhīmasaṃkāśāṃ dṛṣṭvā surapatistadā|| sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṃ surāścāpyabhipūjayan|
tgt: Upon seeing that grim-visaged one slain, the lord of the celestials together with the celestials themselves honouring Kākutstha, exclaimed Well, Well!.

src: uvāca paramaprītaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ purandaraḥ|| surāśca sarve saṃhṛṣṭā viśvāmitramathābruvan|
tgt: And exceedingly pleased, the thousand-eyed Purandara, together with the delighted deities, said to Viśvāmitra.

src: mune kauśika bhadraṃ te sendrāḥ sarve marudgaṇāḥ|| toṣitāḥ karmaṇānena snehaṃ darśaya rāghave| prajāpateḥ kṛśāśvasya putrān satyaparākramān|| tapobalabhṛto brahman rāghavāya nivedaya|
tgt: O ascetic, O Kusika's son, good betide you! all the Maruts with Indra at their head, have been gratified with this act (of Rāma's). Do you, O Brāhmaṇa, confer upon Raghu's descendant the sons of Prajāpati Kțśāśva, of true prowess, and charged with ascetic energy.

src: pātrabhūtaśca te brahmastavānugamane rataḥ|| kartavyaṃ sumahat karma surāṇāṃ rājasūnunā|
tgt: And ever following you, he, O Brāhmaṇa, is fit to receive them of you. And this son of the king is to accomplish a mighty task in the interests of the celestials.

src: evamuktvā surāḥ sarve jagmurhaṣṭā vihāyasam|| viśvāmitraṃ pūjayantastataḥ saṃdhyā pravartate|
tgt: Saying this, the deities, having paid homage to Viśvāmitra, joyfully entered the celestial regions.

src: tato munivaraḥ prītastāṭakāvadhatoṣitaḥ|32|| mūrdhni rāmamupāghrāya idaṃ vacanamabravīt|
tgt: And now came evening on, when that best of ascetics, gratified at the destruction of Tāțakā, smelt Rāma's crown and said these words,

src: ihādya rajanī rāma vasāma śubhadarśana || śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmastadāśramapadaṃ mama|
tgt: Here, O Rāma of gracious presence, shall we pass the night; and morrow morning, went to that hermitage of mine.

src: viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭo daśarathātmajaḥ|| uvāsa rajanī tatra tāṭakāyā vane sukham|
tgt: Hearing Visvāmitra's words, Dasaratha's son, glad at heart, happily passed that night in the forest of Tāțakā.

src: muktaśāpaṃ vanaṃ tacca tasminneva tadāhani| ramaṇīyaṃ vibabhrāja yathā caitrarathaṃ vanam||
tgt: And being thus freed from all disturbances, from that day forth that forest appeared charming, even like to the forest of Caitraratha.

src: nihatya to yakṣasutāṃ sa rāmaḥ praśasyamānaḥ surasiddhasaṃghaiḥ| uvāsa tasmin muninā sahaiva prabhātavelāṃ pratibodhyamānaḥ||
tgt: Having thus slain the Yakşa's daughter, Rāma, eulogised by celestials and Siddhas, spent there that night with the saint, being awakened by the latter at the break of day.

src: ṛṣyamūkāt sa dharmātmā kiṣkindhāṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ| jagāma saha sugrīvo vālivikramapālitām|| samudyamya mahaccāpaṃ rāmaḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam| śarāṃścādityasaṃkāśān gṛhītvā raṇasādhakān||
tgt: Thereupon the high-souled Rāma, along with Sugrīva, proceeded from the mount Rșyamuka to Kiskindha, maintained by Vali's prowess, raising up his gold crested mighty bow and taking his battle arrows like to Aditya.

src: agratastu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ| sugrīvaḥ saṃhatagrīvo lakṣmaṇasya mahābalaḥ||
tgt: The mighty Sugrīva, bending low, proceeded before the high-souled Rama and Laksmana.

src: pṛṣṭhato hanumān vīro nalo nīlaśca vīryavān| tāraścaiva mahātejā hariyūthapayūthapaḥ||
tgt: They were followed by the heroic Hanumān, the mighty Nala and Neela, and the highly powerful Tārā, the leader of the monkey herd.

src: te vīkṣamāṇā vṛkṣāṃśca puṣpabhārāvalambinaḥ| prasannāmbuvahāścaiva saritaḥ sāgaraṃgamāḥ|| kandarāṇi ca śailāṃśca nirdarāṇi guhāstathā| śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīśca priyadarśanāḥ||
tgt: They beheld as they proceeded, trees, lowered down with the weight of flowers, rivers of clear water flowing to the ocean, mountain hollows, hills, caves, cavities, and principal peaks and charming rills.

src: vaidūryavimalaistoyaiḥ padyaiścākośakuḍmalaiḥ| śobhitān sajalān mārge taṭākāṃścāvalokayan|| kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasaiha~sairvañjulairjalakukkuṭaiḥ| cakravākaistathā cānyaiḥ śakunaiḥ pratināditān||
tgt: They. beheld on their way, pools filled with water clear as Baidurya and beautified with lotuses-full blown and buds, and resounded with the cries of Kārandhabas, swans, geese, Banculas, water-fowls, Cakravākas, and various other birds.

src: mṛduśaṣpāṅkurāhārānnirbhayān vanagocarān| carataḥ sarvataḥ paśyan sthalīṣu hariṇān sthitān||
tgt: They surveyed all around in the forest-land, deer ranging fearlessly at large and grazing on tender grass.

src: taṭākavairiṇaścāpi śukladantavibhūṣitān| ghorānekacarānvanyān dviradān kūlaghātinaḥ|| mattān giritaṭotkṛṣṭān parvatāniva jaṅgamān| vānarān dviradaprakhyān mahīreṇusamukṣitān || vane vanacarāṃścānyān khecarāṃśca vihaṃgamān| paśyantastvaritā jagmuḥ sugrīvavaśavartinaḥ||
tgt: They beheld frightful wild elephants having white teeth, ranging alone-the destroyers of river banks and enemies of pools. And observing many an infuriated monkey like to elephants, resembling so many moveable mountains riving the mountainous expanses crusted with dust, and many other wild beasts and birds the followers of Sugrīva wended their way.

src: teṣāṃ tu gacchatāṃ tatra tvaritaṃ raghunandanaḥ| dumaṣaṇḍavanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvamabravīt||
tgt: They proceeding quickly, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, beholding the forest filled with trees, spoke to Sugrīva, saying.

src: eṣa megha ivākāśe vṛkṣaṣaṇḍaḥ prakāśate| meghasaṃghātavipulaḥ paryantakadalīvṛtaḥ|| kimetajjñātumicchāmi sakhe kautūhalaṃ mama| kautūhalāpanayanaṃ kartumicchāmyahaṃ tvayā||
tgt: These trees skirted by plantain groves, dense as a collection of clouds, appear as clouds in the sky. Great is my curiosity, O friend, to learn what are these. 'And I wish to have my curiosity removed by you.

src: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ| gacchannevācacakṣe'tha sugrīvastanmahad vanam||
tgt: Hearing the words of the high-souled Rāghava, Sugrīva began to describe that great forest.

src: etad rāghava vistīrṇamāśramaṃ śramanāśanam| udyānavanasampannaṃ svādumūlaphalodakam|| atra saptajanā nāma munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ| saptavāsannadhaḥśīrṣā niyataṃ jalaśāyinaḥ|| saptarātre kṛtāhārā vāyunācalavāsinaḥ| divaṃ varṣaśatairyātāḥ saptabhiḥ sakalevarāḥ||
tgt: In this extensive asylum, O Rāghava, removing the toil (of the travellers) filled with gardens and trees and abounding in delicious fruits, roots and water, dwelt seven Saints, having control over their senses. Those seven Saints, dwelling on the mountain, passed days and nights in water with their heads down and after seven nights used to live upon air. In this wise, passing seven hundred years they repaired bodily to heaven.

src: teṣāmetatprabhāveṇa dumaprākārasaṃvṛtam| āśramaṃ sudurādharṣamapi sendraiḥ surāsuraiḥ||
tgt: By virtue of their asceticism, this asylum is walled by trees and incapable of being conquered even by Indra, the celestials and the Asuras.

src: pakṣiṇo varjayantyetat tathānye vanacāriṇaḥ| viśanti mohād ye'pyatra na nivartanti te punaḥ||
tgt: Birds or other wild animals do not enter this asylum; whoever entereth this by mistake never returneth.

src: vibhūṣaṇaravāścātra śrūyante sakalākṣarāḥ| tūryagītasvanaścāpi gandho divyaśca rāghava ||
tgt: There is audible, O Rāghava, the sound of the dressing of Apsarās, their sweet-winged accents and that of their music and drums; and herçin pervadeth the celestial fragrance.

src: tretāgnayo'pi dīpyante dhūmo hyeṣa pradṛśyate| veṣṭayanniva vṛkṣāgrān kapotāṅgāruṇo ghanaḥ||
tgt: Here burneth the fire Tretā; and the smoke and cloud sable like to the wings of a pigeon envelope the tops of the trees.

src: ete vṛkṣāḥ prakāśante dhūmasaṃsaktamastakāḥ| meghajālapraticchannā vaidūryagirayo yathā ||
tgt: And there appear the trees, having their tops saturated with smoke and cloaked with clouds, like to so many Baidurya hills.

src: kuru praṇāmaṃ dharmātmasteṣāmuddiśya rāghava| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā prayataḥ saṃhatāñjaliḥ||
tgt: Do you, O Rāghava, O virtuous-souled one, make obeisance to them along with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, with concentrated heart and folded palms.

src: praṇamanti hi ye teṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām| na teṣāmaśubhaṃ kiṃciccharīre rāma vidyate||
tgt: There resteth no sin in their persons, O Rāma, who bow to those self-controlled Saints.

src: tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāñjaliḥ| samuddiśya mahātmānastānṛṣīnabhyavādayat||
tgt: Thereupon Rāma, along with his younger brother Lakşmaņa, made obeisance to those high-souled ones.

src: abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ| sugrīvo vānarāścaiva jagmuḥ saṃhaṣṭamānasāḥ||
tgt: Having paid homage (to the sacred memory of those great ones) the virtuous-souled Rāma his (younger) brother Laksmana, Sugriva and other monkeys, proceeded with delighted hearts.

src: te gatvā dūramadhvānaṃ tasmāt saptajanāśramāt| daddaśustāṃ durādharṣāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām||
tgt: And wending a distant way from that hermitage of the seven great ones, they beheld Kişkindhä, hard to conquer and occupied by Vali.

src: tatastu rāmānujarāmavānarāḥ pragṛhya śastrāṇyuditogratejasaḥ| purī sureśātmajavīryapālitāṃ vadhāya śatroḥ punarāgatāstviha||
tgt: Thereupon, Rāma, his younger brother and the monkeys taking their weapons, entered, to encompass the destruction of their enemies, the city (of Kişkindhā) reared by the prowess of Indra's son.

src: sā tathoktā tu vaidehī nirbhayā śokakarśitā| tṛṇamantarataḥ kṛtvā rāvaṇaṃ pratyabhāṣata||
tgt: Having been thus addressed, Vaidehī unaffected by fear, although exercised with grief, placing a blade of grass between herself and Rāvana, answered him.

src: rājā daśaratho nāma dharmaseturivācalaḥ| satyasaṃdhaḥ parijñāto yasya putraḥ sa rāghavaḥ|| nāmo nāma sa dharmātmā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ| dīrghabāhurviśālākṣo daivataṃ sa patirmama ||
tgt: There was a king named Dasaratha, the bridge of righteousness, like to a mountain, ever bearing regard towards the truth, and renowned among men, whose son is Rāghava. He is named Rāma, and is righteous-souled and celebrated over the three worlds. he is long-armed, of expansive eyes, like to a celestial—he is my husband.

src: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ siṃhaskandho mahādyutiḥ| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā yaste prāṇān vadhiṣyati|| pratyakṣaṃ yadyahaṃ tasya tvayā vai dharṣitā balāt| śayitā tvaṃ hataḥ saṃkhye janasthāne yathā kharaḥ||
tgt: Born in the race of the Ikşvākus, the has the shoulders of a lion and is possessed of exceeding effulgence-the same that along with his brother, Laksmana, shall take your life. If you had wronged me forcibly in his presence, you would have slain in battle in Janasthāna even as Khara.

src: ya ete rākṣasāḥ proktā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ| rāghave nirviṣāḥ sarve suparṇe pannagā yathā||
tgt: All the mighty Rākşasas of grim visages, whom you have extolled (before me), shall be deprived of their venom before Rāma, as serpents are before Suparna,

src: tasya jyāvipramuktāste kharāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| śarīraṃ vidhamiṣyanti gaṅgākūlamivormayaḥ|7||
tgt: The shafts decorated with gold shot by the bow-string of Rāghava, shall pierce their bodies, as the waves of the Ganga (beat against) her banks.

src: asurairvā surairvā tvaṃ yadyavadhyo'si rāvaṇa| utpādya sumahad vairaṃ jīvaṃstasya na mokṣyase ||
tgt: Although, O Rāvana, you may be incapable of being slain either by the gods or the Asuras, yet having roused the high hostility of Rāghava, you will not be able to liberate your life.

src: sa te jīvitaśeṣasya rāghavo'ntakaro balī| paśoḍūṃpagatasyeva jīvitaṃ tava durlabham||
tgt: The strong Rāghava will compass the end of what remains of your life. Like the life of a beast tied to the sacrificial stake, your own is incapable of being reclaimed.

src: yadi paśyet sa rāmastvaṃ roṣadīptena cakṣuṣā| rakṣastvamadya nirdagdho yathā rudreṇa manmathaḥ||
tgt: Should Rāma look at you with eyes aglow with anger, you, O Raksasa, would be consumed even as Manmatha was by, Rudra.

src: yaścandraṃ nabhaso bhūmau pātayennāśayeta vā| sāgaraṃ śoṣayed vāpi sa sītāṃ mocayediha||
tgt: He who is able to bring down the Moon or destroy him, and to drink up the ocean dry, will surely liberate Sītā from here.

src: gatāsustvaṃ gataśrīko gatasattvo gatendriyaḥ| laṅkā vaidhavyasaṃyuktā tvatkṛtena bhaviṣyati ||
tgt: Your days are numbered, and auspiciousness has bidden you adieu. You are shorn of strength, and your senses have been dulled. And it is owing to you that Larkā shall be subject to widowhood.

src: na te pāpamidaṃ karma sukhodakaṃ bhaviṣyati| yāhaṃ nītā vinābhāvaṃ patipārdhvāt tvayā balāt||
tgt: That you by force have for naught carried me away from the side of my husband-this sinful act can never conduce to your felicity.

src: sa hi devarasaṃyukto mama bhartā mahādyutiḥ| nirbhayo vīryamāśritya śūnye vasati daṇḍake||
tgt: That exceedingly effulgent lord of mine along with my husband's younger brother, summoning up their energy, is fearlessly dwelling in the vacant Dandaka.

src: sa te vīryaṃ balaṃ darpamutsekaṃ ca tathāvidham| vyapaneṣyati gātrebhyaḥ śaravarṣeṇa saṃyuge||
tgt: By means of an arrowy shower in conflict, he will take your prowess and strength, your hauteur and wickedness out of your person,

src: yadā vināśo bhūtānāṃ dṛśyate kālacoditaḥ| tadā kārye pramādyanti narāḥ kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ||
tgt: When urged by the Destroyer, the destruction of creatures is perceptible, then, coming under the sway of the Destroyer, men become careless in their actions.

src: māṃ pradhṛṣya sa te kālaḥ prāpto'yaṃ rākṣasādhama| ātmano rākṣasānāṃ ca vadhāyāntaḥpurasya ca||
tgt: Having outraged me, you, O worst of Rāks asas your time come; for compassing your own destruction as well as that of the Rākşasas and those dwelling in your inner apartment.

src: na śakyā yajñamadhyasthā vediḥ srugbhāṇḍamaṇḍitā| dvijātimantrasampūtā caṇḍālenāvamarditum||
tgt: A Candāla cannot tread the dais reared the midst of a sacrifice beauteous with ladies, and vessels, and sanctified by the twice-born ones.

src: tathāhaṃ dharmanityasya dharmapatnī dṛḍhavratā| tvayā spraṣṭuṃ na śakyāhaṃ rākṣasādhama pāpinā||
tgt: So I, the religiously wedded wife of that one, ever intent on virtue, and (always) firm in my vows, is incapable, you vilest of Raksasas, of being touched by you, a sinner.

src: krīḍantī rājahaṃsena padmaṣaṇḍeṣu nityaśaḥ| haṃsī sā tṛṇamadhyasthaṃ kathaṃ drakṣyeta madgukam||
tgt: How can the female that has always ‘sported with her mate amidst lotuses, cast her eyes on a shag staying among rushes.

src: idaṃ śarīraṃ ni:saṃjñaṃ bandha vā ghātayasva vā| nedaṃ śarīraṃ rakṣyaṃ me jīvitaṃ vāpi rākṣasa ||
tgt: Do you either bind or destroy this body deprived of sensation. This body will I not protect, nor yet this life, O Rāvana;

src: na tu śakyamapakrośaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dātumātmanaḥ| evamuktvā tu vaidehī krodhāt suparuṣaṃ vacaḥ||
tgt: And I shall not be able to bring blame on myself in this world. having said these harsh words in wrath, Videha's daughter, Janaki, did not there again say anything to Rāvaņa.

src: rāvaṇaṃ jānakī tatra punarnovāca kiṃcana| sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā paruṣaṃ romaharṣaṇam|| pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṃ bhayasaṃdarśanaṃ vacaḥ|
tgt: Hearing Sita's words, harsh and calculated to make one's down stand on end, Rāvana answered her in words tending to excite one's apprehension,

src: śṛṇumaithili madvākyaṃ māsān dvādaśa bhāmini || kālenānena nābhyeṣi yadi māṃ cāruhāsini| tatastvāṃ prātarāśārthaṃ sūdāśchetsyanti leśaśaḥ||
tgt: Hear, O Maithili, my words. O damsel if, O you of sweet smiles, within this time you do not turn yourself to me, the cooks shall cut you off in pieces to serve my morning mcal.

src: ityuktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ| rākṣasīśca tataḥ kruddha idaṃ vacanamabravīt||
tgt: Having herself spoken thus, Ravana-challenger of foes-growing exceedingly wroth, addressed the Rākşasis in these words,

src: śīghrameva hi rākṣasyo virūpā ghoradarśanāḥ| darpamasyāpaneṣyantu māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ||
tgt: You frightful Rākşasīs terrible to behold, subsisting on flesh and gore, do you at once crush her pride.

src: vacanādeva tāstasya sughorā ghoradarśanāḥ| kṛtaprāñjalayo bhūtvā maithilī paryavārayan||
tgt: As soon as he had said this, those frightful and terrible Rākṣasīs with joined hands encircled Maithili.

src: sa tāḥ provāca rājāsau rāvaṇo ghoradarśanāḥ| pracalya caraṇotkarṣairdārayanniva medinīm||
tgt: Then the grim-visaged king Ravana, as if riving the earth by his tread, proceeding a pace or two, said,

src: aśokavanikāmadhye maithilī nīyatāmiti| tatreyaṃ rakṣyatāṃ gūḍhaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ parivāritā|| tatraināṃ tarjanaioraiḥ punaḥ sāntvaiśca maithilīm| ānayadhvaṃ vaśaṃ sarvā vanyāṃ gajavadhūmiva ||
tgt: Do you take Maithilī to the wood of Asokas. There surrounding her, do you secretly guard her; and there (sometimes) by storming, and (at other) by means of soft speech, do you all strive to bring Mithila's daughter, like a wild female elephant, under your sway.

src: iti pratisamādiṣṭā rākṣasyo rāvaṇena tāḥ| aśokavanikāṃ jagmurmaithilī parigṛhya tu|| sarvakāmaphalairvṛkṣairnānāpuṣpaphalairvṛtām| sarvakālamadaiścāpi dvijaiḥ samupasevitām||
tgt: Thus commanded by Rāvana, those Rākşasis taking Maithili along with them, went to the Asoka wood, abounding with trees granting every desire, and filled with various kinds of fruits and flowers, and frequented by fowls fraught with juices at all seasons.

src: sā tu śokaparitāṅgī maithilī janakātmajā| rākṣasīvaśamāpannā vyāghrīṇāṃ hariṇī yathā||
tgt: And as a doe comes under the subjection of tigresses, Janaka's daughter, Maithili, her frame worked up with grief, came under the sway of the Raksasis.

src: śokena mahatā trastā maithilī janakātmajā| na śarma labhate bhīruḥ pāśabaddhā mṛgī yathā||
tgt: And like a female deer fast bound by a trap, Janaka's timid daughter Maithilī, agitated by the mighty grief, did not attain respite.

src: na vindate tatra tu śarma maithilī virūpanetrābhiratīva tarjitā| patiṃ smarantī dayitaṃ ca devaraṃ vicetanābhūd bhayaśokapīḍitā ||
tgt: And greatly up-braided by the fierce eyes (of the Raksasis), Maithili did not know repose; and, afflicted with grief and fear, she, remembering her beloved lord along with Lakşmaņa swooned away.

src: itaḥ paraṃ prakṣipto'yaṃ sargaḥ|| praveśitāyāṃ sītāyāṃ laṅkāṃ prati pitāmaha| tadā provāca devendra parituṣṭaṃ śatakratum||
tgt: Having been thus addressed, Vaidehi unaffected by fear, although exercised with grief, placing a blade of grass between herself and Ravana, answered him.

src: trailokyasya hitārthāya rakṣasāmahitāya ca| laṅkāṃ praveśitā sītā rāvaṇena durātmanā ||
tgt: On Sītā having entered Lankā, the great father addressed the gratified Devendra of an hundred sacrifices, For bringing about the weal of the three worlds, and the woe of the Rākşasas, Sītā has been taken into Lankā by the wickedminded, Rāvaņa.

src: pativratā mahābhāgā nityaṃ caiva sustraidhitā| apaśyantī ca bhatauraṃ paśyantī rākṣasījanam|| rākṣasībhiḥ parivṛtā bhartṛdarśanalālasā|
tgt: Devoted to her husband, the exalted lady always brought up in happiness, not seeing her husband, and seeing (on the other hand) environed by numbers of Räkşasīs,-is hungering after the sight of her lord.

src: niviṣṭā hi purī laṅkā tīre nadanadīpateḥ|| kathaṃ jñāsyati tāṃ rāmastatrasthāṃ tāmaninditām|
tgt: The city of Lankā is situated on the shores of the lord of rivers and streams. How can Rāma get a knowledge of that blameless one, staying there?

src: duḥśaṃ saṃcintayanitī sā bahuśaḥ paridurlabhā || prāṇayātrāmakurrāṇā prāṇāṃstyakṣyatyasaṃśayam| sa bhūyaḥ saṃśayo jātaḥ sītāyāḥ prāṇasaṃkṣaye||
tgt: Brooding over the various ills she has undergone, that exceedingly rare damsel is passing her days. Surely she will resign her existence. Great is the doubt that has arisen as to Sītā putting a period to her existence.

src: sa tvaṃ śīghramito gatvā sītāṃ paśya śubhānanām| praviśya nagarī laṅkāṃ prayaccha haviruttamam||
tgt: Having yourself from here, do you see the fair-faced Sītā. having entered the city of Lankā, Offer excellent clarified butter.

src: evamukto'tha devendraḥ purī rāvaṇapālitām| āgacchannidrayā sārdha bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ||
tgt: Thus addressed by the reverend chastiser of Pāka, Devendra in company with sleep, approached the city ruled by Rāvana.

src: nidrāṃ covāca gaccha tvaṃ rākṣasān sampramohaya| sā tathoktā maghavatā devī paramaharṣitā|| devakāryārthasiddhayarthaṃ prāmohayata rākṣasān |
tgt: He then addressed sleep, saying. Go you; and stupefy the Räksasas. Thus accosted by Maghavat, that goddess, exceedingly delighted, for securing success to the work of the celestials, covered the Rākşasas with stupor.

src: etasminnantare devaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ śacīpatiḥ|| āsamāda vanasthāṃ tāṃ vacanaṃ cedamabravīt |
tgt: In the meanwhile, that god, the thousand-eyed lord of Śacī went to (Sītā) staying in the woods, and spoke to her these words,

src: devarājo'smi bhadraṃ te iha cāsmi śucismite|| ahaṃ tvāṃ kāryaniddadhyarthaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ| sāhāyyaṃ kalpayiṣyāmi mā śuco janakātmaje ||
tgt: I am the sovereign of the celestials. Good betide you! I am here, O you of luminous smiles! For securing success to the work of the magnanimous Rāghava, I will lend my aid to you. Do not, Odaughter of Janaka, grieve.

src: matprasādāt samudraṃ sa tariṣyati balaiḥ saha| mayaiveha ca rākṣasyo māyāya mohitāḥ śubhe||
tgt: Through my grace, he shall along with his forces cross over the ocean. And, O excellent wench, I have by my supernal power, stupified the Raksasis.

src: tasmādannamidaṃ sīte haviṣyānnahaṃ svayam| sa tvāṃ saṃgṛhya vaidehi āgataḥ saha nidrayā|14||
tgt: And, O Sita, for this reason, I along with sleep, taking these rice, rice boiled in clarified butter, have, O Vaidehi, corne to you.

src: etadatsyasi maddhastānna tvāṃ vādhiṣyate śubhe| kṣudhā tṛṣā ca rambhoru varṣāṇāmayutairapi||
tgt: If you partake of these from my hand, you shall never O beauteous one, be afflicted either with hunger or thirst, O you of thighs resembling rambhā (trunks), for years.

src: evamuktā tu devendramuvāca pariśaṅkitā| kathaṃ jānāmi devendraṃ tvāmihasthaṃ khajāpatim||
tgt: Thus addressed, Sītā, alarmed, said, How can I know you for Devendra, Saci's husband, staying here?

src: devaliṅgāni dṛṣṭāni rāmalakṣmaṇasaṃnidhau| tāni darśaya devendra yadi tvaṃ devarāṭ svayam||
tgt: By the side of Rāma and Lakşmaņa, I had beheld the signs of the celestials. If, O Devendra, you are yourself the sovereign of the celestials, show those to me.

src: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā tathā cakre śacīpatiḥ| gṛthivīṃ nāspṛśat padbhyāmanimeṣekṣaṇāni ca|| arajo'mbaradhārī ca namlīnakusumastathā| taṃ jñātvā lakṣṇaiḥ sītā vāsavaṃ pariharṣitā ||
tgt: Hearing Sītā's words, the lord of Saçī did accordingly. he did not touch the earth with his feet, and his eyes remained winkless. he bloomed in youth, and the blossoms did not fade on his attire. Thereupon knowing him for Vāsava, Sītā was overjoyed.

src: uvāca vākyaṃ rudatī bhagavan rāghavaṃ prati| kaha bhrātrā mahābāhurdiṣṭayaḥ me śrutimāgataḥ||
tgt: And weeping, she spoke regarding Rāghava, By luck it is that I had heard of that mightyarmed one along with his brother.

src: yathā me śvaśuro rājā yathā ca mithilādhipaḥ| sathā tvamadya paśyāmi sanātho me patistvayā||
tgt: As is my father-in-law, the king, as is the master of Mithilā, so are you (to me), you whom I behold to-day; my husband has now found a protector.

src: tavājñayā ca devendra payobhūtamidaṃ haviḥ| aśiṣyāmi tvayā dattaṃ raghūṇāṃ kulavarghanam||
tgt: And by your command, O Devendra, will I partake of this pāyasa cooked with milk, which has been offered to me, and which shall enhance (the prosperity) of our race.

src: indrahastād gṛhītvā tat pāyasaṃ sā śucismitā| nyavedayata bharne sā lakṣmaṇāya ca maithilī||
tgt: Thereupon taking the pāyasa from Indra's hands, that Maithilī of luminous smiles (mentally) offered it to her husband as well as Laksmana.

src: yadi jīvati me bhartā saha bhrātrā mahābalaḥ| idamastu tayorbhaktyā tadāśnāt svayam||
tgt: If my mighty lord live along with his brother, let this through my reverence for them, be theirs. She then partook of the pāyasa herself.

src: itīva tat prāśya havirvarānanā jahau kṣudhāduḥkhasamudbhavaṃ ca tam| indrāt pravṛttimupalabhya jānakī kākutsthayoḥ prītamanā babhūva ||
tgt: Having thus eaten it, that one of excellent countenance, had her hunger and rising sorrow removed; and attaining a mental tendency from Indra, Janaki grew glad with reference to the Kakutsthas.

src: sa āhavanīyāgāre vaitāṃ rātrīṃ śayīta /
tgt: It is from the cart that he should take (the rice required for the sacrifice).

src: gārhapatyāgāre vā devānvā eṣa upāvartate yo vratamupaiti sa yānevopāvarttate teṣāmevaitanmadhye śete 'dhaḥ śayītādhastādiva hi śreyasa upacāraḥ //
tgt: For at first the cart (is the receptacle of the rice) and afterwards this halland because he thinks 'what was at first (in the cart, and hence still unimpaired by entering the householder's abode), that I will operate upon;' for that reason let him take (rice) from the cart.

src: yadvevāpaḥ praṇayati / adbhirvā idaṃ sarvamāptaṃ tatprathamenaivaitatkarmaṇā sarvamāpnoti // yadvevāsyātra /
tgt: Moreover, the cart represents an abundance; for the cart does indeed represent an abundance: hence, when there is much of anything, people say that there are 'cart-loads' of it.

src: tā utsicyottareṇa gārhapatyaṃ sādayati /
tgt: Thus he thereby approaches an abundance, and for this reason he should take from the cart.

src: gṛhā vai gārhapatyo gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhāyām pratitiṣṭhati tatho hainameṣa vajro na hinasti tasmādgārhapatye sādayati //
tgt: The cart further is (one of the means of) the sacrifice; for the cart is indeed (one of the means of) sacrifice. To the cart, therefore, refer the (following) Yagus-texts, and not to a store-room, nor to a jar.

src: yoṣā vā āpo vṛbṣāgnirmithunamevaitatprajananaṃ kriyata evamiva hi mithunaṃ kLptamuttarato hi strī pumāṃsamupaśete //
tgt: The Rishis, it is true, once took (the rice) from a leathern bag, and hence, in the case of the Rishis, the Yagus-texts applied to a leathern bag.

src: tā nāntareṇa saṃcareyuḥ /
tgt: Here, however, they are taken in their natural application.

src: karmaṇo vāṃ veṣāya vāmiti yajño vai karma yajñāya hi tasmādāha karmaṇo vāmiti veṣāya vāmiti veveṣṭīva hi yajñam //
tgt: Because he thinks 'from (or, by means of) the sacrifice I will perform the sacrifice,' let him, therefore, take (rice) from the cart.

src: sa vā anasa eva gṛhṇīyāt /
tgt: Some do indeed take it from a (wooden) jar.

src: uto pātryai gṛāmu tarhyavastadupohya gṛhṇīyādyato yunajāma tato vimuñccanti //
tgt: In that case also he should mutter the Yagus-texts without omitting any; and let him in that case take (the rice) after inserting the wooden sword under[paragraph continues] (the jar).

src: tasya vā etasyānasaḥ /
tgt: He does so, thinking 'where we want to yoke, there we unyoke;' for from the same place where they yoke, they also unyoke.

src: agnireva dhūragnirhi vai dhūratha ya enadvahantyagnidagdhamivaiṣāṃ vaham bhavatyatha yajjaghanena kastambhīm pra ugaṃ vedirevāsya sā nīḍa eva havirdhānam //
tgt: (Like) fire, verily, is the yoke of that very cart; for the yoke is indeed (like) fire: hence the shoulder of those (oxen) that draw this (cart) becomes as if burnt by fire. The middle part of the pole behind the prop represents, as it were, its (the cart's) altar ; and the enclosed space of the cart (which contains the rice) constitutes its havirdhânam (receptacle of the sacrificial food) .

src: dhūrasi dhūrva dhūrvantaṃ dhūrva taṃ yo 'smāndhūrvati taṃ dhūrvayaṃ vayaṃ dhūrvāma ityagnirvā eṣa dhuryastametadatyeṣyanbhavati havirgrahiṣyaṃstasmāevaitānnihnute tatho haitameṣo 'tiyantamagnirdhuryo na hinasti //
tgt: He now touches the yoke, with the text : 'Thou art the yoke (dhur); injure (dhûrv) thou the injurer! injure him that injures us! injure him whom we injure!' For there being a fire in the yoke by which he will have to pass when he fetches the material for the oblation, he thereby propitiates it, and thus that fire in the yoke does not injure him when he passes by.

src: adharmāsaśo vā ahaṃ sapatnāndhūrvāmītyetaddha sma sa tadabhyāha //
tgt: Here now Âruni said: 'Every half-moon I destroy the enemies.' This he said with reference to this point.

src: atha jaghanena kastambhīmīṣāmabhimṛśya japati / devānāmasi vahnitamaṃ sasnitamam papritamaṃ juṣṭatamaṃ devahūtamam / ahrutamasi havirdhānaṃ dṛṃhasva mā hvārityana evaitadupastautyupastutādrātamanaso havirgṛhṇānīti mā te yajñapatirhvārṣīditi yajamāno vai yajñapatistadyajamānāyaivaitaduhvalāmāśāste //
tgt: Thereupon, whilst touching the pole behind the prop, he mutters : 'To the gods thou belongest, thou the best carrying one, the most firmly joined , the most richly filled , the most agreeable (to the gods), the best caller of the gods!' 'Thou art unbent, the receptacle of oblations; be thou firm, waver not!' Thus he eulogises the cart, hoping that he may obtain the oblation from the one thus eulogised and pleased. He adds , 'May thy Lord of Sacrifice not waver!' for Lord of Sacrifice is the sacrificer, and it is for the sacrificer, therefore, that he thus prays for firmness.

src: viṣṇustvā kramatāmiti yajño vai viṣṇuḥ sa devebhya imāṃ vikrāntiṃ vicakrame yaiṣāmiyaṃ vikrāntiridameva prathamena padena paspārāthedamantarikṣaṃ dvitīyena divamuttamenaitāmvevaiṣa etasmai viṣṇuryajño vikrāntiṃ vikramate //
tgt: He now ascends (the cart by the southern wheel), with the text : 'May Vishnu ascend thee!' For Vishnu is the sacrifice; by striding (vi-kram) he obtained for the gods this all-pervading power (vikrânti) which now belongs to them. By his first step he gained this very (earth), by the second the aërial expanse, and by the last step the sky. And this very same pervading power Vishnu, as sacrifice, by his strides obtains for him (the sacrificer).

src: atha prekṣate / uru vātāyeti prāṇo vai vātastadbrahmaṇaiv aitatprāṇāya vātāyorugāyaṃ kurute // athāpāsyati /
tgt: He then looks (at the rice) and (addressing the cart) mutters : 'Wide open (bethou) to the wind!' For wind means breath; so that by this prayer he effects free scope for the air of the (sacrificer's) breath.

src: apahataṃ rakṣa iti yadyatra kiñcidāpannam bhavati yadyu nābhyeva mṛśettannāṣṭrā evaitadrakṣāṃ syato 'pahanti // athābhipadyate /
tgt: With the text , 'Repelled is the Rakshas!' he then throws away whatever (grass, &c.) may have fallen on it. But if nothing (have fallen on it), let him merely touch it. He thereby drives away from it the evil spirits, the Rakshas.

src: yacantām pañcati pañca vā imā aṅgulayaḥ pāṅkto vai yajñastadyajñamevaitadatra dadhāti // atha gṛhṇāti /
tgt: He touches (the rice), with the text , 'Let the five take!' for five are these fingers, and fivefold also is the sacrifice ; so that he thereby puts the sacrifice on it (the cart).

src: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyām pūṣṇo hastābhyām agnaye juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti savitā vai devānām prasavitā tatsavitṛprasūta evaitadgṛhṇātyaśvinorbāhubhyāmityaśvināvadhvaryū pūṣṇo hastābhyāmiti pūṣā bhāgadugho 'śanam pāṇibhyāmupanidhātā satyaṃ devā antammanuṣyāstatsatyenaivaitadgṛhṇāti //
tgt: He then takes (the rice), with the text : 'At the impulse (prasavana) of the divine Savitri, I take thee with the arms of the Asvins, with the hands of Pûshan, thee, agreeable to Agni!' For Savitri is the impeller (prasavitri) of the gods: therefore he takes this as one impelled by Savitri. 'With the arms of the Asvins,' he says, because the two Asvins are the Adhvaryu priests (of the gods). 'With the hands of Pûshan,' he says, because Pûshan is distributer of portions (to the gods), who with his own hands places the food before them.

src: atha devatāyā ādiśati /
tgt: He now announces (the oblation) to the deity (for whom it is intended).

src: sarvā ha vai devatā adhvaryuṃ havirgṛhīṣyantamupatiṣṭhante mama nāma grahīṣyati mama nāma grahīṣyatīti tābhya evaitatsaha satībhyo 'samadaṃ karoti //
tgt: For when the Adhvaryu is about to take the oblation, all the gods draw near to him, thinking, 'My name he will choose! my name he will choose!' and among them who are thus gathered together, he thereby establishes concord.

src: yadveva devatāyā ādiśati / yāvatībhyo ha vai devatābhyo havīṃṣi gṛhyanta ṝṇamu haiva tāstena manyante yadasmai taṃkāmaṃ samardhayeyuryatkāmyā gṛhṇ āti tasmādvai devatāyā 'ādiśatyevameva yathāpūrvaṃ havīṃṣi gṛhītvā //
tgt: Another reason for which he announces (the oblation) to the deity, is this: whichever deities are chosen, they consider it as an obligation that they are bound to fulfil whatever wish he entertains whilst taking (the oblation); and for that reason also he announces it to the deity. After taking the oblations (to the other deities) in the same way as before ,--

src: athābhimṛśati / bhūtāya tvā nārātaya iti tadyata eva gṛhṇāti tadevaitatpunarāpyāyayati //
tgt: He touches (the rice that is left), with the text : 'For existence (or, abundance,--I leave) thee, not for non-offering !' He thereby causes it to increase again.

src: svarabhivikhyeṣamiti parivṛtamiva vā etadano bhavati tadasyaitaccakṣuḥ pāpmagṛhītamiva bhavati yajño vai svarahardevāḥ sūryastatsvarevaitadato bhivipaśyati //
tgt: He now (whilst seated on the cart) looks towards east, with the text : 'May I perceive the light!' For that cart being covered up, its eye is thereby, as it were, affected with evil. Light, moreover, represents the sacrifice, the day, the gods, and the sun; so that he thereby perceives this same (fourfold) light.

src: athāvarohati / dṛṃhantāṃ duryāḥ pṛthivyāmiti gṛhā vai duryāste heta īśvaro gṛhā yajamānasya yo 'syaiṣo 'dhvaryuryajñena carati tam prayantamanu pracyotostasyeśvaraḥ kulaṃ vikṣobdhostānevaitadasyām pṛthivyāṃ dṛṃhati tathā nānupracyavante tathā na vikṣobhante tasmādāha dṛṃhantāṃ duryāḥ pṛthivyāmityatha praityurvantarikṣamanvemīti so 'sāveva bandhuḥ //
tgt: He then descends (from the cart), with the text : 'May those provided with doors stand firm on the earth!' Those provided with doors are the houses: for the houses of the sacrificer might indeed be capable of breaking down behind the back of his Adhvaryu, when he walks forward (from the cart) with the sacrifice, and might crush his (the sacrificer's) family. By this (text), however, he causes them to stand firmly on this earth, so that they do not break down and crush (his family); for this reason he says: 'May those provided with doors stand firm on the earth!' He then walks forward (north of the Gârhapatya fire), with the text , 'I move along the wide aërial realm;' the application of which is the same .

src: sa yasya gārhapatye havīṃṣi śrapayanti / gārhapatye tasya pātrāṇi saṃsādayanti jaghaneno tarhi gārhapatyaṃ sādayedyasyāhavanīye havīṃṣi śrapayantyāhavanīye tasya pātrāṇi saṃsādayanti jaghaneno tarhyāhavanīyaṃ sādayetpṛthivyāstvā nābhau sādayāmīti madhyaṃ vai nābhirmadhyamabhayaṃ tasmādāha pṛthivyāstvā nābhau sādayāmītyadityā upastha ityupastha ivainadabhārṣuriti vā āhuryatsuguptaṃ gopāyanti tasmādāhādityā upastha ityagne havyaṃ rakṣeti tadagnaye caivaitaddhaviḥ paridadāti guptyā asyai ca pṛthivyai tasmādāhāgne havyaṃ rakṣeti //
tgt: householder) whose Gârhapatya fire they (the priests) use for coking oblations, they place the utensils in the Gârhapatya (house); and let him (the Adhvaryu) in that case put (the winnowing basket with the rice) down at the back (or west) side of the Gârhapatya. But in the case of one whose Âhavanîya they use for cooking oblations, they place the utensils together in the Âhavanîya; and let him in that case put it (the rice) down at the back of the Âhavanîya. He should (in either case) do so, with the text , 'On the navel of the earth I place thee!' forthe navel means the centre, and the centre is safe from danger: for this reason he says, 'On the navel of the earth I place thee!' And further, 'In the lap of Aditi (the boundless or inviolable earth)!' for when people guard anything very carefully, they commonly say that 'they, as it were, carried it in their lap;' and this is the reason why he says, 'In the lap of Aditi!' And further, 'O Agni, do thou protect this offering!' whereby he makes this oblation over for protection both to Agni and to this earth: for this reason he says, 'O Agni, do thou protect this offering!'

src: pavitre karoti / pavitre stho vaiṣṇavyāviti yajño vai viṣṇuryajñiye stha ityevaitadāha // te vai dve bhavataḥ /
tgt: He now prepares two strainers (pavitra) , with the text : 'Purifiers (or strainers, pavitra) are ye, and belonging to Vishnu!' For Vishnu is the sacrifice; so that he thereby says, 'You belong to the sacrifice.'

src: ayaṃ vai pavitraṃ yo 'yam pavate so 'yameka ivaiva pavate so 'yam puruṣe 'ntaḥ praviṣṭaḥ prāṅca pratyaṅca tāvimau prāṇodānau tadetasyaivānu mātrāṃ tasmāddve bhavataḥ //
tgt: Two there are of them: for means of cleansing (pavitra) is this (wind) which here ventilates (pavate); and this, it is true, ventilates as one only; but on entering into man, it becomes a forward and a backward one, and they are these two, to wit, the prâna (breathing out) and the udâna (breathing up or in) . And as this (clarifying process) takes placein accordance with the measure of that (process of breathing), therefore there are two (strainers).

src: atho api trīṇi syuḥ / vyāno hi tṛtīyo dve nveva bhavatastābhyāmetāḥ prokṣaṇīrutpūya tābhiḥ prokṣati tadyadetābhyāmutpunāti //
tgt: There may also be three: for the vyâna (or pervading vital air) is a third (kind of breathing); but in reality there are only two. Having then strained the sprinkling water with these two (strainers), he sprinkles with it.

src: vṛtro ha vā idaṃ sarvaṃ vṛtvā śiśye / yadidamantareṇa dyāvāpṛthivī sa yadedaṃ sarvaṃ vṛtvā śiśye tasmādvṛtro nāma //
tgt: Vritra in truth lay covering all this (space) which here extends between heaven and earth, And because he lay covering (vri) all this, therefore his name is Vritra.

src: tamindro jaghāna /
tgt: Him Indra slew.

src: sa hataḥ pūtiḥ sarvata evāpo 'bhipra susrāva sarvataiva hyayaṃ samudrastasmādu haikā āpo bībhatsāñcakrire tā uparyuparyatipupruvire 'ta ime darbhāstā haitā anāpūyitā āpo 'sti vā itarāsu saṃ sṛṣṭamiva yadenā vṛtraḥ pūtirabhiprāsravattadevāsāmetābhyām pavitrābhyāmapahantyatha medhyābhirevādbhiḥ prokṣati tasmādvā etābhyāmutpunāti //
tgt: He being slain flowed forth stinking in all directions towards the water; for in every direction lies the ocean. And in consequence of this, some of the waters became disgusted, and, rising higher and higher, flowed over: whence (sprung) these grasses (of which the strainers are made; for they represent the water which was not putrified. With the other (water), however, somematter has become mixed up, inasmuch as the putrid Vritra flowed into it. This he now removes from it by means of these two strainers; whereupon he sprinkles with the (sacrificially) pure water.

src: sa utpunāti /
tgt: This is the reason why he strains it through them.

src: saviturvaḥ prasava utpunāmyacidreṇa pavitreṇa sūryasya raśmibhiriti savitā vai devānām prasavitā tatsavitṛprasūta evaitadutpunātyacidreṇa pavitreṇeti yo vā ayam pavata eṣo 'cidram pavitrametenaitadāha sūryasya raśmibhirityete vā utpavitāro yatsūryasya raśmayastasmādāha sūryasya raśmibhiriti //
tgt: He strains it, with the text 'By the impulse of Savitri I purify thee with this flawless purifier (or ventilator, pavitra), with the rays of the sun!' For Savitri is the impeller (prasavitri) of the gods, so that he strains this (water) as one impelled by Savitri. 'With this flawless purifier (ventilator, pavitra),' he says, because this (wind) which here ventilates (or purifies, pavate) is a flawless purifier. 'With the rays of the sun,' he says, because they, the rays of the sun, are certainly purifying; and for this reason he says, 'With the rays of the sun.'

src: tāḥ savye pāṇau kṛtvā / dakṣiṇenodiṅgayatyupastautyevainā etanmahayatyeva devīrāpo agreguvo agrepuva iti devyo hyāpastasmādāha devīrāpa ityagreguva iti tā yatsamudraṃ gacanti tenāgreguvo 'grepuva iti tā yatprathamāḥ somasya rājño bhakṣayanti tenāgrepuvo 'gra imamadya yajñaṃ nayatāgre yajñapatiṃ sudhātuṃ yajñapatiṃ devayuvamiti sādhu yajñaṃ sādhu yajamānamityevaitadāha //
tgt: Having taken it (the water with the ladle) in his left hand, he makes it spirt upwards with his right hand, and eulogises and glorifies it, with the text : 'Shining (or divine) waters! ye the first-going, the first-drinking ones!' For the waters are shining; and for this reason he says, 'Shining waters!' 'First-going,' he calls them, because they flow towards the sea and are therefore going in front (or forwards). 'First-drinking,' he calls them, because they are the first that drink of king Soma and are therefore 'drinking first.' And further: 'Forward now lead this sacrifice ,forward the Lord of Sacrifice, the liberal, god-loving Lord of Sacrifice!' whereby he says, 'Well (lead) the sacrifice, well the sacrificer!'

src: yuṣmā indro 'vṛṇīta vṛtratūrya iti / etā u hīndro 'vṛṇīta vṛtreṇa spardhamāna etābhirhyenamahaṃstasmādāha yuṣmā indro 'vṛṇīta vṛtratūrya iti //
tgt: And further : 'You Indra chose (for his companions) in the battle against Vritra!' For Indra, when he was battling with Vritra, did choose them (the waters) and with their help he killed him; and for this reason he says, 'You Indra chose in the battle against Vritra!'

src: yūyamindramavṛṇīdhvaṃ vṛtratūrya iti / etā u hīndramavṛṇata vṛtreṇa spardhamānametābhirhyenamahaṃstasmādāha yūyamindramavṛṇīdhvaṃ vṛtratūrya 'iti //
tgt: 'You chose Indra in the battle against Vritra!' for they, too, chose Indra when he was battling with Vritra, and with them he killed him: therefore he says, 'You chose Indra in the battle against Vritra!' And further : 'Consecrated by sprinkling are ye!' With these words he makes amends to them .

src: tadetābhyo nihnute 'tha haviḥ prokṣatyeko vai prokṣaṇasya bandhurmedhyamevaitatkaroti //
tgt: He then sprinkles the (first) oblation . One and the same meaning applies to the (whole process of) sprinkling, viz.

src: sa prokṣati agnaye tvā juṣṭam prokṣāmīti tadyasyai devatāyai havirbhavati tasyai medhyaṃ karotyevameva yathāpūrvaṃ havīṃṣi prokṣya //
tgt: he thereby makes sacrificially pure that (which he sprinkles). He sprinkles, with the text : 'Thee, agreeable to Agni, I sprinkle!' Thus for whichever deity the oblation is intended, for that one he thereby renders it sacrificially pure.

src: atha yajñapātrāṇi prokṣati / daivyāya karmaṇo śundhadhvaṃ devayajyāyā iti daivyāya hi karmaṇo śundhati devayajyāyai yadvo 'śuddhaḥ parājaghnuridaṃ vastacundhāmīti tadyadevaiṣāmatrāśuddhastakṣā vānyo vāmedhyaḥ kaścitparāhanti tadevaiṣāmetadadbhirmedhyaṃ karoti tasmādāha yadvo 'śuddhāḥ parājaghnuridaṃ vastacundhāmīti //
tgt: He then sprinkles the sacrificial vessels ,with the text , 'Be ye pure for the divine work, for the sacrifice to the gods!' for it is for the divine work, the sacrifice to the gods, that he consecrates them. 'Whatever, that belongs to you, the impure have defiled by touching, that I hereby purify for you!' For whatever belonging to them some impure one--either a carpenter or some other impure person--has on this occasion desecrated by touching, that he thereby renders sacrificially pure for them by means of the water; and therefore he says, 'Whatever, that belongs to you, the impure have defiled by touching, that I hereby purify for you !'

src: atha kṛṣṇājinamādatte /
tgt: He now takes the black antelope skin , for completeness of the sacrifice.

src: yajñasyaiva sarvatvāya yajño ha devebhyo 'pacakrāma sa kṛṣṇo bhūtvā cacāra tasya devā anuvidya tvacamevāvacāyājahruḥ //
tgt: For once upon a time the sacrifice escaped the gods, and having become a black antelope roamed about. The gods having thereupon found it and stripped it of its skin, they brought it (the skin) away with them.

src: tasya yāni śuklāni ca kṛṣṇāni ca lomāni / tānyṛcāṃ ca sāmnāṃ ca rūpaṃ yāni śuklāni tāni sāmnāṃ rūpaṃ yāni kṛṣṇāni tānyṛcāṃ yadi vetarathā yānyeva kṛṣṇāni tāni sāmnāṃ rūpaṃ yāni śuklāni tānyṛcāṃ yānyeva babhrūṇīva harīṇi tāni yajuṣāṃ rūpam //
tgt: Its white and black hairs represent the Rik-verses and the Sâman-verses; to wit, the white the Sâman and the black the Rik; or conversely, the black the Sâman and the white the Rik. The brown and the yellow ones, on the other hand, represent the Yagus-texts.

src: saiṣā trayī vidyā yajñaḥ / tasyā etacilpameṣa varṇastadyatkṛṣṇājinam bhavati yajñasyaiva sarvatvāya tasmātkṛṣṇājinamadhi dīkṣante yajñasyaiva sarvatvāya tasmādadhyavahananamadhipeṣaṇam bhavatyaskannaṃ havirasaditi tadyadevātra taṇḍulo vā piṣṭaṃ vā skandāttadyajñe yajñaḥ pratitiṣṭhāditi tasmādadhyavahananamadhipeṣaṇam bhavati //
