tgt: Now this same threefold science is the sacrifice; that manifold form, that (varying) colour of this (science) is what is (represented by) this black antelope skin. For the completeness of the sacrifice (he takes the skin): hence the rite of initiation (for the Soma-sacrifice) is likewise performed on the black antelope skin;--for the completion of the sacrifice: hence it is also used for husking and bruising (the rice) on, in order that nothing of the oblation may get spilt; and that, if any grain or flour should now be spilt on it, the sacrifice would still remain securely established in the sacrifice.

src: atha kṛṣṇājinamādatte /
tgt: For this reason it is used for husking and bruising upon.

src: śarmāsīti carma vā etatkṛṣṇasya tadasya tanmānuṣaṃ śarma devatrā tasmādāha śarmāsīti tadavadhūnotyavadhūtaṃ rakṣo 'vadhūtā arātaya iti tannāṣṭrā evaitadrakṣaṃsyato 'pahantyatinatyeva pātrāṇyavadhūnoti yadyasyāmedhyamabhūttadyasyaitadavadhūnoti //
tgt: He thus takes the black antelope skin, with the text : 'Bliss-bestowing (sarman) art thou!' For karman ('hide') is the name of that (skin of the) black deer used among men, but sarman (bliss) is (that used) among the gods; and for this reason he says, 'Bliss-bestowing art thou!' He shakes it, with the text , 'Shaken off is the Rakshas, shaken off are the enemies!' whereby he repels from it the evil spirits, the Rakshas.

src: tatpratīcīnagrīvamupastṛṇāti /
tgt: He shakes it whilst holding it apart from the vessels ; whereby he shakes off whatever impure matter there may have been on it.

src: adityāstvagasi prati tvāditirvettvitīyaṃ vai pṛthivyaditistasyā asyai tvagyadidamasyāmadhi kiñca tasmādāhādityāstvagasīti prati tvāditirvettviti prati hi svaḥ saṃ jānīte tatsaṃjñāmevaitatkṛṣṇājināya ca vadati nedanyo 'nyaṃ hinasāta ityabhinihitameva savyena pāṇinā bhavati // atha dakṣiṇenolūkhalamāharati /
tgt: He spreads it (on the ground with the hairy side upwards, and) with its neck-part turned to the west , with the text : 'The skin of Aditi art thou! May Aditi acknowledge thee!' For Aditi is this earth, and whatever is on her, that serves as a skin to her: for this reason he says, 'The skin of Aditi art thou!' And 'may Aditi acknowledge thee!' he says, because one who is related (to another) acknowledges (him). Thereby he establishes a mutual understanding between her and the black antelope skin, (thinking) 'they will not hurt each other.' While it is still being held down with his left hand,--

src: nediha purā nāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyāviśāniti brāhmaṇo hi rakṣasāmapahantā tasmādabhinihitameva savyena pāṇinā bhavati // atholūkhalaṃ nidadhāti /
tgt: He at once takes the mortar with his right hand, fearing lest the evil spirits, the Rakshas, might rush in here in the meantime. For the priest (brâhmana) is the repeller of the Rakshas: therefore, whilst it is still being held down with his left hand,--

src: adrirasi vānaspatyo grāvāsi pṛthubuḍhna iti vā tadyathaivādaḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ grāvabhirabhiṣuṇvantyevamevaitadulūkhalamusalābhyāṃ dṛṣadupalābhyāṃ haviryajñamabhiṣuṇotyadraya iti vai teṣāmekaṃ nāma tasmādāhādrirasīti vānaspatya iti vānaspatyo hyeṣa grāvāsi pṛthubudhna iti grāvā hyeṣa pṛthubudhno hyeṣa prati tvādityāstvagvettviti tatsaṃjñāmevaitatkṛṣṇājināya ca vadati nedanyo 'nyaṃ hinasāta iti //
tgt: He puts the mortar (on it), with the text : 'A wooden stone (adri) art thou!'or 'A broad-bottomed stone (grâvan) art thou!' For, just as there (in the Soma-sacrifice) they press king Soma out with stones (grâvan), thus here also he prepares the oblation (haviryagña) by means of the mortar and pestle, and the large and small mill-stones . Now 'stones (adrayah)' is the common name of these, and therefore he says, 'a stone art thou.' And 'wooden,' he calls it, because this one (the mortar) really is made of wood . Or, he says, 'a broad-bottomed stone (grâvan) art thou,' because it is both a stone and broad-bottomed.

src: agnestanūrasi vāco visarjanamiti yajño hi tenāgnestanūrvāco visarjanamiti yāṃ vā amūṃ havirgrahīṣyanvācaṃ yacatyatra vai taṃ visṛjate tadyadetāmatra vācaṃ visṛjata eṣa hi yajña ulūkhale pratyaṣṭhādeṣa hi prāsāri tasmādāha vāco visarjanamiti //
tgt: He then pours the (two portions of) rice (from the winnowing basket into the mortar), with the text : 'Thou art the body of Agni, thou the releaser of speech!' For it is (material for) sacrifice, and hence (by being offered in the fire) it becomes Agni's body. 'The releaser of speech,' he adds, because he now releases that speech which he restrained when he was about to take the rice (from the cart).

src: sa yadidam purā mānuṣīṃ vācaṃ vyāharet / tatro vaiṣṇāvīmṛcaṃ vā yajurvā japedyajño vai viṣṇustadyajñam punarārabhate tasyo haiṣā prāyaścittirdevavītaye tvā gṛhṇāmīti devānavadityu hi havirgṛhyate //
tgt: Should he, however (by some accident), utter any human sound before this time, let him in that case mutter some Rik or Yagus-text addressed to Vishnu ; for Vishnu is the sacrifice, so that he thereby again obtains a hold on the sacrifice, and penance is thereby done by him (for not keeping silent). He adds: 'For the pleasure of the gods I seize thee!' for the oblation is taken with the intention 'that it shall gladden the gods.'

src: atha musalamādatte /
tgt: He now takes the pestle, with the text , 'A large, wooden stone art thou!' for it is a large stone, and made of wood, too.

src: bṛhadgrāvāsi vānaspatya iti bṛhadgrāvā hyeṣa vānaspatyo hyeṣa tadavadadhāti sa idaṃ devebhyo haviḥ śamīṣva suśami śamīṣveti sa idaṃ devebhyo haviḥ saṃskuru sādhusaṃskṛtaṃ saṃskurvityevaitadāha // atha haviṣkṛtamudvādayati / haviṣkṛdehi haviṣkṛdehīti vāgvai haviṣkṛdvācamevaitadvisṛjate vāgu vai yajñastadyajñamevaitatpunarupahvayate //
tgt: He thrusts it down, with the text , 'Do thou prepare this oblation for the gods ! do thou prepare it thoroughly!' thereby saying, 'Get this oblation ready for the gods! get it quite ready!' He then calls the Havishkrit (preparer of the sacrificial food), 'Havishkrit, come hither! Havishkrit, come hither!' The Havishkrit no doubt is speech, so that he thereby frees speech fromrestraint. And speech, moreover, represents sacrifice , so that he thereby again calls the sacrifice to him.

src: tāni vā etāni /
tgt: Now there are four different forms of this call, viz.

src: catvāri vāca ehīti brāhmaṇasyāgahyādraveti vaiśyasya ca rājanyabandhoścādhāveti śūdrasya sa yadeva brāhmaṇasya tadāhaitaddhi yajñiyatamametadu ha vai vācaḥ śāntataṃ yadehīti tasmādehītyeva brūyāt //
tgt: 'come hither (ehi)!' in the case of a Brâhman; 'approach (âgahi)!' and 'hasten hither (âdrava)!' in the case of a Vaisya and a member of the military caste (râganyabandhu ); and 'run hither (âdhâva)!' in that of a Sûdra. On this occasion he uses the call that belongs to a Brâhman, because that one is best adapted for a sacrifice, and is besides the most gentle:.

src: taddha smaitatpurā /
tgt: let him therefore say, 'come hither (ehi)!'

src: jāyaiva haviṣkṛdupottiṣṭhati tadidamapyetarhi ya eva kaścopottiṣṭhati sa yatraiṣa haviṣkṛtamudvādayati tadeko dṛṣadupale samāhanti tadyadetāmatra vācam pratyudvādayanti //
tgt: Now in former times it was no other than the wife (of the sacrificer) who rose at this (call, to act) as Havishkrit; therefore now also (she or) some one (priest) rises in answer to this call. And at the time when he (the Adhvaryu) calls the Havishkrit, one of the priests beats the two mill-stones.[paragraph continues] The reason why they produce this discordant noise, is this:

src: manorha vā ṝṣabha āsa /
tgt: Manu was in possession of a bull .

src: tasminnasuraghnī sapatnaghnī vākpraviṣṭāsa tasya ha sma śvasathādravathādasurarakṣasāni mṛdyamānāni yanti te hāsurāḥ samūdire pāpaṃ vata no 'yamṛṣabhaḥ sacate kathaṃ nvimaṃ dabhnuyāmeti kilātākulī iti hāsurabrahmāvāsatuḥ //
tgt: Into him had entered an Asura-killing, foe-killing voice; and by his snorting and roaring the Asuras and Rakshas were continually being crushed. Thereupon the Asuras said to one another: 'Evil, alas! this bull inflicts upon us! how can we possibly destroy him?' Now Kilâta and Âkuli were the two priests (brahman) of the Asuras.

src: tau hocatuḥ / śraddhādevī vai manurāvaṃ nu vedāveti tau hāgatyocaturmano yājayāva tveti kenetyanenarṣabheṇeti tatheti tasyālabdhasya sa vāgapacakrāma //
tgt: These two said, 'God-fearing, they say, is Manu: let us two then ascertain!' They then went to him and said: 'Manu! we will sacrifice for thee!' He said: 'Wherewith?' They said: 'With this bull!' He said: 'So be it!' On his (the bull's) being killed the voice went from him.

src: tasyai ha sma yatra vadantyai śṛṇvanti tato ha smaivāsurarakṣasāni mṛdyamānāni yanti te hāsurāḥ samūdira ito vai naḥ pāpīyaḥ sacate bhūyo hi mānuṣī vāgvadatīti kilātākulī haivocatuḥ śraddhādevo vai manurāvaṃ nveva vedāveti tau hāgatyocaturmano y ājayāva tveti kenetyanayaiva jāyayeti tatheti tasyā ālabdhāyai sā vāgapacakrāma //
tgt: It entered into Manâvî, the wife of Manu; and when they heard her speak, the Asuras and Rakshas were continually being crushed. Thereupon the Asuras said to one another: 'Hereby even greater evil is inflicted on us, for the human voice speaks more!' Kilâta and Âkuli then said: 'God-fearing, they say, is Manu: let us then ascertain!' They went to him and said: 'Manu! we will sacrifice for thee!' He said: 'Wherewith?'[paragraph continues] They said: 'With this thy wife!' He said: 'So be it!' And on her being killed that voice went from her.

src: sā yajna=ameva yajñapātrāṇi praviveśa /
tgt: It entered into the sacrifice itself, into the sacrificial vessels; and thence those two (Asura priests) were unable to expel it.

src: tato haināṃ na śekaturnirhantuṃ saiṣāsuraghnī vāgudvadati sa yasya haivaṃviduṣa etāmatra vācam pratyudvādayanti pāpīyāṃso haivāsya sapatnā bhavanti //
tgt: This same Asura-killing, foe-killing voice sounds forth (from the millstones when they are beaten with the wedge). And for whomsoever that knows this, they produce this discordant noise on the present occasion, his enemies are rendered very miserable.

src: kukkuṭo 'si madhujihva iti madhujihvo vai sa devebhya āsīdviṣajihvo 'surebhyaḥ sa yo devebhya āsīḥ sana edhītye vaitadāheṣamūrjamāvada tvayā vayaṃ saṅghātaṃ saṅghātaṃ jeṣmeti nātra tirohitamivāsti // atha śūrpamādatte / varṣavṛddhamasīti varṣavṛddhaṃ hyetadyadi naḍānāṃ yadi veṇūnāṃ yadīṣīkāṇāṃ varṣamuhyevaitā vardhayati //
tgt: He beats the mill-stones with the wedge, with the text : 'A honey-tongued cock (kukkuta ) art thou (O wedge)!' For honey-tongued indeed was he (the bull) for the gods, and poison-tongued for the Asuras: hence he thereby says: 'What thou wert for the gods, that be thou for us!' He adds: 'Sap and strength do thou call hither! with thy help may we conquer in every battle!' In these words there is nothing that is obscure. Thereupon he (the Adhvaryu) takes the winnowing basket, with the text : 'Rain-grown art thou!' For rain-grown it is indeed, whether it be made of reeds or of cane or of rushes, since it is the rain that makes these grow.

src: prati tvā varṣavṛddhaṃ vettviti varṣavṛddhā u hyevaite yadi vrīhayo yadi yavā varṣamuhyevaitānvardhayati tatsaṃjñāmevaitacūrpāya ca vadati nedanyo 'nyaṃ hinasāta iti //
tgt: He then pours out the (threshed) rice (from the mortar into the winnowing basket), with the text : 'May the rain-grown acknowledge (receive) thee!' For rain-grown also are these (grains), whether they be rice or barley, since it is the rain that makes them grow.

src: atha niṣpunāti / parāpūtaṃ rakṣaḥ parāpūtā arātaya ityatha tuṣānprahantyapahataṃ rakṣa iti tannāṣṭrā evaitadrakṣāṃsyato 'pahanti //
tgt: He now winnows (the rice), with the text : 'Cleared off is the Rakshas! cleared off are the evil-doers!' The husks (which have fallen on the ground) he throws away , with the text , 'Expelled is the Rakshas!' for those evil spirits, the Rakshas, he thereby expels.

src: vāyurvo vivinaktvityayaṃ vai vāyuryo 'yam pavata eṣa vā idaṃ sarvaṃ vivinakti yadidaṃ kiṃca vivicyate tadenāneṣa evaitad vivinaktisa yadaita etatprāpnuvanti yatrainān adhyapavinakti //
tgt: He then separates (the husked grains from the unhusked), with the text : 'May the wind separate you!' For it is that wind (which is produced by the winnowing) which here purifies (or blows, pavate); and it is the wind that separates everything here (on earth) that undergoes separation: therefore it also separates here those (two kinds of grain) from each other.

src: athānumantrayate /
tgt: Now when they are undergoing this process, and whilst he is separating (the husked, so as to drop them into a pot),--

src: devo vaḥ savitā hiraṇyapāṇiḥ pratigṛbhṇātvācidreṇa pāṇinā supratigṛhītā asannityatha triḥ phalīkaroti trivṛddhi yajñaḥ //
tgt: He addresses (those in the pot) thus : 'May the divine Savitri, the golden-handed, receive you with a flawless hand!' By this he says: 'May they be well received!' He then cleans them thrice ; for threefold is the sacrifice.

src: taddhaike devebhyaḥ śundhadhvaṃ devebhyaḥ śundhadhvamiti phalīkurvanti tadu tathā na kuryādādiṣṭaṃ vā etaddevatāyai havirbhavatyathaitadvaiśvadevaṃ karoti yadāha devebhyaḥ śundhadhvamiti tatsamadaṃ karoti tasmādu tūṣṇīmeva phalīkuryāt //
tgt: Here now some clean them with the formula: 'For the gods get clean! for the gods get clean!' But let him not do so: for this oblation is intended for some particular deity; and if he were to say, 'For the gods get clean!' he would make it one intended for all the deities, and would thereby raise a quarrel among the deities. Let him therefore do the cleaning silently! Now the one (viz.

src: sa vai kapālānyevānyatara upadadhāti /
tgt: the Âgnîdhra) puts the potsherds on (the Gârhapatya fire); the other (viz.

src: śamenaivaṃvidhenāyaṃ kāmadveṣavigarhiṇā | brahmalokamavāpnoti paritoṣeṇa vaṃcitaḥ ||
tgt: ‘With a tranquillity of this kind, which disdains desire or dislike, he reaches the world of Brahman, deceived by the delight.

src: jñātvā vidvān vitarkāṃstu manaḥsaṃkṣobhakārakān | tadviyuktamavāpnoti dhyānaṃ prītisukhānvitam ||
tgt: ‘But the wise man, knowing that these reasonings bewilder the mind, reaches a (second) stage of contemplation separate from this, which has its own pleasure and ecstasy.

src: hriyamāṇastayā prītyā yo viśeṣaṃ na paśyati | sthānaṃ bhāsvaramāpnoti deveṣvābhāsureṣvapi ||
tgt: ‘And he who, carried away by this pleasure, sees no further distinction, obtains a dwelling full of light, even amongst the Ābhāsura deities.

src: yastu prītisukhāttasmādvivecayati mānasam | tṛtīyaṃ labhate dhyānaṃ sukhaṃ prītivivarjitam ||
tgt: ‘But he who separates his mind from this pleasure and ecstasy, reaches the third stage of contemplation ecstatic but without pleasure.

src: tatra kecidvyavasyaṃti mokṣa ityapi māninaḥ | sukhaduḥkhaparityāgādavyāpārācca cetasaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Upon this stage some teachers make their stand, thinking that it is indeed liberation, since pleasure and pain have been left behind and there is no exercise of the intellect.

src: yastu tasminsukhe magno na viśeṣāya yatnavān | śubhakṛtsnaiḥ sa sāmānyaṃ sukhaṃ prāpnoti daivataiḥ ||
tgt: ‘But he who, immersed in this ecstasy, strives not for a further distinction, obtains an ecstasy in common with the Śubhakṛtsna deities.

src: tādṛśaṃ sukhamāsādya yo na rajyannupekṣate | caturthaṃ dhyānamāpnoti sukhaduḥkhavivarjitam ||
tgt: ‘But he who, having attained such a bliss desires it not but despises it, obtains the fourth stage of contemplation which is separate from all pleasure or pain.

src: asya dhyānasya tu phalaṃ samaṃ devairvṛhatphalaiḥ | kathayaṃti vṛhatphalaṃ vṛhatprajñāparīkṣakāḥ ||
tgt: ‘The fruit of this contemplation which is on an equality with the Vṛhatphala deities, those who investigate the great wisdom call the Vṛhatphala.

src: samādhervyutthitastasmāddṛṣṭvā doṣāṃścharīriṇām | jñānamārohati prājñaḥ śarīravinivṛttaye ||
tgt: ‘But rising beyond this contemplation, having seen the imperfections of all embodied souls, the wise man climbs to a yet higher wisdom in order to abolish all body.

src: tatastaddhyānamutsṛjya viśeṣe kṛtaniścayaḥ | kāmebhya iva satprājño rūpādapi virajyate ||
tgt: ‘Then, having abandoned this contemplation, being resolved to find a further distinction, he becomes as disgusted with form itself as he who knows the real is with pleasures.

src: śarīre khāni yānyasya tānyādau parikalpayan | ghaneṣvapi tato dravyeṣvākāśamadhimucyate ||
tgt: ‘First he makes use of all the apertures of his body; and next he exerts his will to experience a feeling of void space even in the solid parts.

src: ākāśasamamātmānaṃ saṃkṣipya tvaparo budhaḥ | tadaivānaṃtataḥ paśyan viśeṣamadhigacchati ||
tgt: ‘But another wise man, having contracted his soul which is by nature extended everywhere like the ether,  — as he gazes ever further on, detects a yet higher distinction.

src: adhyātmakuśaleṣvanyo nivartyātmānamātmanā | kiṃcinnāstīti saṃpaśyannākiṃcanya iti smṛtaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Another one of those who are profoundly versed in the supreme Self, having abolished himself by himself, sees that nothing exists and is called a Nihilist.

src: tato muṃjādiṣīkeva śakuniḥ paṃjarādiva | kṣetrajño niḥsṛto dehānmukta ityabhidhīyate ||
tgt: ‘Then like the Muñja-reed’s stalk  from its sheath or the bird from its cage, the soul, escaped from the body, is declared to be “liberated.”

src: etattatparamaṃ brahma nirliṃgaṃ dhruvamakṣaram | yanmokṣa iti tattvajñāḥ kathayaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ ||
tgt: ‘This is that supreme Brahman, constant, eternal, and without distinctive signs; which the wise who know reality declare to be liberation.

src: ityupāyaśca mokṣaśca mayā saṃdarśitastava | yadi jñātaṃ yadi ruci yathāvatpratipadyatām ||
tgt: ‘Thus have I shown to thee the means and liberation; if thou hast understood and approved it, then act accordingly.

src: jaigīṣavyo 'tha janako vṛddhaścaiva parāśaraḥ | imaṃ paṃthānamāsādya muktā hyanye ca mokṣiṇaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Jaigīṣavya  and Janaka, and the aged Parāsara, by following this path, were liberated, and so were others who sought liberation.’

src: iti tasya sa tadvākyaṃ gṛhītvā na vicārya ca | pūrvahetubalaprāptaḥ pratyuttaramuvāca saḥ ||
tgt: The prince having not accepted his words but having pondered them, filled with the force of his former arguments, thus made answer:

src: śrutaṃ jñānamidaṃ sūkṣmaṃ parataḥ parataḥ śivam | kṣetreṣvasyāparityāgādavaimyetadanaiṣṭhikam ||
tgt: ‘I have heard this thy doctrine, subtil and pre-eminently auspicious, but I hold that it cannot be final, because it does not teach us how to abandon this soul itself in the various bodies.

src: vikāraprakṛtibhyo hi kṣetrajñaṃ muktamapyaham | manye prasavadharmāṇaṃ vījadharmāṇameva ca ||
tgt: ‘For I consider that the embodied soul, though freed from the evolutes and the evolvents, is still subject to the condition of birth and has the condition of a seed.

src: viśuddho yadyapi hyātmā nirmukta iti kalpyate | atyaṃtastatparityāgaḥ satyātmani na vidyate ||
tgt: ‘Even though the pure soul is declared to be “liberated,” yet as long as the soul remains there can be no absolute abandonment of it.

src: hitvā hitvā trayamidaṃ viśeṣastūpalabhyate | ātmanastu sthitiryatra tatra sūkṣmamidaṃ trayam ||
tgt: ‘If we abandon successively all this triad, yet “distinction” is still perceived; as long as the soul itself continues, there this triad continues in a subtil form.

src: sūkṣmatvāccaiva doṣāṇāmavyāpārācca cetasaḥ | dīrghatvādāyuṣaścaiva mokṣastu parikalpyate ||
tgt: ‘It is held (by some) that this is liberation, because the “imperfections” are so attenuated, and the thinking power is inactive, and the term of existence is so prolonged;

src: ahaṃkāraparityāgo yaścaiṣa parikalpyate | satyātmani parityāgo nāhaṃkārasya vidyate ||
tgt: ‘But as for this supposed abandonment of the principle of egoism, — as long as the soul continues, there is no real abandonment of egoism.

src: saṃkhyādibhiramuktaśca nirguṇo na bhavatyayam | tasmādasati nairguṇye nāsya mokṣo 'bhidhīyate ||
tgt: ‘The soul does not become free from qualities as long as it is not released from number and the rest; therefore, as long as there is no freedom from qualities, there is no liberation declared for it.

src: guṇino hi guṇānāṃ ca vyatireko na vidyate | rūpoṣṇābhyāṃ virahito na hyagnirupalabhyate ||
tgt: ‘There is no real separation of the qualities and their subject; for fire cannot be conceived, apart from its form and heat.

src: prāgdehānna bhaveddehī prāgguṇebhyastathā guṇī | kasmādādau vimuktaḥ sañśarīrī badhyate punaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Before the body there will be nothing embodied, so before the qualities there will be no subject; how, if it was originally free, could the soul ever become bound?

src: kṣetrajño viśarīraśca jño vā syādajña eva vā | yadi jño jñeyamasyāsti jñeye sati na mucyate ||
tgt: ‘The body-knower (the soul) which is unembodied, must be either knowing or unknowing; if it is knowing, there must be some object to be known, and if there is this object, it is not liberated.

src: athājña iti siddho vaḥ kalpitena kimātmanā | vināpi hyātmanājñānaṃ prasiddhaṃ kāṣṭhakuḍyavat ||
tgt: ‘Or if the soul is declared to be unknowing, then of what use to you is this imagined soul? Even without such a soul, the existence of the absence of knowledge is notorious as, for instance, in a log of wood or a wall.

src: parataḥ paratastyāgo yasmāttu guṇavān smṛtaḥ | tasmātsarvaparityāgānmanye kṛtsnāṃ kṛtārthatām ||
tgt: ‘And since each successive abandonment is held to be still accompanied by qualities, I maintain that the absolute attainment of our end can only be found in the abandonment of everything.’

src: iti dharmamarāḍasya viditvā na tutoṣa saḥ | akṛtsnamiti vijñāya tataḥ pratijagāma ha ||
tgt: Thus did he remain unsatisfied after he had heard the doctrine of Arāḍa; then having decided it to be incomplete, he turned away.

src: viśeṣamatha śuśrūṣurudrakasyāśramaṃ yayau | ātmagrāhācca tasyāpi jagṛhe na sa darśanam ||
tgt: Seeking to know the true distinction, he went to the hermitage of Udraka,  but he gained no clear understanding from his treatment of the soul.

src: saṃjñāsaṃjñitvayordoṣaṃ jñātvā hi munirudrakaḥ | ākiṃcinyātparaṃ lebhe saṃjñāsaṃjñātmikāṃ gatim ||
tgt: For the sage Udraka, having learned the inherent imperfections of the name and the thing named, took refuge in a theory beyond Nihilism, which maintained a name and a non-name.

src: yasmāccālaṃbane sūkṣme saṃjñāsaṃjñe tataḥ param | nāsaṃjñī naiva saṃjñīti tasmāttatra gataspṛhaḥ ||
tgt: And since even a name and a non-name were substrata, however subtil, he went even further still and found his restlessness set at rest in the idea that there is no named and no un-named;

src: yataśca buddhistatraiva sthitānyatrāpracāriṇī | sūkṣmāpādi tatastatra nāsaṃjñitvaṃ na saṃjñitā ||
tgt: And because the intellect rested there, not proceeding any further, — it became very subtil, and there was no such thing as un-named nor as named.

src: yasmācca tamapi prāpya punarāvartate jagat | bodhisattvaḥ paraṃ prepsustasmādudrakamatyajat ||
tgt: But because, even when it has reached this goal it yet returns again to the world, therefore the Bodhisattva, seeking something beyond, left Udraka.

src: tato hitvāśramaṃ tasya śreyo 'rthī kṛtaniścayaḥ | bheje gayasya rājarṣernagarīsaṃjñamāśramam ||
tgt: Having quitted his hermitage, fully resolved in his purpose, and seeking final bliss, he next visited the hermitage, called a city, of the royal sage Gaya.

src: atha nairaṃjanātīre śucau śuciparākramaḥ | cakāra vāsamekāṃtavihārābhivratī muniḥ ||
tgt: Then on the pure bank of the Nairañjanā the saint whose every effort was pure fixed his dwelling, bent as he was on a lonely habitation.

src: tatpūrvaṃ paṃceṃdriyavaśoddhatān | tapaḥ vratino bhikṣūn paṃca niraikṣata ||
tgt: Then he saw five mendicants who had come there before him; they had taken vows on themselves and practised austerities, vaunting themselves of control of the five senses.

src: paṃcopatasthurdṛṣṭvātra bhikṣavastaṃ mumukṣavaḥ | puṇyārjitadhanārogyamiṃdriyārthā iveśvaram ||
tgt: Five mendicants, desiring liberation, came up to him when they beheld him there, just as the objects of the senses come up to a percipient who has gained wealth and health by his previous merit.

src: saṃpūjyamānastaiḥ prahvairvinayānatamūrtibhiḥ | tadvaṃśasthāyibhiḥ śiṣyairlolairmana iveṃdriyaiḥ ||
tgt: Being honoured by these disciples who were dwelling in that family, as they bowed reverently with their bodies bent low in humility, as the mind is honoured by the restless senses,

src: mṛtyujanmāṃtakaraṇe syādupāyo 'yamityatha | duṣkarāṇi samārebhe tapāṃsyanaśanena saḥ ||
tgt: And thinking, ‘this may be the means of abolishing birth and death,’ he at once commenced a series of difficult austerities by fasting.

src: upavāsavidhīn nekān kurvan naradurācarān | varṣāṇi ṣaṭkarmaprepsurakarotkārśyamātmanaḥ ||
tgt: For six years, vainly trying to attain merit,  he practised self-mortification, performing many rules of abstinence, hard for a man to carry out.

src: annakāleṣu caikaikaiḥ sakolatilataṃḍulaiḥ | apārapārasaṃsārapāraṃ prepsurapārayat ||
tgt: At the hours for eating, he, longing to cross the world whose farther shore is so difficult to reach, broke his vow with single jujube fruits, sesame seeds, and rice.

src: dehādapacayastena tapasā tasya yaḥ kṛtaḥ | sa evopacayo bhūyastejasāsya kṛto 'bhavat ||
tgt: But the emaciation which was produced in his body by that asceticism, became positive fatness through the splendour which invested him.

src: kṛśo 'pyakṛśakīrtiśrīrhlādaṃ cakre 'nyacakṣuṣam | kumudānāmiva śaracchuklapakṣādicaṃdramāḥ ||
tgt: Though thin, yet with his glory and his beauty unimpaired, he caused gladness to other eyes, as the autumnal moon in the beginning of her bright fortnight gladdens the lotuses.

src: tvagasthiśeṣo niḥśeṣairmedaḥpiśitaśoṇitaiḥ | kṣīṇo 'pyakṣīṇagāṃbhīryaḥ samudra iva sa vyabhāt ||
tgt: Having only skin and bone remaining, with his fat, flesh and blood entirely wasted, yet, though diminished, he still shone with undiminished grandeur like the ocean.

src: atha kaṣṭatapaḥspaṣṭavyarthakliṣṭatanurmuniḥ | bhavabhīrurimāṃ cakre buddhiṃ buddhatvakāṃkṣayā ||
tgt: Then the seer, having his body evidently emaciated to no purpose in a cruel self-mortification; — dreading continued existence, thus reflected in his longing to become a Buddha:

src: nāyaṃ dharmo virāgāya na bodhāya na muktaye | jaṃbumūle mayā prāpto yastadā sa vidhirdhruvaḥ ||
tgt: ‘This is not the way to passionlessness, nor to perfect knowledge, nor to liberation; that was certainly the true way which I found at the root of the Jambu  tree.

src: na cāsau durbalenāptuṃ śakyamityāgatādaraḥ | śarīrabalavṛddhyarthamidaṃ bhūyo 'nvaciṃtayat ||
tgt: ‘But that cannot be attained by one who has lost his strength’, — so resuming his care for his body, he next pondered thus, how best to increase his bodily vigour:

src: kṣutpipāsāśramaklāṃtaḥ śramādasvasthamānasaḥ | prāpnuyānmanasāvāpyaṃ phalaṃ kathamanirvṛtaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Wearied with hunger, thirst, and fatigue, with his mind no longer self-possessed through fatigue, how should one who is not absolutely calm reach the end which is to be attained by his mind?

src: nirvṛtiḥ prāpyate samyaksatateṃdriyatarpaṇāt | saṃtarpiteṃdriyatayā manaḥsvāsthyamavāpyate ||
tgt: ‘True calm is properly obtained by the constant satisfaction of the senses; the mind’s self-possession is only obtained by the senses being perfectly satisfied.

src: svasthaprasannamanasaḥ samādhirupapadyate | samādhiyuktacittasya dhyānayogaḥ pravartate ||
tgt: ‘True meditation is produced in him whose mind is self-possessed and at rest, — to him whose thoughts are engaged in meditation the exercise of perfect contemplation begins at once.

src: dhyānapravartanāddharmāḥ prāpyaṃte yairavāpyate | durlabhaṃ śāṃtamajaraṃ paraṃ tadamṛtaṃ padam ||
tgt: ‘By contemplation are obtained those conditions  through which is eventually gained that supreme calm, undecaying, immortal state, which is so hard to be reached.’

src: tasmādāhāramūlo 'yamupāya itiniścayaḥ | asūrikaraṇe dhīraḥ kṛtvāmitamatirmatim ||
tgt: Having thus resolved, ‘this means is based upon eating food,’ the wise seer of unbounded wisdom, having made up his mind to accept the continuance of life,

src: snāto nairaṃjanātīrāduttatāra śanaiḥ kṛśaḥ | bhaktyāvanataśākhāgrairdattahastastaṭadrumaiḥ ||
tgt: And having bathed, thin as he was, slowly came up the bank of the Nairañjanā, supported as by a hand by the trees on the shore, which bent down the ends of their branches in adoration.

src: atha gopādhipasutā daivatairabhicoditā | udbhūtahṛdayānaṃdā tatra naṃdabalāgamat ||
tgt: Now at that time Nandabalā, the daughter of the leader of the herdsmen, impelled by the gods, with a sudden joy risen in her heart, had just come near,

src: sitaśaṃkhojjvalabhujā nīlakaṃbalavāsinī | sapheṇamālānīlāṃburyamuneva saridvarā ||
tgt: Her arm gay with a white shell, and wearing a dark blue woollen cloth, like the river Yamunā, with its dark blue water and its wreath of foam.

src: sā śraddhāvardhitaprītirvikasallocanotpalā | śirasā praṇipatyainaṃ grāhayāmāsa pāyasam ||
tgt: She, having her joy increased by her faith, with her lotus-like eyes opened wide, bowed down before him and persuaded him to take some milk.

src: kṛtvā tadupabhogena prāptajanmaphalāṃ sa tām | bodhiprāptau samartho 'bhūtsaṃtarpitaṣaḍiṃdriyaḥ ||
tgt: By partaking that food having made her obtain the full reward of her birth, he himself became capable of gaining the highest knowledge, all his six senses being now satisfied,

src: paryāptāpyānamūrtaśca sārdhaṃ suyaśasā muniḥ | kāṃtidhairyaikabhāraikaḥ śaśāṃkārṇavavalbabhau ||
tgt: The seer, having his body now fully robust, together with his glorious fame, one beauty and one majesty being equally spread in both, shone like the ocean and the moon.

src: āvṛtta iti vijñāya taṃ jahuḥ paṃcabhikṣavaḥ | manīṣiṇamivātmānaṃ nirmuktaṃ paṃcadhātavaḥ ||
tgt: Thinking that he had returned to the world the five mendicants left him, as the five elements leave the wise soul when it is liberated.

src: vyavasāyadvitīyo 'tha śādvalāstīrṇabhūtalam | so 'śvatthamūlaṃ prayayau bodhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ ||
tgt: Accompanied only by his own resolve, having fixed his mind on the attainment of perfect knowledge, he went to the root of an Aśvattha tree,  where the surface of the ground was covered with young grass.

src: tatastadānīṃ gajarājavikramaḥ padasvanenānupamena bodhitaḥ | mahāmunerāgatabodhiniścayo jagāda kālo bhujagottamaḥ stutim ||
tgt: Then Kāla,  the best of serpents, whose majesty was like the lord of elephants, having been awakened by the unparalleled sound of his feet, uttered this praise of the great sage, being sure that he was on the point of attaining perfect knowledge:

src: yathā mune tvaccaraṇāvapīḍitā muhurmuhurniṣṭanatīva medinī | yathā ca te rājati sūryavatprabhā dhruvaṃ tvamiṣṭaṃ phalamadya bhokṣyase ||
tgt: ‘Inasmuch as the earth, pressed down by thy feet, O sage, resounds repeatedly, and inasmuch as thy splendour shines forth like the sun, thou shalt assuredly to-day enjoy the desired fruit.

src: yathā bhramaṃtyo divi vāyapaṃktayaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ tvāṃ kamalākṣa kurvate | yathā ca saumyā divi vāṃti vāyavastvamadya buddho niyataṃ bhaviṣyasi ||
tgt: ‘Inasmuch as lines of birds fluttering in the sky offer thee reverential salutation, O lotus-eyed one, and inasmuch as gentle breezes blow in the sky, thou shalt certainly to-day become the Buddha.’

src: tato bhujaṃgapravareṇa saṃstutastṛṇānyupādāya śucīni lāvakāt | kṛtapratijño niṣasāda bodhaye mahātarormūlamupāśritaḥ śuceḥ ||
tgt: Being thus praised by the best of serpents, and having taken some pure grass from a grasscutter, he, having made his resolution, sat down to obtain perfect knowledge at the foot of the great holy tree.

src: tataḥ sa paryaṃkamakaṃpyamuttamaṃ babaṃdha suptoragabhogapiṃḍitam | bhinadmi tāvadbhuvi naitadāsanaṃ na yāmi tāvatkṛtakṛtyatāmiti ||
tgt: Then he sat down on his hams in a posture, immovably firm and with his limbs gathered into a mass like a sleeping serpent’s hood, exclaiming, ‘I will not rise from this position on the earth until  I have obtained my utmost aim.’

src: tato yayurmudamatulāṃ divaukaso vavāsire na mṛgaganā na pakṣiṇaḥ | na sasvanurvanataravo 'nilāhatāḥ kṛtāsane bhagavati niścalātmani ||
tgt: Then the dwellers in heaven burst into unequalled joy; the herds of beasts and the birds uttered no cry; the trees moved by the wind made no sound, when the holy one took his seat firm in his resolve.

src: tato muhūrte 'bhyudite jagaccakṣuṣi bhāskare | bhārgavasyāśramapadaṃ sa dadarśa nṛṇāṃ varaḥ ||
tgt: Then when the sun, the eye of the world, was just risen, he, the noblest of men, beheld the hermitage of the son of Bhṛgu,

src: suptaviśvastahariṇaṃ svasthasthitavihaṃgamam | viśrāṃta iva yaddṛṣṭā kṛtārtha iva cābhavat ||
tgt: Its deer all asleep in quiet trust, its birds tranquilly resting, — seeing it he too became restful, and he felt as if his end was attained.

src: sa vismayanivṛttyarthaṃ tapaḥpūjārthameva ca | svāṃ cānuvartitāṃ rakṣannaśvapṛṣṭhādavātarat ||
tgt: For the sake of ending his wonder and to show reverence for the penances observed, and as expressing his own conformity therewith,  he alighted from the back of his horse.

src: avatīrya ca pasparśa nistīrṇamiti vājinam | chaṃdakaṃ cābravīt prītaḥ snāpayanniva cakṣuṣā ||
tgt: Having alighted, he stroked the horse, exclaiming, ‘All is saved,’ and he spoke well-pleased to Chaṃdaka, bedewing him as it were with tears from his eyes :

src: imaṃ tārkṣyopamajavaṃ turaṃgamanugacchatā | darśitā saumya madbhaktirvikramaścāyamātmanaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Good friend, thy devotion to me and thy courage of soul have been proved by thy thus following this steed whose speed is like that of Tārkṣya.

src: sarvathāsmyanyakāryo 'pi gṛhīto bhavatā hṛdi | bhartṛsnehaśca yasyāyamīdṛśaḥ śakta eva ca ||
tgt: ‘Bent even though I am on other business, I am wholly won in heart by thee, — one who has such a love for his master, and at the same time is able to carry out his wish.

src: asnigdho 'pi samartho 'sti niḥsāmarthyo 'pi bhaktimān | bhaktimāṃscaiva śaktaśca durlabhastvadvidho bhuvi ||
tgt: ‘One can be able without affection, and affectionate though unable; but one like thee, at once affectionate and able, is hard to find in the world.

src: tatprīto 'smi tavānena mahābhāgena karmaṇā | dṛśyate mayi bhāvo 'yaṃ phalebhyo 'pi parāṅmukhe ||
tgt: ‘I am pleased with this noble action of thine; this feeling is seen towards me, even though I am regardless of conferring rewards.

src: ko janasya phalasthasya na syādabhimukho janaḥ | janībhavati bhūyiṣṭhaṃ svajano 'pi viparyaye ||
tgt: ‘Who would not be favourably disposed to one who stands to him as bringing him reward? but even one’s own people commonly become mere strangers in a reverse of fortune.

src: kulārthaṃ dhāryate putraḥ poṣārthaṃ sevyate pitā | āśayāśliṣyati jagannāsti niṣkāraṇāsvatā ||
tgt: ‘The son is maintained for the sake of the family, the father is honoured for the sake of our own (future) support; the world shows kindness for the sake of hope; there is no such a thing as unselfishness without a motive.

src: kimuktvā bahu saṃkṣepātkṛtaṃ me sumahatpriyam | nivartasvāśvamādāya saṃprāpto 'smīpsitaṃ vanam ||
tgt: ‘Why speak many words? in short, thou hast done me a very great kindness; take now my horse and return, I have attained the desired wood.’

src: ityuktvā sa mahābāhuranuśaṃsacikīrṣayā | bhūṣaṇānyavamucyāsmai saṃtaptamanase dadau ||
tgt: Thus having spoken, the mighty hero in his desire to show perfect gentleness  unloosed his ornaments and gave them to the other, who was deeply grieved.

src: mukuṭoddīptakarmāṇaṃ maṇimādāya bhāsvaram | bruvan vākyamidaṃ tasthau sāditya iva maṃdaraḥ ||
tgt: Having taken a brilliant jewel whose effect illumined his diadem, he stood, uttering these words, like the mountain Mandara with the sun resting on it:

src: anena maṇinā chaṃda praṇamya bahuśo nṛpaḥ | vijñāpyo 'muktaviśraṃbhaṃ saṃtāpavinivṛttaye ||
tgt: ‘By thee with this jewel, O Chaṃda, having offered him repeated obeisance, the king, with his loving confidence still unshaken, must be enjoined to stay his grief.

src: jarāmaraṇanāśārthaṃ praviṣṭo 'smi tapovanam | na khalu svargatarṣeṇa nāsnehena na manyunā ||
tgt: “I have entered the ascetic-wood to destroy old age and death, — with no thirst for heaven, with no lack of love nor feeling of anger.

src: tadevamabhiniṣkrāṃtaṃ na māṃ śocitumarhasi | bhūtvāpi hi ciraṃ śleṣaḥ kālena na bhaviṣyati ||
tgt: “Do not think of mourning for me who am thus gone forth from my home; union, however long it may last, in time will come to an end.

src: dhruvo yasmācca viśleṣastasmānmokṣāya me matiḥ | viprayogaḥ kathaṃ na syādbhūyo 'pi svajanādibhiḥ ||
tgt: “Since separation is certain, therefore is my mind fixed on liberation; how shall there not be repeated severings from one’s kindred?

src: śokatyāgāya niṣkrāṃtaṃ na māṃ śocitumarhasi | śokahetuṣu kāmeṣu saktāḥ śocyāstu rāgiṇaḥ ||
tgt: “Do not think of mourning for me who am gone forth to leave sorrow behind; it is the thralls of passion, who are attached to desires, the causes of sorrow, for whom thou shouldst mourn.

src: ayaṃ ca kila pūrveṣāmasmākaṃ niścayaḥ sthiraḥ | iti dāyādabhūtena na śocyo 'smi pathā vrajan ||
tgt: “This was the firm persuasion of our predecessors, — I as one departing by a common road am not to be mourned for by my heir.

src: bhavaṃti hyarthadāyādāḥ puruṣasya viparyaye | pṛthivyāṃ dharmadāyādā durlabhāstu na saṃti vā ||
tgt: “At a man’s death there are doubtless heirs to his wealth; but heirs to his merit are hard to find on the earth or exist not at all.

src: yadapi syādasamaye yāto vanamasāviti | akālo nāsti dharmasya jīvite caṃcale sati ||
tgt: “Even though thou sayest, ‘He is gone at a wrong time to the wood,’ — there is no wrong time for religious duty (dharma), life being fragile as it is.

src: tasmādadyaiva me śreyaścetavyamiti niścayaḥ | jīvite ko hi viśraṃbho mṛtyau pratyarthini sthite ||
tgt: “Therefore my determination is, ‘I must seek my supreme good this very day;’ what confidence can there be in life, when death stands as our adversary?”

src: evamādi tvayā saumya vijñāpyo vasudhādhipaḥ | prayatethāstathā caiva yathā māṃ na smaredapi ||
tgt: ‘Do thou address the king, O friend, with these and such-like words; and do thou use thy efforts so that he may not even remember me.

src: api nairguṇyamasmākaṃ vācyaṃ narapatau tvayā | nairguṇyāttyajyate snehaḥ snehatyāgānna śocyate ||
tgt: ‘Yea, do thou repeat to the king our utter unworthiness; through unworthiness affection is lost, — and where affection is lost, there is no sorrow.’

src: iti vākyamidaṃ śrutvā chaṃdaḥ saṃtāpaviklavaḥ | vāṣpagrathitayā vācā pratyuvāca kṛtāṃjaliḥ ||
tgt: Having heard these words, Chaṃda, overwhelmed with grief, made reply with folded hands, his voice choked by tears :

src: anena tava bhāvena bāṃdhavāyāsadāyinā | bhartaḥ sīdati me ceto nadīpaṃka iva dvipaḥ ||
tgt: ‘At this state of mind of thine, causing affliction to thy kindred, my mind, O my lord, sinks down like an elephant in the mud of a river.

src: kasya notpādayedvāṣpaṃ niścayaste 'yamīdṛśaḥ | ayomaye 'pi hṛdaye kiṃ punaḥ snehaviklave ||
tgt: ‘To whom would not such a determination as this of thine cause tears, even if his heart were of iron, — how much more if it were throbbing with love?

src: vimānaśayanārhaṃ hi saukumāryamidaṃ kva ca | kharadarbhāṃkuravatī tapovanamahī kva ca ||
tgt: ‘Where  is this delicacy of limb, fit to lie only in a palace, — and where is the ground of the ascetic forest, covered with the shoots of rough kusa grass?

src: śrutvā tu vyavasāyaṃ te yadaśvo 'yaṃ mayā hṛtaḥ | balātkāreṇa tannātha daivenaivāsmi kāritaḥ ||
tgt: ‘When, on hearing thy resolve, I first brought thee this horse, — it was fate only, O my lord, which made me do it, mastering my will.

src: kathaṃ hyātmavaśo jānan vyavasāyamimaṃ tava | upānayeyaṃ turagaṃ śokaṃ kapilavastunaḥ ||
tgt: ‘But how could I, O king, by mine own will, knowing this thy decision, — carry back the horse to the sorrow of Kapilavastu?

src: tannārhasi mahābāho vihātuṃ putralālasam | snigdhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca rājānaṃ saddharmamiva nāstikaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Surely thou wilt not abandon, O hero, that fond old king, so devoted to his son, as a heretic might the true religion?

src: saṃvardhanapariśrāṃtāṃ dvitīyāṃ tāṃ ca mātaram | deva nārhasi vismartuṃ kṛtaghna iva satkriyām ||
tgt: ‘And her, thy second mother, worn with the care of bringing thee up, — thou wilt not surely forget her, as an ingrate a benefit?

src: bālaputrāṃ guṇavatīṃ kulaślāghyāṃ pativratām | devīmarhasi na tyaktuṃ klīvaḥ prāptāmiva śriyam ||
tgt: ‘Thou wilt not surely abandon thy queen, endowed with all virtues, illustrious for her family, devoted to her husband and with a young son, as a coward the royal dignity within his reach?

src: putraṃ yāśodharaṃ ślāghyaṃ yaśodharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ | bālamarhasi na tyaktuṃ vyasanīvottamaṃ yaśaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Thou wilt not abandon the young son of Yaśodharā, worthy of all praise, thou the best of the cherishers of religion and fame, as a dissolute spendthrift his choicest glory?

src: atha baṃdhuṃ ca rājyaṃ ca tyaktumeva kṛtā matiḥ | māṃ nārhasi vibho tyaktuṃ tvatpādau hi gatirmama ||
tgt: ‘Or even if thy mind be resolved to abandon thy kindred and thy kingdom, thou wilt not, O master, abandon me, — thy feet are my only refuge.

src: nāsmi yātuṃ puraṃ śakto dahyamānena cetasā | tvāmaraṇye parityajya sumitra iva rāghavam ||
tgt: ‘I cannot go to the city with my soul thus burning, leaving thee behind in the forest as Sumitra  left the son of Raghu.

src: kiṃ hi vakṣyati rājā māṃ tvadṛte nagaraṃ gatam | vakṣyāmyucitadarśitvātkiṃ tavāṃtaḥpurāṇi vā ||
tgt: ‘What will the king say to me, returning to the city without thee? or what shall I say to thy queens by way of telling them good news?

src: yadapyātthāpi nairguṇyaṃ vācyaṃ narapatāviti | kiṃ tadvakṣyāmyabhūtaṃ te nirdoṣasya muneriva ||
tgt: ‘As for what thou saidst, “thou must repeat my unworthiness to the king” — how shall I speak what is false of thee as of a sage without a fault?

src: hṛdayena salajjena jihvayā sajjamānayā | ahaṃ yadyapi vā brūyāṃ kastacchraddhātumarhati ||
tgt: ‘Or even if I ventured to speak it with a heart ashamed and a tongue cleaving to my mouth, who would think of believing it?

src: yo hi caṃdramasastaikṣṇya kathayecchraddadhīta vā | sa doṣāṃstava doṣajña kathayecchraddadhīta vā ||
tgt: ‘He who would tell of or believe the fierceness of the moon, might tell of or believe thy faults, O physician of faults.

src: sānukrośasya satataṃ nityaṃ karuṇavedinaḥ | snigdhatyāgo na sadṛśo nivartasva prasīda me ||
tgt: ‘Him who is always compassionate and who never fails to feel pity, it ill befits to abandon one who loves, — turn back and have mercy on me.’

src: iti śokābhibhūtasya śrutvā chaṃdasya bhāṣitam | svasthaḥ paramayā dhṛtyā jagāda vadatāṃ varaḥ ||
tgt: Having heard these words of Chaṃda overcome with sorrow, — self-possessed with the utmost firmness the best of speakers answered:

src: madviyogaṃ prati cchaṃda saṃtāpastyajyatāmayam | nānābhāvo hi niyataṃ pṛthagjātiṣu dehiṣu ||
tgt: ‘Abandon this distress, Chaṃda, regarding thy separation from me, — change is inevitable in corporeal beings who are subject to different births.

src: svajanaṃ yadyapi snehānna tyajeyaṃ mumukṣayā | mṛtyuranyonyamavaśānasmān saṃtyājayiṣyati ||
tgt: ‘Even if I through affection were not to abandon my kindred in my desire for liberation, death would still make us helplessly abandon one another.

src: mahatyā tṛṣṇayā duḥkhairgarbheṇāsmi yayā dhṛtaḥ | tasyā niṣphalayatnāyāḥ kvāhaṃ mātuḥ kva sā mama ||
tgt: ‘She, my mother, by whom I was borne in the womb with great thirst and pains, — where am I now with regard to her, all her efforts fruitless, and where is she with regard to me?

src: vāsavṛkṣe samāgamya vigacchaṃti yathāṃḍajāḥ | niyataṃ viprayogāṃtastathā bhūtasamāgamaḥ ||
tgt: ‘As birds go to their roosting-tree and then depart, so the meeting of beings inevitably ends in separation.

src: sametya ca yathā bhūyo vyapayāṃti valāhakāḥ | saṃyogo viprayogaśca tathā me prāṇināṃ mataḥ ||
tgt: ‘As clouds, having come together, depart asunder again, such I consider the meeting and parting of living things.

src: yasmādyāti ca loko 'yaṃ vipralabhya parasparam | mamatvaṃ na kṣamaṃ tasmātsvapnabhūte samāgame ||
tgt: ‘And since this world goes away, each one of us deceiving the other, — it is not right to think anything thine own in a time of union which is a dream.

src: sahajena viyujyaṃte parṇarāgeṇa pādapāḥ | anyenānyasya viśleṣaḥ kiṃ punarna bhaviṣyati ||
tgt: ‘Since the trees are parted from the innate colour of their leaves, why should there not still more be the parting of two things which are alien to each other?

src: tadevaṃ sati saṃtāpaṃ mā kārṣīḥ saumya gamyatām | laṃbate yadi tu sneho gatvāpi punarāvraja ||
tgt: ‘Therefore, since it is so, grieve not, my good friend, but go; or if thy love lingers, then go and afterwards return.

src: brūyāścāsmāsvanākṣepaṃ janaṃ kapilavastuni | tyajyatāṃ tadgataḥ snehaḥ śrūyatāṃ cāsya niścayaḥ ||
tgt: ‘Say, without reproaching us, to the people in Kapilavastu, “Let your love for him be given up, and hear his resolve.

src: kṣiprameṣyati vā kṛtvā jarāmṛtyukṣayaṃ kila | akṛtārtho nirālaṃbo nidhanaṃ yāsyatīti vā ||
tgt: “Either he will quickly come back, having destroyed old age and death; or else he will himself perish, having failed in his purpose and lost hold of every support.” '

src: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā kaṃthakasturagottamaḥ | jihvayā lilihe pādau vāṣpamuṣṇaṃ mumoca ca ||
tgt: Having heard his words, Kaṃthaka, the noblest of steeds, licked his feet with his tongue and dropped hot tears.

src: jālinā svastikāṃkena vakramadhyena pāṇinā | āmamarśa kumārastaṃ babhāṣe ca vayasyavat ||
tgt: With his hand whose fingers were united with a membrane and which was marked with the auspicious svastika, and with its middle part curved,  the prince stroked him and addressed him like a friend:

src: muṃca kaṃthaka mā vāṣpaṃ darśiteyaṃ sadaśvatā | mṛṣyatāṃ saphalaḥ śīghraṃ śramaste 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
tgt: ‘Shed not tears, Kaṃthaka, this thy perfect equine nature has been proved, — bear with it, this thy labour will soon have its fruit.’

src: maṇitsaruṃ chaṃdakahastasaṃsthaṃ tataḥ sa dhīro niśitaṃ gṛhītvā | kośādasiṃ kāṃcanabhakticitraṃ vilādivāśīviṣamudbabarha ||
tgt: Then seizing the sharp jewelled sword which was in Chaṃdaka’s hand, he resolutely drew out from the sheath the blade decked with golden ornaments, like a serpent from its hole.

src: niṣkāsya taṃ cotpalapattranīlaṃ ciccheda citraṃ mukuṭaṃ sakeśam | vikīryamāṇāṃśukamaṃtarīkṣe cikṣepa cainaṃ sarasīva haṃsam ||
tgt: Having drawn it forth, dark blue like a blue lotus petal, he cut his decorated tiara and his hair, and he tossed it with its scattered muslin into the air as a grey goose into a lake.

src: pūjābhilāṣeṇa ca bāhumānyāddivaukasastaṃ jagṛhuḥ praviddham | yathāvadenaṃ divi devasaṃghā divyairviśeṣairmahayāṃ ca cakruḥ ||
tgt: And the heavenly beings, with a longing to worship it, seized it respectfully as it was thrown up; and the divine hosts paid it due adoration in heaven with celestial honours.

src: muktvā tvalaṃkārakalatravattāṃ śrīvipravāsaṃ śirasaśca kṛtvā | dṛṣṭvāṃśukaṃ kāṃcanahaṃsacitram vanyaṃ sa dhīro 'bhicakāṃkṣa vāsaḥ ||
tgt: Having thus divorced his ornaments and banished all royal magnificence from his head, and seeing his muslin floating away like a golden goose, the stedfast prince desired a sylvan dress.

src: tato mṛgavyādhavapurdivaukā bhāvaṃ viditvāsya viśuddhabhāvaḥ | kāṣāyavastro 'bhiyayau samīpaṃ taṃ śākyarājaprabhavo 'bhyuvāca ||
tgt: Then a celestial being, wearing the form of a hunter, pure in heart, knowing his thoughts, approached near him in dark-red garments; and the son of the Śākya king thus addressed him:

src: śivaṃ ca kāṣāyamṛṣidhvajaste na yujyate hiṃsramidaṃ dhanuśca | tatsaumya yadyasti na saktiratra mahyaṃ prayacchedamidaṃ gṛhāṇa ||
tgt: ‘Thy red garments are auspicious, the sign of a saint; but this destructive bow is not befitting; therefore, my good friend, if there is no strong preference in the matter, do thou give me that dress and take this of mine.’

src: vyādho 'bravītkāmada kāmamārādanena viśvāsya mṛgān nihatya | arthastu śakropama yadyanena haṃta pratīcchānaya śuklametat ||
tgt: The hunter replied, ‘It has given me my desire,  O giver of desires, as by this I have inspired animals with confidence and then killed them; but if thou hast need of it, O thou who art like Indra, accept it at once and give me the white dress.’

src: pareṇa harṣeṇa tataḥ sa vanyaṃ jagrāha vāso 'ṃśukamutsasarja | vyādhastu divyaṃ vapureva bibhrat tacchuklamādāya divaṃ jagāma ||
tgt: With extreme joy he then took that sylvan dress and gave away the linen one; and the hunter, assuming his heavenly form, having taken the white garment, went to heaven.

src: tataḥ kumāraśca sa cāśvagopastasmiṃstathā yāti visismiyāte | āraṇyake vāsasi caiva bhūyastasminnakārṣṭāṃ bahumānamāśu ||
tgt: Then the prince and the attendant of the horse were filled with wonder as he was thus going, and forthwith they paid great honour anew to that sylvan dress.

src: chaṃdaṃ tataḥ sāśrumukhaṃ visṛjya kāṣāyasaṃvidvṛtakīrtibhṛtsaḥ | yenāśramastena yayau mahātmā saṃdhyābhrasaṃvīta ivādrirājaḥ ||
tgt: Then the great-souled one, having dismissed the weeping Chaṃda, and wearing his fame veiled by the sign of the red garment, went towards the hermitage, like the king of mountains wrapped in an evening cloud.

src: tatastathā bhartari rājyaniḥspṛhe tapovanaṃ yāti vivarṇavāsasi | bhujau samutkṣipya tataḥ sa vājibhṛdbhṛśaṃ vicukrośa papāta ca kṣitau ||
tgt: While his master, thus regardless of his kingdom, was going to the ascetic-wood in mean garments, the groom, tossing up his arms, wailed bitterly and fell on the ground.

src: vilokya bhūyaśca ruroda sasvaraṃ hayaṃ bhujābhyāmupaguhya kaṃthakam | tato nirāśo vilapanmuhurmuhuryayau śarīreṇa puraṃ na cetasā ||
tgt: Having looked again he wept aloud, and embraced the horse Kaṃthaka with his arms; and then, hopeless and repeatedly lamenting, he went in body to the city, not in soul.

src: kvacitpradadhyau vilalāpa ca kvacit kvacitpracaskhāla papāta ca kvacit | ato vrajan bhaktivaśena duḥkhitaścacāra bahvīravaśaḥ pathi kriyāḥ ||
tgt: Sometimes he pondered, sometimes he lamented, sometimes he stumbled, and sometimes he fell; and so going along, wretched through his devoted attachment, he performed all kinds of actions in the road without conscious will.

src: tato visṛjyāśrumukhaṃ rudaṃtaṃ chaṃdaṃ vanacchaṃdatayā nirāsthaḥ | sarvārthasiddho vapuṣābhibhūya tamāśramaṃ siddhamiva prapede ||
tgt: Then having left the weeping tear-faced Chaṃda, — indifferent to all things in his longing for the forest, he by whom all objects are accomplished, overpowering the place by his beauty, entered that hermitage as if it were fully blessed.

src: sa rājasūnurmṛgarājagāmī mṛgājiraṃ tanmṛgavat praviṣṭaḥ | lakṣmīviyukto 'pi śarīralakṣmyā cakṣūṃṣi sarvāśramiṇāṃ jahāra ||
tgt: He the prince with a gait like the lion’s, having entered that arena of deer, himself like a deer, — by the beauty of his person, even though bereft of his magnificence, attracted the eyes of all the dwellers in the hermitage.

src: sthitā hi hastasthayugāstathaiva kautūhalāccakradharāḥ sadārāḥ | tamiṃdrakalpaṃ dadṛśurna jagmurdhuryā ivārdhāvanataiḥ śirobhiḥ ||
tgt: The drivers of wheeled carriages also, with their wives, stood still in curiosity, holding the yokes in their hands, — they gazed on him who was like Indra, and moved not, standing like their beasts of burden with their heads half bent down.

src: viprāśca gatvā bahiridhmahetoḥ prāptāḥ samitpuṣpapavitrahastāḥ | tapaḥpradhānāḥ kṛtabuddhayo 'pi taṃ draṣṭumīyurna maṭhānabhīyuḥ ||
tgt: And the Brāhmans who had gone outside for the sake of fuel, having come with their hands full of fuel, flowers, and kusa grass, — pre-eminent as they were in penances, and proficients in wisdom, went to see him, and went not to their cells.

src: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam aniruddham āmantrayate sma gaccha tvam aniruddha vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ / aniruddho 'py āha
tgt: The Buddha then said to the venerable Aniruddha, “Aniruddha, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

src: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: “My Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

src: Vkn  abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan anyatamasmiṃś caṅkrame caṅkramāmi / tatra śubhavyūho nāma brahmā daśabhir brahmasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ taṃ pradeśam avabhāsya yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasābhivandyaikānte sthitvā mām etad avocat kiyad āyuṣmān aniruddho divyena cakṣuṣā paśyati /
tgt: I remember, Lord, one day when I was taking a walk, the great Brahmā named Śubhavyūha and the ten thousand other Brahmās who accompanied him illuminated the place with their radiance and, having bowed their heads at my feet, withdrew to one side and asked me, ‘Reverend Aniruddha, you have been proclaimed by the Buddha to be the foremost among those who possess the divine eye.

src: ahaṃ mārṣa imaṃ triṃ sāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamuner buddhakṣetraṃ tad yathāpi nāma karatale nyastam āmalakaphalam evaṃ paśyāmi / Vkn  iyaṃ ca kathā pravṛttā vimalakīrtiś ca licchavis taṃ pradeśam upasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasā vanditvaivam āha kiṃ bhadantāniruddha divyaṃ cakṣur abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam utānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam /
tgt: To what distance does the divine vision of the venerable Aniruddha extend?’ I answered, ‘Friends, I see the entire billionworld galactic universe of the Lord Śākyamuni just as plainly as a man of ordinary vision sees a myrobalan nut on the palm of his hand.’ When I had said these words, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and, having bowed his head at my feet, said to me, ‘Reverend Aniruddha, is your divine eye compounded in nature? Or is it uncompounded in nature?

src: yady abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ tad bāhyaiḥ pañcābhijñaiḥ samam,
tgt: If it is compounded in nature, it is the same as the superknowledges of the outsiders.

src: athānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ anabhisaṃskāro 'saṃskṛtas tena na śakyaṃ draṣṭum / tat kathaṃ sthaviraḥ paśyati /
tgt: If it is uncompounded in nature, then it is not constructed and, as such, is incapable of seeing. Then, how do you see, O elder?’

src: so 'haṃ tūṣṇīm abhūvam / Vkn  sa ca brahmā tasya satpuruṣasyemaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptas taṃ namaskṛtyaitad avocat
tgt: “At these words, I became speechless, and Brahmā also was amazed to hear this teaching from that good man.

src: ke loke divyacakṣuṣaḥ /
tgt: Having bowed to him, he said, ‘Who then, in the world, possesses the divine eye?’

src: āha buddhā bhagavanto loke divyacakṣuṣo ye samāhitāvasthāṃ ca na vijahati sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi ca paśyanti / na ca dvayaprabhāvitāḥ /
tgt: “Vimalakīrti answered, ‘In the world, it is the buddhas who have the divine eye. They see all the buddhafields without even leaving their state of concentration and without being affected by duality.’

src: Vkn  atha sa brahmemaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā daśasahasraparivāro 'dhyāśayenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayati sma /
tgt: “Having heard these words, the ten thousand Brahmās were inspired with high resolve and conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: sa māṃ vanditvā taṃ ca satpuruṣam abhivādya tatraivāntarhitaḥ /
tgt: Having paid homage and respect both to me and to that good man, they disappeared.

src: ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: As for me, I remained speechless, and therefore I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

src: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam upālim āmantrayate sma gaccha tvam upāle vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
tgt: The Buddha then said to the venerable Upāli, “Upāli, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

src: upālir apy āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: Upāli replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

src: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan anyatamau dvau bhikṣū āpattim āpannau, tau bhagavataḥ paryapatrapamāṇau bhagavantaṃ nopasaṃkrāmataḥ / tau yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntāv upasaṃkrāmya mām etad avocatām /
tgt: Lord, I remember that one day there were two monks who had committed some infraction and were too ashamed to appear before the Lord, so they came to me and said, ‘Reverend Upāli, we have both committed an infraction but are too ashamed to appear before the Buddha.

src: tāv āvāṃ paryapatrapamāṇau bhagavantam upasaṃkramituṃ notsahāvahe /
tgt: Venerable Upāli, kindly remove our anxieties by absolving us of these infractions.’

src: Vkn  so 'haṃ bhagavaṃs tau bhikṣū dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayāmi / vimalakīrtiś ca licchavis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ sa mām etad avocat mā bhadantopāle etau bhikṣū āgāḍhīkārṣīḥ,
tgt: “Lord, while I was giving those two monks some religious discourse, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and said to me, ‘Reverend Upāli, do not aggravate further the sins of these two monks.

src: vinodayānayor āpattim, mā āvilīkārṣīḥ /
tgt: Without perplexing them, relieve their remorse.

src: na hi bhadantopāle āpattir adhyātmapratiṣṭhitā na bahirdhāsaṃkrānto nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate /
tgt: Reverend Upāli, sin is not to be apprehended within, or without, or between the two.

src: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā cittasaṃkleśāt satvāḥ saṃkliśyante cittavyavadānād viśudhyante /
tgt: The Buddha has said, “Living beings are afflicted by the passions of thought, and they are purified by the purification of thought.”

src: cittaṃ ca bhadantopāle nādhyātmapratiṣṭhitaṃ na bahirdhā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate /
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Upāli, the mind is neither within nor without, nor is it to be apprehended between the two.

src: yathā cittaṃ tathāpattiḥ, yathāpattis tathā sarvadharmāḥ,
tgt: Sin is just the same as the mind, and all things are just the same as sin.

src: tathatāṃ na vyativartante /
tgt: They do not escape this same reality.

src: yā bhadantopāle cittasya prakṛtir yayā cittaprakṛtyā bhadantasya cittaṃ vimuktam, kiṃ jātu sā cittaprakṛtiḥ saṃkliṣṭā /
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Upāli, this nature of the mind, by virtue of which your mind, reverend, is liberateddoes it ever become afflicted?’

src: āha no hidam /
tgt: “ ‘Never,’ I replied.

src: āha tatprakṛtikāni bhadantopāle sarvasatvānāṃ cittāni /
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Upāli, the minds of all living beings have that very nature.

src: Vkn  saṃkalpo bhadantopāle kleśaḥ / akalpāvikalpā ca prakṛtiḥ / viparyāsaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, aviparyastā ca prakṛtiḥ /
tgt: Reverend Upāli, conceptualization is total affliction, and not conceptualizing and not discriminating is their true nature. Misapprehension is total affliction, and nonmisapprehension is their true nature.

src: ātmasamāropaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, nairātmyā ca prakṛtiḥ /
tgt: The presumption of self is total affliction, and selflessness is their true nature.

src: utpannabhagnānavasthitā bhadantopāle sarvadharmā māyāmeghavidyutsadṛśāḥ / nirapekṣāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kṣaṇam api nāvatiṣṭhante / svapnamarīcisadṛśāḥ sarvadharmā vitathadarśanāḥ / dakacandrapratibimbasadṛśāḥ sarvadharmāś cittaparikalpenotpadyante /
tgt: Reverend Upāli, all things are without production, destruction, and duration, like magical illusions, clouds, and lightning all things are evanescent, not remaining even for an instant all things are like dreams, hallucinations, and unreal visions all things are like the reflection of the moon in water and like a mirrorimage they are born of mental construction.

src: ye tv evaṃ jānanti te vinayadharā ity ucyante / ya evaṃ vinītās te suvinītāḥ /
tgt: Those who know this are called the true upholders of the discipline, and those disciplined in that way are indeed well disciplined.’ ”

src: Vkn  atha tau bhikṣu etad avocatām prajñādharo vinayadharo 'yam upāsakaḥ /
tgt: “Then the two monks said, ‘This householder is extremely well endowed with wisdom.

src: na tv ayaṃ bhadantopālir yo bhagavatā vinayadharāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ /
tgt: The reverend Upāli, who was proclaimed by the Lord as the foremost of the upholders of the discipline, is not his equal.’

src: tāv aham evaṃ vadāmi mā bhikṣū atra gṛhapatisaṃjñām utpādayatām /
tgt: “I then said to the two monks, ‘Do not entertain the notion that he is a mere householder!

src: tathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā nāsti kaścic chrāvako vā bodhisatvo vā, ya etasya pratibhānam ācchindyāt / tādṛśa etasya prajñālokaḥ /
tgt: With the exception of the Tathāgata himself, there is no disciple or bodhisattva capable of competing with his eloquence or rivaling the brilliance of his wisdom.’

src: Vkn  atha tau bhikṣū vinītakaukṛtyāv adhyāśayena tatraivānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpāditavantau,
tgt: “Thereupon, the two monks, delivered from their anxieties and inspired with a high resolve, conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: taṃ ca satpuruṣam abhivandyaivam āhatuḥ
tgt: Bowing down to that good man, they made the wish

src: sarvasatvā īdṛśasya pratibhānasya lābhino bhavantu / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: ‘May all living beings attain eloquence such as this!’ Therefore, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

src: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ rāhulam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ rāhula vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
tgt: The Buddha then said to the venerable Rāhula, “Rāhula, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

src: rāhulo 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: Rāhula replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

src: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye saṃbahulā licchavikumārakā yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mām etad avocan tvaṃ rāhula tasya bhagavataḥ putraś cakravartirājyam utsṛjya pravrajitaḥ,
tgt: Lord, I remember that one day many young Licchavi gentlemen came to the place where I was and said to me, ‘Reverend Rāhula, you are the son of the Lord, and, having renounced a kingdom of a universal monarch, you have left the world.

src: tatra ke te pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsāḥ /
tgt: What are the virtues and benefits you saw in leaving the world?’

src: teṣām ahaṃ yathārūpaṃ pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsā nirdiśāmi, vimalakīrtir licchavir yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām abhivandyaitad avocat Vkn  na bhadantarāhula evaṃ pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsā nirdeṣṭavyā yathā tvaṃ nirdiśasi /
tgt: “As I was teaching them properly the benefits and virtues of renouncing the world, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and, having greeted me, said, ‘Reverend Rāhula, you should not teach the benefits and virtues of renunciation in the way that you do.

src: nirguṇā niranuśaṃsā hi pravrajyā /
tgt: Renunciation is itself the very absence of virtues and benefits.

src: yatra bhadantarāhula saṃskṛtapravṛttis tatra guṇānuśaṃsā / pravrajyā cāsaṃskṛtā, asaṃskṛte ca na guṇā nānuśāṃsā /
tgt: Reverend Rāhula, one may speak of benefits and virtues in regard to compounded things, but renunciation is uncompounded, and there can be no question of benefits and virtues in regard to the uncompounded.

src: pravrajyā bhadantarāhula arūpiṇi rūpavigatā, panthā nirvāṇasya,
tgt: It is free of the extreme views of beginning and end. It is the path of liberation.

src: praśaṃsitā paṇḍitaiḥ, parigṛhītāryaiḥ, parājayaḥ sarvamārāṇām,
tgt: It is praised by the wise, embraced by the noble ones, and causes the defeat of all māras.

src: pañcagatyuttāraṇī, pañcacakṣuviśodhanī, pañcabalapratilambhā, pañcendriyapratiṣṭhā,
tgt: It liberates from the five states of existence, purifies the five eyes, cultivates the five powers, and supports the five spiritual faculties.

src: pareṣām anupaghātaḥ, pāpadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭā,
tgt: Renunciation is totally harmless to others and is not adulterated with evil things.

src: paratīrthyapramardanī, prajñaptisamatikrāntā,
tgt: It disciplines the outsiders, transcending all denominations.

src: paṅke saṃkramaḥ, amamā mamakāravigatā, aparigrahā, anupādānā, anākulā,
tgt: It is the bridge over the swamp of desire, without grasping, and free of the habits of “I” and “mine.” It is without attachment and without disturbance, eliminating all commotion.

src: ākulaprahīṇā, svacittadarśanī paracittasaṃrakṣaṇī, śamathānukūlā,
tgt: It disciplines one’s own mind and protects the minds of others. It favors mental quiescence and stimulates transcendental analysis.

src: sarvato 'navadyā / iyam ucyate pravrajyā /
tgt: It is irreproachable in all respects and so is called renunciation.

src: ya evaṃ pravrajitās te supravrajitāḥ / Vkn  pravrajata yūyaṃ kumārakāḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye /
tgt: Those who leave the mundane in this way are called “truly renunciant.” Young men, renounce the world in the light of this clear teaching!

src: durlabho hi buddhotpādaḥ,
tgt: The appearance of the Buddha is extremely rare.

src: durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpat, durlabho manuṣyapratilambhaḥ /
tgt: Human life endowed with leisure and opportunity is very hard to obtain. To be a human being is very precious.’

src: te kumārakā evam āhuḥ śrutam asmābhir gṛhapate, na tathāgato 'navasṛṣṭaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrājayatīti /
tgt: “The young men complained, ‘But, householder, we have heard the Tathāgata declare that one should not renounce the world without the permission of one’s parents.’

src: sa tān āha utpādayata yūyaṃ kumārakāḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam / pratipattyā ca saṃpādayata,
tgt: “Vimalakīrti answered, ‘Young men, you should cultivate yourselves intensively to conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: saiva yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyati pravrajyā sopasaṃpat /
tgt: That in itself will be your renunciation and high ordination!’

src: Vkn  tatra dvātriṃśatā licchavikumārair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni /
tgt: “Thereupon, thirtytwo of the Licchavi youths conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

src: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvam ānanda vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
tgt: The Buddha then said to the venerable Ānanda, “Ānanda, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

src: ānanda āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: Ānanda replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

src: tatra ca kṣīreṇa kṛtyam āsīt / so 'ham anyatamasmin brāhmaṇamahāśālasya gṛhamūle pātraṃ gṛhītvā sthitaḥ / vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ / sa māṃ vanditvaivam āha Vkn  kiṃ bhadantānanda kālyam eva pātram ādāyāsmin gṛhadvārasamīpe tiṣṭhasi /
tgt: Lord, I remember one day when the body of the Lord manifested some indisposition and he required some milk I took the bowl and went to the door of the mansion of a great brahmin family. The Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there, and, having saluted me, said, ‘Reverend Ānanda, what are you doing on the threshold of this house with your bowl in your hand so early in the morning?’

src: tam enam aham etad avocam bhagavato gṛhapate kāyasya kaścid evābādhaḥ /
tgt: “I replied, ‘The body of the Lord manifests some indisposition, and he needs some milk.

src: tat paryeṣāmi /
tgt: Therefore, I have come to fetch some.’

src: sa mām evam āha alaṃ bhadantānanda mā evaṃ vocaḥ /
tgt: “Vimalakīrti then said to me, ‘Reverend Ānanda, do not say such a thing!

src: vajrasaṃhatano hi bhadantānanda tathāgatakāyaḥ sarvākuśalavāsanāprahīṇaḥ sarvamahaujaskakuśaladharmasamanvāgataḥ /
tgt: Reverend Ānanda, the body of the Tathāgata is tough as a diamond, having eliminated all the instinctual traces of evil and being endowed with all goodness.

src: kutas tasya vyādhiḥ kuta upadravaḥ /
tgt: How could disease or discomfort affect such a body?

src: Vkn  tūṣṇīṃbhūto bhadantānanda gaccha / mā bhagavantam abhyācakṣva /
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, go in silence, and do not belittle the Lord.

src: mā kasyacid bhūya evaṃ vocaḥ /
tgt: Do not say such things to others.

src: mā mahaujaskā devaputrā anyabuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitāś ca bodhisatvāḥ śroṣyanti /
tgt: It would not be good for the powerful gods or for the bodhisattvas coming from the various buddhafields to hear such words.

src: rājñas tāvad bhadantānanda cakravartina itvarakuśalamūlasamanvāgatasya vyādhir na saṃvidyate /
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, a universal monarch, who is endowed only with a small root of virtue, is free of diseases.

src: kutas tasya bhagavato 'pramāṇakuśalasamanvāgatasya vyādhir bhaviṣyati /
tgt: How then could the Lord, who has an infinite root of virtue, have any disease?

src: nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate /
tgt: It is impossible.

src: gaccha gaccha bhadantānanda / mā mām adhyapatrāpaya, mā anyatīrthikacarakaparivrājakanigranthājīvāḥ śroṣyanti,
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, do not bring shame upon us, but go in silence, lest the outsider sectarians should hear your words.

src: mā teṣām evaṃ bhaviṣyati /
tgt: They would say, “For shame!

src: kīdṛśo bata ayam eṣāṃ śāstā yaḥ svayam eva tāvad ātmānaṃ glānaṃ na śaknoti paritrātum,
tgt: The teacher of these people cannot even cure his own sicknesses.

src: tataḥ pracchannaṃ bhadantānanda gaccha śīghram / mā kaścic chṛṇuyāt /
tgt: How then can he cure the sicknesses of others?” Reverend Ānanda, go then discreetly so that no one observes you.

src: Vkn  api tu bhadantānanda dharmakāyās tathāgatā nāmiṣakāyāḥ /
tgt: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, the tathāgatas have the body of the Dharmanot a body that is sustained by material food.

src: lokottarakāyās tathāgatāḥ sarvalokadharmasamatikrāntāḥ /
tgt: The tathāgatas have a transcendental body that has transcended all mundane qualities.

src: anābādhas tathāgatasya kāyaḥ sarvāsravavinivṛtaḥ / asaṃskṛtas tathāgatasya kāyaḥ sarvasaṃkhyāvigataḥ /
tgt: There is no injury to the body of a tathāgata, as it is rid of all defilements. The body of a tathāgata is uncompounded and free of all formative activity.

src: tasya bhadanto vyādhim icchatīty ayuktam asadṛśam /
tgt: Reverend Ānanda, to believe there can be illness in such a body is irrational and unseemly!’

src: Vkn  tasya me bhagavan mahadapatrāpyaṃ jātam / mā me bhagavato 'ntikād duḥśrutaṃ durgṛhītaṃ vā kṛtam iti /
tgt: “When I had heard these words, I wondered if I had previously misheard and misunderstood the Buddha, and I was very much ashamed.

src: so 'ham antarīkṣāc chabdam aśrauṣam /
tgt: Then I heard a voice from the sky

src: evam etad ānanda yathā gṛhapatir nirdiśati /
tgt: ‘Ānanda! The householder speaks to you truly.

src: atha ca punaḥ pañcakaṣāye bhagavān utpannaḥ, tenānarthalūhadaridracaryayā satvā vinetavyāḥ /
tgt: Nevertheless, since the Buddha has appeared during the time of the five corruptions, he disciplines living beings by acting lowly and humble.

src: tad gaccha tvam ānanda kṣīraṃ gṛhītvā, mā paryapatrapaś ceti /
tgt: Therefore, Ānanda, do not be ashamed, and go and get the milk!’

src: Vkn  īdṛśā bhagavan vimalakīrter licchaveḥ praśnavyākaraṇanirdeśāḥ / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: “Lord, such was my conversation with the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, and therefore I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

src: Vkn  evaṃ tāni pañcamātrāṇi śrāvakaśatāny anutsahamānāni bhagavate nivedayanti / ye ca tair vimalakīrtinā licchavinā sārdhaṃ kathāsaṃlāpāḥ kṛtās tān sarvān bhagavate nivedayanti sma /
tgt: In the same way, the rest of the five hundred disciples were reluctant to go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, and each told the Buddha his own adventure, recounting all his conversations with the Licchavi Vimalakīrti.

src: Vkn  tatra bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ maitreya vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
tgt: The Buddha then said to the bodhisattva Maitreya, “Maitreya, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

src: maitreyo 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
tgt: Maitreya replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

src: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye saṃtuṣitena devaputreṇa sārdhaṃ tuṣitakāyikaiś ca devaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayāmi yad idaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānām avivartyāṃ bhūmim ārabhya /
tgt: Lord, I remember that one day I was engaged in a conversation with the gods of the Tuṣita heaven, the god Saṃtuṣita and his retinue, about the stage of nonregression of the great bodhisattvas.

src: tatra ca vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ pradeśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām etad avocata
tgt: At that time, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and addressed me as follows

src: Vkn  tvaṃ maitreya ekajātipratibaddho bhagavatā vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
tgt: “ ‘Maitreya, the Buddha has prophesied that only one more birth stands between you and unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: tat katamayāsi maitreya jātyāu vyākṛtaḥ,
tgt: What kind of birth does this prophecy concern, Maitreya?

src: kim atītayā vānāgatayota pratyutpannayā /
tgt: Is it past? Is it future? Or is it present?

src: tatra yātītā jātiḥ sā kṣīṇā,
tgt: If it is a past birth, it is already finished.

src: yāpy anāgatā sāpy asaṃprāptā, pratyutpannāyāḥ sthitir nāsti jāteḥ /
tgt: If it is a future birth, it will never arrive. If it is a present birth, it does not abide.

src: yathoktaṃ bhagavatā tathā hi tvaṃ bhikṣaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe jāyase jīryasi mriyase cyavase upapadyase ceti /
tgt: For the Buddha has declared, “Bhikṣus, in a single moment, you are born, you age, you die, you transmigrate, and you are reborn.”

src: ajātitaś ca niyāmāvakrāntiḥ / na cājātir vyākriyate / nāpy ajātir abhisaṃbudhyate /
tgt: But birthlessness applies to the stage of destiny for the ultimate, in which there is neither prophecy nor attainment of perfect enlightenment.

src: Vkn  tat kathaṃ tvaṃ maitreya vyākṛtas tathatotpādena tathatānirodhena vā /
tgt: “ ‘Therefore, Maitreya, is your reality from birth? Or is it from cessation?

src: na ca tathatotpadyate na nirudhyate, na nirotsyate / yā ca sarvasatvānāṃ tathatā, yā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ tathatā,
tgt: Your reality as prophesied is not born and does not cease, nor will it be born nor will it cease. Furthermore, your reality is just the same as the reality of all living beings, the reality of all things, and the reality of all the holy ones.

src: evaṃ yadi tvaṃ vyākṛtaḥ sarvasatvā api vyākṛtā bhavanti /
tgt: If your enlightenment can be prophesied in such a way, so can that of all living beings.

src: na hi tathatā dvayaprabhāvitā nānātvaprabhāvitā /
tgt: Because reality does not consist of duality or of diversity.

src: tad yadā maitreyo bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate, sarvasatvā api tasmin samaye tādṛśīm eva bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante /
tgt: Maitreya, whenever you attain buddhahood, which is the perfection of enlightenment, at the same time all living beings will also attain buddhahood.

src: sarvasatvānubodho hi bodhiḥ /
tgt: Enlightenment consists of the realizations of all living beings.

src: yadā ca maitreyaḥ parinirvāsyati, sarvasatvā api tadā parinirvāsyanti /
tgt: Maitreya, at the moment when you attain ultimate liberation, all living beings will also attain ultimate liberation.

src: na hy aparinirvṛtānāṃ sarvasatvānāṃ tathāgatāḥ parinirvānti /
tgt: The tathāgatas do not enter ultimate liberation until all living beings have entered ultimate liberation.

src: parinirvṛtāni te satvāni paśyanti nirvāṇaprakṛtikāni /
tgt: For, since all living beings are utterly liberated, the tathāgatas see them as having the nature of ultimate liberation.

src: tasmād iha maitreya mā etān devaputrān ullāpaya mā visaṃvādaya /
tgt: “ ‘Therefore, Maitreya, do not fool and delude these deities!

src: Vkn  na bodhau kaścit pratiṣṭhate, na nivartate /
tgt: No one abides in, or regresses from, enlightenment.

src: api tu khalu punar maitreya yaiṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ bodhiparikalpanadṛṣṭis tām etām utsarjaya /
tgt: Maitreya, you should introduce these deities to the repudiation of all discriminative constructions concerning enlightenment.

src: na hi bodhiḥ kāyenābhisaṃbudhyate, na cittena /
tgt: “ ‘Enlightenment is perfectly realized neither by the body nor by the mind.

src: vyupaśamo bodhiḥ sarvanimittānām,
tgt: Enlightenment is the eradication of all marks.

src: asamāropo bodhiḥ sarvārambaṇānām, apracāro bodhiḥ sarvamanaskārāṇām,
tgt: Enlightenment is free of presumptions concerning all objects. Enlightenment is free of the functioning of all intentional thoughts.

src: paricchedo bodhiḥ sarvadṛṣṭigatānām, vigamo bodhiḥ sarvaparikalpānām, visaṃyogo bodhiḥ sarveñjitamanyasyanditānām,
tgt: Enlightenment is the annihilation of all convictions. Enlightenment is free from all discriminative constructions. Enlightenment is free from all vacillation, mentation, and agitation.

src: anadhiṣṭhānaṃ bodhiḥ sarvapraṇidhānānām, asaṅgapraveśo bodhiḥ sarvodgrahavigatā,
tgt: Enlightenment is not involved in any commitments. Enlightenment is the arrival at detachment, through freedom from all habitual attitudes.

src: sthitā bodhir dharmadhātusthāne, anugatā bodhis tathatāyām, pratiṣṭhitā bodhir bhūtakoṭyām,
tgt: The ground of enlightenment is the ultimate realm. Enlightenment is realization of reality. Enlightenment abides at the realitylimit.

src: advayā bodhir manodharmavigatā /
tgt: Enlightenment is without duality, since therein are no minds and no things.

src: samā bodhir ākāśasamatayā,
tgt: Enlightenment is equality, since it is equal to infinite space.

src: asaṃskṛtā bodhir utpādabhaṅgasthityanyathātvavigatā,
tgt: “ ‘Enlightenment is unconstructed, because it is neither born nor destroyed, neither abides nor undergoes any transformation.

src: parijñā bodhiḥ sarvasatvacittacaritāśayānām,
tgt: Enlightenment is the complete knowledge of the thoughts, deeds, and inclinations of all living beings.

src: advārā bodhir āyatanānām,
tgt: Enlightenment is not a door for the sensemedia.

src: asaṃsṛṣṭā bodhiḥ sarvavāsanānusaṃdhikleśavigatā,
tgt: Enlightenment is unadulterated, since it is free of the afflictions of the instinctually driven succession of lives.

src: na deśasthā na pradeśasthā bodhiḥ sthānāsthānavigatā,
tgt: Enlightenment is neither somewhere nor nowhere, abiding in no location or dimension.

src: tathatāpratiṣṭhitā bodhiḥ sarvato 'dṛśyā /
tgt: Enlightenment, not being contained in anything, does not stand in reality.

src: nāmadheyamātraṃ bodhis tac ca nāma nirīhakam,
tgt: Enlightenment is merely a name and even that name is motionless.

src: nirātmikā bodhir āyūhaniryūhavigatā, anākulā bodhiḥ prakṛtipariśuddhā,
tgt: Enlightenment, free of abstention and undertaking, is energyless. There is no agitation in enlightenment, as it is utterly pure by nature.

src: prakāśā bodhiḥ svabhāvapariśuddhā,
tgt: Enlightenment is radiance, pure in essence.

src: anudgrahā bodhir adhyālambanavigatā, nirnānātvā bodhiḥ sarvadharmasamatāvabodhatvāt,
tgt: Enlightenment is without subjectivity and completely without object. Enlightenment, which penetrates the equality of all things, is undifferentiated.

src: anupamā bodhir upamopanyāsavigatāḥ,
tgt: Enlightenment, which is not shown by any example, is incomparable.

src: sūkṣmā bodhir duranubodhatvāt,
tgt: Enlightenment is subtle, since it is extremely difficult to realize.

src: sarvatrānugatā bodhir ākāśasvabhāvatvāt /
tgt: Enlightenment is allpervasive, as it has the nature of infinite space.

src: sā na śakyā kāyena vācā cittenābhisaṃboddhum /
tgt: Enlightenment cannot be realized, either physically or mentally.

src: Vkn  iha bhagavan nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne tataḥ pariṣado dvayor devaputraśatayor anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt /
