src: mayaiva nagaraṃ caitadgrastamadya ca me cirāt / tvayā kṛtaḥ sa śāpāntastadgṛhāṇādhunā varam // iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā śrīdattaḥ sādaro 'bhyadhāt / kimanyena vareṇādhya jīvatveṣa sakhā mama //
tgt: Now to-day, after a long time, you have brought my curse to an end in the manner foretold, therefore receive now some boon.” When he heard that speech of hers, Śrīdatta said respectfully: “Mother, grant that my friend may be restored to life.

src: evamastviti sā cāsmai varaṃ dattvā tirodhadhe / akṣatāṅgaḥ sa cottasthau jīvanniṣṭhurakaḥ punaḥ //
tgt: What need have I of any other boon?” “So be it,” she said, and after granting the boon disappeared. And Niṣṭhuraka rose up again alive without a scratch on his body.

src: tenaiva saha ca prātaḥ prahṛṣṭo vismitaśca saḥ / tataḥ pratasthe śrīdattaḥ prāpa cojjayinīṃ kramāt //
tgt: Then Śrīdatta set out the next morning with him delighted and astonished and at last reached Ujjayinī.

src: tatra saṃbhāvayāmāsa sakhīnmārgonmukhānsa tān / darśanena yathāyāto nīlakaṇṭhānivāmbudaḥ // kṛtātithyavidhiścāsau svagṛhaṃ bāhuśālinā / nīto 'bhūtkathitāśeṣanijavṛttāntakautukaḥ //
tgt: There he revived by his appearance the spirits of his friends, who were anxiously expecting him, as the arrival of the cloud revives the peacocks. And after he had told all the wonders of his adventures Bāhuśālin went through the usual formalities of hospitality, taking him to his own home.

src: tatropacaryamāṇaḥ san pitṛbhyāṃ bāhuśālinaḥ / sa uvāsa samaṃ mittraiḥ śrīdattaḥ svagṛhe yathā //
tgt: There Śrīdatta was taken care of by the parents of Bāhuśālin, and lived with his friends as comfortably as if he were in his own house.

src: kadācitso 'tha saṃprāpte madhumāsamahotsave / yātrāmupavane draṣṭuṃ jagāma sakhibhiḥ saha //
tgt: Once on a time, when the great feast of springtide[10] had arrived, he went with his friends to behold some festal rejoicings in a garden.

src: tatra kanyāṃ dadarśaikāṃ rājñaḥ śrībimbakeḥ sutām / āgatāmākṛtimatīṃ sākṣādiva madhuśriyam //
tgt: There he beheld a maiden, the daughter of King Bimbaki, who had come to see the show, looking like the Goddess of the Splendour of Spring present in bodily form.

src: sā mṛgāṅkavatī nāma hṛdayaṃ tasya tatkṣaṇam / viveśa dattamārgeva dṛṣṭyāsya savikāsayā //
tgt: She, by name Mṛgāṅkavatī, that moment penetrated into his heart, as if through the openings left by the expansion of his eye.

src: tasyā api muhuḥ snigdhā prathamapremaśaṃsinī / nyastā taṃ prati dūtīva dṛṣṭiścakre gatāgatam //
tgt: Her passionate look, too, indicative of the beginning of love, fixed on him, went and returned like a confidante.

src: praviṣṭāṃ vṛkṣagahanaṃ tāmapaśyannatha kṣaṇāt / śrīdattaḥ śūnyahṛdayo diśo 'pi na dadarśa saḥ //
tgt: When she entered a thicket of trees, Śrīdatta, not beholding her, suddenly felt his heart so empty that he did not know where he was.

src: jñātaṃ mayā te hṛdayaṃ sakhe māpahnavaṃ kṛthāḥ / tadehi tatra gacchāvo yatra rājasutā gatā // ityuktaśceṅgitajñena suhṛdā bāhuśālinā / tatheti sa yayau tasyāḥ saṃnikarṣaṃ suhṛtsakhaḥ //
tgt: His friend Bāhuśālin, who thoroughly understood the language of gestures, said to him: “My friend, I know your heart, do not deny your passion, therefore come, let us go to that part of the garden where the king’s daughter is.” He consented and went near her, accompanied by his friend.

src: hā kaṣṭamahinā daṣṭā rājaputrīti tatkṣaṇam / ākranda udabhūttatra śrīdattahṛdayajvaraḥ // viṣaghnamaṅgulīyaṃ ca vidyā ca suhṛdo 'sya me / astīti gatvā jagade kañcukī bāhuśālinā // sa ca tatkṣaṇamabhyetya kañcukī caraṇānataḥ / nikaṭaṃ rājaduhituḥ śrīdattamanayaddrutam //
tgt: That moment a cry was heard there which gave great pain to the heart of Śrīdatta: “Alas, the princess has been bitten by a snake!” Bāhuśālin then went and said to the chamberlain: “My friend here possesses a ring that counteracts the effects of poison, and also healing spells.” Immediately the chamberlain came and, bowing at his feet, quickly led Śrīdatta to the princess.

src: so 'pi tasyāstadaṅgulyāṃ nicikṣepāṅgulīyakam / tato jajāpa vidyāṃ ca tena pratyujjijīva sā //
tgt: He placed the ring on her finger and then muttered his spells, so that she revived.

src: atha sarvajane hṛṣṭe śrīdattastutitatpare / tatraiva jñātavṛttānto rājā bimbakirāyayau //
tgt: Then all the attendants were delighted, and loud in praise of Śrīdatta, and the King Bimbaki hearing the circumstances came to the place.

src: tenāsau sakhibhiḥ sārdhamagṛhītāṅgulīyakaḥ / pratyājagāma śrīdatto bhavanaṃ bāhuśālinaḥ //
tgt: Accordingly Śrīdatta returned with his friends to the house of Bāhuśālin without taking back the ring.

src: tatra tasmai suvarṇādi yatprītaḥ prāhiṇonnṛpaḥ / tadbāhuśālinaḥ pitre samagraṃ sa samarpayat //
tgt: And all the gold and other presents which the delighted king sent to him there he handed over to the father of Bāhuśālin.

src: atha tāṃ cintayan kāntāṃ sa tathā paryatapyata / yathā kiṃkāryatāmūḍhā vayasyas tasya jajñire //
tgt: Then, thinking upon that fair one, he was so much afflicted that his friends became utterly bewildered as to what to do with him.

src: tato bhāvanikā nāma rājaputryāḥ priyā sakhī / aṅgulīyārpaṇavyājāttasyāntikamupāyayau // uvāca cainaṃ matsakhyās tasyāḥ subhaga sāṃpratam / tvaṃ vā prāṇaprado bhartā mṛtyurvāpyeṣa niścayaḥ // ityukte bhāvanikayā śrīdattaḥ sa ca sāpi ca / bāhuśālī ca te 'nye ca mantraṃ saṃbhūya cakrire // harāmo nibhṛtaṃ yuktyā rājaputrīmimāṃ vayam / nivāsahetor guptaṃ ca gacchāmo mathurāmitaḥ // iti saṃmantrite samyakkāyasiddhyai ca saṃvidi / anyonyaṃ sthāpitāyāṃ sā yayau bhāvanikā tataḥ //
tgt: Then a dear friend of the princess, Bhāvanikā by name, came to him on pretence of returning the ring, and said to him: “That friend of mine, illustrious sir, has made up her mind that either you must save her life by becoming her husband, or she will be married to her grave.” When Bhāvanikā had said this Śrīdatta and Bāhuśālin and the others quickly put their heads together and came to the following resolution:— “We will carry off this princess secretly by a stratagem, and will go unperceived from here to Mathurā and live there.” The plan having been thoroughly talked over, and the conspirators having agreed with one another what each was to do in order to carry it out, Bhāvanikā then departed.

src: anyedyurbāhuśālī ca vayasyatritayānvitaḥ / vaṇijyāvyapadeśena jagāma mathurāṃ prati //
tgt: And the next day Bāhuśālin, accompanied by three of his friends, went to Mathurā on pretext of trafficking, and as he went he posted in concealment at intervals swift horses for the conveyance of the princess.

src: śrīdatto 'pi tataḥ kācmidduhitrā sahitāṃ striyam / sāyaṃ rājasutāvāse pāyayitvā madhu nyadhāt // tato 'tra dīpoddeśena dattvāgniṃ vāsaveśmani / pracchannaṃ bhāvanikayā ninye rājasutā bahiḥ //
tgt: But Śrīdatta then brought at eventide a woman with her daughter into the palace of the princess, after making them both drink spirits, and then Bhāvanikā, on pretence of lighting up the palace, set fire to it, and secretly conveyed the princess out of it;

src: tatkṣaṇaṃ tāṃ ca saṃprāpya śrīdattaḥ sa bahiḥ sthitaḥ / prākprasthitasya nikaṭaṃ prāhiṇodbāhuśālinaḥ // dadau mitradvayaṃ cāsyāḥ paścādbhāvanikāṃ tathā / tanmandire ca dagdhā sā kṣībā strī sutayā saha //
tgt: and that moment Śrīdatta, who was remaining outside, received her, and sent her on to Bāhuśālin, who had started in the morning, and directed two of his friends to attend on her and also Bhāvanikā. Now that drunken woman and her daughter were burnt in the palace of the princess, and people supposed that the princess had been burnt with her friend.

src: lokastu tāṃ sakhīyuktāṃ mene dagdhāṃ nṛpātmajām / prātaśca pūrvavattatra śrīdatto dadṛśe janaiḥ //
tgt: But Śrīdatta took care to show himself in the morning, as before, in the city;

src: tato rātrau dvitīyasyāṃ sa gṛhītamṛgāṅkakaḥ / śrīdattaḥ prayayau pūrvaprasthitāṃ tāṃ priyāṃ prati //
tgt: then on the second night, taking with him his sword Mṛgāṅka, he started to follow his beloved, who had set out before him.

src: tayā ca rātryātikramya dūramadhvānam utsukaḥ / vindhyāṭavīmatha prāpa sa prātaḥ prahare gate //
tgt: And in his eagerness he accomplished a great distance that night, and when the morning watch[11] had passed he reached the Vindhya forest.

src: tatrādāvanimittāni paścāt pathi dadarśa tān / sarvān prahārābhihatān sahabhāvanikān sakhīn // te ca dṛṣṭvā nijagadustaṃ saṃbhrāntamupāgatam / muṣitāḥ smo nipatyādya bahvaśvārohasenayā //
tgt: There he first beheld unlucky omens, and afterwards he saw all those friends of his, together with Bhāvanikā, lying in the road gashed with wounds. And when he came up all distracted they said to him: “We were robbed to-day by a large troop of horsemen that set upon us.

src: ekena cāśvāroheṇa rājaputrī bhayākulā / asmāsvetadavastheṣu nītāśvamadhiropya sā //
tgt: And after we were reduced to this state one of the horsemen threw the terrified princess on his horse and carried her off.

src: dūraṃ na yāvan nītā ca tāvadgacchānayā diśā / asmākamantike mā sthāḥ sarvathābhyadhikā ca sā // iti taiḥ preṣito mittrairmuhuḥ paśyanvivṛtya saḥ / javena rājatanayāṃ śrīdatto 'nusasāra tām //
tgt: So before she has been carried a great distance, go in this direction; do not remain near us, she is certainly of more importance than we.” Being urged on with these words by his friends, Śrīdatta rapidly followed after the princess, but could not help frequently turning round to look at them.

src: gatvā sudūraṃ lebhe ca tāmaśvārohavāhinīm / yuvānamekaṃ tanmadhye kṣatriyaṃ sa dadarśa ca //
tgt: And after he had gone a considerable distance he caught up that troop of cavalry, and he saw a young man of the warrior caste in the midst of it.

src: tenopari ruraṃgasya gṛhītāṃ taṃ nṛpātmajām / apaśyacca yayau cāsya kṣatrayūno 'ntikaṃ kramāt // sāntvena rājaputrīṃ tāmamuñcantaṃ ca pādataḥ / aśvādākṣipya dṛṣadi śrīdattastamacūrṇayat //
tgt: And he beheld that princess held by him upon his horse. So he slowly approached that young warrior; and when soft words would not induce him to let the princess go, he hurled him from his horse with a blow of his foot and dashed him to pieces on a rock.

src: taṃ hatvā ca tam evāśvam āruhya nijaghāna tān / anyān api bahūn kruddhān aśvārohān pradhāvitān //
tgt: And after he had slain him he mounted on his horse and slew a great number of the other horsemen who charged him in anger.

src: hataśeṣāstataste ca taddṛṣṭvā tasya tādṛśam / vīrasyāmānuṣaṃ vīryaṃ palāyya sabhayaṃ yayuḥ //
tgt: And then those who remained alive, seeing that the might which the hero displayed was more than human, fled away in terror;

src: sa cāpi turagārūḍho rājaputryā tayā saha / mṛgāṅkavatyā śrīdattaḥ prayayau tān sakhīn prati // stokaṃ gatvā ca tasyāśvaḥ saṃgrāme vraṇito bhṛśam / sabhāryasyāvatīrṇasya papāta prāpa pañcatām //
tgt: and Śrīdatta mounted on the horse with the Princess Mṛgāṅkavatī and set out to find those friends of his. And after he had gone a little way he and his wife got off the horse, which had been severely wounded in the fight, and soon after it fell down and died.

src: tatkālaṃ cāsya tatraiva sā mṛgāṅkavatī priyā / trāsāyāsapariśrāntā tṛṣārtā samapadyata //
tgt: And then his beloved Mṛgāṅkavatī, exhausted with fear and exertion, became very thirsty.

src: sthāpayitvā ca tāṃ tatra gatvā dūramitastataḥ / jalamanviṣyataścāsya savitāstamupāyayau //
tgt: And leaving her there, he roamed a long distance hither and thither, and while he was looking for water the sun set.

src: tataḥ sa labdhe 'pi jale mārganāśavaśādbhraman / cakravākavadutkūjaṃstāṃ nināya niśāṃ vane //
tgt: Then he discovered that though he had found water he had lost his way, and he passed that night in the wood roaming about, moaning aloud like a Cakravāka.[12] And in the morning he reached that place, which was easy to recognise by the carcase of the horse.

src: prātaḥ prāpa ca tatsthānaṃ patitāśvopalakṣitam / na ca tatra kacitkāntāṃ rājaputrīṃ dadarśa tām //
tgt: And nowhere there did he behold his beloved princess.

src: tataḥ sa mohād vinyasya bhuvi khaḍgaṃ mṛgāṅkakam / vṛkṣāgramārurohaināmavekṣitumitastataḥ // tatkṣaṇaṃ tena mārgeṇa ko 'pyagācchavarādhipaḥ / sa cāgatyaiva jagrāha vṛkṣamūlānmṛgāṅkakam //
tgt: Then in his distraction he placed his sword Mṛgāṅka on the ground and climbed to the top of a tree, in order to cast his eye in all directions for her. That very moment a certain Śavara chieftain passed that way, and he came up and took the sword from the foot of the tree.

src: taṃ dṛṣṭvāpi sa vṛkṣāgrādavatīryaiva pṛṣṭavān / priyāpravṛttimatyārtaḥ śrīdattaḥ śavarādhipam //
tgt: Beholding that Śavara chieftain, Śrīdatta came down from the top of the tree and in great grief asked him for news of his beloved.

src: itastvaṃ gaccha matpallīṃ jāne sā tatra te gatā / ahaṃ tatraiva caiṣyāmi dāsyāsyasimimaṃ ca te //
tgt: The Śavara chieftain said: “Leave this place and come to my village; I have no doubt she whom you seek has gone there;

src: ityuktvā preṣitastena śabareṇa sa cotsukaḥ / śrīdattastāṃ yayau pallīṃ tadīyaiḥ puruṣaiḥ saha // śramaṃ tāvadvimuñceti tatroktaḥ puruṣaiśca taiḥ / prāpya pallīpatergehaṃ śrānto nidrāṃ kṣaṇādyayau //
tgt: and I shall come there and return you this sword.” When the Śavara chieftain urged him to go with these words, Śrīdatta, being himself all eagerness, went to that village with the chief’s men. And there those men said to him: “Sleep off your fatigue.” And when he reached the house of the chief of the village, being tired, he went to sleep in an instant.

src: prabuddhaśca dadarśa svau pādau nigaḍasaṃyutau / alabdhatadgatī kāntāprāptyupāyodyamāviva //
tgt: And when he woke up he saw his two feet fastened with fetters, like the two efforts he had made in order to obtain his beloved, which failed to reach their object.

src: atha kṣaṇaṃ dattasukhāṃ kṣaṇāntaravimāthinīm / daivasyeva gatiṃ tatra tasthau śocansa tāṃ priyām //
tgt: Then he remained there weeping for his darling, who, like the course of destiny, had for a moment brought him joy, and the next moment blasted his hopes.

src: ekadā tamuvācaitya ceṭī mocanikābhidhā / āgato 'si mahābhāga kutreha bata mṛtyave //
tgt: One day a serving-maid of the name of Mocanikā came to him and said: “Illustrious sir, unwittingly you have come hither to your death.

src: kāryasiddhyai sa hi kāpi prayātaḥ śabarādhipaḥ / āgatya caṇḍikāyāstvāmupahārīkariṣyati // etadarthaṃ hi tena tvamito vindhyāṭavītaṭāt / prāpya yuktyā visṛjyeha nītaḥ saṃprati bandhanam //
tgt: For the Śavara chieftain has gone somewhither to accomplish certain weighty affairs, and when he returns he will offer you to Caṇḍikā.[13] For with that object he decoyed you here by a stratagem from this slope of the wild Vindhya hill, and immediately threw you into the chains in which you now are.

src: bhagavatyupahāratve yata evāsi kalpitaḥ / ata eva sadā vastrairbhojanaiścopacaryase //
tgt: And it is because you are intended to be offered as a victim to the goddess that you are continually served with garments and food.

src: ekastu muktyupāyaste vidyate yadi manyase / astyasya sundarī nāma śabarādhipateḥ sutā // atyarthaṃ sā ca dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ jāyate madanāturā / tāṃ bhajasva vayasyāṃ me tataḥ kṣemamavāpsyasi // tayetyukto vimuktyarthī sa śrīdattastatheti tām / gāndharvavidhinā guptaṃ bhāryāṃ vyadhita sundarīm //
tgt: But I know of only one expedient for delivering you, if you agree to it. This Śavara chieftain has a daughter named Sundarī, and she having seen you is becoming exceedingly lovesick; marry her who is my friend, then you will obtain deliverance.”[14] When she said this to him Śrīdatta consented, desiring to be set at liberty, and secretly made that Sundarī his wife by the gāndharva form of marriage.

src: rātrau rātrau ca sā tasya bandhanāni nyavārayat / acirācca sagarbhā sā sundarī samapadyata //
tgt: And every night she removed his chains, and in a short time Sundarī became pregnant.

src: tatsarvamatha tanmātā buddhvā mocanikāmukhāt / jāmātṛsnehato gatvā svairaṃ śrīdattamabravīt // putra śrīcaṇḍanāmāsau kopanaḥ sundarīpitā / na tvāṃ kṣameta tadgaccha vismartavyā na sundarī //
tgt: Then her mother, having heard the whole story from the mouth of Mocanikā, out of love for her son-in-law Śrīdatta, went and of her own accord said to him: “My son, Śrīcaṇḍa, the father of Sundarī, is a wrathful man, and will show thee no mercy;

src: ityuktvā mocitaḥ śvaśrvā khaḍgaṃ śrīcaṇḍahastagam / sundaryai nijamāvedya śrīdattaḥ prayayau tataḥ //
tgt: but thou must not forget Sundarī.” When his mother-in-law had said this, she set him at liberty, and Śrīdatta departed, after telling Sundarī that the sword which was in her father’s possession really belonged to himself.

src: viveśa cādyāṃ tāmeva cintākrānto nijāṭavīm / mṛgāṅkavatyāḥ padavīṃ tasya jijñāsituṃ punaḥ //
tgt: So he again entered, full of anxiety, that forest in which he had before wandered about, in order again to search for traces of Mṛgāṅkavatī.

src: nimittaṃ ca śubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tamevoddeśamāyayau / yatrāsyāśvo mṛtaḥ so 'tha yatra sā hāritā vadhūḥ // tatra caikaṃ dadarśārāllubdhakaṃ saṃmukhāgatam / dṛṣṭvā ca pṛṣṭavāṃstasyāḥ pravṛttiṃ hariṇīdṛśaḥ //
tgt: And having seen an auspicious omen he came to that same place where that horse of his died before, and whence his wife was carried off. And there he saw near him[15] a hunter coming towards him, and when he saw him he asked him for news of that gazelle-eyed lady.

src: kiṃ śrīdattastvamityukto lubdhakena ca tatra saḥ / sa eva mandabhāgyo 'hamityuvāca viniḥśvasan // tataḥ sa lubdhako 'vādīttarhi vacmi sakhe śṛṇu / dṛṣṭā sā te mayā bhāryā krandantī tvāmitastataḥ // pṛṣṭvā tataśca vṛttāntamāśvāsya ca kṛpākulaḥ / nijāṃ pallīmito 'raṇyāddīnāṃ tāṃ nītavānaham //
tgt: Then the hunter asked him: “Are you Śrīdatta?” and he, sighing, replied: “I am that unfortunate man.” Then that hunter said: “Listen, friend, I have somewhat to tell you. I saw that wife of yours wandering hither and thither lamenting your absence, and having asked her her story, and consoled her, moved with compassion I took her out of this wood to my own village.

src: tatra cālokya taruṇān pulindān sabhayena sā / mathurānikaṭaṃ grāmaṃ nītā nāgasthalaṃ mayā // tatra ca sthāpitā gehe sthavirasya dvijanmanaḥ / viśvadattābhidhānasya nyāsīkṛtya sagauravam //
tgt: But when I saw the young Pulindas[16] there I was afraid, and I took her to a village named Nāgasthala, near Mathurā.[17] And then I placed her in the house of an old Brāhman named Viśvadatta, commending her with all due respect to his care.

src: tataś cāham ihāyāto buddhvā tvannāma tanmukhāt / tām anveṣṭuṃ tato gaccha śīghraṃ nāgasthalaṃ prati // ityukto lubdhakenāśu sa śrīdattastato yayau / taṃ ca nāgasthalaṃ prāpadaparedyurdinātyaye //
tgt: And thence I came here, having learnt your name from her lips. Therefore you had better go quickly to Nāgasthala to search for her.” When the hunter had told him this Śrīdatta quickly set out, and he reached Nāgasthala in the evening of the second day.

src: tacchrutvā viśvadattastaṃ śrīdattaṃ nijagāda saḥ / mathurāyāṃ suhṛnme 'sti brāhmaṇo guṇināṃ priyaḥ // upādhyāyaśca mantrī ca śūrasenasya bhūpateḥ / tasya haste tvadīyā sā gṛhiṇī sthāpitā mayā //
tgt: Then he entered the house of Viśvadatta and when he saw him said: “Give me my wife, who was placed here by the hunter.” Viśvadatta when he heard that answered him: “I have a friend in Mathurā, a Brāhman, dear to all virtuous men, the spiritual preceptor and minister of the King Śūrasena;

src: bhayaṃ hi vijano grāmo na tadrakṣākṣamo bhavet / tatprātastatra gaccha tvamadya viśramyatāmiha //
tgt: in his care I placed your wife; for this village is an out-of-the-way place and would not afford her protection.

src: ityukto viśvadattena sa nītvātraiva tāṃ niśām / prātaḥ pratasthe prāpacca mathurāmapare dine //
tgt: So go to that city to-morrow morning, but to-day rest here.” When Viśvadatta said this, he spent that night there, and the next morning he set off, and reached Mathurā on the second day.

src: dīrghādhvamalinastasminnagare bahireva saḥ / snānaṃ cakre pariśrānto nirmale dīrghikājale //
tgt: Being weary and dusty with the long journey, he bathed outside that city in the pellucid water of a lake.

src: tata evāmbumadhyācca vastraṃ cauraniveśitam / prāptavānañcalagranthibaddhahāramaśaṅkitam // atha tadvastramādāya sa taṃ hāramalakṣayan / priyāṃ didṛkṣuḥ śrīdatto viveśa mathurāṃ purīm //
tgt: And he drew out of the middle of the lake a garment placed there by some robbers, not suspecting any harm. But in one corner of the garment, which was knotted up, a necklace was concealed.[18] Then Śrīdatta took that garment, and in his eagerness to meet his wife did not notice the necklace, and so entered the city of Mathurā.

src: tatra tatpratyabhijñāya vastraṃ hāramavāpya ca / sa caura ityavaṣṭabhya ninye nagararakṣibhiḥ // darśitaśca tathābhūto nagarādhipateśca taiḥ / tenāpyāvedito rājñe rājāpyasyādiśadvadham // tato vadhyabhuvaṃ hantuṃ nīyamānaṃ dadarśa tam / sā mṛgāṅkavatī dūrātpaścātprahataḍiṇḍimam //
tgt: Then the city police recognised the garment, and finding the necklace, arrested Śrīdatta as a thief, and carried him off, and brought him before the chief magistrate exactly as he was found with the garment in his possession; by him he was handed up to the king, and the king ordered him to be put to death.[19] Then as he was being led off to the place of execution, with the drum being beaten behind him,[20] his wife Mṛgāṅkavatī saw him in the distance.

src: so 'yaṃ me nīyate bhartā vadhāyeti sasaṃbhramam / sā gatvā mantrimukhyaṃ tamabravīdyadgṛhe sthitā // nivārya vadhakānso 'tha mantrī vijñapya bhūpatim / śrīdattaṃ mocayitvā taṃ vadhādānāyayadgṛham //
tgt: She went in a state of the utmost distraction and said to the chief minister, in whose house she was residing: “Yonder is my husband being led off to execution.” Then that minister went and ordered the executioners to desist, and by making a representation to the king got Śrīdatta pardoned, and had him brought to his house.

src: kathaṃ so 'yaṃ pitṛvyo me gatvā deśāntaraṃ purā / ihaiva daivādvigatabhayaḥ prāpto 'dya mantritām // iti taṃ mantriṇaṃ so 'tha śrīdattas tadgṛhāgataḥ / pratyabhijñātavān pṛṣṭvā papātāsya ca pādayoḥ // so 'pi taṃ pratyabhijñāya bhrātuḥ putraṃ savismayaḥ / kaṇṭhe jagrāha sarvaṃ ca vṛttāntaṃ paripṛṣṭavān //
tgt: And when Śrīdatta reached his house, and saw that minister, he recognised him and fell at his feet, exclaiming: “What! is this my uncle Vigatabhaya, who long ago went to a foreign country, and do I now by good luck find him established in the position of a minister?” He too recognised, to his astonishment, Śrīdatta as his brother’s son, and embraced him, and questioned him about all his adventures.

src: tatastasmai sa nikhilaṃ śrīdattaḥ svapiturvadhāt / ārabhya nijavṛttāntaṃ pitṛvyāya nyavedayat //
tgt: Then Śrīdatta related to his uncle his whole history, beginning with the execution of his father.

src: so 'pi muktvāśru vijane bhrātuḥ putraṃ tamabhyadhāt / adhṛtiṃ mā kṛthāḥ putra mama siddhā hi yakṣiṇī //
tgt: And he, after weeping, said to his nephew in private: “Do not despond, my son, for I once brought a female Yakṣa into subjection by means of magic;

src: pañca vājisahasrāṇi hemakoṭīśca sapta sā / prādānmahyamaputrāya tattavaivākhilaṃ dhanam //
tgt: and she gave me, though I have no son, five thousand horses and seventy millions of gold pieces;

src: ityuktvā sa pitṛvyastāṃ śrīdattāyārpayatpriyām / śrīdatto 'pyāttavibhavastatra tāṃ pariṇītavān //
tgt: and all that wealth is at your disposal.” After telling him this, his uncle brought him his beloved, and he, having obtained wealth, married her on the spot.

src: tataśca tasthau tatraiva saṃgataḥ kāntayā tayā / mṛgāṅgavatyā sānando rātryeva kumudākaraḥ //
tgt: And then he remained there in joy, united with that beloved Mṛgāṅkavatī as a bed of white lotuses[21] with the night.

src: bāhuśālyādicintā tu tasyābhūtpūrṇasaṃpadaḥ / indoḥ kalaṅkalekheva hṛdi mālinyadāyinī //
tgt: But even when his happiness was at its full, anxiety for Bāhuśālin and his companions clouded his heart, as a spot of darkness does the full moon.

src: ekadā sa pitṛvyastaṃ rahaḥ śrīdattamabhyadhāt / putra rājñaḥ sutāstyasya śūrasenasya kanyakā // mayā cāvantideśe sā neyā dātuṃ tadājñayā / tattenaivāpadeśena hṛtvā tubhyaṃ dadāmi tām //
tgt: Now one day his uncle said secretly to Śrīdatta: “My son, the King Śūrasena has a maiden daughter, and in accordance with his orders I have to take her to the land of Avanti to give her away in marriage; so I will take her away on that very pretext, and marry her to you.

src: tatastadanuge prāpte bale sati ca māmake / yadrājyaṃ te śriyādiṣṭaṃ tatprāpsyasyacirāditi // niścityaitacca tāṃ kanyāṃ gṛhītvā yayatustataḥ / śrīdattastatpitṛvyaśca sasainyau saparigrahau //
tgt: Then, when you have got possession of the force that follows her, with mine already at your disposal, you will soon gain the kingdom that was promised you by the goddess Srī.” Having resolved on this, and having taken that maiden, Śrīdatta and his uncle set out with their army and their attendants.

src: tato vindhyāṭavīm etau prāptamātrāvatarkitau / caurasenātimahatī rurodha śaravarṣiṇī //
tgt: But as soon as they had reached the Vindhya forest, before they were aware of the danger, a large army of brigands set upon them showering arrows.

src: prahāramūrcchitaṃ baddhvā śrīdattaṃ bhagnasainikam / ninyuścaurāḥ svapallīṃ te svīkṛtya sakalaṃ dhanam //
tgt: After routing Śrīdatta’s force and seizing all the wealth, they bound Śrīdatta himself, who had fainted from his wounds, and carried him off to their village.

src: te ca taṃ prāpayāmāsuścaṇḍikāsadma bhīṣaṇam / upahārāya ghaṇṭānāṃ nādairmṛtyurivāhvayat //
tgt: And they took him to the awful temple of Durgā, in order to offer him up in sacrifice, and, as it were, summoned Death with the sound of their gongs.

src: tatrāpaśyacca taṃ patnī sā pallīpatiputrikā / sundarī draṣṭumāyātā devīṃ bālasutānvitā //
tgt: There Sundarī saw him, one of his wives, the daughter of the chief of the village, who had come with her young son to visit the shrine of the goddess.

src: niṣiddhavatyā madhyasthāndasyūnānandapūrṇayā / sa śrīdattastayā sākaṃ tanmandiramathāviśat //
tgt: Full of joy she ordered the brigands who were between her and her husband to stand aside, and then Śrīdatta entered her palace with her.

src: tadaiva pallīrājyaṃ tat prāpa pitrā yad arpitam / prāg evānanyaputreṇa sundaryai gacchatā divam //
tgt: Immediately Śrīdatta obtained the sovereignty of that village, which Sundarī’s father, having no son, bequeathed to her when he went to heaven.

src: taṃ ca caurasamākrāntaṃ sapitṛvyaparicchadam / sakalatraṃ ca lebhe 'sau taṃ khaḍgaṃ ca mṛgāṅkakam //
tgt: So Śrīdatta recovered his wife and his sword Mṛgāṅka, and also his uncle and his followers, who had been overpowered by the robbers.

src: taraiva śūrasenasya sutāṃ tāṃ pariṇīya ca / śrīdatto 'pi mahānrājā nagare samapadyata //
tgt: And while he was in that town he married the daughter of Śūrasena, and became a great king there.

src: prajighāya sa dūtāṃśca tataḥ śvaśurayostayoḥ / bimbakestasya tasyāpi śūrasenasya bhūpateḥ // tamupājagmatustau ca senāsamudayānvitau / taṃ vijñāyaiva saṃbandhaṃ mudā duhitṛvatsalau // te 'pi rūḍhavraṇāḥ svasthāstadviyuktā vayasyakāḥ / bāhuśāliprabhṛtayastadbuddhvā tamupāyayuḥ //
tgt: And from that place he sent ambassadors to his two fathers-in-law, to Bimbaki and King Śūrasena. And they, being very fond of their daughters, gladly recognised him as a connection, and came to him accompanied by the whole of their armies. And his friends Bāhuśālin and the others, who had been separated from him, when they heard what had happened, came to him with their wounds healed and in good health.

src: atha śvaśurasaṃyukto gatvā taṃ pitṛghātinam / cakre vikramaśaktiṃ sa vīraḥ krodhānalāhutim //
tgt: Then the hero marched, united with his fathers-in-law, and made that Vikramaśakti, who had put his father to death, a burnt-offering in the flame of his wrath.

src: tataśca sābdhivalayāṃ śrīdattaḥ prāpya medinīm / nananda virahottīrṇaḥ sa mṛgāṅkavatīsakhaḥ //
tgt: And then Śrīdatta, having gained dominion over the sea-encircled earth, and deliverance from the sorrow’ of separation, joyed in the society of Mṛgāṅkavatī.

src: itthaṃ narapate dīrghaviyogavyasanārṇavam / taranti ca labhante ca kalyāṇaṃ dhīracetasaḥ //
tgt: Even so, my king, do men of firm resolution cross the calamitous sea of separation and obtain prosperity.

src: iti saṃgatakācchrutvā kathāṃ sa dayitotsukaḥ / tāṃ nināya niśāṃ mārge sahasrānīkabhūpatiḥ // tato manorathārūḍhaḥ puraḥ prahitamānasaḥ / prātaḥ sahasrānīko 'sau pratasthe svāṃ priyāṃ prati //
tgt: [M] (Main story line continued) After hearing this tale from Saṃgataka, the King Sahasrānīka, though longing for the sight of his beloved one, managed to get through that night on the journey. Then, engrossed with his desire, sending his thoughts on before, in the morning Sahasrānīka set out to meet his darling.

src: dinaiḥ katipayaistaṃ ca jamadagneravāpa saḥ / mṛgairapi parityaktacāpalaṃ śānamāśramam //
tgt: And in a few' days he reached that peaceful hermitage of Jamadagni, in which even the deer laid aside their wantonness.

src: yat venam utpatha gatam dvija vākya vajra niṣpluṣṭa pauruṣa bhagam niraye patantam trātvā arthitaḥ jagati putra padam ca lebhe dugdhā vasūni vasudhā sakalāni yena
tgt: Mahārāja Vena went astray from the path of righteousness, and the brāhmaṇas chastised him by the thunderbolt curse. By this King Vena was burnt with his good deeds and opulence and was en route to hell. The Lord, by His causeless mercy, descended as his son, by the name of Pṛthu, delivered the condemned King Vena from hell, and exploited the earth by drawing all kinds of crops as produce.

src: nābheḥ asau ṛṣabhaḥ āsa sudevi sūnuḥ yaḥ vai cacāra sama dṛk jaḍa yoga caryām yat pāramahaṁsyam ṛṣayaḥ padam āmananti svasthaḥ praśānta karaṇaḥ parimukta saṅgaḥ
tgt: The Lord appeared as the son of Sudevī, the wife of King Nābhi, and was known as Ṛṣabhadeva. He performed materialistic yoga to equibalance the mind. This stage is also accepted as the highest perfectional situation of liberation, wherein one is situated in one’s self and is completely satisfied.

src: satre mama āsa bhagavān haya śīraṣā atha sākṣāt saḥ yajña puruṣaḥ tapanīya varṇaḥ chandaḥ mayaḥ makha mayaḥ akhila devatā ātmā vācaḥ babhūvuḥ uśatīḥ śvasataḥ asya nastaḥ
tgt: The Lord appeared as the Hayagrīva incarnation in a sacrifice performed by me [Brahmā]. He is the personified sacrifices, and the hue of His body is golden. He is the personified Vedas as well, and the Supersoul of all demigods. When He breathed, all the sweet sounds of the Vedic hymns came out of His nostrils.

src: matsyaḥ yuga anta samaye manunā upalabdhaḥ kṣoṇīmayaḥ nikhila jīva nikāya ketaḥ visraṁsitān uru bhaye salile mukhāt me ādāya tatra vijahāra ha veda mārgān
tgt: At the end of the millennium, the would-be Vaivasvata Manu, of the name Satyavrata, would see that the Lord in the fish incarnation is the shelter of all kinds of living entities, up to those in the earthly planets. Because of my fear of the vast water at the end of the millennium, the Vedas come out of my [Brahmā’s] mouth, and the Lord enjoys those vast waters and protects the Vedas.

src: kṣīra udadhau amara dānava yūtha pānām unmathnatām amṛta labdhaya ādi devaḥ pṛṣṭhena kacchapa vapuḥ vidadhāra gotram nidrākṣaṇaḥ adri parivarta kaṣāṇa kaṇḍūḥ
tgt: The primeval Lord then assumed the tortoise incarnation in order to serve as a resting place [pivot] for the Mandara Mountain, which was acting as a churning rod. The demigods and demons were churning the Ocean of Milk with the Mandara Mountain in order to extract nectar. The mountain moved back and forth, scratching the back of Lord Tortoise, who, while partially sleeping, was experiencing an itching sensation.

src: trai piṣṭapa uru bhaya hā saḥ nṛsiṁha rūpam kṛtvā bhramat bhru kuṭi daṁṣṭra karāla vaktram daitya indram āśu gadayā abhipatantam ārāt ūrau nipātya vidadāra nakhaiḥ sphurantam
tgt: The Personality of Godhead assumed the incarnation of Nṛsiṁhadeva in order to vanquish the great fears of the demigods. He killed the king of the demons [Hiraṇyakaśipu], who challenged the Lord with a club in his hand, by placing the demon on His thighs and piercing him with His nails, rolling His eyebrows in anger and showing His fearful teeth and mouth.

src: antaḥ sarasi uru balena pade gṛhītaḥ grāheṇa yūtha patiḥ ambuja hastaḥ ārtaḥ āha idam ādi puruṣa akhila loka nātha tīrtha śravaḥ śravaṇa maṅgala nāma dheya
tgt: The leader of the elephants, whose leg was attacked in a river by a crocodile of superior strength, was much aggrieved. Taking a lotus flower in his trunk, he addressed the Lord, saying, “O original enjoyer, Lord of the universe! O deliverer, as famous as a place of pilgrimage! All are purified simply by hearing Your holy name, which is worthy to be chanted.”

src: śrutvā hariḥ tam araṇa arthinam aprameyaḥ cakra āyudhaḥ pataga rāja bhuja adhirūḍhaḥ cakreṇa nakra vadanam vinipāṭya tasmāt haste pragṛhya bhagavān kṛpayā ujjahāra
tgt: The Personality of Godhead, after hearing the elephant’s plea, felt that the elephant needed His immediate help, for he was in great distress. Thus at once the Lord appeared there on the wings of the king of birds, Garuḍa, fully equipped with His weapon, the wheel [cakra]. With the wheel He cut to pieces the mouth of the crocodile to save the elephant, and He delivered the elephant by lifting him by his trunk.

src: jyāyān guṇaiḥ avarajaḥ api aditeḥ sutānām lokān vicakrame imān yat atha adhiyajñaḥ kṣmām vāmanena jagṛhe tripada chalena yācñām ṛte pathi caran prabhubhiḥ na cālyaḥ
tgt: The Lord, although transcendental to all material modes, still surpassed all the qualities of the sons of Aditi, known as the Ādityas. The Lord appeared as the youngest son of Aditi. And because He surpassed all the planets of the universe, He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. On the pretense of asking for a measurement of three footsteps of land, He took away all the lands of Bali Mahārāja. He asked simply because without begging, no authority can take one’s rightful possession.

src: na arthaḥ baleḥ ayam urukrama pāda śaucam āpaḥ śikhā dhṛtavataḥ vibudha adhipatyam yaḥ vai pratiśrutam ṛte na cikīrṣat anyat ātmānam aṅga manasā haraye abhimene
tgt: Bali Mahārāja, who put on his head the water washed from the lotus feet of the Lord, did not think of anything besides his promise, in spite of being forbidden by his spiritual master. The king dedicated his own personal body to fulfill the measurement of the Lord’s third step. For such a personality, even the kingdom of heaven, which he conquered by his strength, was of no value.

src: tubhyam ca nārada bhṛśam bhagavān vivṛddha bhāvena sādhu parituṣṭaḥ uvāca yogam jñānam ca bhāgavatam ātma sa tattva dīpam yat vāsudeva śaraṇāḥ viduḥ añjasā eva
tgt: O Nārada, you were taught about the science of God and His transcendental loving service by the Personality of Godhead in His incarnation of Haṁsāvatāra. He was very much pleased with you, due to your intense proportion of devotional service. He also explained unto you, lucidly, the full science of devotional service, which is especially understandable by persons who are souls surrendered unto Lord Vāsudeva, the Personality of Godhead.

src: cakram ca dikṣu avihatam daśasu sva tejaḥ manvantareṣu manu vaṁśa dharaḥ bibharti duṣṭeṣu rājasu damam vyadadhāt sva kīrtim satye tri pṛṣṭhe uśatīm prathayan caritraiḥ
tgt: As the incarnation of Manu, the Lord became the descendant of the Manu dynasty and ruled over the miscreant kingly order, subduing them by His powerful wheel weapon. Undeterred in all circumstances, His rule was characterized by His glorious fame, which spread over the three lokas, and above them to the planetary system of Satyaloka, the topmost in the universe.

src: dhanvantariḥ ca bhagavān svayam eva kīrtiḥ nāmnā nṛṇām puru rujām rujaḥ āśu hanti yajñe ca bhāgam amṛta āyuḥ ava avarundhe āyuṣya vedam anuśāsti avatīrya loke
tgt: The Lord in His incarnation of Dhanvantari very quickly cures the diseases of the ever-diseased living entities simply by His fame personified, and only because of Him do the demigods achieve long lives. Thus the Personality of Godhead becomes ever glorified. He also exacted a share from the sacrifices, and it is he only who inaugurated the medical science or the knowledge of medicine in the universe.

src: kṣatram kṣayāya vidhinā upabhṛtam mahātmā brahma dhruk ujjhita patham naraka ārti lipsu uddhanti asau avanikaṇṭakam ugra vīryaḥ triḥ sapta kṛtvaḥ urudhāra paraśvadhena
tgt: When the ruling administrators, who are known as the kṣatriyas, turned astray from the path of the Absolute Truth, being desirous to suffer in hell, the Lord, in His incarnation as the sage Paraśurāma, uprooted those unwanted kings, who appeared as the thorns of the earth. Thus He thrice seven times uprooted the kṣatriyas with His keenly sharpened chopper.

src: yayā sammohitaḥ jīvaḥ ātmānam tri guṇa ātmakam paraḥ api manute anartham tat kṛtam ca abhipadyate
tgt: Due to this external energy, the living entity, although transcendental to the three modes of material nature, thinks of himself as a material product and thus undergoes the reactions of material miseries.

src: anartha upaśamam sākṣāt bhakti yogam adhokṣaje lokasya ajānataḥ vidvān cakre sātvata saṁhitām
tgt: The material miseries of the living entity, which are superfluous to him, can be directly mitigated by the linking process of devotional service. But the mass of people do not know this, and therefore the learned Vyāsadeva compiled this Vedic literature, which is in relation to the Supreme Truth.

src: yasyām vai śrūyamāṇāyām kṛṣṇe parama pūruṣe bhaktiḥ utpadyate puṁsaḥ śoka moha bhaya apahā
tgt: Simply by giving aural reception to this Vedic literature, the feeling for loving devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, sprouts up at once to extinguish the fire of lamentation, illusion and fearfulness.

src: saḥ saṁhitām bhāgavatīm kṛtvā anukramya ca ātma jam śukam adhyāpayām āsa nivṛtti niratam muniḥ
tgt: The great sage Vyāsadeva, after compiling the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and revising it, taught it to his own son, Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who was already engaged in self-realization.

src: śaunakaḥ uvāca saḥ vai nivṛtti nirataḥ sarvatra upekṣakaḥ muniḥ kasya vā bṛhatīm etām ātma ārāmaḥ samabhyasat
tgt: Śrī Śaunaka asked Sūta Gosvāmī: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī was already on the path of self-realization, and thus he was pleased with his own self. So why did he take the trouble to undergo the study of such a vast literature?

src: sūtaḥ uvāca ātmārāmāḥ ca munayaḥ nirgranthāḥ api urukrame kurvanti ahaitukīm bhaktim ittham bhūta guṇaḥ hariḥ
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī said: All different varieties of ātmārāmas [those who take pleasure in the ātmā, or spirit self], especially those established on the path of self-realization, though freed from all kinds of material bondage, desire to render unalloyed devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead. This means that the Lord possesses transcendental qualities and therefore can attract everyone, including liberated souls.

src: hareḥ guṇa ākṣipta matiḥ bhagavān bādarāyaṇiḥ adhyagāt mahat ākhyānam nityam viṣṇu jana priyaḥ
tgt: Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, son of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, was not only transcendentally powerful. He was also very dear to the devotees of the Lord. Thus he underwent the study of this great narration [Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam].

src: parīkṣitaḥ atha rājarṣeḥ janma karma vilāpanam saṁsthām ca pāṇḍu putrāṇām vakṣye kṛṣṇa kathā udayam
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī thus addressed the ṛṣis headed by Śaunaka: Now I shall begin the transcendental narration of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and topics of the birth, activities and deliverance of King Parīkṣit, the sage amongst kings, as well as topics of the renunciation of the worldly order by the sons of Pāṇḍu.

src: yadā mṛdhe kaurava sṛñjayānām vīreṣu atho vīra gatim gateṣu vṛkodara āviddha gadā abhimarśa bhagna uru daṇḍe dhṛtarāṣṭra putre bhartuḥ priyam drauṇiḥ iti sma paśyan kṛṣṇā sutānām svapatām śirāṁsi upāharat vipriyam eva tasya jugupsitam karma vigarhayanti
tgt: When the respective warriors of both camps, namely the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas, were killed on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra and the dead warriors obtained their deserved destinations, and when the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra fell down lamenting, his spine broken, being beaten by the club of Bhīmasena, the son of Droṇācārya [Aśvatthāmā] beheaded the five sleeping sons of Draupadī and delivered the heads as a prize to his master, foolishly thinking that he would be pleased. Duryodhana, however, disapproved of the heinous act, and he was not pleased in the least.

src: mātā śiśūnām nidhanam sutānām niśamya ghoram paritapyamānā tadā arudat vāṣpa kala ākula akṣī tām sāntvayan āha kirīṭamālī
tgt: Draupadī, the mother of the five children of the Pāṇḍavas, after hearing of the massacre of her sons, began to cry in distress with eyes full of tears. Trying to pacify her in her great loss, Arjuna spoke to her thus:

src: tadā śucaḥ te pramṛjāmi bhadre yat brahma bandhoḥ śiraḥ ātatāyinaḥ gāṇḍīva muktaiḥ viśikhaiḥ upāhare tvā ākramya yat snāsyasi dagdha putrā
tgt: O gentle lady, when I present you with the head of that brāhmaṇa, after beheading him with arrows from my Gāṇḍīva bow, I shall then wipe the tears from your eyes and pacify you. Then, after burning your sons’ bodies, you can take your bath standing on his head.

src: iti priyām valgu vicitra jalpaiḥ saḥ sāntvayitvā acyuta mitra sūtaḥ anvādravat daṁśitaḥ ugra dhanvā kapi dhvajaḥ guru putram rathena
tgt: Arjuna, who is guided by the infallible Lord as friend and driver, thus satisfied the dear lady by such statements. Then he dressed in armor and armed himself with furious weapons, and getting into his chariot, he set out to follow Aśvatthāmā, the son of his martial teacher.

src: tam āpatantam saḥ vilakṣya dūrāt kumāra hā udvigna manāḥ rathena parādravat prāṇa parīpsuḥ urvyām yāvat gamam rudra bhayāt yathā kaḥ
tgt: Aśvatthāmā, the murderer of the princes, seeing from a great distance Arjuna coming at him with great speed, fled in his chariot, panic stricken, just to save his life, as Brahmā fled in fear from Śiva.

src: yadā aśaraṇam ātmānam aikṣata śrānta vājinam astram brahma śiraḥ mene ātma trāṇam dvija ātma jaḥ
tgt: When the son of the brāhmaṇa [Aśvatthāmā] saw that his horses were tired, he considered that there was no alternative for protection outside of his using the ultimate weapon, the brahmāstra [nuclear weapon].

src: atha upaspṛśya salilam sandadhe tat samāhitaḥ ajānan api saṁhāram prāṇa kṛcchre upasthite
tgt: Since his life was in danger, he touched water in sanctity and concentrated upon the chanting of the hymns for throwing nuclear weapons, although he did not know how to withdraw such weapons.

src: tataḥ prāduṣkṛtam tejaḥ pracaṇḍam sarvataḥ diśam prāṇa āpadam abhiprekṣya viṣṇum jiṣṇuḥ uvāca ha
tgt: Thereupon a glaring light spread in all directions. It was so fierce that Arjuna thought his own life in danger, and so he began to address Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

src: arjunaḥ uvāca kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā bāho bhaktānām abhayaṅkara tvam ekaḥ dahyamānānām apavargaḥ asi saṁsṛteḥ
tgt: Arjuna said: O my Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, You are the almighty Personality of Godhead. There is no limit to Your different energies. Therefore only You are competent to instill fearlessness in the hearts of Your devotees. Everyone in the flames of material miseries can find the path of liberation in You only.

src: tvam ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣāt īśvaraḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ māyām vyudasya cit śaktyā kaivalye sthitaḥ ātmani
tgt: You are the original Personality of Godhead who expands Himself all over the creations and is transcendental to material energy. You have cast away the effects of the material energy by dint of Your spiritual potency. You are always situated in eternal bliss and transcendental knowledge.

src: saḥ eva jīva lokasya māyā mohita cetasaḥ vidhatse svena vīryeṇa śreyaḥ dharma ādi lakṣaṇam
tgt: And yet, though You are beyond the purview of the material energy, You execute the four principles of liberation characterized by religion and so on for the ultimate good of the conditioned souls.

src: tathā ayam ca avatāraḥ te bhuvaḥ bhāra jihīrṣayā svānām ca ananya bhāvānām anudhyānāya ca asakṛt
tgt: Thus You descend as an incarnation to remove the burden of the world and to benefit Your friends, especially those who are Your exclusive devotees and are constantly rapt in meditation upon You.

src: kim idam svit kutaḥ vā iti deva deva na vedmi aham sarvataḥ mukham āyāti tejaḥ parama dāruṇam
tgt: O Lord of lords, how is it that this dangerous effulgence is spreading all around? Where does it come from? I do not understand it.

src: śrī bhagavān uvāca vettha idam droṇa putrasya brāhmam astram pradarśitam na eva asau veda saṁhāram prāṇa bādhe upasthite
tgt: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Know from Me that this is the act of the son of Droṇa. He has thrown the hymns of nuclear energy [brahmāstra], and he does not know how to retract the glare. He has helplessly done this, being afraid of imminent death.

src: na hi asya anyatamam kiñcit astram prati avakarśanam jahi astra tejaḥ unnaddham astra jñaḥ hi astra tejasā
tgt: O Arjuna, only another brahmāstra can counteract this weapon. Since you are expert in the military science, subdue this weapon’s glare with the power of your own weapon.

src: sūtaḥ uvāca śrutvā bhagavatā proktam phālgunaḥ para vīra hā spṛṣṭvā āpaḥ tam parikramya brāhmam brāhma astram sandadhe
tgt: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Hearing this from the Personality of Godhead, Arjuna touched water for purification, and after circumambulating Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he cast his brahmāstra weapon to counteract the other one.

src: saṁhatya anyonyam ubhayoḥ tejasī śara saṁvṛte āvṛtya rodasī kham ca vavṛdhāte arka vahni vat
tgt: When the rays of the two brahmāstras combined, a great circle of fire, like the disc of the sun, covered all outer space and the whole firmament of planets.

src: dṛṣṭvā astra tejaḥ tu tayoḥ trīn lokān pradahat mahat dahyamānāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ sāṁvartakam amaṁsata
tgt: All the population of the three worlds was scorched by the combined heat of the weapons. Everyone was reminded of the sāṁvartaka fire which takes place at the time of annihilation.

src: prajā upadravam ālakṣya loka vyatikaram ca tam matam ca vāsudevasya sañjahāra arjunaḥ dvayam
tgt: Thus seeing the disturbance of the general populace and the imminent destruction of the planets, Arjuna at once retracted both brahmāstra weapons, as Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa desired.

src: tataḥ āsādya tarasā dāruṇam gautamī sutam babandha amarṣa tāmra akṣaḥ paśum raśanayā yathā
tgt: Arjuna, his eyes blazing in anger like two red balls of copper, dexterously arrested the son of Gautamī and bound him with ropes like an animal.

src: śibirāya ninīṣantam rajjvā baddhvā ripum balāt prāha arjunam prakupitaḥ bhagavān ambuja īkṣaṇaḥ
tgt: After binding Aśvatthāmā, Arjuna wanted to take him to the military camp. The Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa, looking on with His lotus eyes, spoke to Arjuna in an angry mood.

src: mā enam pārtha arhasi trātum brahma bandhum imam jahi yaḥ asau anāgasaḥ suptān avadhīt niśi bālakān
tgt: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Arjuna, you should not show mercy by releasing this relative of a brāhmaṇa [brahma-bandhu], for he has killed innocent boys in their sleep.

src: mattam pramattam unmattam suptam bālam striyam jaḍam prapannam viratham bhītam na ripum hanti dharma vit
tgt: A person who knows the principles of religion does not kill an enemy who is careless, intoxicated, insane, asleep, afraid or devoid of his chariot. Nor does he kill a boy, a woman, a foolish creature or a surrendered soul.

src: sva prāṇān yaḥ para prāṇaiḥ prapuṣṇāti aghṛṇaḥ khalaḥ tat vadhaḥ tasya hi śreyaḥ yat doṣāt yāti adhaḥ pumān
tgt: A cruel and wretched person who maintains his existence at the cost of others’ lives deserves to be killed for his own well-being, otherwise he will go down by his own actions.

src: pratiśrutam ca bhavatā pāñcālyai śṛṇvataḥ mama āhariṣye śiraḥ tasya yaḥ te mānini putra hā
tgt: Furthermore, I have personally heard you promise Draupadī that you would bring forth the head of the killer of her sons.

src: tat asau vadhyatām pāpaḥ ātatāyī ātma bandhu hā bhartuḥ ca vipriyam vīra kṛtavān kula pāṁsanaḥ
tgt: This man is an assassin and murderer of your own family members. Not only that, but he has also dissatisfied his master. He is but the burnt remnants of his family. Kill him immediately.

src: sūtaḥ uvāca evam parīkṣatā dharmam pārthaḥ kṛṣṇena coditaḥ na aicchat hantum guru sutam yadyapi ātma hanam mahān
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Although Kṛṣṇa, who was examining Arjuna in religion, encouraged Arjuna to kill the son of Droṇācārya, Arjuna, a great soul, did not like the idea of killing him, although Aśvatthāmā was a heinous murderer of Arjuna’s family members.

src: atha upetya sva śibiram govinda priya sārathiḥ nyavedayat tam priyāyai śocantyai ātma jān hatān
tgt: After reaching his own camp, Arjuna, along with his dear friend and charioteer [Śrī Kṛṣṇa], entrusted the murderer unto his dear wife, who was lamenting for her murdered sons.

src: tathā āhṛtam paśu vat pāśa baddham avāk mukham karma jugupsitena nirīkṣya kṛṣṇā apakṛtam guroḥ sutam vāma svabhāvā kṛpayā nanāma ca
tgt: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Draupadī then saw Aśvatthāmā, who was bound with ropes like an animal and silent for having enacted the most inglorious murder. Due to her female nature, and due to her being naturally good and well-behaved, she showed him due respects as a brāhmaṇa.

src: uvāca ca asahantī asya bandhana ānayanam satī mucyatām mucyatām eṣaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ nitarām guruḥ
tgt: She could not tolerate Aśvatthāmā’s being bound by ropes, and being a devoted lady, she said: Release him, release him, for he is a brāhmaṇa, our spiritual master.

src: sa rahasyaḥ dhanuḥ vedaḥ sa visarga upasaṁyamaḥ astra grāmaḥ ca bhavatā śikṣitaḥ yat anugrahāt
tgt: It was by Droṇācārya’s mercy that you learned the military art of throwing arrows and the confidential art of controlling weapons.

src: saḥ eṣaḥ bhagavān droṇaḥ prajā rūpeṇa vartate tasya ātmanaḥ ardham patnī āste na anvagāt vīrasūḥ kṛpī
tgt: He [Droṇācārya] is certainly still existing, being represented by his son. His wife Kṛpī did not undergo a satī with him because she had a son.

src: tat dharma jña mahā bhāga bhavadbhiḥ gauravam kulam vṛjinam na arhati prāptum pūjyam vandyam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
tgt: O most fortunate one who know the principles of religion, it is not good for you to cause grief to glorious family members who are always respectable and worshipful.

src: mā rodīt asya jananī gautamī pati devatā yathā aham mṛta vatsā ārtā rodimi aśru mukhī muhuḥ
tgt: My lord, do not make the wife of Droṇācārya cry like me. I am aggrieved for the death of my sons. She need not cry constantly like me.

src: yaiḥ kopitam brahma kulam rājanyaiḥ ajita ātmabhiḥ tat kulam pradahati āśu sa anubandham śucā arpitam
tgt: If the kingly administrative order, being unrestricted in sense control, offends the brāhmaṇa order and enrages them, then the fire of that rage burns up the whole body of the royal family and brings grief upon them all.

src: sūtaḥ uvāca dharmyam nyāyyam sa karuṇam nirvyalīkam samam mahat rājā dharma sutaḥ rājñyāḥ pratyanandat vacaḥ dvijāḥ
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī said: O brāhmaṇas, King Yudhiṣṭhira fully supported the statements of the Queen, which were in accordance with the principles of religion and were justified, glorious, full of mercy and equity, and without duplicity.

src: nakulaḥ sahadevaḥ ca yuyudhānaḥ dhanañjayaḥ bhagavān devakī putraḥ ye ca anye yāḥ ca yoṣitaḥ
tgt: Nakula and Sahadeva [the younger brothers of the King] and also Sātyaki, Arjuna, the Personality of Godhead Lord Sri Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, and the ladies and others all unanimously agreed with the King.

src: tatra āha amarṣitaḥ bhīmaḥ tasya śreyān vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ na bhartuḥ na ātmanaḥ ca arthe yaḥ ahan suptān śiśūn vṛthā
tgt: Bhīma, however, angrily disagreed with them and recommended killing this culprit, who had murdered sleeping children for no purpose and for neither his nor his master’s interest.

src: niśamya bhīma gaditam draupadyāḥ ca catuḥ bhujaḥ ālokya vadanam sakhyuḥ idam āha hasan iva
tgt: Caturbhuja [the four-armed one], or the Personality of Godhead, after hearing the words of Bhīma, Draupadī and others, saw the face of His dear friend Arjuna, and He began to speak as if smiling.

src: śrī bhagavān uvāca brahma bandhuḥ na hantavyaḥ ātatāyī vadha arhaṇaḥ mayā eva ubhayam āmnātam paripāhi anuśāsanam kuru pratiśrutam satyam yat tat sāntvayatā priyām priyam ca bhīmasenasya pāñcālyāḥ mahyam eva ca
tgt: The Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: A friend of a brāhmaṇa is not to be killed, but if he is an aggressor he must be killed. All these rulings are in the scriptures, and you should act accordingly. You have to fulfill your promise to your wife, and you must also act to the satisfaction of Bhīmasena and Me.

src: sūtaḥ uvāca arjunaḥ sahasā ājñāya hareḥ hārdam atha asinā maṇim jahāra mūrdhanyam dvijasya saha mūrdhajam
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Just then Arjuna could understand the motive of the Lord by His equivocal orders, and thus with his sword he severed both hair and jewel from the head of Aśvatthāmā.

src: vimucya raśanā baddham bāla hatyā hata prabham tejasā maṇinā hīnam śibirāt nirayāpayat
tgt: He [Aśvatthāmā] had already lost his bodily luster due to infanticide, and now, moreover, having lost the jewel from his head, he lost even more strength. Thus he was unbound and driven out of the camp.

src: vapanam draviṇa adānam sthānāt niryāpaṇam tathā eṣaḥ hi brahma bandhūnām vadhaḥ na anyaḥ asti daihikaḥ
tgt: Cutting the hair from his head, depriving him of his wealth and driving him from his residence are the prescribed punishments for the relative of a brāhmaṇa. There is no injunction for killing the body.

src: putra śoka āturāḥ sarve pāṇḍavāḥ saha kṛṣṇayā svānām mṛtānām yat kṛtyam cakruḥ nirharaṇa ādikam
tgt: Thereafter, the sons of Pāṇḍu, and Draupadī, overwhelmed with grief, performed the proper rituals for the dead bodies of their relatives.

src: sūtaḥ uvāca atha te samparetānām svānām udakam icchatām dātum sa kṛṣṇāḥ gaṅgāyām puraskṛtya yayuḥ striyaḥ
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thereafter the Pāṇḍavas, desiring to deliver water to the dead relatives who had desired it, went to the Ganges with Draupadī. The ladies walked in front.

src: te ninīya udakam sarve vilapya ca bhṛśam punaḥ āplutāḥ hari pādābja rajaḥ pūta sarit jale
tgt: Having lamented over them and sufficiently offered Ganges water, they bathed in the Ganges, whose water is sanctified due to being mixed with the dust of the lotus feet of the Lord.

src: tatra āsīnam kuru patim dhṛtarāṣṭram saha anujam gāndhārīm putra śoka artām pṛthām kṛṣṇām ca mādhavaḥ
tgt: There sat the King of the Kurus, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, along with his younger brothers and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī and Draupadī, all overwhelmed with grief. Lord Kṛṣṇa was also there.

src: sāntvayām āsa munibhiḥ hata bandhūn śucārpitān bhūteṣu kālasya gatim darśayan na pratikriyām
tgt: Citing the stringent laws of the Almighty and their reactions upon living beings, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the munis began to pacify those who were shocked and affected.

src: sādhayitvā ajāta śatroḥ svam rājyam kitavaiḥ hṛtam ghātayitvā asataḥ rājñaḥ kaca sparśa kṣata āyuṣaḥ
tgt: The clever Duryodhana and his party cunningly usurped the kingdom of Yudhiṣṭhira, who had no enemy. By the grace of the Lord, the recovery was executed, and the unscrupulous kings who joined with Duryodhana were killed by Him. Others also died, their duration of life having decreased for their rough handling of the hair of Queen Draupadī.

src: yājayitvā aśvamedhaiḥ tam tribhiḥ uttama kalpakaiḥ tat yaśaḥ pāvanam dikṣu śata manyoḥ iva atanot
tgt: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa caused three well-performed aśvamedha-yajñas [horse sacrifices] to be conducted by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira and thus caused his virtuous fame to be glorified in all directions, like that of Indra, who had performed one hundred such sacrifices.

src: āmantrya pāṇḍu putrān ca śaineya uddhava saṁyutaḥ dvaipāyana ādibhiḥ vipraiḥ pūjitaiḥ pratipūjitaḥ
tgt: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa then prepared for His departure. He invited the sons of Pāṇḍu, after having been worshiped by the brāhmaṇas, headed by Śrīla Vyāsadeva. The Lord also reciprocated greetings.

src: gantum kṛtamatiḥ brahman dvārakām ratham āsthitaḥ upalebhe abhidhāvantīm uttarām bhaya vihvalām
tgt: As soon as He seated Himself on the chariot to start for Dvārakā, He saw Uttarā hurrying toward Him in fear.

src: uttarā uvāca pāhi pāhi mahā yogin deva deva jagat pate na anyam tvat abhayam paśye yatra mṛtyuḥ parasparam
tgt: Uttarā said: O Lord of lords, Lord of the universe! You are the greatest of mystics. Please protect me, protect me, for there is no one else who can save me from the clutches of death in this world of duality.

src: abhidravati mām īśa śaraḥ tapta ayasaḥ vibho kāmam dahatu mām nātha mā me garbhaḥ nipātyatām
tgt: O my Lord, You are all-powerful. A fiery iron arrow is coming towards me fast. My Lord, let it burn me personally, if You so desire, but please do not let it burn and abort my embryo. Please do me this favor, my Lord.

src: sūtaḥ uvāca upadhārya vacaḥ tasyāḥ bhagavān bhakta vatsalaḥ apāṇḍavam idam kartum drauṇeḥ astram abudhyata
tgt: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Having patiently heard her words, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is always very affectionate to His devotees, could at once understand that Aśvatthāmā, the son of Droṇācārya, had thrown the brahmāstra to finish the last life in the Pāṇḍava family.

src: tarhi eva atha muni śreṣṭha pāṇḍavāḥ pañca sāyakān ātmanaḥ abhimukhān dīptān ālakṣya astrāṇi upādaduḥ
tgt: O foremost among the great thinkers [munis] [Śaunaka], seeing the glaring brahmāstra proceeding towards them, the Pāṇḍavas took up their five respective weapons.

src: vyasanam vīkṣya tat teṣām ananya viṣaya ātmanām sudarśanena sva astreṇa svānām rakṣām vyadhāt vibhuḥ
tgt: The almighty Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, having observed that a great danger was befalling His unalloyed devotees, who were fully surrendered souls, at once took up His Sudarśana disc to protect them.

src: antaḥsthaḥ sarva bhūtānām ātmā yoga īśvaraḥ hariḥ sva māyayā āvṛṇot garbham vairāṭyāḥ kuru tantave
tgt: The Lord of supreme mysticism, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, resides within everyone’s heart as the Paramātmā. As such, just to protect the progeny of the Kuru dynasty, He covered the embryo of Uttarā by His personal energy.

src: yadyapi astram brahma śiraḥ tu amogham ca apratikriyam vaiṣṇavam tejaḥ āsādya samaśāmyat bhṛgu udvaha
tgt: O Śaunaka, glory of Bhṛgu’s family, although the supreme brahmāstra weapon released by Aśvatthāmā was irresistible and without check or counteraction, it was neutralized and foiled when confronted by the strength of Viṣṇu [Lord Kṛṣṇa].

src: mā maṁsthāḥ hi etat āścaryam sarva āścarya maye acyute yaḥ idam māyayā devyā sṛjati avati hanti ajaḥ
tgt: O brāhmaṇas, do not think this to be especially wonderful in the activities of the mysterious and infallible Personality of Godhead. By His own transcendental energy He creates, maintains and annihilates all material things, although He Himself is unborn.

src: brahma tejaḥ vinirmuktaiḥ ātma jaiḥ saha kṛṣṇayā prayāṇa abhimukham kṛṣṇam idam āha pṛthā satī
tgt: Thus saved from the radiation of the brahmāstra, Kuntī, the chaste devotee of the Lord, and her five sons and Draupadī addressed Lord Kṛṣṇa as He started for home.

src: kuntī uvāca namasye puruṣam tvā ādyam īśvaram prakṛteḥ param alakṣyam sarva bhūtānām antaḥ bahiḥ avasthitam
tgt: Śrīmatī Kuntī said: O Kṛṣṇa, I offer my obeisances unto You because You are the original personality and are unaffected by the qualities of the material world. You are existing both within and without everything, yet You are invisible to all.

src: māyā javanikā ācchannam ajñā adhokṣajam avyayam na lakṣyase mūḍha dṛśā naṭaḥ nāṭya dharaḥ yathā
tgt: Being beyond the range of limited sense perception, You are the eternally irreproachable factor covered by the curtain of deluding energy. You are invisible to the foolish observer, exactly as an actor dressed as a player is not recognized.

src: tathā paramahaṁsānām munīnām amala ātmanām bhakti yoga vidhāna artham katham paśyema hi striyaḥ
tgt: You Yourself descend to propagate the transcendental science of devotional service unto the hearts of the advanced transcendentalists and mental speculators, who are purified by being able to discriminate between matter and spirit. How then can we women know You perfectly?

src: kṛṣṇāya vāsudevāya devakī nandanāya ca nanda gopa kumārāya govindāya namaḥ namaḥ
tgt: Let me therefore offer my respectful obeisances unto the Lord, who has become the son of Vasudeva, the pleasure of Devakī, the boy of Nanda and the other cowherd men of Vṛndāvana, and the enlivener of the cows and the senses.

src: namaḥ paṅkaja nābhāya namaḥ paṅkaja māline namaḥ paṅkaja netrāya namaḥ te paṅkaja aṅghraye
tgt: My respectful obeisances are unto You, O Lord, whose abdomen is marked with a depression like a lotus flower, who are always decorated with garlands of lotus flowers, whose glance is as cool as the lotus and whose feet are engraved with lotuses.

src: yathā hṛṣīkeśa khalena devakī kaṁsena ruddhā ati ciram śuca arpitā vimocitā aham ca saha ātma jā vibho tvayā eva nāthena muhuḥ vipat gaṇāt
tgt: O Hṛṣīkeśa, master of the senses and Lord of lords, You have released Your mother, Devakī, who was long imprisoned and distressed by the envious King Kaṁsa, and me and my children from a series of constant dangers.

src: viṣāt mahā agneḥ puruṣa ada darśanāt asat sabhāyāḥ vana vāsa kṛcchrataḥ mṛdhe mṛdhe aneka mahā ratha astrataḥ drauṇi astrataḥ ca āsma hare abhirakṣitāḥ
tgt: My dear Kṛṣṇa, Your Lordship has protected us from a poisoned cake, from a great fire, from cannibals, from the vicious assembly, from sufferings during our exile in the forest and from the battle where great generals fought. And now You have saved us from the weapon of Aśvatthāmā.

src: vipadaḥ santu tāḥ śaśvat tatra tatra jagat guro bhavataḥ darśanam yat syāt apunaḥ bhava darśanam
tgt: I wish that all those calamities would happen again and again so that we could see You again and again, for seeing You means that we will no longer see repeated births and deaths.

src: janma aiśvarya śruta śrībhiḥ edhamāna madaḥ pumān na eva arhati abhidhātum vai tvām akiñcana gocaram
tgt: My Lord, Your Lordship can easily be approached, but only by those who are materially exhausted. One who is on the path of [material] progress, trying to improve himself with respectable parentage, great opulence, high education and bodily beauty, cannot approach You with sincere feeling.

src: namaḥ akiñcana vittāya nivṛtta guṇa vṛttaye ātma ārāmāya śāntāya kaivalya pataye namaḥ
tgt: My obeisances are unto You, who are the property of the materially impoverished. You have nothing to do with the actions and reactions of the material modes of nature. You are self-satisfied, and therefore You are the most gentle and are master of the monists.

src: manye tvām kālam īśānam anādi nidhanam vibhum samam carantam sarvatra bhūtānām yat mithaḥ kaliḥ
tgt: My Lord, I consider Your Lordship to be eternal time, the supreme controller, without beginning and end, the all-pervasive one. In distributing Your mercy, You are equal to everyone. The dissensions between living beings are due to social intercourse.

src: na veda kaścit bhagavan cikīrṣitam tava īhamānasya nṛṇām viḍambanam na yasya kaścit dayitaḥ asti karhicit dveṣyaḥ ca yasmin viṣamā matiḥ nṛṇām
tgt: O Lord, no one can understand Your transcendental pastimes, which appear to be human and so are misleading. You have no specific object of favor, nor do You have any object of envy. People only imagine that You are partial.

src: janma karma ca viśva ātman ajasya akartuḥ ātmanaḥ tiryak nṛ ṛṣiṣu yādaḥsu tat atyanta viḍambanam
tgt: Of course it is bewildering, O soul of the universe, that You work, though You are inactive, and that You take birth, though You are the vital force and the unborn. You Yourself descend amongst animals, men, sages and aquatics. Verily, this is bewildering.

src: gopī ādade tvayi kṛtāgasi dāma tāvat yā te daśā aśru kalila añjana sambhrama akṣam vaktram ninīya bhaya bhāvanayā sthitasya sā mām vimohayati bhīḥ api yat bibheti
tgt: My dear Kṛṣṇa, Yaśodā took up a rope to bind You when You committed an offense, and Your perturbed eyes overflooded with tears, which washed the mascara from Your eyes. And You were afraid, though fear personified is afraid of You. This sight is bewildering to me.

src: kecit āhuḥ ajam jātam puṇya ślokasya kīrtaye yadoḥ priyasya anvavāye malayasya iva candanam
tgt: Some say that the Unborn is born for the glorification of pious kings, and others say that He is born to please King Yadu, one of Your dearest devotees. You appear in his family as sandalwood appears in the Malaya hills.

src: apare vasudevasya devakyām yācitaḥ abhyagāt ajaḥ tvam asya kṣemāya vadhāya ca sura dviṣām
tgt: Others say that since both Vasudeva and Devakī prayed for You, You have taken Your birth as their son. Undoubtedly You are unborn, yet You take Your birth for their welfare and to kill those who are envious of the demigods.

src: bhāra avatāraṇāya anye bhuvaḥ nāvaḥ iva udadhau sīdantyāḥ bhūri bhāreṇa jātaḥ hi ātma bhuvā arthitaḥ
tgt: Others say that the world, being overburdened like a boat at sea, is much aggrieved, and that Brahmā, who is Your son, prayed for You, and so You have appeared to diminish the trouble.

src: bhave asmin kliśyamānānām avidyā kāma karmabhiḥ śravaṇa smaraṇa arhāṇi kariṣyan iti kecana
tgt: And yet others say that You appeared for the sake of rejuvenating the devotional service of hearing, remembering, worshiping and so on in order that the conditioned souls suffering from material pangs might take advantage and gain liberation.

src: śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti abhīkṣṇaśaḥ smaranti nandanti tava īhitam janāḥ te eva paśyanti acireṇa tāvakam bhava pravāha uparamam pada ambujam
tgt: O Kṛṣṇa, those who continuously hear, chant and repeat Your transcendental activities, or take pleasure in others’ doing so, certainly see Your lotus feet, which alone can stop the repetition of birth and death.

src: api adya naḥ tvam sva kṛta īhita prabho jihāsasi svit suhṛdaḥ anujīvinaḥ yeṣām na ca anyat bhavataḥ pada ambujāt parāyaṇam rājasu yojita aṁhasām
tgt: O my Lord, You have executed all duties Yourself. Are you leaving us today, though we are completely dependent on Your mercy and have no one else to protect us, now when all kings are at enmity with us?

src: ke vayam nāma rūpābhyām yadubhiḥ saha pāṇḍavāḥ bhavataḥ adarśanam yarhi hṛṣīkāṇām iva īśituḥ
tgt: As the name and fame of a particular body is finished with the disappearance of the living spirit, similarly if You do not look upon us, all our fame and activities, along with the Pāṇḍavas and Yadus, will end at once.

src: viśvāmitre gate rājā vaidehaṃ mithilādhipam| āpṛṣdaiva jagāmāśu rājā daśarathaḥ purīm||
tgt: When Viśvāmitra had gone away, king Dasaratha, greeting Mithila's lord, Vaideha, actively prepared for setting out for his own capital.

src: atha rājā videhānāṃ dadau kanyādhanaṃ bahu| gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvaraḥ|| kambalānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ kṣaumān koṭyambarāṇi ca| hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ divyarūpaṃ svalaṃkṛtam|| dadau kanyāśataṃ tāsāṃ dāsīdāsamanuttamam| hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya muktānāṃ vidrumasya ca ||
tgt: Then the king of the Videhas gave a dower consisting of various things. And Mithilā's lord gave many hundred thousands of kine, and excellent woollen stuffs, and Koțis of common cloths; and elephants, and horses, and cars, and footmen, as well as an hundred damsels adorned, endowed with elegance to form goodly waitingmaids. And well-pleased the king gave as a noble dower gold and silver and pearls and coral.

src: dadau rājā susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ kanyādhanamanuttamam| dattvā bahuvidhaṃ rājā samanujñāpya pārthivam|| praviveśa svanilayaṃ mithilāṃ mithileśvaraḥ| rājāpyayodhyādhipatiḥ saha putrairmahātmabhiḥ|| ṛṣīn sarvān puraskṛtya jagāma sabalānugaḥ|
tgt: Having given divers kinds of articles, that king, the lord of Mithila, bidding adieu to the monarch (Dasaratha), re-entered his own capital. And the master of Ayodhyā accompanied with his high-souled sons, and headed by the saints in a body, started on the journey, followed by his own army.

src: gacchantaṃ tu naravyāghra sarṣisaṅgha sarāghavam|| ghorāstu pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti samantataḥ| bhaumāścaiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam||
tgt: As that tiger-like one was on his way, in company with Rāghava and the saints, the fowls began to utter frightful cries all around, and the beasts on earth to stream in a Southern direction.

src: tān dṛṣṭvā rājaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhaṃ paryapṛcchata| asaumyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāścāpi pradakṣiṇāḥ|| kimidaṃ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati|
tgt: Beholding them, that tiger-like monarch asked Vasistha, saying, Those birds of fierce aspects emit frightful cries and beasts stream in a Southerly direction. What is this? My heart tremble and my mind is not at ease.

src: rājño daśarathasyaitacchrutvā vākyaṃ mahānṛṣiḥ|| uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇī śrūyatāmasya yat phalam| upasthitaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ divyaṃ pakṣimukhāccyutam|| mṛgāḥ praśamayantyete saṃtāpastyajyatāmayam|
tgt: Hearing the speech of king Dasaratha, that mighty saint spoke sweetly, saying, 'These fowls of the air by their cries presage some dreadful impending evil; but these beasts betoken peace restored. Therefore do you renounce anxiety'

src: teṣāṃ: saṃvadatāṃ tatra vāyuḥ prādurbabhūva ha|| kampayan medinī sarvāṃ pātayaṃśca mahādumān| tamasā saṃvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarve nāvediṣurdiśaḥ|| bhasmanā cāvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ sammūḍhamiva tadbalam|
tgt: As they were thus conversing, there blew a strong wind; and all the earth began to speak; and the trees to topple down. And a deep gloom enveloped the sun; and no quarter could be discovered. And enveloped in ashes, that host became stupefied.

src: vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaścānye rājā ca sasutastadā|| sasaṃjñā iva tatrāsan sarvamanyadvicetanam| tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camūḥ||
tgt: At that dreadful hour, Vasiştha and the other saints and the king alone retained their senses, all else were deprived of their senses, and the army was enveloped with ashes.

src: dadarśa bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyeyaṃ rājā rājavimardanam|| kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva duḥsaham| jvalantamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanaiḥ|| skandhe cāsajjya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam| pragṛhya śaramugraṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam ||
tgt: The king saw that repressor of kings, the descendant of Bhrgu, Jamadagni's son, dreadful to behold, wearing a head of matted locks, like to the Kailāsa, had to baffle, resembling the fire at the universal dissolution, difficult to bear, flaming in energy, incapable of being looked at by the unrighteous, with his axe on his shoulder, equipped with a bow like to the lighting, and fierce arrows, looking like Śiva the slayer of Tripura.

src: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| vasiṣṭhapramukhā viprā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ|| saṃgatā munayaḥ sarve saṃjajalpuratho mithaḥ|
tgt: Beholding him of dreadful appearance like to flaming fire, the Vipras headed by Viśvāmitra, engaged in reciting mantras and and offering oblations to the fire, those saints assembled together, began to converse with each other.

src: kaccit pitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṃ notsādayiṣyati|| pūrvaṃ kṣatravadhaṃ kṛtvā gatamanyurgatajvaraḥ| kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalvasya cikīrṣitam||
tgt: Is this one, enraged because of the slaughter of this sire, intent upon exterminating the Kș atriyas? Formerly, having slaughtered the Kșatriyas, he pacified his ire and mental ferment, 'therefore, the annihilate the Ksatriya once again can never be his endeavour.

src: evamuktvāya̭mādāya bhārgavaṃ bhīmadarśanam| ṛṣayo rāmarāmeti madhuraṃ vākyamabruvan||
tgt: Having said this, the saints offered Arghya to Bhrgu's son of dreadful appearance; and addressed him in soothing words, saying, 'Q Rāma! O Rāma.

src: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāmṛṣidattāṃ pratāpavān| rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyo'bhyabhāṣata||
tgt: Accepting that homage rendered to him by the saints, that puissant one, Jamadagni's son, Rāma, addressed Rāma, the son of Dasaratha.

src: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastataḥ| jagāma bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ śatrughnamanudarśayan||
tgt: Having quartered his forces, Bharata eager (to go to Rāma's place), went to see his brother, showing to Satrughna the signs of Rāma's abode being in the vicinity.

src: ṛṣi vasiṣṭhaṃ saṃdiśya mātṛmeṃ śīghramānaya| iti tvaritamagre sa jagāma guruvatsalaḥ||
tgt: And having desired Vasistha, saying, “Bring my mothers without delay," that one attached to his superiors went before.

src: sumantrastvapi śatrughnamadūrādanvapadyata| rāmadarśanajastoṃ bharatasyeva tasya ca||
tgt: And eager to see Rāma even like Bharata himself, Sumantra followed Bharata at a short distance.

src: gacchannevātha bharatastāpasālayasaṃsthitām| bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭī śrīmānuṭajaṃ ca dadarśa ha||
tgt: As Bharata passed on, he observed a neat cottage of leaves stationed among the asylums of anchorets, furnished with a portion having a wall with a door.

src: śālāyāstvagratastasyā dadarśa bharatastadā| kāṣṭhāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇyapacitāni ca|| sa lakṣmaṇasya rāmasya dadarśāśramamīyuṣaḥ| kṛtaṃ vṛkṣeṣvabhijñānaṃ kuśacīraiḥ kvacit kvacit||
tgt: Before the cottage, Bharata saw fuel broken up, and flowers gathered. And he saw at places signs of Kuśa and bark set up on trees when Rāma and Lakşmaņa (first) arrived at their asylum.

src: dadarśa bhavane tasmin mahataḥ saṃcayān kṛtān| mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca karīṣaiḥ śītakāraṇāt||7
tgt: And in that habitation, Bharata saw great heaps of dry dung of deer and buffaloes, gathered for preventing cold.

src: gacchanneva mahābāhuryutimān bharatastadā| śatrughnaṃ cābravīddhṛṣṭastānamātyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ||
tgt: As he proceeded, the intelligent and mightyarmed Bharata with a cheerful heart remarked to Śatrughna and all the courtiers.

src: manye prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yamabravīt| nātidūre hi manye'haṃ nadī mandākinīmitaḥ||
tgt: I conceive, we have reached the tract that was mentioned by Bharadvāja. Hard by this spot, I fancy, is the river Mandākini.

src: uccairbaddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhavedayam| abhijñānakṛtaḥ panthā vikāle gantumicchatā||
tgt: On high are barks set up by Lakşmaņa. Having to pass by the way at unusual hours, (Laksmana) has marked it with signs.

src: itaścodāttadantānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām| śailapārśve parikrāntamanyonyamabhigarjatām||
tgt: On the side of the hill is the way by which long-tusked elephants pass to and fro with vehemence, roaring at each other.

src: yamevādhātumicchanti tāpasāḥ satataṃ vane| tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūmaḥ saṃkulaḥ kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ||
tgt: Here is seen the dense and dark smoke of that which the anchorets are ever anxious to preserve in the forest, fire.

src: atrāhaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ gurusatkārakāriṇam| ārya drakṣyāmi saṃhṛṣṭaṃ maharṣimiva rāghavam||
tgt: Even here shall I with a delighted heart see that foremost of men, the noble Rāghava resembling a Maharși, ever engaged in serving his superiors.

src: atha gatvā muhūrta tu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghavaḥ| mandākinīmanu prāptastaṃ janaṃ cedamabravīt||
tgt: Then going to Citrakuta, that descendant of Raghu, coming to the Mandakini, said to the men.

src: jagatyāṃ puruṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rataḥ| janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam||
tgt: That foremost of men in all the world, the lord of all, coming into seclusion, is in his yoga posture. O fie upon my birth and my life!

src: matkṛte vyasanaṃ prāpto lokanātho mahādyutiḥ| sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ||
tgt: For me, having come by misfortune, and renounced every comfort, the effulgent lord of men, Rāghava, is dwelling in the woods.

src: iti lokasamānuṣṭaḥ pādeṣvadya prasādayan| rāmaṃ tasya patiṣyāmi sītāyā lakṣmaṇasya ca ||
tgt: I shall be taxed of men on the score. To-day (first) pacifying him, I will fall at the feet of Rāma as well as of Sitã and Lakşmaņa.

src: evaṃ sa vilapaṃstasmin vane daśarathātmajaḥ| dadarśa mahatīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām||
tgt: Having thus bewailed, Dasaratha's son saw a splendid, charming, and holy dwelling in that forest, composed of leaves.

src: sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām| viśālāṃ mṛdubhistīrṇāṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare|| śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukai rasādhanaiḥ| rukmapṛṣṭhairmahāsāraiḥ śobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ|| arkaraśmipratīkāśaioraistūṇagataiḥ śaraiḥ| śobhitāṃ dīptavadanaiḥ sarbhogavatīmiva|| mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṃ ca virājitām| rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām|| godhāṅgaliaurāsaktaiścitrakāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| arisaṃdhairanādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgaiḥ siṃhaguhāmiva || prāgudakapravaṇāṃ vediṃ viśālāṃ dīptapāvakām| dadarśa bharatastatra puṇyāṃ rāmaniveśane||
tgt: And Bharata beheld in Rāma's habitation a sacred structure made of leaves, covered with a profusion of Sāla, palm, and Aśvakarņa leaves; spread with soft Kuśa, like a dais in a sacrifice; adorned with bows resembling the iris, plaited on the back with gold, of mighty force, and capable of achieving arduous feets and destroying foes; and garnished with arrows in quivers, seeming like the rays of the sun, with flaming mouths, like to the Bhogavatī with serpents; and exceedingly beautified with golden sheaths and scimitars and shields spangled with gold and nice guana finger-fences decked with gold; inaccessible to foes like a lion's den to deer; and furnished with a spacious dais inclined on the north-east, with a fire flaming on it.

src: nirīkṣya sa muhūrtaṃ tu dadarśa bharato gurum| uṭaje rāmamāsīnaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam|| kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ taṃ tu cīravalkalavāsasam| dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhitaḥ pāvakopamam|| siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam| pṛthivyāḥ sāgarāntāyā bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam|| upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam| sthaṇḍile darbhasaṃstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca||
tgt: And looking around, anon Bharata saw his superior Rāma seated in the cottage bearing a head of matted locks, clad in a black deer-skin, and having tattered cloth and bark for his garment. And he saw Råma seated like to a flame, with leonine shoulders, mighty arms, and eyes resembling lotuses, the righteous lord of this world bounded by the seas, saw the mightyarmed on like to the eternal Brahma, seated on a skin-seat on the ground along with Sītā and Lakş mana.

src: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmānśokamohapariplutaḥ| abhyadhāvata dharmātmā bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ||
tgt: And seeing him, overwhelmed with grief and affliction, the righteous and graceful son of Kaikeyi, Bharata, rushed (towards him).

src: dṛṣṭvaiva vilalāpā” bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā| aśaknuvan vārayituṃ dhairyād vacanamabruvan ||
tgt: And soon as Bharata saw Rāma, he, exceedingly distressed, broke out into lamentations in words choked with sorrow. And incapable of holding himself in patience, he said.

src: yaḥ saṃsadi prakṛtibhirbhaved yukta upāsitum| vanyairmṛgairupāsīnaḥ so'yamāste mamāgrajaḥ||
tgt: That elder brother of mine, who (seated) in court should be surrounded by the subjects intent upon paying him homage, is now surrounded by wild deer.

src: vāsobhirbahusāhauryo mahātmā purocitaḥ| mṛgājine so'yamiha pravaste dharmamācaran||
tgt: He that used to adorn his person with attire worth many thousands (of things), engaged in observing morality, is clad in deer-skin.

src: adhārayad yo vividhāścitrāḥ sumanasaḥ sadā| so'yaṃ jaṭābhāramimaṃ sahate rāghapaḥ katham||
