tgt: Why does he that always wore variegated blossoms, Rāghava, bears this burthen of matted locks?

src: yasya yajñairyathādiṣṭairyukto dharmasya saṃcayaḥ| śarīrakleśasambhūtaṃ sa dharma parimārgate||
tgt: He who is worthy of acquiring religious merit by celebrating sacrifices according to the ordinance, is now following morality by afflicting his person.

src: candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgamupasevitam| malena tasyāṅgamidaṃ kathamāryasya sevyate||
tgt: How is the person of that one whose body used to be daubed with costly sandal, covered with dust.

src: manimittamidaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ| dhigjīvitaṃ nṛśaṃsasya mama lokavigarhitam||
tgt: It is for me that Rama, although deserving of comfort, has come by this misfortune. Wicked that I am, fie upon my life despised of men!

src: ityevaṃ vilapana dīnaḥ prasvinamukhapaṅkajaḥ| pādāvaprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan||
tgt: Thus lamenting in woeful guise, with the lotus of his countenance covered with sweat, Bharata coming at Rāma's feet, fell at them bewailing.

src: duḥkhābhitapto bharato rājaputro mahābalaḥ| uktvā''ryeti sakṛddīnaṃ punarnovāca kiṃcana||
tgt: And inflamed with grief, the exceedingly powerful prince Bharata, having in distress of spirit uttered, O noble one, again said nothing.

src: bāṣpaiḥ pihitakaṇṭhaśca prekṣya rāmaṃ yaśasvinam| āryetyevābhisaṃkruśya vyāhatu nāśakat tataḥ||
tgt: And beholding the illustrious Rāma, Bharata with his utterance choked with emotion, exclaimed, O noble one, and was unable to say anything further.

src: śatrughnaścāpi rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan| tāvubhau ca samāliṅgaya rāmo'pyaśrūṇyavartayat|| tataḥ sumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatū rājasutāvaraṇye| divākaraścaiva niśākaraśca yathāmbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām||
tgt: Then Śatrughna also weeping paid homage unto the feet of Rāma. And shedding tears, Rāma embraced them both. Then as in the sky, the Sun and the Moon meet with śukra and Brhaspati, those two princes (Rāma and Laks mana) met with Sumantra and Guha in the forest.

src: tān pārthivān vāraṇayūthapārhān samāgatāṃstatra mahatyaraṇye| vanaukasaste'bhisamīkṣya sarve tvaśrūṇyamuñcan pravihāya harṣam||
tgt: And beholding those kings resembling leaders of elephant-herds met together in that mighty forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears. forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears.

src: sa jitvā dhanadaṃ rāma bhrātaraṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ| mahāsenaprasūtiṃ tadyayau śaravaṇaṃ mahat||
tgt: O Rāma, having, vanquished his brother, the lord of riches, the king of Räkşasas went to the great wood of reeds, where Mahasena was born.

src: athāpaśyaddaśagrīvo raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat| gabhastijālasaṃvītaṃ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram|| sa parvataṃ samāruhya kaṃcidramyavanāntaram| prekṣate puṣpakaṃ tatra rāmaviṣṭambhitaṃ tadā||
tgt: The Ten-necked Rāvana saw the great golden wood of reeds. Furnished with networks of solar rays, and appearing like a second Sun, and ascending the mountain, he was surveying the heart of the forest, when, O Rama, Puspaka was (suddenly) deprived of its motion.

src: viṣṭabdhaṃ kimidaṃ kasmānāgamatkāmagaṃ kṛtam| acintayadrākṣasendraḥ sacivaistaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ|| kinimittamicchayā me nedaṃ gacchati puṣpakam| parvatasyopariṣṭhasya karmedaṃ kasyacidbhavet|| tato'bravīttadā rāma mārīco buddhikovidaḥ| nedaṃ niṣkāraṇaṃ rājanpuṣpakaṃ yanna gacchati|| atha vā puṣpakamidaṃ dhanadānānyavāhanam| ato nispandamabhavaddhanādhyakṣavinākṛtam||
tgt: The lord of Räkşasas, could not comprehend how the car which had been so made as to course in accordance with the wish of the rider, could have its course impeded; and thereat he in company with his. councillors thought, 'Wherefore does not his Puşpaka course at my desire over this mountain? Whose act is this?' Thereat Mārīca foremost of intelligent ones said, 'That Puspaka does not course cannot, sire, be without cause; or it may be that in consequence of Puşpaka not having borne any other than the bestower of riches, it has ceased its course not having the lord of wealth for its rider.'

src: iti vākyāntare tasya karālaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ| vāmano vikaṭo muṇḍī nandī hasvabhujo balī|| tataḥ pārśvamupāgabhya bhavasyānucaro'bravīt| nandīśvaro vacaścedaṃ rākṣasendramaśaṅkitaḥ||
tgt: As they were speaking thus, that attendant of Bhava, Nandi, terrific, of yellow black hue, dwarfish, frightful, with his head shaven, having short arms, and stout, coming up to them, said (this). And the lordly Nandi, undaunted, addressed the sovereign of the Raksasas, saying.

src: nivartasva daśagrīva śaile krīḍati śaṃkaraḥ| suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṃ devagandharvarakṣasām|| sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāmagamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ|
tgt: Desist you O Ten-necked one; Śankara sport in the mountain; and (now) He is incapable of being approached by every one, birds, serpents and Yaksas; gods, Gandharvas and Raksasas?

src: iti nandivacaḥ śrutvā krodhātkampitakuṇḍalaḥ|| roṣāttu tāmranayanaḥ puṣpakādavaruhya saḥ| ko'yaṃ śaṃkara ityuktvā śailamūlamupāgataḥ|| so'paśyannandinaṃ tatra devasyādūrataḥ sthitam| dīptaṃ śūlamavaṣṭabhya dvitīyamiva śaṃkaram||
tgt: Hearing Nandi's speech, (Ravana), wrought up with wrath, his eyes coppery, and his earrings shaking, leapt down from Puspaka. And saying, 'who is this Sankara? and he came down to the base of the mount. He beheld there Nandi stationed at the side of the deity, supporting himself on his flaming dart, resembling a second Sankara.

src: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vānaramukhamavajñāya sa rākṣasaḥ| prahāsaṃ mumuce tatra satoya iva toyadaḥ||
tgt: And seeing that one having the face of a monkey, the Raksasas, deriding him, burst out into laughter, and seemed as if a mass of clouds were sending roars.

src: taṃ kuddho bhagavānandī śaṃkarasyāparā tanuḥ| abravīttatra tadrakṣo daśānanamupasthitam||
tgt: Thereat, growing enraged, the reverend Nandi Sankara's other body spoke into that Rākṣasa The Ten-necked one present there.

src: yasmādvānararūpaṃ māmavajñāya daśānana| aśanīpātasaṃkāśamapahāsaṃ pramuktavān|| tasmānmavīryasaṃyuktā madrūpasamatejasaḥ| utpatsyanti vadhārtha hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ||
tgt: “As O Daśānana, deriding me for my monkery-form, you have indulged in a laughter resembling the bursting of thunder, do monkeys endowed with prowess, and possessed of my form and energy shall be born for compassing the destruction of your race.

src: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāḥ krūra mana:saṃpātaraṃhasaḥ| yuddhonmattā balodriktāḥ śailā iva visarpiṇaḥ|| te tava prabalaṃ darpamutsedhaṃ ca pṛthagvidham| vyapaneṣyanti saṃbhūya sahāmātyamutasya ca||
tgt: And armed with teeth and claws, and fierce and furnished with the fleetness of thought, and mad for encounter, and bursting with vigour, and resembling moving mountains and being born, they shall crush your high pride and power along with your courtiers and sons.

src: kiṃ tvidānī mayā śakyaṃ hantuṃ tvāṃ he niśācara| na hantavyo hatastvaṃ hi pūrvameva svakarmabhiḥ||
tgt: But, O night-ranger, I can even now end you quite; yet I must not slay you for you have ere this been slain by your acts.

src: ityudīritavākye tu deve tasminmahātmani| devadundubhyo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā||
tgt: When that high-souled god had spoken thus celestial kettle-drums sounded and a blossomy shower rained from the sky.

src: acintayitvā sa tadā nandivākyaṃ mahābalaḥ| parvataṃ tu samāsādya vākyamāha daśānanaḥ||
tgt: But without heeding Nandi's speech, that highly powerful one Daśānana coming to the mountain, said.

src: puṣpakasya gatiśchinnā yatkṛte mama gacchataḥ| tamimaṃ śailamunmūlaṃ karomi tava gopate||
tgt: 'O Gopati, I will even uproot this mountain, for whom Pușpaka was deprived of its motion as I was journeying.

src: kena prabhāveṇa bhavā nityaṃ krīḍati rājavat| vijñātavyaṃ na jānīte bhayasthānamupasthitam||
tgt: It must be known by what influence Bhavasvara sport here king-like. He does not know that an occasion of fear has presented itself?'

src: evamuktvā taṃ rāma bhujānvikṣipya parvate| tolayāmāsa taṃ śīghraṃ sa śailaṃ samakampata||
tgt: Having said this, O Rama, Ravana seizing the mountain with his arms, lifted it up at once; and then the mountain trembled greatly.

src: cā nātpartatasyaiva rāṇā devasya kampitāḥ| cacāla pārvatī cāpi tadāśliṣṭā maheśvaram||
tgt: And in consequence of the mountain shaking the attendants of the deity (dwelling in it) also shook. And Pārvatí also trembled and embraced Mahesvara. as

src: tato rāma mahādavo devānāṃ pravaro haraḥ| pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ śailaṃ pīḍayāmāsa līlayā||
tgt: Then, O Rāma, Mahadeva foremost of the deities even Hara, as in sport pressed the mount with his great toe.

src: pīḍitāstu tatastasya śailastambhopamā bhujāḥ| vismitāścābhavaṃstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ||
tgt: Thereat his arms, resembling blocks of stone felt the shock and then there the councillors of that Rākşasa were struck with amaze.

src: rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṃ pīḍanāttathā| mukto virāvaḥ sahasā trailokyaṃ yena kampitam||29
tgt: The Rākṣasa, from wrath and the pain felt in his arms, set up a shout that shook the entire triune world.

src: menire vajraniṣpeṣaṃ tasyāmātyā yugakṣaye| tadā vartmasu calitā devā indrapurogamāḥ|| samudrāścāpi saṃkṣubdhāścalitāścāpi parvatāḥ| yakṣā vidyādharāḥ siddhāḥ kimetaditi cābruvan||31
tgt: His councillors considered it the concussion of the thunder at the universal disruption. And then the celestials with Indra at their head shook on their way; and the sea was wild and the mountains shook. And Yakşas and Vidyadharas and Siddhas asked, "What is this.'

src: toṣayasva mahādevaṃ nīlakaṇṭhamumāpatim| tamṛte śaraṇaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmo'tra daśānana||
tgt: 'Do you propitiate Uma's lord the bluethroated Mahādeva; for, O Daśānana, save him your refuge see we none in this matter.

src: stutibhiḥ praṇato bhūtvā tameva śaraṇaṃ vraja| kṛpāluḥ śaṃkarastuṣṭaḥ prasādaṃ te vidhāsyati ||
tgt: Bowing yourself down, do you seek him as your shelter. Then the kind Sankara, on being gratified, will confer on you his favour.

src: evamuktastadāmātyaistuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam | samābhirvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ praṇabhya sa daśānanaḥ| saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu rudato rakṣaso gatam||
tgt: Thus accosted by his councillors, the Tenfaced one, bowing down to him having the bull for his standard, began to hymn him with various soma hymns; and the Rākşasa passed away a good thousand years in lamentations.

src: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāne viṣṭhitaṃ prabhuḥ| muktvā cāsya bhujārāma prāha vākyaṃ daśānanam||
tgt: Thereat that Lord Mahādeva, pleased, set free the hands of Daśānana stationed at the top of the mount, and O Rāma, addressed him, saying.

src: prīto'smi tava vīrasya śauṭīryācca daśānana| śailākrāntena yo muktastvayārāvaḥ sudāruṇaḥ|| yasmāllokatrayaṃ caitadrāvitaṃ bhayamāgatam| tasmāttvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā rājanbhaviṣyasi ||
tgt: O Daśānana, pleased am I with you on account of your hymns. And as in consequence of your arms having been hurt by the mountain, you have uttered a terrific yell, which struck horror into the worlds and put them shaking, therefore, o King, your name shall be Ravana.

src: devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale| evaṃ tvāmabhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam||
tgt: And deities and men, Yakşas and others living on earth shall call you Rāvana terror to creatures,

src: gaccha paulastya visrabdhaṃ pathā yena tvamicchasi| mayā caivābhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām||
tgt: Go, O Paulastya, which way you wish with confidence, and permitted by me, O Lord of Raksasas, go you.

src: evamuktastu laṅkeśaḥ : śaṃbhunā svayamabravīt| prīto yadi mahādeva varaṃ me dehi yācataḥ||
tgt: Thus accosted by Sambhu, Larkā's lord said of himself. 'If you are pleased with me, grant me a boon, who ask you for it.

src: avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ devagandharvadānavaiḥ| rākṣasairguhyakai gairye cānye balavattarāḥ||
tgt: I have already obtained a boon, bestowing on me immunity from death at the hands of gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas; and Rākşasas and Guyhakas and Nāgas; and others also that are of more than ordinary strength.

src: mānuṣāna gaṇe deva svalpāste mama saṃmatāḥ| dīrghamāyuśca meṃ prāptaṃ brahmaṇastripurāntaka| vāñchitaṃ cāyuṣaḥ śeṣaṃ śastraṃ tvaṃ ca prayaccha me||
tgt: Man count I not ogod: They, I deem, are insignificant. I have also, O destroyer of Tripura, received a long lease of life from Brahmä. Now I wish to pass the remainder of my days in peace: and do you grant me a weapon.

src: evamuktastatastena rāvaṇena sa śaṃkaraḥ| dadau khaṅgaṃ mahādīptaṃ candrahāsamiti śrutam| āyuṣaścāvaśaṣaṃ ca dadau bhūtapatistadā||
tgt: Thus addressed by him, (Ravana,) Sankara gave him an exceedingly effulgent sword, famed as Candrahāsa; and the master of spectres then also granted him peace for the rest of his life.

src: dattvovāca tataḥ śaṃbhu vajñeyamidaṃ tvayā| avajñātaṃ yadi hi te māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ||
tgt: And making (the sword) over to him, Sambhu said, “You must not disregard this. If disregarded, it will for certain come (back) to me?'

src: evaṃ maheśveṇaiva kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ| abhivādya mahādevamārurohātha puṣpakam||
tgt: Having thus received his his name from Mahesvara, Rāvana, saluting Mahadeva, ascended Puspaka.

src: tato mahītalaṃ rāma paryakrāmata rāvaṇaḥ| kṣatriyānsumahāvīryānbādhamānastatastataḥ|| kecittejasvinaḥ śūrāḥ kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ| tacchāsanamakurvanto vineśuḥ saparicchadāḥ||
tgt: Then, O Rāma, Rāvaņa, began to go round the earth. And opposed at places, by the heroic Kșatriyas endowed with energy and irrepressible in fight, fight, who refused submission, he exterminated them along with their retainers.

src: apare durjayaṃ rakṣo jānantaḥ prājñasaṃmatāḥ| jitāḥ sma ityabhāṣanta rākṣasaṃ baladarpitam||
tgt: While other men of wisdom, knowing the Räkşasa to be invincible, said to the Rākṣasas elated with strength, "We have been conquered?”

src: te dūtā rāmavākyena coditā laghuvikramāḥ| prajagmurmadhurāṃ śīghraṃ cakrurvāsaṃ na cādhvani||
tgt: Having been despatched by Rama, quickmoving emissaries speedily arrived at Mathurā.

src: tatastribhirahorātraiḥ saṃprāpya mathurāmatha| śatrughnāya yathātattvamācakhyuḥ sarva eva tat||
tgt: Continually travelling for three nights and days, they arrived there and communicated to Šatrughna the intelligence.

src: lakṣmaṇasya parityāgaṃ pratijñāṃ rāghavasya ca| putrayorabhiṣekaṃ ca paurānugamanaṃ tathā|| kuśasya nagarī ramyā vindhyaparvatarodhasi| kuśāvatīti nāmnā sā kṛtā rāmeṇa dhīmatā||
tgt: Having informed him of the renouncing of Lakşmaņa, Rāma's promise and the following of the citizens they said:-The intelligent Rāma has reared for Kuśī the spacious city of Kuśavati at the foot of the Vindhya range.

src: śrāvastīti purī ramyā śrāvitā ca lavasya ha| ayodhyā vijanāṃ kṛtvā rāghavo bharatastathā|| svargasya samanodyogaṃ kṛtavantau mahārathau|
tgt: The city of Śrāvasti has been reared for Lava, and the mighty car-warriors Rama and Bharata, making Ayodhyā void of men, have addressed themselves for repairing to heaven. Having speedily communicated to him this intelligence the emissaries took rest.

src: evaṃ sarvaṃ nivedyāśu śatrughnāya mahātmane|| viremuste tato dūtāstvara rājeti cābruvan| tacchrutvā ghorasaṃkāśaṃ kulakṣayamupasthitam|| prakṛtīstu samānīya kāñcanaṃ ca purodhasam| teṣāṃ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttamabravīdraghunandanaḥ|||||
tgt: There upon they asked Satrughna to proceed soon. Observing the dreadful destruction of his race, Satrughna sent for his subjects and priests and informed them of everything.

src: ātmanaśca viparyāsaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha| tataḥ putradvayaṃ vīraḥ so'bhyaṣiñcannarādhipaḥ||
tgt: He also communicated to them his own destruction with his brothers. There upon the king Satrughna determined upon installing his two sons in the kingdom.

src: subāhurmathurāṃ lebhe śatrughātī ca vai diśam| dvidhā kṛtvā tu tāṃ senāṃ mādhurī putrayordvayoḥ| dhanaṃ ca yuktaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayāmāsa pārthivaḥ|| subāhuṃ madhurāyāṃ ca vaidiśe śatrughātinam| yayau sthāpya tadāyodhyāṃ rathenaikena rāghavaḥ||
tgt: Subāhu was placed on the throne of Mathurā and Satrughāti became the king of Vidiśā. Having thus established Subāhu in Mathură, and Śatrughātī in Vidiśā, the great hero Satrughna ascended his car and went to Ayodhyā.

src: vai sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| sūkṣmakṣaumāmbaradharaṃ munibhiḥ sārdhamakṣayaiḥ|| so'bhivādya tato rāmaṃ prāñjaliḥ prayatendriyaḥ| uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmamevānucintayan||
tgt: And there he saw the great Rāma, clothed in silk raiment burning like fire in the midst of the ascetics. There upon remembering his duty he saluted Rāma, conversant with piety and with folded hands said.

src: kṛtvāviṣekaṃ sutayordvayo rāghavanandana| tavānugamane rājanviddhimāṃ kṛtaniścayam|| na cānyadadya vaktavyamato vīra na śāsanam| vihanyamānamicchāmi madvidhena viśeṣataḥ|| tasya tāṃ buddhimaklībāṃ vijñāya raghunandanaḥ| bāḍhamityeva śatrughnaṃ rāmo vākyamuvāca ha||
tgt: I have placed my two sons on the throne of my kingdom. I have now resolved upon following you, O King. O hero, do not command me otherwise. I pray only that I may not neglect your command. There upon understanding the firm resolution of Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu agreed.

src: tasya vākyasya vākyānte vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ| ṛkṣarākṣasasaṅghāśca samāpeturanekaśaḥ||
tgt: Immediately after Råma had said this, monkeys assuming shapes at will bears and Rākşasas, began to assemble there.

src: sugrīvaṃ te puraskṛtya sarva eva samāgatāḥ| taṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭumanasaḥ svargāyābhimukhaṃ sthitam|| devaputrā ṛṣisutā gandharvāṇāṃ sutāstathā|
tgt: Apprised of Rama's determination of going to heaven, monkeys, born of the celestials, Rșis and Gandharvas taking Sugriva before them, came there to see Rama.

src: rāmakṣayaṃ viditvā te sarva eva samāgatāḥ|| tavānugamane rājansaṃprāptāḥ sma samāgatāḥ| yadi rāma vināsmābhirgacchestvaṃ puruṣocama|| yamadaṇḍamivodyamya tvayā sma vinipātitāḥ| etasminnantare rāmaṃ sugrīvo'pi mahābalaḥ| praṇamya vidhivadvīraṃ vijñāpayitumudyataḥ|21|| abhiṣicyāṅgadaṃ vīramāgato'smi nareśvara| tavānugamane rājanviddhimāṃ kṛtaniścayam||
tgt: All they came there knowing the departure of Rāma to heaven and said: "O Răma, O foremost of men, if you do repair to heaven forsaking us all, it will be hurling Yama's rod upon us.” The highly powerful Sugrīva too saluting Rāma said:— lord of men, having placed Angada on the throne I have come hither. I have determined upon following you, O King.

src: tairevamuktaḥ kākutstho bāḍhamityabravītsmayan| bibhīṣaṇamathovāca rākṣasendraṃ mahāyaśāḥ|| yāvatprajā dhariṣyanti tāvattvaṃ vai bibhīṣaṇa| rākṣasendra mahāvīrya laṅkāsthaḥ svaṃ dhariṣyasi|| yāvaccandraśca sūryaśca yāvattiṣṭhati medinī| yāvacca matkathā loke tāvadrājyaṃ tavāstviha||25
tgt: Hearing the words of monkeys, Rāma said that their desire would be fulfilled. He then said to Vibhīşaņa the king of Räkşasas:-As long as people shall breathe, O Vibhisana, O highly powerful lord of Rakşasas, you shall preserve your body in Lankä. As long as the moon, the sun and the earth shall exist and as long as my story shall remain current, your kingdom shall be in existence.

src: śāsitaśca sakhitvena kārya te mama śāsanam| prajāḥ saṃrakṣa dharmeṇa nottaraṃ vaktumarhasi|| kiṃcānyadvaktumicchāmi rākṣasendra mahābala| ārādhaya jagatrāthamikṣvākukuladaivatam|| ārādhanīyamaniśaṃ deverapi savāsavaiḥ| tatheti pratijagrāha rāmavākyaṃ bibhīṣaṇaḥ| rājā rākṣasamukhyānāṃ rāghavājñāmanusmaran|28||
tgt: You did, out of friendship, carry out my behests and perform my works. Do you piously govern your subjects. I should not speak any thing else. What shall I say more to you, O highly powerful lord of Rakşasas. Worshhip Jagannath (the lord of the world), the presiding deity of the Ikşvāku race.

src: tamevamuktvā kākutstho hanūmantamathābravīt| jīvite kṛtabuddhistvaṃ mā pratijñāṃ vṛthā kṛthāḥ||29 matkathāḥ parcariṣyanti yāvalloke harīśvara| tāvadramasva suprīto madvākyamanupālayan|30|| evamuktastu hanumānarāghaveṇa mahātmanā| vākyaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa paraṃ harṣamavāpa ca|31|| yāvattava kathā loke vicariṣyati pāvanī| tāvatsthāsyāmi medinyāṃ tavājñāmanupālayan||
tgt: Having thus addressed the king of Rakşasas always obeying Rāghava's command, Käkutstha said to Hanumān:— It is settled that you shall live forever, do you, now observe your promise. As long as my history shall run current in this world do you at my command live happily. Being thus addressed by the high-souled Rāghava Hanumān attained to great delight and said. As long as the sacred theme shall pass current in this world I shall live here carrying out your commands.

src: yāvatkaliśca saṃprāptastāvajjīvata sarvadā|| jāmbavantaṃ tathoktvā tu vṛddhaṃ brahmasutaṃ tadā| maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva pañca jāmbavatā saha|
tgt: There upon he said to the Jämbavān, Brahma's son, Mainda, Dvivida and five others in his company: “As long as the Kali age exists do you all live.”

src: tadevamuktvā kākutsthaḥ sarvāṃstānṛkṣavānarān| uvāca bāḍhaṃ gacchadhvaṃ mayā sādhaṃ yathoditam||
tgt: Having thus addressed them all Kākuthstha said to bears and monkeys. Do you come all with me.

src: kṛtabuddhiṃ nivāsāya tatraiva sa munistadā| bharataṃ kekayīputramātithyena nyamantrayat||
tgt: Then the ascetic asked Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, when he had decided for staying there, to receive his hospitality.

src: abravīd bharatastvenaṃ nanvidaṃ bhavatā kṛtam| pādyamaya̭mathātithyaṃ vane yadupapadyate||
tgt: Thereat Bharata said, “You have for certain done this, (have offered me) water for washing my feet, Arghya, and hospitality with what can be procured in the forest.

src: athovāca bharadvājo bharataṃ prahasanniva| jāne tvāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ tuṣyestvaṃ yena kenacit||
tgt: Then Bharadvāja as if in jest, said to Bharata, "I know you to be of a complacent disposition; and that you are pleased with anything and everything."

src: senāyāstu tavaivāsyāḥ kartumicchāmi bhojanam| mama prītiyathārūpā tvamarho manujarṣabha||
tgt: But I wish to feast your forces. And, O best of men, it behoves you to act in harmony with my desire.

src: kimarthaṃ cāpi nikṣipya dūre balamihāgataḥ| kasmānnehopayāto'si sabalaḥ puruṣarṣabha||
tgt: Why did you coming higher, leave your army at a distance:? And, you man of men, why did you not come accompanied with your forces?

src: bharataḥ pratyuvācedaṃ prāñjalistaṃ tapodhanam| na sainyenopayāto'smi bhagavan bhagavadbhayāt||
tgt: Bharata replied to him, saying, “I had not come accompanied with my forces, from fear of you, O reverend Sir.”

src: rājñā hi bhagavan nityaṃ rājaputreṇa vā tathā| yatnataḥ parihartavyā viṣayeṣu tapasvinaḥ||
tgt: O worshipful one, kings and their sons should always carefully avoid the regions of ascetics.

src: vājimukhyā manuṣyāśca mattāśca varavāraṇāḥ| pracchādya bhagavan bhūmiṃ mahatīmanuyānti mām||
tgt: Choice steeds, men, and mad elephants of the best kind, covering a spacious tract of country, come in my train, respected Sir.

src: te vṛkṣānudakaṃ bhūmimāśrameṣūṭajāṃstathā| na hiṃsyuriti tenāhameka evāgatastataḥ||
tgt: That these might not injure trees or water or the grounds of the cottages pertaining to the asylums, have I come hither alone.

src: ānīyatāmitaḥ senetyājñaptaḥ paramarṣiṇā| tathānucakre bharataḥ senāyāḥ samupāgamam||
tgt: "Bring the forces here,", thus desired by the mighty ascetic, Bharata accordingly caused the troops to be brought in.

src: agniśālāṃ praviśyātha pītvāpaḥ parimṛjya ca| ātithyasya kriyāhetorviśvakarmāṇamāhvayat||
tgt: Then entering the chamber of the sacrificial fire, (Bharadvāja) having sipped water and rubbed his lips therewith, invoked Viśvakarmā for the purpose of entertaining his guest.

src: āhvaye viśvakarmāṇamahaṃ tvaṣṭārameva ca| ātithyaṃ kartumicchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām||
tgt: I invoke Visvakarmā; even Tvasta himself. I wish to entertain guests. Let him accomplish this for me.

src: āhvayelokapālāṃstrīn devāśakrapurogamān| ātithyaṃ kartumicchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām||
tgt: I invoke the three guardians of the worlds, gods headed by Sakra. I wish to entertain guests. Let them accomplish this for me,

src: prāksrotasaśca yā nadyastiryaksrotasa eva ca| pṛthivyāmantarikṣe ca samāyāntvadya sarvaśaḥ||
tgt: Let those rivers that flow westwards, and those that move tortuously on the earth and in the sky, come hither in a body.

src: anyāḥ sravantu maireyaṃ surāmanyāḥ suniṣṭhitām| aparāścodakaṃ śītamikṣukāṇḍarasopamam||
tgt: And let others run Maireya, and others refined wine, and others again cool waters resembling the juice of the sugarcane.

src: āhvaye devagandharvān viśvāvasuhahāhuhūn| tathaivāpsaraso devagandharvaiścāpi sarvaśaḥ||
tgt: I invoke the celestials and the Gandharvas and Viśvāvasu and Hahā and Huhu and also the divine Apsaras and Gandharvis all.

src: ghṛtācīmatha viśvācī miśrakeśīmalambuṣām| nāgadattāṃ ca hemāṃ ca somāmadrikṛtasthalīm||
tgt: And Ghịtâcī, Viśvācī, Misrakesi and Alambuşā; and Nāgadattā and Hemā and Somā residing in the mountain.

src: śakraṃ yāścopatiṣṭhanti brahmāṇaṃ yāśca bhāminīḥ| sarvāstumburuṇā sārdhamāhvaye saparicchadāḥ||
tgt: And those ladies that attend Sakra, and those that attend Brahmā. I invoke all these females well attired, in company with Tumuru.

src: vanaṃ kuruṣu yad divyaṃ vāsobhūṣaṇapatravat| divyanārīphalaṃ śaśvat tatkauberamihaiva tu||
tgt: And let that beautiful forest of Kubera in the north Kuru, having its foliage resembling attires and ornaments, and its fruits debonair damsels, exist even at this very spot.

src: iha bhagavān somo vidhattāmannamuttamam| bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca coṣyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu|| vicitrāṇi ca mālyāni pādapapracyutāni ca| surādīni ca peyāni māṃsāni vividhāni ca|||
tgt: And here let the worshipful Soma yield me excellent viands of diverse kinds in plenty; things; that may be eaten or enjoyed, sucked or licked; and variegated blossoms growing in the trees, and wines and (other) drinks, and meats of various kinds.

src: evaṃ samādhinā yuktastejasāpratimena ca| śikṣāsvarasamāyuktaṃ suvrataścābravīnmuniḥ||
tgt: Thus, furnished with unrivalled ascetic energy, did that anchorite observing excellent vows, express himself orthoepically in consonance with Śikṣā.

src: manasā dhyāyatastasya prāmukhasya kṛtāñjaleḥ| ājagmustāni sarvāṇi daivatāni pṛthak pṛthak || me
tgt: And as he sat with joined hands facing the west with a rapt mind, there came separately all those deities.

src: malayaṃ darduraṃ caiva tataḥ svedanudo'nilaḥ| upaspṛśya vavau yuktyā supriyātmā sukhaṃ śivaḥ||
tgt: And then touching Malaya and Dardura, and laden (with perfumes), a delicious and welcome wind began to blow delightfully, removing sweat.

src: tato'bhyavarṣanta ghanā divyāḥ kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ| devadundubhighoṣaśca dikṣu sarvāsu śuśruve||
tgt: And the clouds poured down a pleasant shower of blossoms; and from all sides were heard sounds of celestial kettle-drums.

src: pravavuścottamā vātā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ| prajagurdevagandharvā vīṇāḥ pramumucuḥ svarān ||
tgt: And a rare breeze set in, and the multitudes of Apsaras danced; and the celestials and the Gandharvas sang, and the Vinas let out their notes.

src: sa śabdo dyāṃ ca bhūmī ca prāṇināṃ śravaṇāni ca| viveśoccāvacaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ samo layaguṇānvitaḥ||
tgt: And the dulcet sounds high and low furnished with Sama and measure, entered the Earth and the firmament and the ears of all creatures.

src: tasminnevaṃgate śabde divye śrotrasukhe nṛṇām| dadarśa bhārataṃ sainyaṃ vidhānaṃ viśvakarmaṇaḥ||
tgt: When that celestial symphony delightful to the ears of men, had thus developed itself, Bharata's forces saw the workmanship of Visvakarman.

src: babhūva hi samā bhūmiḥ samantāt pañcayojanam| śādvalairbahubhiśchannā nīlavaidūryasaṃnibhaiḥ||
tgt: That spot widening into a level plain measuring five Yojanas was covered with thick grass resembling blue lapises.

src: tasmin bilvāḥ kapitthāśca panasā bījapūrakāḥ| āmalakyo babhūvuśca cūtāśca phalabhūṣitāḥ||
tgt: And on it stood Bilvas, and Kapitthas, Panasas, citrons, and Amalakas, and mangoes, embellished with fruits.

src: uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyaśca vanaṃ divyopabhogavat| ājagāma nadī saumyā tīrajairbahubhirvṛtā||
tgt: From the north Kuru had spread a wood capable of conferring every enjoyment; and a beautiful river coursed through bordered by many a tree.

src: catuḥśālāni śubhrāṇi śālāśca gajavājinām| harmyaprāsādasaṃyuktatoraṇāni śubhāni ca|| sitameghanibhaṃ cāpi rājaveśma sutoraṇam| śuklamālyakṛtākāraṃ divyagandhasamukṣitam|| caturasramasambādhaṃ śayanāsanayānavat| divyaiḥ sarvarasairyuktaṃ divyabhojanavastravat|| upakalpitasarvānnaṃ dhautanirmalabhājanam| klṛptasarvāsanaṃ śrīmatsvāstīrṇaśayanottamam||
tgt: And there had arisen white edifices having four divisions; and stables for horses and elephants; and grand gateways belonging to places and mansions; and royal residences with graceful gates, resembling white clouds, bearing white garlands and washed with fragrant waters, having four corners, and spacious, fitted up with beds, seats, and vehicles, having every kind of excellent sapid food, stocked with excellent edibles and apparels, having every variety of food, possessing washed and bright vessels, with every description of seats, graceful, and accommodated with choice beds with coverlets.

src: praviveśa mahābāhuranujñāto maharṣiṇā| veśma tad ratnasampūrṇa bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ|| anujagmuśca te sarve mantriṇaḥ sapurohitāḥ| babhūvuśca mudā yuktāstaṃ dṛṣṭvā veśmasaṃvidhim||
tgt: Permitted by the Maharsi, Kaikeyi's son, Bharata, entered that mansion abounding in gems. And he was followed by the counsellors and the priests; and the latter beholding the arrangements of the palace, were filled with delight.

src: tatra rājāsanaṃ divyaṃ vyajanaṃ chatrameva ca| bharato mantribhiḥ sārdhamabhyavartata rājavat||
tgt: And Bharata in company with the counsellors there went round the august royal seat, the chowri, and the umbrella, worthy of a king. And having bowed down to Rāma, he worshipped that seat.

src: āsanaṃ pūjayāmāsa rāmāyābhipraṇamya ca| vālavyajanamādāya nyaṣīdat sacivāsane||
tgt: And then holding the chowri of hair, he sat down on the seat of a minister.

src: ānupūrvyāniṣeduśca sarve mantripurohitāḥ| tataḥ senāpatiḥ paścāt praśāstā ca nyaṣīdata||
tgt: Then the counsellors and priests seated themselves according to rank. And thereafter the general and the protector of the encampment (got themselves seated).

src: tatastatra muhūrtena nadyaḥ pāyasakardamāḥ| upātiṣṭhanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt||
tgt: Then at Bharadvāja's command, came into being near Bharata streams having Pāyasa for their slime.

src: āsāmubhayataḥ kūlaṃ pāṇḍumṛttikalepanāḥ| ramyāścāvasathā divyā brāhmaṇasya prasādajāḥ||
tgt: And at the pleasure of the Brāhmaṇa, on both their banks arose charming dwellings, covered with pale clay.

src: tenaiva ca muhūrtena divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ| āgurviṃśatisāhasrā brāhmaṇā prahitāḥ striyaḥ|||
tgt: And at that very moment there came twenty thousand women commissioned by Brahma, adorned with divine ornaments.

src: suvarṇamaṇimuktena pravālena ca śobhitāḥ| āgurviṃśatisāhasrāḥ kuberaprahitāḥ striyaḥ|| yābhirgṛhītaḥ puruṣaḥ sonmāda iva lakṣyate|
tgt: And there came also twenty thousand females sent by Kuvera, decked out in gold and gems, pearls and corals. The sight of these was capable of filling men's mind with enchanting ravishment.

src: āgurviṃśatisāhasrā nandanādapsarogaṇāḥ|| nāradastumbururgopaḥ prabhayā sūryavarcasaḥ| ete gandharvarājāno bharatasyāgrato jaguḥ||
tgt: And there came from Nandana twenty thousand damsels; and Nārada and Tumburů and Gopa, resembling the sun in splendour. The Gandharba kings began to sing before Bharata.

src: alambuṣā miśrakeśī puṇḍarīkātha vāmanā| upānṛtyanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt||
tgt: And Alambusa, and Misrakesi, and Puņdarīka, and Vāmana danced before Bharata, at the command of Bharadvāja.

src: yāni mālyāni deveṣu yāni caitrarathe vane| prayāge tānyadṛśyanta bharadvājasya tejasā||
tgt: And those blossoms that are in the celestial regions, and that bloom in the forest of Caitraratha, became visible in Prayāga at the energy of Bharadvāja.

src: bilvā mārdaṅgikā āsan śamyāgrāhā bibhītakāḥ| aśvatthā nartakāścāsan bharadvājasya tejasā||
tgt: And Vilwas did the office of players of the Mặdanga, and Bibhitakas, that of keepers of Soma, and Asvatthas became dancers, at the energy of Bharadvāja.

src: tataḥ saralatālāśca tilakāḥ satamālakāḥ| prahṛṣṭāstatra sampetuḥ kubjā bhūtvātha. vāmanāḥ||
tgt: And Saralas, Tālas, Tilakas, and Tamālas, being delighted, became hump-backed ones and dwarfs.

src: śiṃśapāmalakī jambūryāścānyāḥ kānane latāḥ| mālatī mallikā jātiyaścānyāḥ kānane latāḥ| pramadāvigrahaṃ kṛtvā bharadvājāśrame'vasan||
tgt: And Sinsapās, Āmalakīs, Jambūs and other plants of the forest, wearing the forms of females, stood at the mansion of Bharadvāja.

src: surāṃ surāpāḥ pibata pāyasaṃ ca bubhukṣitāḥ| māṃsāni ca sumedhyāni bhakṣyantāṃ yo yadicchati||
tgt: Let wine-drinkers drink wine, the hungry eat Pāyasa, and those that are inclined to it, feed on clean meat.

src: ucchodya snāpayanti sma nadītīreṣu valguṣu | apyekamekaṃ puruṣaṃ pramadāḥ sapta cāṣṭa ca||
tgt: And every seven or eight females taking a man, bathed him on the lovely banks of the rivers.

src: saṃvāhantyaḥ samāpeturnāryo vipulalocanāḥ| parimṛjya tadānyonyaṃ pāyayanti varāṅganāḥ||
tgt: And damsels furnished with expansive eyes, having wiped the persons (of the bathers), pressed their legs, and those magnificent women made them drink (wine).

src: hayān gajān kharānuṣṭrāṃstathaiva surabheḥ sutān| abhojayan vāhanapāsteṣāṃ bhojyaṃ yathāvidhi||
tgt: And the keepers duly fed excellent horses, elephants, camels and Surabhi's sons (oxen), with their (proper) food.

src: ikhūśca madhulājāṃśca bhojayanti sma vāhanān| ikṣvākuvarayodhānāṃ codayanto mahābalāḥ||
tgt: And some persons possessed of mighty strength, being directed thereto, fed the bearers of the foremost Ikşvāku warriors with sugercanes, honey, and fried paddy.

src: nāśvabandho'śvamājānānna gajaṃ kuñjaragrahaḥ| mattapramattamuditā sā camūstatra sambabhau||
tgt: And the groom forgot his horse, and the elephant-keeper his elephant: that army there became transported with wine and exhilaration.

src: tarpitāḥ sarvakāmaiśca raktacandanaruṣitāḥ| apsarogaṇasaṃyuktāḥ sainyā vācamudīrayan||
tgt: And sumptuously entertained with every enjoyment, with their bodies decked with red sandal, the soldiery in the company of bevies of Apsaras, exclaimed.

src: naivāyodhyāṃ gamiṣyāmo na gamiṣyāma daṇḍakān| kuśalaṃ bharatasyāstu rāmasyāstu tathā sukham||
tgt: To Ayodhyā will we not go, nor yet to Dandaka. Peace be to Bharata, and may Rāma reap happiness!

src: iti pādātayodhāśca hastyaśvārohabandhakāḥ| anāthāstaṃ vidhiṃ labdhvā vācametāmudīrayan||
tgt: Thus did footmen and the riders and keepers of elephants and horses, as well as others, having experienced such a state, utter words.

src: samprahṛṣṭā vineduste narāstatra sahasraśaḥ| bharatasyānuyātāraḥ svargo'yamiti cābruvan|| nṛtyantaśca hasantaśca gāyantaścaiva sainikāḥ| samantāt paridhāvanto mālyopetāḥ sahasraśaḥ||
tgt: And men by thousand, exceedinly delighted, sent up shouts. And saying. “This is heaven,” the retiune of Bharata, the soldiers, began to dance and laugh and sing; and bearing garlands, they on all sides rushed by thousands.

src: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣāṃ tadannamamṛtopamam| divyānudvīkṣya bhakṣyāṃstānabhavad bhakṣaṇe matiḥ||
tgt: And beholding the inviting viands resembling ambrosia, they although already fed, became desirous of eating once again.

src: preṣyāśceṭyaśca vadhvaśca balasthāścāpi sarvaśaḥ| babhūvuste bhṛśaṃ prītāḥ sarve cāhatavāsasaḥ||
tgt: And wearing new clothes, all the servants, and maids, and females of the household, became exceedingly well pleased.

src: kuñjarāśca khagoṣṭrāśca go'śvāśca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ| babhūvuḥ subhṛtāstatra nāto hyanyamakalpayam||
tgt: And elephants, and asses, camels, kine and horses, and beats and birds, being fed their fill, did not hunger after anything else.

src: nāśuklavāsāstatrāsīt kṣudhito malino'pi vā| rajasā dhvastakeśo vā naraḥ kaścidadṛśyata||
tgt: And there appeared no one who wore a soiled habit, or who was hungry, or melancholy, or whose hair was covered with dust.

src: ājaiścāpi,ca vārāhairniṣṭhānavarasaṃcayaiḥ| phalaniṣūhasaṃsiddhaiḥ sūpairgandharasānvitaiḥ|| puṣpadhvajavatīḥ pūrṇāḥ śuklasyānasya cābhitaḥ| dadṛśurvismitāstatra narā lauhīḥ sahasraśaḥ||
tgt: And the people with wonder beheld before them vessels of precious metals by thousands graceful with chaplets of flowers, filled with essences of fruits and fragrant soups and curries and the flesh of goats and bears, and white rice.

src: babhūvurvanapārveṣu kūpāḥ pāyasakardamāḥ| tāśca kāmadudhā gāvo dumāścāsan madhucyutaḥ||
tgt: And there were on the skirts of the wood wells having Pāyasa for their slime; and the kine yeilded whatever was asked and all the trees dropped honey.

src: vāpyo maireyapūrṇāśca mṛṣṭamāṃsacayairvṛtāḥ| prataptapiṭharaiścāpi mārgamāyūrakaukkuṭaiḥ||
tgt: And the tanks were filled with Maireya as well as with clean hot meat of dear, peacocks, and cocks, dressed in pans.

src: pātrīṇāṃ ca sahasrāṇi sthālīnāṃ niyutāni ca| nyarbudāni ca pātrāṇi śātakumbhamayāni ca|71||
tgt: And there were rice-holders by thousands, and curry-pots by hundred thousands, and golden vessels by Arbudas.

src: sthālyaḥ kumbhyaḥ karambhyaśca dadhipūrṇāḥ susaṃskṛtāḥ| yauvanasthasya gaurasya kapitthasya sugandhinaḥ|| hradāḥ pūrṇā rasālasya danaḥ śvetasya cāpare| babhūvuḥ pāyasasyānye śarkarāṇāṃ ca saṃcayāḥ||
tgt: And there were pitchers and water-pots and cleaned vessels for churning curd, filled with the same. And there were tanks of savoury and yellow butter-milk, well-tempered. And there were tanks filled with Rasāla;* and others filled with milk, and with sugar. *A preparation of butter-milk.

src: kalkāṃścūrṇakaṣāyāṃśca snānāni vividhāni ca| dadṛśurbhājanasthāni tīrtheṣu saritāṃ narāḥ|| śuklānaṃśumataścāpi dantadhāvanasaṃcayān| śuklāṃścandanakalkāṃśca samudreṣvavatiṣṭhataḥ|| darpaṇān parimṛṣṭāṃśca vāsasāṃ cāpi saṃcayān| pādukopānahaṃ caiva yugmānyatra sahasraśaḥ|| āñjanīḥ kaṅkatān kūrcāśchatrāṇi ca dhanūṃṣi ca| marmatrāṇāni citrāṇi śayanānyāsanāni ca||
tgt: And men saw sediments, acrid powders and various others things in vessels, for the purpose of bath, on the terraces of tanks; and toothcleaning sticks of Ansuman and other (trees); and white sandal paste lying before; and cleaned mirros; and lots of cloths; and sandals; and shoes in pairs by thousand; and collyrium-pots; and combs; and brushes; and bows at some places; and mail; and various kinds of seats and beds.

src: pratipānahvadān pūrṇān kharoṣṭragajavājinām| avagāhya sutīrthāṃśca hradān sotpalapuṣkarān| ākāśavarṇapratimān svacchatoyān sukhāplavān|| nīlavaidūryavarṇāśca mṛdūn yavasasaṃcayān| nirvāpārthaṃ paśūnāṃ te dadṛśustatra sarvaśaḥ|79 ||
tgt: And they saw reservoirs for asses, camels, elephants, and horses, with easy descents, filled with water to assist their digestion; and pools furnished with lotuses, of the hue of the firmament, with transparent water, comfortable for ablutions; and tender (plots of) grass all around coloured like blue lapises, to serve as pasture for beasts.

src: sabrahmacāriṇy ekāham atīte kṣapaṇaṃ smṛtam / janmany ekodakānāṃ tu trirātrāc chuddhir iṣyate //
tgt: If a fellow-student has died, the Smriti prescribes an impurity of one day; on a birth the purification of the Samanodakas is declared (to take place) after three (days and) nights.

src: strīṇām asaṃskṛtānāṃ tu tryahāc chudhyanti bāndhavāḥ / yathoktenaiva kalpena śudhyanti tu sanābhayaḥ //
tgt: (On the death) of females (betrothed but) not married (the bridegroom and his) relatives are purified after three days, and the paternal relatives become pure according to the same rule.

src: akṣāralavaṇānnāḥ syur nimajjeyuś ca te tryaham / māṃsāśanaṃ ca nāśnīyuḥ śayīraṃś ca pṛthak kṣitau //
tgt: Let (mourners) eat food without factitious salt, bathe during three days, abstain from meat, and sleep separate on the ground.

src: saṃnidhāv eṣa vai kalpaḥ śāvāśaucasya kīrtitaḥ / asaṃnidhāv ayaṃ jñeyo vidhiḥ saṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ //
tgt: The above rule regarding impurity on account of a death has been prescribed (for cases where the kinsmen live) near (the deceased); (Sapinda) kinsmen and (Samanodaka) relatives must know the following rule (to refer to cases where deceased lived) at a distance (from them).

src: vigataṃ tu videśasthaṃ śṛṇuyād yo hy anirdaśam / yac cheṣaṃ daśarātrasya tāvad evāśucir bhavet //
tgt: He who may hear that (a relative) residing in a distant country has died, before ten (days after his death have elapsed), shall be impure for the remainder of the period of ten (days and) nights only.

src: atikrānte daśāhe ca trirātram aśucir bhavet / saṃvatsare vyatīte tu spṛṣṭvaivāpo viśudhyati //
tgt: If the ten days have passed, he shall be impure during three (days and) nights; but if a year has elapsed (since the occurrence of the death), he becomes pure merely by bathing.

src: nirdaśaṃ jñātimaraṇaṃ śrutvā putrasya janma ca / savāsā jalam āplutya śuddho bhavati mānavaḥ //
tgt: A man who hears of a (Sapinda) relative's death, or of the birth of a son after the ten days (of impurity have passed), becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his garments.

src: bāle deśāntarasthe ca pṛthakpiṇḍe ca saṃsthite / savāsā jalam āplutya sadya eva viśudhyati //
tgt: If an infant (that has not teethed), or a (grownup relative who is) not a Sapinda, die in a distant country, one becomes at once pure after bathing in one's clothes.

src: antardaśāhe syātāṃ cet punar maraṇajanmanī / tāvat syād aśucir vipro yāvat tat syād anirdaśam //
tgt: If within the ten days (of impurity) another birth or death happens, a Brahmana shall remain impure only until the (first) period of ten days has expired.

src: trirātram āhur āśaucam ācārye saṃsthite sati / tasya putre ca patnyāṃ ca divārātram iti sthitiḥ // śrotriye tūpasaṃpanne trirātram aśucir bhavet / mātule pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ śiṣyartvigbāndhaveṣu ca //
tgt: They declare that, when the teacher (akarya) has died, the impurity (lasts) three days; if the (teacher's) son or wife (is dead, it lasts) a day and a night; that is a settled (rule). For a Srotriya who resides with (him out of affection), a man shall be impure for three days; for a maternal uncle, a pupil, an officiating priest, or a maternal relative, for one night together with the preceding and following days.

src: prete rājani sajyotir yasya syād viṣaye sthitaḥ / aśrotriye tv ahaḥ kṛtsnam anūcāne tathā gurau //
tgt: If the king in whose realm he resides is dead, (he shall be impure) as long as the light (of the sun or stars shines), but for (an intimate friend) who is not a Srotriya (the impurity lasts) for a whole day, likewise for a Guru who knows the Veda and the Angas.

src: śuddhyed vipro daśāhena dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ / vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śudhyati //
tgt: A Brahmana shall be pure after ten days, a Kshatriya after twelve, a Vaisya after fifteen, and a Sudra is purified after a month.

src: na vardhayed aghāhāni pratyūhen nāgniṣu kriyāḥ / na ca tatkarma kurvāṇaḥ sanābhyo 'py aśucir bhavet //
tgt: Let him not (unnecessarily) lengthen the period of impurity, nor interrupt the rites to be performed with the sacred fires; for he who performs that (Agnihotra) rite will not be impure, though (he be) a (Sapinda) relative.

src: divākīrtim udakyāṃ ca patitaṃ sūtikāṃ tathā / śavaṃ tatspṛṣṭinaṃ caiva spṛṣṭvā snānena śudhyati //
tgt: When he has touched a Kandala, a menstruating woman, an outcast, a woman in childbed, a corpse, or one who has touched a (corpse), he becomes pure by bathing.

src: ācamya prayato nityaṃ japed aśucidarśane / saurān mantrān yathotsāhaṃ pāvamānīś ca śaktitaḥ //
tgt: He who has purified himself by sipping water shall, on seeing any impure (thing or person), always mutter the sacred texts, addressed to Surya, and the Pavamani (verses).

src: nāraṃ spṛṣṭvāsthi sasnehaṃ snātvā vipro viśudhyati / ācamyaiva tu niḥsnehaṃ gām ālabhyārkam īkṣya vā //
tgt: A Brahmana who has touched a human bone to which fat adheres, becomes pure by bathing; if it be free from fat, by sipping water and by touching (afterwards) a cow or looking at the sun.

src: ādiṣṭī nodakaṃ kuryād ā vratasya samāpanāt / samāpte tūdakaṃ kṛtvā trirātreṇaiva śudhyati //
tgt: He who has undertaken the performance of a vow shall not pour out libations (to the dead) until the vow has been completed; but when he has offered water after its completion, he becomes pure in three days only.

src: vṛthāsaṃkarajātānāṃ pravrajyāsu ca tiṣṭhatām / ātmanas tyāgināṃ caiva nivartetodakakriyā // pāṣaṇḍam āśritānāṃ ca carantīnāṃ ca kāmataḥ / garbhabhartṛdruhāṃ caiva surāpīnāṃ ca yoṣitām //
tgt: Libations of water shall not be offered to those who (neglect the prescribed rites and may be said to) have been born in vain, to those born in consequence of an illegal mixture of the castes, to those who are ascetics (of heretical sects), and to those who have committed suicide, To women who have joined a heretical sect, who through lust live (with many men), who have caused an abortion, have killed their husbands, or drink spirituous liquor.

src: ācāryaṃ svam upādhyāyaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum / nirhṛtya tu vratī pretān na vratena viyujyate //
tgt: A student does not break his vow by carrying out (to the place of cremation) his own dead teacher (akarya), sub-teacher (upadhyaya), father, mother, or Guru.

src: dakṣiṇena mṛtaṃ śūdraṃ puradvāreṇa nirharet / paścimottarapūrvais tu yathāyogaṃ dvijanmanaḥ //
tgt: Let him carry out a dead Sudra by the southern gate of the town, but (the corpses of) twice-born men, as is proper, by the western, northern, or eastern (gates).

src: na rājñām aghadoṣo 'sti vratināṃ na ca sattriṇām / aindraṃ sthānam upāsīnā brahmabhūtā hi te sadā //
tgt: The taint of impurity does not fall on kings, and those engaged in the performance of a vow, or of a Sattra; for the (first are) seated on the throne of Indra, and the (last two are) ever pure like Brahman.

src: rājño mahātmike sthāne sadyaḥśaucaṃ vidhīyate / prajānāṃ parirakṣārtham āsanaṃ cātra kāraṇam //
tgt: For a king, on the throne of magnanimity, immediate purification is prescribed, and the reason for that is that he is seated (there) for the protection of (his) subjects.

src: ḍimbhāhavahatānāṃ ca vidyutā pārthivena ca / gobrāhmaṇasya caivārthe yasya cecchati pārthivaḥ //
tgt: (The same rule applies to the kinsmen) of those who have fallen in a riot or a battle, (of those who have been killed) by lightning or by the king, and (of those who perished fighting) for cows and Brahmanas, and to those whom the king wishes (to be pure).

src: somāgnyarkānilendrāṇāṃ vittāppatyor yamasya ca / aṣṭānāṃ lokapālānāṃ vapur dhārayate nṛpaḥ //
tgt: A king is an incarnation of the eight guardian deities of the world, the Moon, the Fire, the Sun, the Wind, Indra, the Lords of wealth and water (Kubera and Varuna), and Yama.

src: lokeśādhiṣṭhito rājā nāsyāśaucaṃ vidhīyate / śaucāśaucaṃ hi martyānāṃ lokebhyaḥ prabhavāpyayau //
tgt: Because the king is pervaded by those lords of the world, no impurity is ordained for him; for purity and impurity of mortals is caused and removed by (those) lords of the world.

src: udyatair āhave śastraiḥ kṣatradharmahatasya ca / sadyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yajñas tathāśaucam iti sthitiḥ //
tgt: By him who is slain in battle with brandished weapons according to the law of the Kshatriyas, a (Srauta) sacrifice is instantly completed, and so is the period of impurity (caused by his death); that is a settled rule.

src: vipraḥ śudhyaty apaḥ spṛṣṭvā kṣatriyo vāhanāyudham / vaiśyaḥ pratodaṃ raśmīn vā yaṣṭiṃ śūdraḥ kṛtakriyaḥ //
tgt: (At the end of the period of impurity) a Brahmana who has performed the necessary rites, becomes pure by touching water, a Kshatriya by touching the animal on which he rides, and his weapons, a Vaisya by touching his goad or the nose-string (of his oxen), a Sudra by touching his staff.

src: etad vo 'bhihitaṃ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu dvijottamāḥ / asapiṇḍeṣu sarveṣu pretaśuddhiṃ nibodhata //
tgt: Thus the purification (required) on (the death of) Sapindas has been explained to you, O best of twice-born men; hear now the manner in which men are purified on the death of any (relative who is) not a Sapinda.

src: asapiṇḍaṃ dvijaṃ pretaṃ vipro nirhṛtya bandhuvat / viśudhyati trirātreṇa mātur āptāṃś ca bāndhavān //
tgt: A Brahmana, having carried out a dead Brahmana who is not a Sapinda, as (if he were) a (near) relative, or a near relative of his mother, becomes pure after three days;

src: yady annam atti teṣāṃ tu daśāhenaiva śudhyati / anadann annam ahnaiva na cet tasmin gṛhe vaset //
tgt: But if he eats the food of the (Sapindas of the deceased), he is purified in ten days, (but) in one day, if he does not eat their food nor dwells in their house.

src: anugamyecchayā pretaṃ jñātim ajñātim eva ca / snātvā sacailaḥ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati //
tgt: Having voluntarily followed a corpse, whether (that of) a paternal kinsman or (of) a stranger, he becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his clothes, by touching fire and eating clarified butter.

src: na vipraṃ sveṣu tiṣṭhatsu mṛtaṃ śūdreṇa nāyayet / asvargyā hy āhutiḥ sā syāc chūdrasaṃsparśadūṣitā //
tgt: Let him not allow a dead Brahmana to be carried out by a Sudra, while men of the same caste are at hand; for that burnt-offering which is defiled by a Sudra's touch is detrimental to (the deceased's passage to) heaven.

src: jñānaṃ tapo 'gnir āhāro mṛn mano vāry upāñjanam / vāyuḥ karmārkakālau ca śuddheḥ kartṝṇi dehinām //
tgt: The knowledge (of Brahman) austerities, fire, (holy) food, earth, (restraint of) the internal organ, water, smearing (with cowdung), the wind, sacred rites, the sun, and time are the purifiers of corporeal (beings).

src: sarveṣām eva śaucānām arthaśaucaṃ paraṃ smṛtaṃ / yo 'rthe śucir hi sa śucir na mṛdvāriśuciḥ śuciḥ //
tgt: Among all modes of purification, purity in (the acquisition of) wealth is declared to be the best; for he is pure who gains wealth with clean hands, not he who purifies himself with earth and water.

src: kṣāntyā śudhyanti vidvāṃso dānenākāryakāriṇaḥ / pracchannapāpā japyena tapasā vedavittamāḥ //
tgt: The learned are purified by a forgiving disposition, those who have committed forbidden actions by liberality, secret sinners by muttering (sacred texts), and those who best know the Veda by austerities.

src: mṛttoyaiḥ śudhyate śodhyaṃ nadī vegena śudhyati / rajasā strī manoduṣṭā saṃnyāsena dvijottamāḥ //
tgt: By earth and water is purified what ought to be made pure, a river by its current, a woman whose thoughts have been impure by the menstrual secretion, a Brahmana by abandoning the world (samnyasa).

src: adbhir gātrāṇi śudhyanti manaḥ satyena śudhyati / vidyātapobhyāṃ bhūtātmā buddhir jñānena śudhyati //
tgt: The body is cleansed by water, the internal organ is purified by truthfulness, the individual soul by sacred learning and austerities, the intellect by (true) knowledge.

src: eṣa śaucasya vaḥ proktaḥ śarīrasya vinirṇayaḥ / nānāvidhānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ śuddheḥ śṛṇuta nirṇayam //
tgt: Thus the precise rules for the purification of the body have been declared to you; hear now the decision (of the law) regarding the purification of the various (inanimate) things.

src: taijasānāṃ maṇīnāṃ ca sarvasyāśmamayasya ca / bhasmanādbhir mṛdā caiva śuddhir uktā manīṣibhiḥ //
tgt: The wise ordain that all (objects) made of metal, gems, and anything made of stone are to be cleansed with ashes, earth, and water.

src: nirlepaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhāṇḍam adbhir eva viśudhyati / abjam aśmamayaṃ caiva rājataṃ cānupaskṛtam //
tgt: A golden vessel which shows no stains, becomes pure with water alone, likewise what is produced in water (as shells and coral), what is made of stone, and a silver (vessel) not enchased.

src: apām agneś ca saṃyogād dhaimaṃ raupyaṃ ca nirbabhau / tasmāt tayoḥ svayonyaiva nirṇeko guṇavattaraḥ //
tgt: From the union of water and fire arose the glittering gold and silver; those two, therefore, are best purified by (the elements) from which they sprang.

src: tāmrāyaḥkāṃsyaraityānāṃ trapuṇaḥ sīsakasya ca / śaucaṃ yathārhaṃ kartavyaṃ kṣārāmlodakavāribhiḥ // dravāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śuddhir utpavanaṃ smṛtam / prokṣaṇaṃ saṃhatānāṃ ca dāravāṇāṃ ca takṣaṇam //
tgt: Copper, iron, brass, pewter, tin, and lead must be cleansed, as may be suitable (for each particular case), by alkaline (substances), acids or water. The purification prescribed for all (sorts of) liquids is by passing two blades of Kusa grass through them, for solid things by sprinkling (them with water), for (objects) made of wood by planing them.

src: mārjanaṃ yajñapātrāṇāṃ pāṇinā yajñakarmaṇi / camasānāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca śuddhiḥ prakṣālanena tu //
tgt: At sacrifices the purification of (the Soma cups called) Kamasas and Grahas, and of (other) sacrificial vessels (takes place) by rubbing (them) with the hand, and (afterwards) rinsing (them with water).

src: carūṇāṃ sruksruvāṇāṃ ca śuddhir uṣṇena vāriṇā / sphyaśūrpaśakaṭānāṃ ca musalolūkhalasya ca //
tgt: The Karu and (the spoons called) Sruk and Sruva must be cleaned with hot water, likewise (the wooden sword, called) Sphya, the winnowing-basket (Surpa), the cart (for bringing the grain), the pestle and the mortar.

src: adbhis tu prokṣaṇaṃ śaucaṃ bahūnāṃ dhānyavāsasām / prakṣālanena tv alpānām adbhiḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate //
tgt: The manner of purifying large quantities of grain and of cloth is to sprinkle them with water; but the purification of small quantities is prescribed (to take place) by washing them.

src: cailavac carmaṇāṃ śuddhir vaidalānāṃ tathaiva ca / śākamūlaphalānāṃ ca dhānyavac chuddhir iṣyate // kauśeyāvikayor ūṣaiḥ kutapānām ariṣṭakaiḥ / śrīphalair aṃśupaṭṭānāṃ kṣaumāṇāṃ gaurasarṣapaiḥ //
tgt: Skins and (objects) made of split cane must be cleaned like clothes; vegetables, roots, and fruit like grain; Silk and woollen stuffs with alkaline earth; blankets with pounded Arishta (fruit); Amsupattas with Bel fruit; linen cloth with (a paste of) yellow mustard.

src: kṣaumavac chaṅkhaśṛṅgāṇām asthidantamayasya ca / śuddhir vijānatā kāryā gomūtreṇodakena vā // prokṣaṇāt tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca palālaṃ caiva śudhyati / mārjanopāñjanair veśma punaḥpākena mṛnmayam //
tgt: A man who knows (the law) must purify conch-shells, horn, bone and ivory, like linen cloth, or with a mixture of cow's urine and water. Grass, wood, and straw become pure by being sprinkled (with water), a house by sweeping and smearing (it with cowdung or whitewash), an earthen (vessel) by a second burning.

src: madyair mūtraiḥ purīṣair vā ṣṭhīvanaih pūyaśoṇitaiḥ / saṃspṛṣṭaṃ naiva śuddhyeta punaḥpākena mṛnmayam //
tgt: An earthen vessel which has been defiled by spirituous liquor, urine, ordure, saliva, pus or blood cannot be purified by another burning.

src: saṃmārjanopāñjanena sekenollekhanena ca / gavāṃ ca parivāsena bhūmiḥ śudhyati pañcabhiḥ //
tgt: Land is purified by (the following) five (modes, viz.) by sweeping, by smearing (it with cowdung), by sprinkling (it with cows' urine or milk), by scraping, and by cows staying (on it during a day and night).

src: pakṣijagdhaṃ gavā ghrātam avadhūtam avakṣutam / dūṣitaṃ keśakīṭaiś ca mṛtprakṣepeṇa śudhyati //
tgt: (Food) which has been pecked at by birds, smelt at by cows, touched (with the foot), sneezed on, or defiled by hair or insects, becomes pure by scattering earth (over it).

src: yāvan nāpaity amedhyāktād gandho lepaś ca tatkṛtaḥ / tāvan mṛdvāri cādeyaṃ sarvāsu dravyaśuddhiṣu //
tgt: As long as the (foul) smell does not leave an (object) defiled by impure substances, and the stain caused by them (does not disappear), so long must earth and water be applied in cleansing (inanimate) things.

src: trīṇi devāḥ pavitrāṇi brāhmaṇānām akalpayan / adṛṣṭam adbhir nirṇiktaṃ yac ca vācā praśasyate //
tgt: The gods declared three things (to be) pure to Brahmanas, that (on which) no (taint is) visible, what has been washed with water, and what has been commended (as pure) by the word (of a Brahmana).

src: āpaḥ śuddhā bhūmigatā vaitṛṣṇyaṃ yāsu gor bhavet / avyāptāś ced amedhyena gandhavarṇarasānvitāḥ //
tgt: Water, sufficient (in quantity) in order to slake the thirst of a cow, possessing the (proper) smell, colour, and taste, and unmixed with impure substances, is pure, if it is collected on (pure) ground.

src: nityaṃ śuddhaḥ kāruhastaḥ paṇye yac ca prasāritam / brahmacārigataṃ bhaikṣyaṃ nityaṃ medhyam iti sthitiḥ //
tgt: The hand of an artisan is always pure, so is (every vendible commodity) exposed for sale in the market, and food obtained by begging which a student holds (in his hand) is always fit for use; that is a settled rule.

src: nityam āsyaṃ śuci strīṇāṃ śakuniḥ phalapātane / prasrave ca śucir vatsaḥ śvā mṛgagrahaṇe śuciḥ //
tgt: The mouth of a woman is always pure, likewise a bird when he causes a fruit to fall; a calf is pure on the flowing of the milk, and a dog when he catches a deer.

src: śvabhir hatasya yan māṃsaṃ śuci tan manur abravīt / kravyādbhiś ca hatasyānyaiś caṇḍālādyaiś ca dasyubhiḥ //
tgt: Manu has declared that the flesh (of an animal) killed by dogs is pure, likewise (that) of a (beast) slain by carnivorous (animals) or by men of low caste (Dasyu), such as Kandalas.

src: ūrdhvaṃ nābher yāni khāni tāni medhyāni sarvaśaḥ / yāny adhas tāny amedhyāni dehāc caiva malāś cyutāḥ //
tgt: All those cavities (of the body) which lie above the navel are pure, (but) those which are below the navel are impure, as well as excretions that fall from the body.

src: makṣikā vipruṣaś chāyā gaur aśvaḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ / rajo bhūr vāyur agniś ca sparśe medhyāni nirdiśet //
tgt: Flies, drops of water, a shadow, a cow, a horse, the rays of the sun, dust, earth, the wind, and fire one must know to be pure to the touch.

src: viṇmūtrotsargaśuddhyarthaṃ mṛdvāry ādeyam arthavat / daihikānāṃ malānāṃ ca śuddhiṣu dvādaśasv api //
tgt: In order to cleanse (the organs) by which urine and faeces are ejected, earth and water must be used, as they may be required, likewise in removing the (remaining ones among) twelve impurities of the body.

src: vasā śukram asṛṅ majjā mūtraviṭ ghrāṇakarṇaviṭ / śleśma aśru dūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ //
tgt: Oily exudations, semen, blood, (the fatty substance of the) brain, urine, faeces, the mucus of the nose, ear-wax, phlegm, tears, the rheum of the eyes, and sweat are the twelve impurities of human (bodies).

src: ekā liṅge gude tisras tathaikatra kare daśa / ubhayoḥ sapta dātavyā mṛdaḥ śuddhim abhīpsatā //
tgt: He who desires to be pure, must clean the organ by one (application of) earth, the anus by (applying earth) three (times), the (left) hand alone by (applying it) ten (times), and both (hands) by (applying it) seven (times).

src: etac chaucaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇām / triguṇaṃ syād vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam //
tgt: Such is the purification ordained for householders; (it shall be) double for students, treble for hermits, but quadruple for ascetics.

src: kṛtvā mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā khāny ācānta upaspṛśet / vedam adhyeṣyamāṇaś ca annam aśnaṃś ca sarvadā //
tgt: When he has voided urine or faeces, let him, after sipping water, sprinkle the cavities, likewise when he is going to recite the Veda, and always before he takes food.

src: trir ācāmed apaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāt tato mukham / śarīraṃ śaucam icchan hi strī śūdras tu sakṛt sakṛt //
tgt: Let him who desires bodily purity first sip water three times, and then twice wipe his mouth; but a woman and a Sudra (shall perform each act) once (only).

src: śūdrāṇāṃ māsikaṃ kāryaṃ vapanaṃ nyāyavartinām / vaiśyavac chaucakalpaś ca dvijocchiṣṭaṃ ca bhojanam //
tgt: Sudras who live according to the law, shall each month shave (their heads); their mode of purification (shall be) the same as that of Vaisyas, and their food the fragments of an Aryan's meal.

src: nocchiṣṭaṃ kurvate mukhyā vipruṣo 'ṅgaṃ na yānti yāḥ / na śmaśrūṇi gatāny āsyaṃ na dantāntaradhiṣṭhitam //
tgt: Drops (of water) from the mouth which do not fall on a limb, do not make (a man) impure, nor the hair of the moustache entering the mouth, nor what adheres to the teeth.

src: spṛśanti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān / bhaumikais te samā jñeyā na tair āprayato bhavet //
tgt: Drops which trickle on the feet of him who offers water for sipping to others, must be considered as equal to (water collected on the ground; they render him not impure.

src: ucchiṣṭena tu saṃspṛṣṭo dravyahastaḥ kathaṃ cana / anidhāyaiva tad dravyam ācāntaḥ śucitām iyāt //
tgt: He who, while carrying anything in any manner, is touched by an impure (person or thing), shall become pure, if he performs an ablution, without putting down that object.

src: vānto viriktaḥ snātvā tu ghṛtaprāśanam ācaret / ācāmed eva bhuktvānnaṃ snānaṃ maithuninaḥ smṛtam // suptvā kṣutvā ca bhuktvā ca niṣṭhīvyoktvānṛtāni ca / pītvāpo 'dhyeṣyamāṇaś ca ācāmet prayato 'pi san //
tgt: He who has vomited or purged shall bathe, and afterwards eat clarified butter; but if (the attack comes on) after he has eaten, let him only sip water; bathing is prescribed for him who has had intercourse with a woman. Though he may be (already) pure, let him sip water after sleeping, sneezing, eating, spitting, telling untruths, and drinking water, likewise when he is going to study the Veda.

src: eṣāṃ śaucavidhiḥ kṛtsno dravyaśuddhis tathaiva ca / ukto vaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ strīṇāṃ dharmān nibodhata //
tgt: Thus the rules of personal purification for men of all castes, and those for cleaning (inanimate) things, have been fully declared to you: hear now the duties of women.

src: bālayā vā yuvatyā vā vṛddhayā vāpi yoṣitā / na svātantryeṇa kartavyaṃ kiṃ cid kāryaṃ gṛheṣv api //
tgt: By a girl, by a young woman, or even by an aged one, nothing must be done independently, even in her own house.

src: bālye pitur vaśe tiṣṭhet pāṇigrāhasya yauvane / putrāṇāṃ bhartari prete na bhajet strī svatantratām // pitrā bhartrā sutair vāpi necched viraham ātmanaḥ / eṣāṃ hi viraheṇa strī garhye kuryād ubhe kule //
tgt: In childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth to her husband, when her lord is dead to her sons; a woman must never be independent. She must not seek to separate herself from her father, husband, or sons; by leaving them she would make both (her own and her husband's) families contemptible.

src: sadā prahṛṣṭayā bhāvyaṃ gṛhakārye ca dakṣayā / susaṃskṛtopaskarayā vyaye cāmuktahastayā //
tgt: She must always be cheerful, clever in (the management of her) household affairs, careful in cleaning her utensils, and economical in expenditure.

src: yasmai dadyāt pitā tv enāṃ bhrātā vānumate pituḥ / taṃ śuśrūṣeta jīvantaṃ saṃsthitaṃ ca na laṅghayet //
tgt: Him to whom her father may give her, or her brother with the father's permission, she shall obey as long as he lives, and when he is dead, she must not insult (his memory).

src: maṅgalārthaṃ svastyayanaṃ yajñaś cāsāṃ prajāpateḥ / prayujyate vivāhe tu pradānaṃ svāmyakāraṇam //
tgt: For the sake of procuring good fortune to (brides), the recitation of benedictory texts (svastyayana), and the sacrifice to the Lord of creatures (Pragapati) are used at weddings; (but) the betrothal (by the father or guardian) is the cause of (the husband's) dominion (over his wife).

src: anṛtāv ṛtukāle ca mantrasaṃskārakṛt patiḥ / sukhasya nityaṃ dāteha paraloke ca yoṣitaḥ //
tgt: The husband who wedded her with sacred texts, always gives happiness to his wife, both in season and out of season, in this world and in the next.

src: viśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā guṇair vā parivarjitaḥ / upacāryaḥ striyā sādhvyā satataṃ devavat patiḥ //
tgt: Though destitute of virtue, or seeking pleasure (elsewhere), or devoid of good qualities, (yet) a husband must be constantly worshipped as a god by a faithful wife.

src: nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthag yajño na vrataṃ nāpy upoṣaṇam / patiṃ śuśrūṣate yena tena svarge mahīyate //
tgt: No sacrifice, no vow, no fast must be performed by women apart (from their husbands); if a wife obeys her husband, she will for that (reason alone) be exalted in heaven.

src: pāṇigrāhasya sādhvī strī jīvato vā mṛtasya vā / patilokam abhīpsantī nācaret kiṃ cid apriyam //
tgt: A faithful wife, who desires to dwell (after death) with her husband, must never do anything that might displease him who took her hand, whether he be alive or dead.

src: kāmaṃ tu ksapayed dehaṃ puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ / na tu nāmāpi gṛhṇīyāt patyau prete parasya tu //
tgt: At her pleasure let her emaciate her body by (living on) pure flowers, roots, and fruit; but she must never even mention the name of another man after her husband has died.

src: āsītā maraṇāt ksāntā niyatā brahmacāriṇī / yo dharma ekapatnīnāṃ kāṅkṣantī tam anuttamam //
tgt: Until death let her be patient (of hardships), self-controlled, and chaste, and strive (to fulfil) that most excellent duty which (is prescribed) for wives who have one husband only.

src: anekāni sahasrāṇi kumārabrahmacāriṇām / divaṃ gatāni viprāṇām akṛtvā kulasaṃtatim //
tgt: Many thousands of Brahmanas who were chaste from their youth, have gone to heaven without continuing their race.

src: mṛte bhartari sāḍhvī strī brahmacarye vyavasthitā / svargaṃ gacchaty aputrāpi yathā te brahmacāriṇaḥ // apatyalobhād yā tu strī bhartāram ativartate / seha nindām avāpnoti paralokāc ca hīyate //
tgt: A virtuous wife who after the death of her husband constantly remains chaste, reaches heaven, though she have no son, just like those chaste men. But a woman who from a desire to have offspring violates her duty towards her (deceased) husband, brings on herself disgrace in this world, and loses her place with her husband (in heaven).

src: nānyotpannā prajāstīha na cāpy anyaparigrahe / na dvitīyaś ca sādhvīnāṃ kva cid bhartopadiśyate //
tgt: Offspring begotten by another man is here not (considered lawful), nor (does offspring begotten) on another man's wife (belong to the begetter), nor is a second husband anywhere prescribed for virtuous women.

src: patiṃ hitvāpakṛṣṭaṃ svam utkṛṣṭaṃ yā niṣevate / nindyaiva sā bhavel loke parapūrveti cocyate //
tgt: She who cohabits with a man of higher caste, forsaking her own husband who belongs to a lower one, will become contemptible in this world, and is called a remarried woman (parapurva).

src: vyabhicārāt tu bhartuḥ strī loke prāpnoti nindyatām / śṛgālayoniṃ prāpnoti pāparogaiś ca pīḍyate //
tgt: By violating her duty towards her husband, a wife is disgraced in this world, (after death) she enters the womb of a jackal, and is tormented by diseases (the punishment of) her sin.

src: śūnāṃ ca patitānāṃ ca śvapacāṃ pāparogiṇām / vayasānāṃ kṛmīṇāṃ ca śanakair nirvaped bhuvi //
tgt: Let him gently place on the ground (some food) for dogs, outcasts, Kandalas (Svapak), those afflicted with diseases that are punishments of former sins, crows, and insects.

src: evaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūtāni brāhmaṇo nityam arcati / sa gacchati paraṃ sthānaṃ tejomūrtiḥ pathā rjunā //
tgt: That Brahmana who thus daily honours all beings, goes, endowed with a resplendent body, by a straight road to the highest dwelling-place (i.e. Brahman).

src: kṛtvaitad balikarmaivam atithiṃ pūrvam āśayet / bhikṣāṃ ca bhikṣave dadyād vidhivad brahmacāriṇe //
tgt: Having performed this Bali offering, he shall first feed his guest and, according to the rule, give alms to an ascetic (and) to a student.

src: yat puṇyaphalam āpnoti gāṃ dattvā vidhivad guroḥ / tat puṇyaphalam āpnoti bhikṣāṃ dattvā dvijo gṛhī //
tgt: A twice-born householder gains, by giving alms, the same reward for his meritorious act which (a student) obtains for presenting, in accordance with the rule, a cow to his teacher.

src: bhikṣām apy udapātraṃ vā satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam / vedatattvārthaviduṣe brāhmaṇāyopapādayet //
tgt: Let him give, in accordance with the rule, to a Brahmana who knows the true meaning of the Veda, even (a small portion of food as) alms, or a pot full of water, having garnished (the food with seasoning, or the pot with flowers and fruit).

src: naśyanti havyakavyāni narāṇām avijānatām / bhasmībhūteṣu vipreṣu mohād dattāni dātṛbhiḥ //
tgt: The oblations to gods and manes, made by men ignorant (of the law of gifts), are lost, if the givers in their folly present (shares of them) to Brahmanas who are mere ashes.

src: vidyātapaḥsamṛddheṣu hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu / nistārayati durgāc ca mahataś caiva kilbiṣāt //
tgt: An offering made in the mouth-fire of Brahmanas rich in sacred learning and austerities, saves from misfortune and from great guilt.

src: saṃprāptāya tv atithaye pradadyād āsanodake / annaṃ caiva yathāśakti satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam //
tgt: But let him offer, in accordance with the rule, to a guest who has come (of his own accord) a seat and water, as well as food, garnished (with seasoning), according to his ability.

src: śilān apy uñchato nityaṃ pañcāgnīn api juhvataḥ / sarvaṃ sukṛtam ādatte brāhmaṇo 'narcito vasan //
tgt: A Brahmana who stays unhonoured (in the house), takes away (with him) all the spiritual merit even of a man who subsists by gleaning ears of corn, or offers oblations in five fires.

src: tṛṇāni bhūmir udakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā / etāny api satāṃ gehe nocchidyante kadā cana //
tgt: Grass, room (for resting), water, and fourthly a kind word; these (things) never fail in the houses of good men.

src: ekarātraṃ tu nivasann atithir brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ / anityaṃ hi sthito yasmāt tasmād atithir ucyate //
tgt: But a Brahmana who stays one night only is declared to be a guest (atithi); for because he stays (sthita) not long (anityam), he is called atithi (a guest).

src: naikagrāmīṇam atithiṃ vipraṃ sāṅgatikaṃ tathā / upasthitaṃ gṛhe vidyād bhāryā yatrāgnayo 'pi vā //
tgt: One must not consider as a guest a Brahmana who dwells in the same village, nor one who seeks his livelihood by social intercourse, even though he has come to a house where (there is) a wife, and where sacred fires (are kept).

src: upāsate ye gṛhasthāḥ parapākam abuddhayaḥ / tena te pretya paśutāṃ vrajanty annādidāyinaḥ //
tgt: Those foolish householders who constantly seek (to live on) the food of others, become, in consequence of that (baseness), after death the cattle of those who give them food.

src: apraṇodyo 'tithiḥ sāyaṃ sūryoḍho gṛhamedhinā / kāle prāptas tv akāle vā nāsyānaśnan gṛhe vaset //
tgt: A guest who is sent by the (setting) sun in the evening, must not be driven away by a householder; whether he have come at (supper-) time or at an inopportune moment, he must not stay in the house without entertainment.

src: na vai svayaṃ tad aśnīyād atithiṃ yan na bhojayet / dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ vātithipūjanam //
tgt: Let him not eat any (dainty) food which he does not offer to his guest; the hospitable reception of guests procures wealth, fame, long life, and heavenly bliss.

src: āsanāvasathau śayyām anuvrajyām upāsanām / uttameṣūttamaṃ kuryād dhīne hīnaṃ same samam //
tgt: Let him offer (to his guests) seats, rooms, beds, attendance on departure and honour (while they stay), to the most distinguished in the best form, to the lower ones in a lower form, to equals in an equal manner.

src: vaiśvadeve tu nirvṛtte yady anyo 'tithir āvrajet / tasyāpy annaṃ yathāśakti pradadyān na baliṃ haret //
tgt: But if another guest comes after the Vaisvadeva offering has been finished, (the householder) must give him food according to his ability, (but) not repeat the Bali offering.

src: na bhojanārthaṃ sve vipraḥ kulagotre nivedayet / bhojanārthaṃ hi te śaṃsan vāntāśīty ucyate budhaiḥ //
tgt: A Brahmana shall not name his family and (Vedic) gotra in order to obtain a meal; for he who boasts of them for the sake of a meal, is called by the wise a foul feeder (vantasin).

src: na brāhmaṇasya tv atithir gṛhe rājanya ucyate / vaiśyaśūdrau sakhā caiva jñātayo gurur eva ca //
tgt: But a Kshatriya (who comes) to the house of a Brahmana is not called a guest (atithi), nor a Vaisya, nor a Sudra, nor a personal friend, nor a relative, nor the teacher.

src: yadi tv atithidharmeṇa kṣatriyo gṛham āvrajet / bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu kāmaṃ tam api bhojayet //
tgt: But if a Kshatriya comes to the house of a Brahmana in the manner of a guest, (the house-holder) may feed him according to his desire, after the above-mentioned Brahmanas have eaten.

src: vaiśyaśūdrāv api prāptau kuṭumbe 'tithidharmiṇau / bhojayet saha bhṛtyais tāv ānṛśaṃsyaṃ prayojayan //
tgt: Even a Vaisya and a Sudra who have approached his house in the manner of guests, he may allow to eat with his servants, showing (thereby) his compassionate disposition.

src: itarān api sakhyādīn samprītyā gṛham āgatān / prakṛtyānnaṃ yathāśakti bhojayet saha bhāryayā //
tgt: Even to others, personal friends and so forth, who have come to his house out of affection, he may give food, garnished (with seasoning) according to his ability, (at the same time) with his wife.

src: suvāsinīḥ kumārīś ca rogiṇo garbhiṇīḥ striyaḥ / atithibhyo 'gra evaitān bhojayed avicārayan //
tgt: Without hesitation he may give food, even before his guests, to the following persons, (viz.) to newly-married women, to infants, to the sick, and to pregnant women.

src: adattvā tu ya etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṅkte 'vicakṣaṇaḥ / sa bhuñjāno na jānāti śvagṛdhrair jagdhim ātmanaḥ //
tgt: But the foolish man who eats first without having given food to these (persons) does, while he crams, not know that (after death) he himself will be devoured by dogs and vultures.

src: bhuktavatsv atha vipreṣu sveṣu bhṛtyeṣu caiva hi / bhuñjīyātāṃ tataḥ paścād avaśiṣṭaṃ tu dampatī //
tgt: After the Brahmanas, the kinsmen, and the servants have dined, the householder and his wife may afterwards eat what remains.

src: devān ṛṣīn manuṣyāṃś ca pitṝn gṛhyāś ca devatāḥ / pūjayitvā tataḥ paścād gṛhasthaḥ śeṣabhug bhavet //
tgt: Having honoured the gods, the sages, men, the manes, and the guardian deities of the house, the householder shall eat afterwards what remains.

src: aghaṃ sa kevalaṃ bhuṅkte yaḥ pacaty ātmakāraṇāt / yajñaśiṣṭāśanaṃ hy etat satām annaṃ vidhīyate //
tgt: He who prepares food for himself (alone), eats nothing but sin; for it is ordained that the food which remains after (the performance of) the sacrifices shall be the meal of virtuous men.

src: rājartviksnātakagurūn priyaśvaśuramātulān / arhayen madhuparkeṇa parisaṃvatsarāt punaḥ //
tgt: Let him honour with the honey-mixture a king, an officiating priest, a Snataka, the teacher, a son-in-law, a father-in-law, and a maternal uncle, (if they come) again after a full year (has elapsed since their last visit).

src: rājā ca śrotriyaś caiva yajñakarmaṇy upasthitau / madhuparkeṇa saṃpūjyau na tv ayajña iti sthitiḥ //
tgt: A king and a Srotriya, who come on the performance of a sacrifice, must be honoured with the honey-mixture, but not if no sacrifice is being performed; that is a settled rule.

src: sāyaṃ tv annasya siddhasya patny amantraṃ baliṃ haret / vaiśvadevaṃ hi nāmaitat sāyaṃ prātar vidhīyate //
tgt: But the wife shall offer in the evening (a portion) of the dressed food as a Bali-oblation, without (the recitation of) sacred formulas; for that (rite which is called the) Vaisvadeva is prescribed both for the morning and the evening.

src: pitṛyajñaṃ tu nirvartya vipraś candrakṣaye 'gnimān / piṇḍānvāhāryakaṃ śrāddhaṃ kuryān māsānumāsikam //
tgt: After performing the Pitriyagna, a Brahmana who keeps a sacred fire shall offer, month by month, on the new-moon day, the funeral sacrifice (Sraddha, called) Pindanvaharyaka.

src: pitṝṇāṃ māsikaṃ śrāddham anvāhāryaṃ vidur budhāḥ / tac cāmiṣeṇā kartavyaṃ praśastena prayatnataḥ //
tgt: The wise call the monthly funeral offering to the manes Anvaharya (to be offered after the cakes), and that must be carefully performed with the approved (sorts of) flesh (mentioned below).

src: tatra ye bhojanīyāḥ syur ye ca varjyā dvijottamāḥ / yāvantaś caiva yaiś cānnais tān pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ //
tgt: I will fully declare what and how many (Brahmanas) must be fed on that (occasion), who must be avoided, and on what kinds of food (they shall dine).

src: dvau daive pitṛkārye trīn ekaikam ubhayatra vā / bhojayet susamṛddho 'pi na prasajjeta vistare //
tgt: One must feed two (Brahmanas) at the offering to the gods, and three at the offering to the manes, or one only on either occasion; even a very wealthy man shall not be anxious (to entertain) a large company.

src: satkriyāṃ deśakālau ca śaucaṃ brāhmaṇasaṃpadaḥ / pañcaitān vistaro hanti tasmān neheta vistaram //
tgt: A large company destroys these five (advantages) the respectful treatment (of the invited, the propriety of) place and time, purity and (the selection of) virtuous Brahmana (guests); he therefore shall not seek (to entertain) a large company.

src: prathitā pretakṛtyaiṣā pitryaṃ nāma vidhukṣaye / tasmin yuktasyaiti nityaṃ pretakṛtyaiva laukikī //
tgt: Famed is this rite for the dead, called (the sacrifice sacred to the manes (and performed) on the new-moon day; if a man is diligent in (performing) that, (the reward of) the rite for the dead, which is performed according to Smarta rules, reaches him constantly.

src: śrotriyāyaiva deyāni havyakavyāni dātṛbhiḥ / arhattamāya viprāya tasmai dattaṃ mahāphalam //
tgt: Oblations to the gods and manes must be presented by the givers to a Srotriya alone; what is given to such a most worthy Brahmana yields great reward.

src: ekaikam api vidvāṃsaṃ daive pitrye ca bhojayet / puṣkalaṃ phalam āpnoti nāmantrajñān bahūn api //
tgt: Let him feed even one learned man at (the sacrifice) to the gods, and one at (the sacrifice) to the manes; (thus) he will gain a rich reward, not (if he entertains) many who are unacquainted with the Veda.

src: dūrād eva parīkṣeta brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam / tīrthaṃ tad dhavyakavyānāṃ pradāne so 'tithiḥ smṛtaḥ //
tgt: Let him make inquiries even regarding the remote (ancestors of) a Brahmana who has studied an entire (recension of the) Veda;(if descended from a virtuous race) such a man is a worthy recipient of gifts (consisting) of food offered to the gods or to the manes, he is declared (to procure as great rewards as) a guest (atithi).

src: sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇām anṛcāṃ yatra bhuñjate / ekas tān mantravit prītaḥ sarvān arhati dharmataḥ //
tgt: Though a million of men, unaquainted with the Rikas, were to dine at a (funeral sacrifice), yet a single man, learned in the Veda, who is satisfied (with his entertainment), is worth them all as far as the (production of) spiritual merit (is concerned).

src: jñānotkṛṣṭāya deyāni kavyāni ca havīṃṣi ca / na hi hastāv asṛgdigdhau rudhireṇaiva śudhyataḥ // yāvato grasate grāsān havyakavyeṣv amantravit / tāvato grasate preto dīptaśūlarṣṭyayoguḍān //
tgt: Food sacred to the manes or to the gods must be given to a man distinguished by sacred knowledge; for hands, smeared with blood, cannot be cleansed with blood. As many mouthfuls as an ignorant man swallows at a sacrifice to the gods or to the manes, so many red-hot spikes, spears, and iron balls must (the giver of the repast) swallow after death.

src: jñānaniṣṭhā dvijāḥ ke cit taponiṣṭhās tathāpare / tapaḥsvādhyāyaniṣṭhāś ca karmaniṣṭhās tathāpare //
tgt: Some Brahmanas are devoted to (the pursuit of) knowledge, and others to (the performance of) austerities; some to austerities and to the recitation of the Veda, and others to (the performance of) sacred rites.

src: jñānaniṣṭheṣu kavyāni pratiṣṭhāpyāni yatnataḥ / havyāni tu yathānyāyaṃ sarveṣv eva caturṣv api //
tgt: Oblations to the manes ought to be carefully presented to those devoted to knowledge, but offerings to the gods, in accordance with the reason (of the sacred law), to (men of) all the four (above-mentioned classes).

src: aśrotriyaḥ pitā yasya putraḥ syād vedapāragaḥ / aśrotriyo vā putraḥ syāt pitā syād vedapāragaḥ //
tgt: If there is a father ignorant of the sacred texts whose son has learned one whole recension of the Veda and the Angas, and a son ignorant of the sacred texts whose father knows an entire recension of the Veda and the Angas,

src: jyāyāṃsam anayor vidyād yasya syāc chrotriyaḥ pitā / mantrasaṃpūjanārthaṃ tu satkāram itaro 'rhati //
