src: mā naḥ asmin maghavan pr̥t su aṁhasi nahi te antaḥ śavasaḥ pari naśe akrandayaḥ nadyaḥ roruvat vanā kathā na kṣoṇīḥ bhiyasā sam ārata
tgt: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength. Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear?

src: arca akrāya śākine śacī vate śr̥ṇvantam indram mahayan abhi stuhi yaḥ dhr̥ṣṇunā śavasā rodasī iti ubhe iti vr̥ṣā vr̥ṣa tvā vr̥ṣabhaḥ ni r̥ñjate
tgt: Sing hymns of praise to Ṣakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who hearcth thee, Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth.

src: arca dive br̥hate śūṣyam vacaḥ sva kṣatram yasya dhr̥ṣataḥ dhr̥ṣat manaḥ br̥hat śravāḥ asuraḥ barhaṇā kr̥taḥ puraḥ hari bhyām vr̥ṣabhaḥ rathaḥ hi saḥ
tgt: Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway. High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he.

src: tvam divaḥ br̥hataḥ sānu kopayaḥ ava tmanā dhr̥ṣatā śambaram bhinat yat māyinaḥ vrandinaḥ mandinā dhr̥ṣat śitām gabhastim aśanim pr̥tanyasi
tgt: The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Ṣambara, When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and twoedged, against the banded sorcerers.

src: ni yat vr̥ṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cit vrandinaḥ roruvat vanā prācīnena manasā barhaṇāvatā yat adya cit kr̥ṇavaḥ kaḥ tvā pari
tgt: When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which 8usga kept confined, Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done?

src: tvam āvitha naryam turvaśam yadum tvam turvītim vayyam śatakrato itiśata krato tvam ratham etaśam kr̥tvye dhane tvam puraḥ navatim dambhayaḥ nava
tgt: Thou helpest Narya, Turvaṣa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turvîti, Ṣatakratu! Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles.

src: saḥ gha rājā sat patiḥ śūśuvat janaḥ rāta havyaḥ prati yaḥ śāsam invati ukthā vā yaḥ abhi gr̥ṇāti rādhasā dānuḥ asmai uparā pinvate d ivaḥ
tgt: A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law, Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky.

src: asamam kṣatram asamā manīṣā pra soma pāḥ apasā santu neme ye te indra daduṣaḥ vardhayanti mahi kṣatram sthaviram vr̥ṣṇyam ca
tgt: His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma, Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver.

src: tubhya it ete bahulāḥ adri dugdhāḥ camū sadaḥ camasāḥ indra pānāḥ vi aśnuhi tarpaya kāmam eṣām atha manaḥ vasu deyāya kr̥ṣva
tgt: Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles. Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure.

src: apām atiṣṭhat dharuṇa hvaram tamaḥ antaḥ vr̥trasya jaṭhareṣu parvataḥ abhi īm indraḥ nadyaḥ vavriṇā hitāḥ viśvāḥ anu sthāḥ pravaṇeṣu jighnate
tgt: There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters' flow: in Vr̥itra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed. But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivitics.

src: saḥ śe vr̥dham adhi dhāḥ dyumnam asme iti mahi kṣatram janāṣāṭ indra tavyam rakṣa ca naḥ maghonaḥ pāh i sūrīn rāye ca naḥ su apatyai iṣe dhāḥ
tgt: So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people. Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.

src: divaḥ cit asya varimā vi papratha indram na mahnā pr̥thivī cana prati bhīmaḥ tuviṣmān carṣaṇi bhyaḥ ātapaḥ śiśīte vajram tejase na vaṁsagaḥ
tgt: THOUGH e'en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match. Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull.

src: saḥ arṇavaḥ na nadyaḥ samudriyaḥ prati gr̥bhṇāti vi śritāḥ varīma bhiḥ indraḥ somasya pītaye vr̥ṣa yate sanāt saḥ yudhmaḥ ojasā panasyate
tgt: Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width. He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might.

src: tvam tam indra parvatam na bhojase mahaḥ nr̥mṇasya dharmaṇām irajyasi pra vīryeṇa devatāti cekite viśvasmai ugraḥ karmaṇe puraḥ h itaḥ
tgt: Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as't were, even that famed mountain down. Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed.

src: saḥ it vane namasyu bhiḥ vacasyate cāru janeṣu pra bruvāṇaḥ indri yam vr̥ṣā chanduḥ bhavati haryataḥ vr̥ṣā kṣemeṇa dhenām maghavā yat invati
tgt: He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indrapower. A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice.

src: saḥ it mahāni sam ithāni majmanā kr̥ṇoti yudhmaḥ ojasā janebhyaḥ adha cana śrat dadhati tviṣi mate indrāya vajram ni ghanighnate vadham
tgt: Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind; And men have faith in Indra, the respIendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death.

src: saḥ hi śravasyuḥ sadanāni kr̥trimā kṣmayā vr̥dhānaḥ ojasā vi nāśayan jyotīṁṣi kr̥ṇvan avr̥kāṇi yajyave ava su kratuḥ sartavai apaḥ sr̥jat
tgt: Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art, He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper.

src: dānāya manaḥ soma pāvan astu te arvāñcā harī iti vandana śrut ā kr̥dhi yamiṣṭhāsaḥ sārathayaḥ ye indrca te na tvā ketāḥ ā dabhnuvanti bhūrṇayaḥ
tgt: Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise. Those charioteers of' thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray.

src: apra kṣitam vasu bibharṣi hastayoḥ aṣāl̥ham sahaḥ tanvi sr̥utaḥ dadhe āvr̥tāsaḥ avatāsaḥ na kartr̥ bhiḥ tanūṣu te kratavaḥ indra bhūrayaḥ
tgt: Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might. O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.

src: eṣaḥ pra pūrvīḥ ava tasya camriṣaḥ atyaḥ na yoṣām ut ayaṁsta bhurvaṇiḥ dakṣam mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayam ratham āvr̥tya hari yogam r̥bhvasam
tgt: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare. He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds.

src: tam gūrtayaḥ neman iṣaḥ parīṇasaḥ samudram na sam caraṇe san iṣyavaḥ patim dakṣasya vidathasya nu sahāḥ girim na venāḥ adhi roha tejasā
tgt: To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood. To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones.

src: saḥ turvaṇiḥ mahān areṇu paiṁsye gireḥ bhr̥ṣṭiḥ na bhrājate tujā śavaḥ yena śuṣṇam māyinam āyasaḥ made dudhraḥ ābhūṣu rāmayat ni dāman i
tgt: Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak; Wherewith the iron one, fierce e'en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Sushna fast in bonds.

src: devī yadi taviṣī tvāvr̥dhā ūtaye indram siṣakti uṣasam na sūryaḥ yaḥ dhr̥ṣṇunā śavasā bādhate tamaḥ iyarti reṇum br̥hat arhari svani ḥ
tgt: When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn, Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing.

src: vi yat tiraḥ dharuṇam acyutam rajaḥ atisthipaḥ divaḥ ātāsu barhaṇā svaḥ mīl̥he yat made indra harṣyā ahan vr̥tram niḥ apām aubjaḥ arṇavam
tgt: When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved, In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vr̥itra dead and broughtest floods of rain.

src: tvam divaḥ dharuṇam dhiṣe ojasā pr̥thivyāḥ indra sadaneṣu māhinaḥ tvam sutasya made ariṇāḥ apaḥ vi vr̥trasya samayā pāṣyā arujaḥ
tgt: Thou with thy might didst grasp,the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth. Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vr̥itra's stony fences through and through.

src: pra maṁhiṣṭhāya br̥hate br̥hat raye satya śuṣmāya tavase matim bhare apām iva pravaṇe yasya duḥ dharam rādhaḥ viśva āyu śavase apa vr̥tam
tgt: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,– Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength.

src: agha te viśvam anu ha asat iṣṭaye āpaḥ nimnāiva savanā haviṣmataḥ yat parvate na sam aśīta haryataḥ indrasya vajraḥ śnathitā hiraṇyayaḥ
tgt: Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee-the offerer's libations like floods to the depth, When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold.

src: asmai bhīmāya namasā sam adhvare uṣaḥ na śubhre ā bhara panīyase yasya dhāma śravase nāma indriyam jyotiḥ akāri haritaḥ na ayase
tgt: To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite, Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed.

src: ime te indra te vayam puru stuta ye tvā ārabhya carāmasi prabhuvaso itiprabhu vaso nahi tvat anyaḥ girvaṇaḥ giraḥ saghat kṣoṇīḥ iva prati naḥ harya tat vacaḥ
tgt: Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee. Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn.

src: bhūri te indra vīryam tava smasi asya stotuḥ magha van kāmam ā pr̥ṇa anu te dyauḥ br̥hatī vīryam mame iyam ca te pr̥thivī neme ojase
tgt: Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper. After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself.

src: tvam tam indra parvatam mahām urum vajreṇa vajrin parva śaḥ cakartitha ava asr̥jaḥ ni vr̥tāḥ sartavai apaḥ satrā viśvam dadhiṣe kevalam sahaḥ
tgt: Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud. Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.

src: nu cit sahaḥ jāḥ amr̥taḥ ni tundate hotā yat dūtaḥ abhavat vivasvataḥ vi sādhiṣṭhebhiḥ pathi bhiḥ rajaḥ mame ā deva tātā haviṣā vivāsati
tgt: NE'ER waxeth faint the Immortal, Son of Strength, since he, the Herald, hath become Vivasvan's messenger.

src: ā svam adma yuvamānaḥ ajaraḥ tr̥ṣu aviṣyan ataseṣu tiṣṭhati atyaḥ na pr̥ṣṭham pruṣitasya rocate divaḥ na sānu stanayan acikradat
tgt: Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads. His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven?

src: kroṇā rudrebhiḥ vasu bhiḥ puraḥ hitaḥ hotā ni sattaḥ rayiṣāṭ amatyarḥ rathaḥ na vikṣu r̥ñjasānaḥ āyuṣu vi ānuṣak vāryā devaḥ r̥ṇvati
tgt: Set high in place o'er all that Vasus, Rudras do, immortal, Lord of riches, seated as High Priest; Hastening like a car to men, to those who live, the God without delay gives boons to be desired.

src: vi vāta jūtaḥ ataseṣu tiṣṭhate vr̥thā juhūbhiḥ sr̥ṇyā tuvi svaṇiḥ tr̥ṣu yat agne vaninaḥ vr̥ṣa yase kr̥ṣṇam te ema ruśat ūrme ajara
tgt: Urged by the wind be spreads through dry wood as he lists, armed with his tongues for sickles, with a mighty roar. Black is thy path, Agni, changeless, with glittering waves! when like a bull thou rushest eager to the trees.

src: tapuḥ jambhaḥ vane ā vāta coditaḥ yūthe na sāhvān ava vāti vaṁsagaḥ abhi vrajan akṣitam pājasā rajaḥ sthātuḥ caratham bhayate patatri ṇaḥ
tgt: With teeth of flame, wind-driven, through the wood he speeds, triumphant like a bull among the herd of cows, With bright strength roaming to the everlasting air: things fixed, things moving quake before him as he flies.

src: dadhuḥ tvā bhr̥gavaḥ mānuṣeṣu ā rayim na cārum su havam janebhyaḥ hotāram agne atithim vareṇyam mitram na śevam divyāya janmane
tgt: The Bhr̥igus established thee among mankind for men, like as a treasure, beauteous, easy to invoke; Thee, Agni, as a herald and choice-worthy guest, as an auspicious Friend to the Celestial Race.

src: hotāram sapta juhvaḥ yajiṣṭham yam vāghataḥ vr̥ṇate adhvareṣu agnim viśveṣām aratim vasūnām saparyāmi prayasā yāmi ratnam
tgt: Agni, the seven tongues' deftest Sacrificer, him whom the priests elect at solemn worship, The Herald, messenger of all the Vasus, I serve with dainty food, I ask for riches.

src: acchidrā sūno iti sahasaḥ naḥ adya stotr̥ bhyaḥ mitra mahaḥ śarma yaccha agne gr̥ṇantam aṁhasaḥ uruṣya ūrjaḥ napāt pūḥ bhiḥ āyasībhiḥ
tgt: Grant, Son of Strength, thou rich in friends, a refuge without a flaw this day to us thy praisers. O Agni, Son of Strength, with forts of iron preserve thou from distress the man who lauds thee.

src: bhava varūtham gr̥ṇate vibhāvaḥ bhava maghavan maghavat bhyaḥ śarma uruṣya agne aṁhasaḥ gr̥ṇantam prātaḥ makṣu dhiyāvasuḥ jagamyāt
tgt: Be thou a refuge, Bright One, to the singer, a shelter, Bounteous Lord, to those who worship. Preserve the singer from distress, O Agni. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

src: vayāḥ it agne agnayaḥ te anye tve iti viśve amr̥tāḥ mādayante vaiśvānara nābhiḥ asi kṣitīnām sthūṇāiva janān upa mit yayantha
tgt: THE other fires are, verily, thy branches; the Immortals all rejoice in thee, O Agni. Centre art thou, Vaigvdnara, of the people, sustaining men like a deep-founded pillar.

src: mūrdhā divaḥ nābhiḥ agniḥ pr̥thivyāḥ atha abhavat aratiḥ rodasyoḥ tam tvā devāsaḥ ajanayanta devam vaiśvānara jyotiḥ it āryāya
tgt: The forehead of the sky, earth's centre, Agni became the messenger of earth and heaven. Vaiṣvânara, the Deities produced thee, a God, to be a light unto the Ârya.

src: ā sūrye na raśmayaḥ dhruvāsaḥ vaiśvānare dadhire agnā vasūni yā parvateṣu oṣadhīṣu ap su yā mānuṣeṣu asi tasya rājā
tgt: As in the Sun firm rays are set for ever, treasures are in Vaiṣvânara, in Agni. Of all the riches in the hills, the waters, the herbs, among mankind, thou art the Sovran.

src: br̥hatīivetibr̥hatī iva sūnave rodasī iti giraḥ hotā manuṣyaḥ na dakṣaḥ svaḥ vate satya śuṣmāya pūvīrḥ vaiśvānarāya nr̥ tamāya yahvīḥ
tgt: As the great World-halves, so are their Son's praises; skilled, as a man, to act, is he the Herald. Vaiṣvânara, celestial, truly mighty, most manly One, hath many a youthful consort.

src: divaḥ cit te br̥hataḥ jāta vedaḥ vaiśvānara pra ririce mahi tvam rājā kr̥ṣṭīnām asi mānuṣīṇām yudhā devebhyaḥ varivaḥ cakartha
tgt: Even the lofty heaven, O Jâtavedas Vaiṣvânara, hath not attained thy greatness. Thou art the King of lands where men are settled, thou hast brought comfort to the Gods in battle.

src: pra nu mahi tvam vr̥ṣabhasya vocam yam pūravaḥ vr̥tra hanam sacante vaiśvānaraḥ dasyum agniḥ jaghanvān adhūnot kāṣṭhāḥ ava śambaram bhet
tgt: Now will I tell the greatness of the Hero whom Prarti's sons follow as Vr̥itra's slayer: Agni Vaiṣvânara struck down the Dasyu, cleave Ṣambara through and shattered down his fences.

src: vaiśvānaraḥ mahimnā viśva kr̥ṣṭiḥ bharat vājeṣu yajataḥ vibhāvā śāta vaneye śatinībhiḥ agniḥ puru nīthe jarate sūnr̥tāvān
tgt: Vaiṣvânara, dwelling by his might with all men, far-shining, holy mid the Bharadvâjas, Is lauded, excellent, with hundred praises by Purunîtha, son of Ṣatavani.

src: vahnim yaśasam vidathasya ketum supra avyam dūtam sadyaḥ artham dvi janmānam rayim iva pra śastam rātim bharat bhr̥gave mātariśvā
tgt: As 'twere Some goodly treasure Mâtariṣvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhr̥igu, Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy.

src: asya śāsuḥ ubhayāsaḥ sacante haviṣmantaḥ uśijaḥ ye ca martāḥ d ivaḥ cit pūrvaḥ ni asādi hotā āpr̥cchyaḥ viśpatiḥ vikṣu vedhāḥ
tgt: Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship. As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer.

src: tam navyasī hr̥daḥ ā jāyamānam asmat su kīrtiḥ madhu jihvam aśyāḥ yam r̥tvijaḥ vr̥jane mānuṣāsaḥ prayasvantaḥ āyavaḥ jījananta
tgt: May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e'en at his birth, is sweet as honey; Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created.

src: uśik pāvakaḥ vasuḥ mānuṣeṣu vareṇyaḥ hotā adhāyi vikṣu damūnā gr̥ha patiḥ dame ā agniḥ bhuvat rayi patiḥ rayīṇām
tgt: Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy. May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling.

src: tam tvā vayam patim agne rayīṇām pra śaṁsāmaḥ mati bhiḥ gotamāsaḥ āśum na vājam bharam marjayantaḥ prātaḥ makṣu dhiyāvasuḥ jagamyāt
tgt: As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches, Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

src: asmai it oṁ iti pra tavase turāya prayaḥ na harmi stomam māhināya r̥cīṣamāya adhri gave oham indrāya brahmāṇi rāta tamā
tgt: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands, My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra.

src: asmai it oṁ iti prayaḥ iva pra yaṁsi bharāmi āṅgūṣam bādhe su vr̥kti indrāya hr̥dā manasā manīṣā pratnāya patye dhiyaḥ marjayanta
tgt: Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor. For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit.

src: asmai it oṁ iti tyam upa mam svaḥ sām bharāmi āṅgūṣam āsyena maṁhiṣṭham acchokti bhiḥ matīnām suvr̥kti bhiḥ sūrim vavr̥dhadhyai
tgt: To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer, To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver.

src: asmai it oṁ iti stomam sam hinomi ratham na taṣṭāiva tat sināya giraḥ ca girvāhase su vr̥kti indrāya viśvam invam medhirāya
tgt: Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,– Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra.

src: asmai it oṁ iti saptim iva śravasyā indrāya arkam juhvā sam añje vīram dāna okasam vandadhyai purām gūrta śravasam darmāṇam
tgt: So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as 'twere a horse, through love of glory, To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles.

src: iti tvaṣṭā takṣat vajram svapaḥ tamam svaryam raṇāya vr̥trasya cit vidat yena marma tujan īśānaḥ tujatā kiyedhāḥ
tgt: Even for him hath Tvashṭar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle, Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vr̥itra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker.

src: asya it oṁ iti mātuḥ savaneṣu sadyaḥ mahaḥ pitum papivān cāru annā muṣāyat viṣṇuḥ pacatam sahīyān vidhyat varāham tiraḥ adrim astā
tgt: As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Vishṇu had drunk up the draught, he plundered. The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain.

src: asmai it oṁ iti gnāḥ cit deva patnīḥ indrāya arkam ahi hatye ūvur ity ūvuḥ pari dyāvāpr̥thivī iti jabhre urvī iti na asya te iti mahimānam pari staitistaḥ
tgt: To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Goda, wove praises. The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not.

src: asya it eva pra ririce mahitvam divaḥ pr̥thivyāḥ pari antarikṣāt sva rāṭ indraḥ dame ā viśva gūrtaḥ su ariḥ amatraḥ vavakṣe raṇāya
tgt: Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven. Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle.

src: asya it eva śavasā śuṣantam vi vr̥ścat vajreṇa vr̥tram indraḥ gāḥ na vrāṇāḥ avanīḥ amuñcat abhi śravaḥ dāvane sa cetāḥ
tgt: Through his own strength Indra with bolt of thunder cut piece-meal Vr̥itra, drier up of waters. He let the floods go free, like cows imprisoned, for glory, with a heart inclined to bounty.

src: asya it oṁ iti tveṣasā ranta sindhavaḥ pari yat vajreṇa sīm ayacchat īśāna kr̥t dāśuṣe daśasyan turvītaye gādham turvaṇiḥ karitikaḥ
tgt: The rivers played, through his impetuous splendour, since with his bolt he compassed them on all sides. Using his might and favouring him who worshipped, he made a ford, victorious, for Turvîti.

src: asmai it oṁ iti pra bhara tūtujānaḥ vr̥trāya vajram īśānaḥ kiyedhāḥ goḥ na parva vi rada tiraścā iṣyan arṇāṁsi apām caradhyai
tgt: Vast, with thine ample power, with eager movement, against this Vr̥itra cast thy bolt of thunder. Rend thou his joints, as of an ox, dissevered, with bolt oblique, that floods of rain may follow.

src: asya it oṁ iti pra brūhi pūrvyāṇi turasya karmāṇi navyaḥ ukthaiḥ yudhe yat iṣṇānaḥ āyudhāni r̥ghāyamāṇaḥ ni riṇāti śatrūn
tgt: Sing with new lauds his exploits wrought aforetime, the deeds of him, yea, him who moveth swiftly, When, hurling forth his weapons in the battle, he with impetuous wrath lays low the foemen.

src: asya it oṁ iti bhiyā girayaḥ ca dr̥l̥hāḥ dyāvā ca bhūmā januṣaḥ tujeteiti upo iti venasya joguvānaḥ oṇim sadyaḥ bhuvat vīryāya nodhāḥ
tgt: When he, yea, he, comes forth the firm. Set mountains and the whole heaven and earth, tremble for terror. May Nodhas, ever praising the protection of that dear Friend, gain quickly strength heroic.

src: asmai it oṁ iti tyat anu dāyi eṣām ekaḥ yat vavne bhūreḥ īśānaḥ pra etaśam sūrye paspr̥dhānam sauvaśvye suṣvim āvat indraḥ
tgt: Now unto him of these things hath been given what he who rules alone o'er much, electeth. Indra hath helped Etaṣa, Soma-presser, contending in the race of steeds with Sarya.

src: eva te hāri yojana su vr̥kti indra brahmāṇi gotamāsaḥ akran ā eṣu viśva peśasam dhiyam dhāḥ prātaḥ makṣu dhiyāvasuḥ jagamyāt
tgt: Thus to thee, Indra, yoker of Bay Coursers, the Gotamas have brought their prayers to please thee. Bestow upon them thought, decked with all beauty. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

src: pra manmahe śavasānāya śūṣam āṅgūṣam girvaṇase aṅgirasvat suvr̥kt i bhiḥ stuvate r̥gmiyāya arcāma arkam nare vi śrutāya
tgt: LIKE Angiras a gladdening laud we ponder to him who loveth song, exceeding mighty. Let us sing glory to the far-famed Hero who must be praised with fair hymns by the singer.

src: pra vaḥ mahe mahi namaḥ bharadhvam āṅgūṣyam śavasānāya sāma yena naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ pada jñāḥ arcantaḥ aṅgirasaḥ gāḥ avindan
tgt: Unto the great bring ye great adoration, a chant with praise to him exceeding mighty, Through whom our sires, Angirases, singing praises and knowing well the places, found the cattle.

src: indrasya aṅgirasām ca iṣṭau vidat saramā tanayāya dhāsim br̥haspatiḥ bhinat adrim vidat gāḥ sam usriyābhiḥ vāvaśanta naraḥ
tgt: When Indra and the Angirases desired it, Saramâ found provision for her offspring. Br̥ihaspati cleft the mountain, found the cattle: the heroes shouted with the kine in triumph.

src: saḥ su stubhā saḥ stubhā sapta vipraiḥ svareṇa adrim svaryaḥ nava gvaiḥ saraṇyu bhiḥ phali gam indra śakra valam raveṇa daśa gvaiḥ
tgt: Mid shout, loud shout, and roar, with the Navagvas, seven singers, hast thou, heavenly, rent the mountain; Thou hast, with speeders, with Daṣagvas, Indra, Ṣakra, with thunder rent obstructive Vala.

src: gr̥ṇānaḥ aṅgiraḥ bhiḥ dasma vi vaḥ uṣasā sūryeṇa gobhiḥ andhaḥ vi bhūmyāḥ aprathayaḥ indra sānu divaḥ rajaḥ uparam astabhāyaḥ
tgt: Praised by Angirases, thou, foe-destroyer, hast, with the Dawn, Sun, rays, dispellcd the darkness. Thou Indra, hast spread out the earths high ridges, and firmly fixed the region under heaven.

src: tat oṁ iti prayakṣa tamam asya karma dasmasya cāru tamam asti daṁsaḥ upa hvare yat uparāḥ apinvat madhu arṇasaḥ nadyaḥ catasraḥ
tgt: This is the deed most worthy of all honour, the fairest marvel of the Wonder-Worker, That, nigh where heaven bends down, he made four rivers flow full with waves that carry down sweet water.

src: dvitā vi vavre sa najā sanīl̥e itisa nīl̥e ayāsyaḥ stavamānebhiḥ arkaiḥ bhagaḥ na meneiti parame vi oman adhārayat rodasī iti su daṁsāḥ
tgt: Unwearied, won with lauding hymns, he parted of old the ancient Pair, united ever. In highest sky like Bhaga, he the doer of marvels set both Dames and earth and heaven.

src: sanāt divam pari bhūma virūpeitivi rūpe punaḥ bhuvā yuvatī iti svebhiḥ evaiḥ kr̥ṣṇebhiḥ aktā uṣāḥ ruśat bhiḥ vapuḥ bhiḥ ā carataḥ anyāanyā
tgt: Still born afresh, young Dames, each in her manner, unlike in hue, the Pair in alternation Round heaven and earth from ancient time have travelled, Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with limbs of splendour.

src: sanemi sakhyam su apasyamānaḥ sūnuḥ dādhāra śavasā su daṁsāḥ āmāsu cit dadhiṣe pakvam antariti payaḥ kr̥ṣṇāsu ruśat rohiṇīṣu
tgt: Rich in good actions, skilled in operation, the Son with might maintains his perfect friendship. Thou in the raw cows, black of hue or ruddy, storest the ripe milk glossy white in colour.

src: sanāt sa nīl̥āḥ avanīḥ avātāḥ vratā rakṣante amr̥tāḥ sahaḥ bhiḥ puru sahasrā janayaḥ na patnīḥ duvasyanti svasāraḥ ahrayāṇam
tgt: Their paths, of old connected, rest uninjured; they with great might preserve the immortal statutes. For many thousand holy works the Sisters wait on the haughty Lord like wives and matrons.

src: sanāyuvaḥ namasā navyaḥ arkaiḥ vasu yavaḥ matayaḥ dasma dadruḥ patim na patnīḥ uśatīḥ uśantam spr̥śanti tvā śavasāvan manīṣāḥ
tgt: Thoughts ancient, seeking wealth, with adoration, with newest lauds have sped to thee, O Mighty. As yearning wives cleave to their yearning husband, so cleave our hymns to thee, O Lord most potent.

src: sanāt eva tava rāyaḥ gabhastau na kṣīyante na upa dasyanti dasma dyumān asi kratu mān indra dhīraḥ śikṣa śacī vaḥ tava naḥ śacībhiḥ
tgt: Strong God, the riches which thy hands have holden from days of old have perished not nor wasted. Splendid art thou, O Indra, wise, unbending:strengthen us with might, O Lord of Power.

src: sanāyate gotamaḥ indra navyam atakṣat brahma hari yojanāya su nīthāya naḥ śavasāna nodhāḥ prātaḥ makṣu dhiyāvasuḥ jagamyāt
tgt: O mighty Indra, Gotama's son Nodhas hath fashioned this new prayer to thee Eternal, Sure leader, yoker of the Tawny Coursers. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

src: tvam mahān indra yaḥ ha śuṣmaiḥ dyāvā jajñānaḥ pr̥thivī iti ame ghāḥ yat ha te viśvā girayaḥ cit abhvā bhiyā dr̥l̥hāsaḥ kiraṇāḥ na aijan
tgt: THOU art the Mighty One; when born, O Indra, with power thou tcrrifiedst earth and heaven – When, in their fear of thee, all firm-set mountains and monstrous creatures shook like dust before thee.

src: ā yat harī iti indra vi vratā veḥ ā te vajram jaritā bāhvoḥ dhāt yena aviharyatakrato ity aviharyata krato amitrān puraḥ iṣṇāsi puru hūta pūrvīḥ
tgt: When thy two wandering Bays thou drawest hither, thy praiser laid within thine arms the thunder, Wherewith, O Much-invoked, in will resistless, thou smitest foemen down and many a castle.

src: vr̥jane pr̥kṣe āṇau yūne kutsāya dyumate sacā ahan
tgt: Faithful art thou, these thou defiest, Indra; thou art the R̥ibhus' Lord, heroic, victor. Thou, by his side, for young and glorious Kutsa, with steed and car in battle slewest Ṣushṇa,

src: tvam ha tyat indra codīḥ sakhā vr̥tram yat vajrin vr̥ṣa karman ubhnāḥ yat ha śūra vr̥ṣa maṇaḥ parācaiḥ vi dasyūn yonau akr̥taḥ vr̥thāṣāṭ
tgt: That, as a friend, thou furtheredst, O Indra, when, Thunderer, strong in act, thou crushedst Vr̥itra; When, Hero, thou, great-souled, with easy conquest didst rend the Dasyus in their distant dwelling.

src: tvam ha tyat indra ariṣaṇyan dr̥l̥hasya cit martānām ajuṣṭau vi asmat ā kāṣṭhāḥ arvate vaḥ ghanāiva vajrin śnathihi amitrān
tgt: This doest thou, and art not harmed, O Indra, e'en in the anger of the strongest mortal. Lay thou the race-course open for our horses: as with a club, slay, Thunderarmed! our foemen.

src: tvām ha tyat indra arṇa sātau svaḥ mīl̥he naraḥ ājā havante tava svadhāvaḥ iyam ā sa marye ūtiḥ vājeṣu atasāyyā bhūt
tgt: Hence men invoke thee, Indra, in the tumult of battle, in the light-bestowing conflict. This aid of thine, O Godlike One, was ever to be implored in deeds of might in combat.

src: tvam ha tyat indra sapta yudhyan puraḥ vajrin puru kutsāya dardaḥ barhiḥ na yat su dāse vr̥thā varka aṁhoḥ rājan varivaḥ pūrave kaḥ
tgt: Warring for Pûrukutsa thou, O Indra, Thunder-armed I breakest down the seven castles; Easily, for Sudis, like grass didst rend them, and out of need, King, broughtest gain to Pûru.

src: tvam tyām naḥ indra deva citrām iṣam āpaḥ na pīpayaḥ pari jman yayā śūra prati asmabhyam yaṁsi tmanam ūrjam na viśvadha kṣaradhyai
tgt: O Indra, God who movest round about us, feed us with varied food plenteous as water- Food wherewithal, O Hero, thou bestowest vigour itself to flow to us for ever.

src: akāri te indra gotamebhiḥ brahmāṇi āuktā namasā hari bhyām su peśasam vājam ā bhara naḥ prātaḥ makṣu dhiyāvasuḥ jagamyāt
tgt: Prayers have been made by Gotamas, O Indra, addressed to thee, with laud for thy Bay Horses. Bring us in noble shape abundant riches. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

src: vr̥ṣṇe śardhāya su makhāya vedhase nodhaḥ su vr̥ktim pra bhara marut bhyaḥ apaḥ na dhīraḥ manasā su hastyaḥ giraḥ sam añje vidatheṣu ābhuvaḥ
tgt: BRING for the manly host, wise and majestical, O Nodhas, for the Maruts bring thou a pure gift. I deck my songs as one deft-handed, wise in mind prepares the water that hath power in solemn rites.

src: te jajñire divaḥ r̥ṣvāsaḥ ukṣaṇaḥ rudrasya maryā asurāḥ arepasaḥ pāvakāsaḥ śucayaḥ sūryāḥ iva satvānaḥ na drapsinaḥ ghora varpasaḥ
tgt: They spring to birth, the lofty Ones, the Bulls of Heaven, divine, the youths of Rudra, free from spot and stain; The purifiers, shining brightly even as suns, awful of form like giants, scattering rain-drops down.

src: yuvānaḥ rudrāḥ ajarāḥ abhok hanaḥ vavakṣuḥ adhri gāvaḥ parvatāḥ iva dr̥l̥hā cit viśvā bhuvanāni pārthivā pra cyāvayanti divyāni majmanā
tgt: Young Rudras, demon-slayers, never growing old, they have waxed, even as mountains, irresistible. They make all beings tremble with their mighty strength, even the very strongest, both of earth and heaven.

src: citraiḥ añji bhiḥ vapuṣe vi añjate vakṣaḥ su rukmān adhi yetire śubhe aṁseṣu eṣām ni mimr̥kṣuḥ r̥ṣṭayaḥ sākam jajñire svadhayā divaḥ naraḥ
tgt: With glittering ornaments they deck them forth for show; for beauty on their breasts they bind their chains of gold. The lances on their shoulders pound to pieces; they were born together, of themselves, the Men of Heaven.

src: īśāna kr̥taḥ dhunayaḥ riśādasaḥ vātān vi dyutaḥ taviṣībhiḥ akrata duhanti ūdhaḥ divyāni dhūtayaḥ bhūmim pinvanti payasā pari jrayaḥ
tgt: Loud roarers, giving strength, devourers of the foe, they make the winds, they make the lightnings with their powers. The restless shakers drain the udders of the sky, and ever wandering round fill the earth full with milk.

src: pinvanti apaḥ marutaḥ su dānavaḥ payaḥ ghr̥ta vat vidatheṣu ābhuvaḥ atyam na mihe vi nayanti vājinam utsam duhanti stanayantam akṣitam
tgt: The bounteous Maruts with the fatness dropping milk fill full the waters which avail in solenm rites. They lead, as 'twere, the Strong Horse forth, that it may rain: they milk the thundering, the neverfailing spring.

src: mahiṣāsaḥ māyinaḥ citra bhānavaḥ girayaḥ na sva tavasaḥ raghu syadaḥ mr̥gāḥ iva hastinaḥ svādatha vanā yat āruṇīṣu taviṣīḥ ayugdhvam
tgt: Mighty, with wondrous power and marvellously bright, selfstrong like mountains, ye glide swiftly on your way. Like the wild elephants ye eat the forests up when ye assume your strength among the bright red flames.

src: siṁhāḥ iva nānadati pra cetasaḥ piśāḥ iva su piśaḥ viśva vedasaḥ kṣapaḥ jinvantaḥ pr̥ṣatībhiḥ r̥ṣṭi bhiḥ sam it sa bādhaḥ śavasā ahi manyavaḥ
tgt: Exceeding wise they roar like lions mightily, they, all-possessing, are beauteous as antelopes; Stirring the darkness with lances and spotted deer, combined as priests, with serpents' fury through their might.

src: rodasī iti ā vadata gaṇa śriyaḥ nr̥ sācaḥ śūrāḥ śavasā ahi manyavaḥ ā vandhureṣu amatiḥ na darśatā vidyut na tasthau marutaḥ ratheṣu vaḥ
tgt: Heroes who march in companies, befriending man, with serpents' ire through strength, ye greet the earth and heaven. Upon the seats, O Maruts, of your chariots, upon the cars stands lightning visible as light.

src: viśva vedasaḥ rayi bhiḥ sam okasaḥ sam miślāsaḥ taviṣībhiḥ vi rapśinaḥ astāraḥ iṣum dadhire gabhastyoḥ ananta śuṣmāḥ vr̥ṣa khādayaḥ naraḥ
tgt: Lords of all riches, dwelling in the home of wealth, endowed with mighty vigour, singers loud of voice, Heroes, of powers infinite, armed with strong men's rings, the archers, they have laid the arrow on their arms.

src: hiraṇyayebhiḥ pavi bhiḥ payaḥ vr̥dhaḥ ut jighnante āpathyaḥ na parvatān makhāḥ ayāsaḥ sva sr̥taḥ dhruva cyutaḥ dudhra kr̥taḥ marutaḥ bhrājat r̥ṣṭayaḥ
tgt: They who with golden fellies make the rain increase drive forward the big clouds like wanderers on the way. Self-moving, brisk, unwearied, they o'erthrow the firm; the Maruts with bright lances make all things to reel.

src: ghr̥ṣum pāvakam vaninam vi carṣaṇim rudrasya sūnum havasā gr̥ṇīmas i rajaḥ turam tavasam mārutam gaṇam r̥jīṣiṇam vr̥ṣaṇam saścata śriye
tgt: The progeny of Rudra we invoke with prayer, the brisk, the bright, the worshipful, the active Ones To the strong band of Maruts cleave for happiness, the chasers of the sky, impetuous, vigorous.

src: pra nu saḥ martaḥ śavasā janān ati tasthau vaḥ ūtī marutaḥ yam āvata arvat bhiḥ vājam bharate dhanā nr̥ bhiḥ āpr̥cchyam kratum ā kṣeti puṣyati
tgt: Maruts, the man whom ye have guarded with your help, he verily in strength surpasseth all mankind. Spoil with his steeds he gaineth, treasure with his men; he winneth honourable strength and prospereth.

src: carkr̥tyam marutaḥ pr̥t su dustaram dyu mantam śuṣmam maghavat su dhattana dhana spr̥tam ukthyam viśva carṣaṇim tokam puṣyema tanayam śatam himāḥ
tgt: O Maruts, to the worshippers give glorious strength invincible in battle, brilliant, bringing wealth, Praiseworthy, known to all men. May we foster well, during a hundred winters, son and progeny.

src: nu sthiram marutaḥ vīra vantam r̥ti saham rayim asmāsu dhatta sahasriṇam śatinam śūśu vāṁsam prātaḥ makṣu dhiyāvasuḥ jagamyāt
tgt: Will ye then, O ye Maruts, grant us riches, durable, rich in men, defying onslaught. A hundred, thousandfold, ever increasing? May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

src: paśvā na tāyum guhā catantam namaḥ yujānam namaḥ vahantam
tgt: ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow; Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods : there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones.

src: sajoṣāḥ dhīrāḥ padaiḥ anu gman upa tvā sīdan viśve yajatrāḥ
tgt: ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow; Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods : there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones.

src: r̥tasya devāḥ anu vratā guḥ bhuvat pariṣṭiḥ dyauḥ na bhūma
tgt: The Gods approached the ways of holy Law; there was a gathering vast as heaven itself.

src: vardhanti īm āpaḥ panvā su śiśvim r̥tasya yonā garbhe su jātam
tgt: The waters feed with praise the growing Babe, born nobly in the womb, the seat of Law.

src: puṣṭiḥ na raṇvā kṣitiḥ na pr̥thvī giriḥ na bhujma kṣodaḥ na śam bhu
tgt: Like grateful food, like some wide dwelling place, like a fruit-bearing hill, a wholesome stream.

src: atyaḥ na ajman sarga prataktaḥ sindhuḥ na kṣodaḥ kaḥ im varāte
tgt: Like a steed urged to run in swift career, rushing like Sindhu, who may check his course?

src: jāmiḥ sindhūnām bhrātāiva svasrām ibhyān na rājā vanāni atti
tgt: Kin as a brother to his sister floods, he eats the woods as a King eats the rich.

src: yat vāta jūtaḥ vanā vi asthāt agniḥ ha dāti roma pr̥thivyāḥ
tgt: When through the forest, urged by wind, he spreads, verily Agni shears the hair of earth.

src: śvasiti ap su haṁsaḥ na sīdan kratvā cetiṣṭhaḥ viśām uṣaḥ bhut
tgt: Like a swan sitting in the floods he pants wisest in mind mid men he wakes at morn.

src: somaḥ na vedhāḥ r̥ta prajātaḥ paśuḥ na śiśvā vi bhuḥ dūre bhāḥ
tgt: A Sage like Soma, sprung from Law, he grew like some young creature, mighty, shining far.

src: rayiḥ na citrā sūraḥ na sam dr̥k āyuḥ na prāṇaḥ nityaḥ na sūnuḥ
tgt: LIKE the Sun's glance, like wealth of varied sort, like breath which is the life, like one's own son,

src: takvā na bhūrṇiḥ vanā saisakti payaḥ na dhenuḥ śuciḥ vibhāvā
tgt: Like a swift bird, a cow who yields her milk, pure and refulgent to the wood he speeds.

src: dādhāra kṣemam okaḥ na raṇvaḥ yavaḥ na pakvaḥ jetā janānām
tgt: He offers safety like a pleasant home, like ripened corn, the Conqueror of men.

src: r̥ṣiḥ na stubhvā vikṣu pra śastaḥ vājī na prītaḥ vayaḥ dadhāti
tgt: Like a Seer lauding, famed among the folk; like a steed friendly he vouchsafes us power.

src: duroka śociḥ kratuḥ na nityaḥ jāyāiva yonau aram viśvasmai
tgt: With flame insatiate, like eternal might; caring for each one like a dame at home;

src: citraḥ yat abhrāṭ śvetaḥ na vikṣu rathaḥ na rukmī tveṣaḥ samat su
tgt: Bright when he shines forth, whitish mid the folk, like a car, gold-decked, thundering to the fight.

src: senāiva sr̥ṣṭā amam dadhāti astuḥ na didyut tveṣa pratīkā
tgt: He strikes with terror like a dart shot forth, e'en like an archer's arrow tipped with flame;

src: yamaḥ ha jātaḥ yamaḥ jani tvam jāraḥ kanīnām patiḥ janīnām
tgt: Master of present and of future life, the maidens' lover and the matrons' Lord.

src: tam vaḥ carāthā vayam vasatyā astam na gāvaḥ nakṣante iddham
tgt: To him lead all your ways: may we attain the kindled God as cows their home at eve.

src: sindhuḥ na kṣodaḥ pra nīcīḥ ainot navante gāvaḥ svaḥ dr̥śīke
tgt: He drives the flames below as floods their swell: the rays rise up to the fair place of heaven.

src: vaneṣu jāyuḥ marteṣu mitraḥ vr̥ṇīte śruṣtim rājāiva ajuryam
tgt: VICTORIOUS in the wood, Friend among men, ever he claims obedience as a King.

src: kṣemaḥ na sādhuḥ kratuḥ na bhadraḥ bhuvat su ādhīḥ hotā havya vāṭ
tgt: Gracious like peace, blessing like mental power, Priest was he, offering-bearer, full of thought.

src: balinoktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śukro vacanamabravīt | manasvino hi ye śūrāḥ pataṃti samare budhā || 32 || ye śastreṇa hatāḥ sadyo mriyamāṇā vrajaṃti vai | triviṣṭapaṃ na saṃdeha iti vedānuśāsanam || 33 ||
tgt: 32-33. On hearing the words uttered by Bali, Śukra spoke these words: “Those heroic persons who are high-souled and intelligent, who are learned, and who fall down dead in battle on being struck by a weapon go to heaven. This is undoubtedly the statement of the Vedas.”

src: evamāśvāsayāmāsa balinaṃ bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ | tapastatāpa vividhaṃ daityānāṃ siddhidāyakam || 34 ||
tgt: 34. Thus, the son of Bhṛgu consoled Bali. He then performed various kinds of penance conducive to the achievement of Siddhis by Daityas.

src: tathā daitya gatāḥ sarve bhṛguṇā ca pracoditāḥ | pātālamavasansarve balimukhyāḥ sukhena vai || 35 ||
tgt: 35. All the Daityas urged by Bhṛgu went to Pātāla. All the Daityas, the chief among whom was Bali, stayed in Pātāla in happiness. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES: Arthaśāstra—A treatise on political economy. It is the title of a famous work of Kauṭilya or Ārya Cāṇakya who masterminded the revolution in Pāṭalīputra (Magadha), uprooted the Nanda dynasty and installed Candragupta Maurya as the King. Kauṭilya refers to many predecessors. Hence the Arthaśāstra mentioned here may be a more ancient work than that of Kauṭilya.[Sanskrit text for this chapter is available]

src: | ṛṣaya ūcuḥ | rājyaṃ prāpto hi deveṃdraḥ kathitaste guruṃ vinā | guroravajñayā jāto rājyabhraṃśo hi tasya tu || 1 || kena praṇoditaśceṃdro babhūva ciramāsane | tatsarvaṃ kathayāśu tvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ || 2 ||
tgt: The sages enquired: 1-2. It has been mentioned by you that Devendra regained kingdom without his preceptor. It was on account of disrespect to his preceptor that he had been dethroned from his kingdom. Urged by whom did he retain his position for a long time? Do tell us all these things quickly. We are very eager to hear it.

src: lomaśa uvāca | guruṇāpi vinā rājyaṃ kṛtavānsa śacīpatiḥ | viśvarūpoktavidhinā iṃdro rājye sthito mahān || 3 ||
tgt: Lomaśa replied: 3-4. The consort of Śacī (Indra) ruled over the kingdom (of heaven) without his preceptor (Bṛhaspati). The great Indra (could) continue (to rule) over the kingdom due to the (religious) performance in accordance with the injunctions of Viśvarūpa.

src: viśvakarmasuto viprā viśvarūpo mahānṛpaḥ | purohito'tha śakrasya yājakaścābhavattadā || 4 ||
tgt: 5-6. O Brāhmaṇas, Viśvarūpa,[1] a great king, was the son of Viśvakarmā. He became the preceptor and performer of sacrifices for Śakra.

src: tasminyajñe'vadānaiśca yajane asurānsurān | manuṣyāṃścaiva triśirā aparokṣaṃ śacīpateḥ || 5 ||
tgt: In that Yajña, Triśiras (one with three heads) performed the worship with partial oblations separately for Asuras, Suras and human beings.

src: devāndadāti sākrośaṃ daityāṃstūṣṇīmathādadāt | manuṣyānmadhyapātena pratyahaṃ sa grahāndvijaḥ || 6 ||
tgt: In the direct presence of Indra everyday he used to give ladles (full of Soma) to Devas with a loud shout, to Daityas silently, and to human being in a fallen middle tone.

src: ekadā tu maheṃdreṇa sūcito gurulāghavāt | alakṣyamāṇena tadā jñātaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam || 7 ||
tgt: 7-8. Once he was detected due to his partiality (regarding relative importance of oblations) by Indra who remained concealed and unobserved. Then the desired object (of Triśiras) was understood (by Indra).

src: daityānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthamavadānaṃ prayacchati | asau purohito'smākaṃ pareṣāṃ ca phalapradaḥ || 8 ||
tgt: (Deveṇdra thought) ‘He is making this piecemeal offering for the sake of accomplishing the task of Daityas. He is our preceptor, but gives the benefit to (our) enemies.’

src: iti matvā tadā śakro vajreṇa śataparvaṇā | ciccheda tacchirāṃsyeva tatkṣaṇādabhavadvadhaḥ || 9 ||
tgt: 9. After thinking thus, Śakra cut off his heads instantaneously by means of his Vajra (thunderbolt) of hundred spikes. The death was instantaneous.

src: yenākarotsomapānamajāyaṃta kapiṃjalāḥ | tatonyena surāpānātkalaviṃkā bhavanmukhāt || 10 || anyānanādajāyaṃta tittirā viśvarūpiṇaḥ | evaṃ hato viśvarūpaḥ śakreṇa maṃdabhāginā || 11 ||
tgt: 10-11. The Kapiñjala (a sort of partridge) birds were born from the face with which he drank Soma juice. Then from the other face with which-he drank liquor, the Kalaviṅka (sparrow) birds were born. From the other (third) face, the Tittira birds of various forms were born. Thus, Viśvarūpa was killed by Śakra, the ill-fated one.

src: brahmahatyā tadodbhūtā durdharṣā ca bhayāvahā | durdharṣā durmukhā duṣṭā caṇḍālarajasānvitā || 12 ||
tgt: 12-14. The female fiend (born of and called) Brahmahatyā (‘Brāhmaṇa-murder’) manifested there. She was terrific and unthwartable. She was evil-faced, wicked, full of Cāṇḍāla impurity and could not be blocked or defeated.

src: brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṃganāgamaḥ | ityeṣāmapyaghavatāmidameva ca niṣkṛtiḥ || 13 ||
tgt: The terrible sinners are those who slay Brāhmaṇas, those who drink liquor, those who steal (gold etc.) and those who defile and outrage the modesty of the preceptor’s wife. The means of expiation for these sinners is the utterance of the names of Viṣṇu, since the mind has him for its object.

src: nāmavyāharaṇaṃ viṣṇoryatastadviṣayā matiḥ | triśirā dhūmrahastā sā śakraṃ grastumupāyayau || 14 ||
tgt: The three-headed fiend with smoke-coloured hands rushed forth to swallow Indra.

src: tato bhayena mahatā palāyanaparo'bhavat | palāyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā hyanuyātā bhayāvahā || 15 ||
tgt: 15. Thereupon (Indra) fled from there out of great fear. On seeing him fleeing, the terrible (devil) chased him.

src: yato dhāvati sā'dhāvattiṣṭhaṃtamanutiṣṭhati | aṃgakṛtā yathā chāyā śakrasyapariveṣṭitum | āyāti tāvatsahasā iṃdro'pyapsu nyamajjata || 16 || śīghratvena yathā viprāściraṃtanajalecaraḥ || 17 ||
tgt: 16-17. Wherever he ran, she too ran after him. If he stood anywhere, she too stood beside him. She behaved in the manner of a shadow of one’s own body. When she came so close as to envelop him, Indra sank beneath the waters suddenly, O Brāhmaṇas, like an old aquatic being.

src: evaṃ divyaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ varṣāṇāṃ ca śacīpateḥ | vasatastasya duḥkhena tathā caiva śatadvayam | arājakaṃ tadā jātaṃ nākapṛṣṭhe bhayāvaham || 18 || tadā ciṃtānvitā devā ṛṣayo'pi tapasvinaḥ | trailokyaṃ cā'padā grastaṃ babhūva ca tadā dvijāḥ || 19 ||
tgt: 18-19. Thus three hundred divine years passed since the consort of Śacī (Indra) began staying (beneath the waters) with great misery. A terrific state of anarchy spread throughout heaven. Thereupon Devas, sages and ascetics became anxious and worried. All the three worlds were overwhelmed by adversity, O Brāhmaṇas.

src: eko'pi brahmahā yatra rāṣṭre vasati nirbhayaḥ | akālamaraṇaṃ tatra sādhūnāmupajāyate || 20 ||
tgt: 20. Even if there is a single Brāhmaṇa-slayer in a kingdom staying there with impunity, untimely death of good men will take place there.

src: rājā pāpayuto yasminrāṣṭre vasati tatra vai | durbhikṣaṃ caiva maraṇaṃ tathaivopadravā dvijāḥ || 21 ||
tgt: 21. The king of the state wherein he (the Brāhmaṇa-slayer) lives, becomes contaminated by the sin. There will be (prevalence of) famine, death and calamities.

src: bhavaṃti bahavo'narthāḥ prajānāṃ nāśahetave | tasmādrājñā tu kartavyo dharmmaḥ śraddhāpareṇa hi || 22 ||
tgt: 22. There will be many misfortunes causing the destruction of the subjects. Hence, Dharma should be practised by a king with great faith.

src: tathā prakṛtayo rājñaḥ śucajitvena pratiṣṭhitāḥ | indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tena pāpena vai dvijāḥ | nānāvidhairmahātāpaiḥ sopadravamabhūjjagat || 23 ||
tgt: 23. Similarly, the ministers of the king too should be installed with purity. Sin was committeed by Indra and due to that sin, O Brāhmaṇas, the whole of the universe met with calamities along with great distress of diverse kinds.

src: śaunaka uvāca | aśvamedhaśatenaiva prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mahattaram | devānāmakhilaṃ sūta kasmādvighramajāyata | śakrasya ca mahābhāga yathāvatkathayasva na || 24 ||
tgt: Śaunaka enquired: 24. It was by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices that the great realm of Devas was acquired by him, O Sūta. Why then did Śakra meet with obstacles, O highly fortunate one? Do tell us exactly as it happened.

src: sūta uvāca | devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ | karmmaiva sukhaduḥkhānāṃ hetubhūtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 25 ||
tgt: Sūta replied: 25. In the case of Devas, Dānavas and particularly that of human beings, Karman alone is undoubtedly the cause of happiness and misery.

src: indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ viprā mahadbhūtaṃ jugupsitam | guroravajñā ca kṛtā viśvarūpavadhaḥ kṛtaḥ || 26 || gautamasya guroḥ patnī sevitā tasya tatphalam | prāptaṃ maheṃdreṇa ciraṃ yasya nāsti pratikriyā || 27 ||
tgt: 26-27. An immensely reprehensible act has been committed by Indra, O Brāhmaṇas, He insulted his Guru (preceptor Bṛhaspati). Viśvarūpa was slain. The wife of Gautama, his Guru (preceptor, elderly one), was carnally approached. It was the fruit of all these sins that was reaped by Mahendra for a long time. There was no way of atonement for the same.

src: ye hi dṛṣkaṭatakarmmāṇo na kurvaṃti ca niṣkṛtim | durdaśāṃ prapnuvantyete yathaivendraḥ śatakratuḥ || 28 ||
tgt: 28. If persons committing wicked and sinful deeds, do not perform expiatory rites (for the same), they do incur miseries just like Indra, (though) he had performed a hundred sacrifices.

src: duṣkṛtopārjitasyā taḥ prāyāścittaṃ hi tatkṣaṇāt | kartavyaṃ vidhivadviprāḥ sarvapāpopaśāṃtaye || 29 ||
tgt: 29. If sins are committed, atonement should be performed instantaneously in accordance with the injunctions, O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of quelling all the sins.

src: tataḥ svadharmaniṣṭhāṃ ca ye kurvaṃti sadā narāḥ | prātarmadhyāhnasāyāhne teṣāṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyati || 31 || prāpnuvaṃtyuttamaṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā | tasmādasau durācāraḥ prāpte vai karmaṇaḥ phalam || 32 ||
tgt: 30-32. If minor sins are repeatedly performed, they turn into major sins. Those men who steadfastly cling to their duties of the morning, midday and dusk can get their sins destroyed. They attain the excellent world. There is no doubt about it. Hence, this person of evil conduct (i.e. Indra) reaped the fruit of his karman.

src: sa pradhārya tadā sarve lokapālāstvarānvitāḥ | bṛhaspatimupāgamya sarvamātmani dhiṣṭhitam | kathayāmāsuravyagrā iṃdrasya ca guruṃ prati || 33 ||
tgt: 33. All the Guardians of the Quarters hurriedly deliberated together. They approached Bṛhaspati and reported to the preceptor about Indra everything they had in their mind.

src: devairuktaṃ vaco viprā niśamya ca bṛhaspatiḥ | arājakaṃ ca saṃprāptaṃ ciṃtayāmāsa buddhimān || 34 ||
tgt: 34. On hearing the words uttered by Devas, Bṛhaspati, the intelligent (preceptor), thought about the anarchy that had begun to spread.

src: kiṃ kāryaṃ cādya kartavyaṃ kathaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati | devānāṃ cādya lokānāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām || 35 || manasaiva ca tatsarvaṃ kāryākāryaṃ vicārya ca | jagāma śakraṃ tvarito devaiḥ saha mahāyaśāḥ || 36 ||
tgt: 35-36. ‘What shall be done now? How will they secure welfare—Devas, the worlds and sages of sanctified souls?’ In his mind, he thought over the details of what should and what should not be done. Accompanied by Devas, the preceptor of great fame went to Indra.

src: prāpto jalāśayaṃ taṃ ca yatrāste hi puraṃdaraḥ | yasya tīre sthitā hatyā caṃḍālīva bhayāvahā || 37 ||
tgt: 37. They reached the lake where Purandara (Indra) was lying (hidden) and on the bank of which was staying the (devil of) Brāhmaṇa slaughter terrible like a Caṇḍālī.

src: tatroviṣṭāste sarve devā ṛṣigaṇānvitāḥ | āhvānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tasya śakrasya guruṇā svayam || 38 ||
tgt: 38. All the Devas, accompanied by the groups of sages sat there. Then Śakra was called by the preceptor himself.

src: samutthitastataḥ śakro dadarśa svaguruṃ tadā | bāṣpapūritavaktro hi bṛhaspatimabhāṣata || 39 ||
tgt: 39. Thereupon, Indra got up and saw his preceptor. With tears flowing over his face, he spoke to Bṛhaspati.

src: praṇipatya ca tatratyānkṛtāñjalirabhāṣata | tadā dīnamukho bhūtvā manasā saṃvimṛśya ca || 40 || svayameva kṛtaṃ pūrvamajñānalakṣaṇaṃ mahat | adhunaiva mayā kāryaṃ kiṃ kartavyaṃ vada prabho || 41 ||
tgt: 40-41. He bowed down to all the persons assembled there. He pondered over the great (blunders) committed by himself before, as a result of ignorance. He joined his palms in reverence and with a piteous face spoke: “O Lord, tell me what should be done by me just now?”

src: prahasyovāca bhagavānbṛhaspati rudāradhīḥ | purā tvayā kṛtaṃ yacca tasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam || 42 || māṃ ca uddiśya bho iṃdra tadbhogādeva saṃkṣayaḥ | prāyaścitaṃ hi hatyāyā na dṛṣṭaṃ smṛtikāribhiḥ || 43 ||
tgt: 42-43. The holy lord Bṛhaspati of liberal mind laughed and said: “O Indra, this is the result of that act of yours committed previously against me. Only by experiencing its result, can it be annihilated. But, no atonement for Brāhmaṇa-slaughter has been seen (i.e. laid down) by the authors of Smṛti texts.

src: ajñānato hi yajjātaṃ pāpaṃ tasya pratikriyā | kathitā dharmmaśāstrajñaiḥ sakāmasya na vidyate || 44 ||
tgt: 44. Expiation has been prescribed by those conversant with Dharma Śāstras (Code of Laws) for the sin committed unknowingly. There is no atonement for an offence wilfully committed.

src: sakāmena kṛtaṃ pāpamakāmaṃ naiva jāyate | tābhyāṃ viṣayabhedena prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 45 ||
tgt: 45. A sin committed by a person intentionally does not become one committed unintentionally. Expiation is laid down for both based on the differences in the objects.

src: maraṇāṃto vidhiḥ kāryo kāmena hi kṛtena hi | ajñānajanite pāpe prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 46 ||
tgt: 46. If a sin is committed wilfully (deliberately), the expiation is to be performed up to death. Atonement is laid down in case of sins committed unknowingly.

src: tasmāttvayā kṛtaṃ yacca svayameva hato dvijaḥ | purohitaśca vidvāṃśca tasmānnāsti pratikriyā || 47 ||
tgt: 47. Since this has been intentionally done by you, since the twice-born, the learned priest has been killed, there is no atonement.

src: yāvanmaraṇamapyeti tāvadapsu sthiro bhava || 48 ||
tgt: 48. Stay in the waters here and wait for your death.

src: śatāśvamedhasaṃjñaṃ ca yatphalaṃ tava durmate | tannaṣṭaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva ghātito hi dvijo yadā || 49 ||
tgt: 49. The meritorious deed of yours termed ‘performance of one hundred horse-sacrifices’, O evil-minded one, has already been destroyed at the very moment when the twice-born was killed by you.

src: sacchidre ca yathā toyaṃ na tiṣṭhati ghaṭe'ṇvapi | tathaiva sukṛtaṃ pāpe hīyate ca pradakṣiṇam || 50 ||
tgt: 50. Just as not a drop of water remains in a pot with holes, similarly meritorious deeds of a sinner go on reducing every moment.

src: tasmācca daivasaṃyogātprāptaṃ svargādikaṃ ca yaiḥ | yathoktaṃ tadbhavetteṣāṃ dharmiṣṭhānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 51 ||
tgt: 51. Hence, by good luck, if heaven etc. are attained, those can be retained only by really righteous ones. There is no doubt about it.”

src: etacchrutvā vacastasya śakro vacanamabravīt | kukarmaṇā madīyena prāptametanna saṃśayaḥ || 52 ||
tgt: 52. On hearing his statement, Indra spoke these words: “Undoubtedly this has fallen to my lot through my own misdeeds.

src: amarāvatī māśu tvaṃ gaccha devarṣibiḥ saha | lokānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthe devānāṃ ca bṛhaspate | iṃdraṃ kuru mahābhāga yaste manasi rocate || 53 ||
tgt: 53. Hasten to Amarāvatī along with the celestial sages, O Bṛhaspati. For the purpose of accomplishing the tasks of the worlds as well as of Devas, O sage of great fortune, crown as Indra, anyone whom you approve in your mind.

src: yathā mṛtastathā haṃ vai brahmahatyāvṛto mahān | rāgadveṣasamutthena pāpenāsmi pariplutaḥ || 54 ||
tgt: 54. Enveloped by the great devil of Brahmahatyā, I am just like one who is dead. I have been overwhelmed by the sin arising from Rāga (attachment) and Dveṣa (hatred).

src: tasmāttvarānvitā yūyaṃ devarājānamāśuḥ vai | kurvatu madanujñātāḥ satyaṃ prativadāmi vaḥ || 55 ||
tgt: 55. Hence hasten all of you to make someone king of Devas. You have my permission for the same. I am speaking the truth to you.”

src: evamuktāstadā sarve bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ | etyāmarāvatīṃ tūrṇaṃ puraṃdaraviceṣṭitam | kathayāmāsuravyagrā śacīṃ prati yathā tathā || 56 ||
tgt: 56. On being told thus, all those (Devas) with Bṛhaspati at their head came to Amarāvatī immediately and coolly told Śacī everything about Indra’s activities as they had taken place.

src: rājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ vimṛśaṃtaḥ parasparam || 57 ||
tgt: 57. They consulted one another and began to deliberate thus: ‘What should be done for the sake of the kingdom?’

src: evaṃ vimṛśyamānānāṃ devānāṃ tatra nāradaḥ | yadṛcchayāgatastatra devarṣiramitadyutiḥ || 58 ||
tgt: 58. While Devas were thus deliberating, Nārada, the celestial sage of unmeasured splendour, came there by chance.

src: uvāca pūjito devānkasmādyūyaṃ vicetasaḥ | tenoktāḥ kathayāmāsuḥ sarvaṃ śakrasya ceṣṭitam || 59 ||
tgt: 59. On being honoured, he asked Devas: “Why are you all sad and perplexed?” On being enquired (thus) they spoke everything about Śakra’s activities:

src: gatamiṃdrasya ceṃdratvamenasā parameṇa tu | tataḥ provāca tāndevāndevarṣirnārado vacaḥ || 60 ||
tgt: 60. “Indra’s status of being the lord (of Devas) has come to an end on account of a great sin.” Thereupon Nārada, the celestial sage, spoke these words to those Devas:

src: yūyaṃ devāśca sarvajñāstapasā vikrameṇa ca | tasmādiṃdro hi kartavyo nahuṣaḥ somavaṃśajaḥ || 61 || so'sminrāṣṭre pratiṣṭhāpyastvaritenaiva nirjarāḥ | ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ tena mahātmanā | kṛtamasti mahābhāgā nahuṣeṇa ca yajvanā || 62 ||
tgt: 61-62. “You are omniscient Devas endowed with the power of penance and valour. Hence Nahuṣa,[2] born in the Lunar race, should be made Indra. He should be established in this realm, O Devas, immediately. Ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed by that noble-souled Nahuṣa, O highly fortunate ones. Nahuṣa was a regular performer of Yajñas

src: śacyā śrutaṃ ca tadvākyaṃ nāradasya mukhodgatam | gatāṃtaḥpuramavyagrā bāṣpapūritalocanā || 63 ||
tgt: 63-67. That statement coming out of the mouth of Nārada was heard by Sacī. With her eyes filled with tears and not engaged in anything (seriously), she went into the inner apartment.

src: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve devānvamodayan || 64 || nahuṣaṃ rājyamāroḍhumaikapadyena te yadā | ānīto hi tadā rājā nahuṣo hyamarāvatīm || 65 || rājyaṃ dattaṃ maheṃdrasya suraiḥ sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ | tadāgastyādayaḥ sarve nahuṣaṃ paryupāsata || 66 ||
tgt: On hearing the words of Nārada, all the Devas congratulated him. They approved of his suggestion to make Nahuṣa the ruler of the realm unanimously. Then, king Nahuṣa was brought to Amarāvatī and the kingdom of Mahendra was given to him by all the Suras and great sages.

src: gaṃdharvāpsaraso yakṣā vidyādharamahoragāḥ | yakṣāḥ suparṇāḥ patagā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ || 67 ||
tgt: Then all of them served Nahuṣa. Agastya and others (sages), Gandharvas, Apsarās, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, the great serpents, Rākṣasas, the birds of bright wings (suparṇas like Garuḍa) and other heaven-dwellers (served him).

src: tadā mahotsavo jāto devapuryāṃ niraṃtaraḥ | śaṃkhatūryamṛdaṃgāni nedurduṃdubhayaḥ samam || 68 ||
tgt: 68. Then in the city of Devas, there was a continuous grand celebration. Concḥs, musical instruments, Mṛdaṅgas and Dundubhis sounded simultaneously.

src: gāyakāśca jagustatra tathā vādyāni vādakāḥ | nartakā nanṛtustatra tathā rājyamahotsave || 69 ||
tgt: 69. In that grand celebration of the kingdom of Devas, musicians sang songs, players of instruments played on them and dancers danced.

src: abhiṣiktastadā tatra bṛhaspatipurogamaiḥ || 70 ||
tgt: 70. Then he was coronated there by the sages, of whom Bṛhaspati was the foremost.

src: arcito devasūktaiśca yathā vadgrahapūjanam | kṛtavāṃścaiva ṛṣibhirvidvadbhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ || 71 ||
tgt: 71. He was worshipped with Deva-Sūkta and was made to perform the worship of Planets in due procedure and with formalities.

src: tathā ca sarvaiḥ paripūjito mahānrājā surāṇāṃ nahuṣastadānīm | iṃdrāsane ceṃd samānarūpaḥ saṃstūyamānaḥ parameṇa varcasā || 72 ||
tgt: 72. The great king Nahuṣa was duly honoured and respected by the learned sages of sanctified souls and by all others also. As the king of Suras, he sat on the throne of Indra. He had the same features as those of Indra. Endowed with the greatest splendour, he was eulogized by all.

src: sugaṃdhadīpaiśca suvāsasā yuto'laṃkārabhogaiḥ suvirājitāṃgaḥ | babhau tadānīṃ nahuṣo munīdraiḥ saṃstūyamāno hi tathā'mareṃdraiḥ || 73 ||
tgt: 73. Dressed in excellent sweet-scented bright garments and with his person adorned excellently with ornaments and articles of enjoyment, Nahuṣa appeared resplendent as he was being eulogized by prominent sages and leading Devas.

src: iti paramakalānvito'sau suramunivaragaṇaiśca pūjyamānaḥ | nahuṣanṛpavaro'bhavattadānīṃ hṛdi mahatā hṛcchayenataptaḥ || 74 ||
tgt: 74. Thus the great king Nahuṣa who was endowed with great ingenuity and worshipped by groups of great Devas and sages, became severely tormented at heart by intense passion (lust).

src: nahuṣa uvāca | iṃdrāṇī kathamadyaiva nāyāti mama sannidhau | tāṃ cāhvayata śīghraṃ bho mā vilaṃbitumarhatha || 75 ||
tgt: Nahuṣa said: 75. How is it that Indrāṇī does not come near me? Call her quickly. It does not behove you to delay.

src: nahupasya vacaḥ śrutvā bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ | śacībhavanamāsādya uvāca ca savistaram || 76 ||
tgt: 76. On hearing the words of Nahuṣa, the liberal-minded Bṛhaspati went to Śacī’s abode and spoke in detail:

src: śakrasya durnimittena hyanīto nahuṣo'tra vai | rājyārte bhāmini tvaṃ ca arddhāsanagatā bhava || 77 ||
tgt: 77. “It was on account of the calamity fallen on Indra that Nahuṣa was brought here for the sake of the kingdom. O beautiful lady, occupy half of his seat.”

src: śacī prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalmaṣam | asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ | ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ kṛtamanena vai || 78 || tasmānna yogyo prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalpaṇaṣam | asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ | avāhyavāhanenaiva atrāgatya labheta mām || 79 ||
tgt: 78-79. Śacī laughed and spoke to sinless Bṛhaspati: “He has occupied the seat of Indra without completing the quota of (hundred) Yajñas. Only ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed by him. Hence, he is not qualified enough to obtain me. Let this be thought over truthfully. If this senseless fellow still continues to be desirous of me, wife of another person, let him obtain me by coming here by means of a vehicle that is carried by undeserving carriers.”

src: tatheti gatvā tvarito bṛhaspatiruvāca tam | nahuṣaṃ kāmasaṃtaptaṃ śacyoktaṃ ca yathātatham || 80 ||
tgt: 80. Saying “So be it”, Bṛhaspati returned hurriedly to Nahuṣa who had been distressed through intense lust. He reported to him what was spoken by Śacī in her own words.

src: tatheti matvā rājāsau nahuṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ | vimṛśya parayā buddhyā avāhyaṃ kiṃ praśasyate || 81 || sa buddhyā ca ciraṃ smṛtvā brāhmaṇāścatapasvinaḥ | avāhyāśca bhavaṃtyasmādātmānaṃ vāhayāmyaham || 82 || dvābhyāṃ ca tasyāḥ prāptyarthamiti me hṛdi vartate | śibikāṃ ca dadau tābhyāṃ dvijābhyāṃ kāmamohitaḥ || 83 ||
tgt: 81-84. Saying “So be it”, Nahuṣa who was deluded by lust, thought over it. He deliberated on this intelligently: ‘Who can be the carrier not worthy of being so?’ After thinking about it intelligently and trying to remember for a long time (he decided thus): “The Brāhmaṇas and the ascetics are not usually thought of as carriers. I shall make two of them bear me in order to reach her. This is my decision.” So (the king) who was deluded by lust gave the palanquin to two Brāhmaṇas.

src: upaviśya tadā tasyāṃ śivabikāyāṃ samāhitaḥ | sarpasarpeti vacanānnodayāmāsa tau tadā || 84 ||
tgt: Seated in that palanquin with great concentration, he urged them on with the words “Sarpa, sarpa” (Move on, move on). (Sarpa means ‘serpent’ also.)

src: agastyaḥ śibikāvāhī tataḥ kruddho'śapannṛpam | viprāṇāmavamaṃtā tvamunmatto'jagaro bhava || 85 ||
tgt: 85. Agastya who had been one of the palanquin-bearers became infuriated and cursed the king. “You are a lunatic and despiser of Brāhmaṇas; you be a python.”

src: śāpoktimātrato rājā patito brāhmaṇasya hi | tatraivājagaro bhūtvā vipraśāpo duratyayaḥ || 86 ||
tgt: 86. Immediately, after the utterance of the curse by the Brāhmaṇa, the king became a python and fell from there itself. Indeed the curse of a Brāhmaṇa is untransgressable.

src: yathā hi nahuṣo jātastathā sarve'pi tādṛśāḥ | viprāṇāmavamānena patinti niraye'śucau || 87 ||
tgt: 87. Just as Nahuṣa became (a python), so also all like him fell into dirty hell by disrespecting Brāhmaṇas.

src: tasmāsarvaprayatnena padaṃ prāpya vicakṣaṇaiḥ | apramattairnarairbhāvyamihāmutra ca labdhaye || 88 ||
tgt: 88. Hence, in order to attain benefits here and hereafter, a wise, circumspect person who has achieved a position of importance, should refrain in all possible ways from committing blunders.

src: tathaiva nahuṣaḥ sarppo jātoraṇye mahābhaye | evaṃ caivābhavattatra devaloke hyarājakam || 89 ||
tgt: 89. Nahuṣa became a serpent in a very dreadful forest. Hence there prevailed anarchy in the world of Devas.

src: tathaiva te surāḥ sarve vismayāviṣṭacetasaḥ | aho bata mahatkaṣṭaṃ prāptaṃ rājñā hyanena vai || 90 ||
tgt: 90. Similarly, all the Devas were struck with consternation. “Alas! What a wretched condition the king has fallen into!

src: na martya loko na svargo jāto hyasya durātmanaḥ | satāmavajñayā sadyaḥ sukṛtaṃ dagdhameva hi || 91 ||
tgt: 91. This evil-minded fellow has obtained neither the mortal world nor the heavenly world. His (fund of) merits has been instantaneously burnt down,

src: yājñiko hyaparo loke kathyatāṃ ca mahāmune | tadovāca mahātejā nārado munisattamaḥ || 92 ||
tgt: 92. If there is any other person who has performed (many) Yajñas, let him be named, O great sage.” Then the excellent sage Nārada of great splendour said:

src: yayātiṃ ca mahābhāgā ānayadhvaṃ tvarānvitāḥ | devadūtāstu vai tūrṇaṃ yayātiṃ drutamānayan || 93 ||
tgt: 93. “O highly fortunate ones, hasten to bring Yayāti.[3]” Messengers of Devas went immediately and brought Yayāti quickly.

src: kva gamiṣyati caṃdro'yaṃ vijaye pṛccha satvaram | tayoktā vijayā devī taṃ papraccha yathocitam || 40 ||
tgt: She said to her maid Vijayā, “Where is Candra going now? O Vijayā, go and enquire immediately.” On being thus instructed by her, the gentle lady Vijayā asked him suitably.

src: kathitaṃ tena tatsarvaṃ dakṣasyaiva makhādikam | tacchrutvā tvaritā devī vijayā jātasaṃbhramā | kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ yaduktaṃ śaśinā bhṛśam || 41 ||
tgt: 41. Everything about Dakṣa’s sacrifice and other things were told by him. On hearing it the gentle lady Vijayā became agitated. Hurriedly (she went to Satī) and told her everything exactly as it was said by the Moon-god.

src: vimṛśya kāraṇaṃ devī kimāhvānaṃ karoti na | dakṣaḥ pitā me mātā ca vismṛtā māṃ kuto'dhunā || 42 || pṛcchāmi śaṃkaraṃ cādya kāraṇaṃ kṛtaniścayā | sthāpayitvā sakhīstatra āgatā śaṃkaraṃ prati || 43 ||
tgt: 42-43. The goddess began to ponder over the reason thus: ‘Why does he not invite (us)? Dakṣa is my father. Why has my mother forgotten me now? I shall ask Śaṅkara now about the reason (thereof).’ After deciding thus, she asked the friends to stay there and approached Śaṅkara.

src: dadarśataṃ sabhāmadhye trilocanamavasthitam | gaṇaiḥ parivṛtaṃ sarvaiścaṃḍamuṃḍādibhistadā || 44 || bāṇo bhṛṃgistathā naṃdī śailādo hi mahātapāḥ | mahākālo mahācaṃḍo mahāmuṃḍo mahāśirāḥ || 45 || dhūmrākṣo dhūmraketuśca dhūmrapādastathaiva ca | ete cānye ca bahavo gaṇā rudrānuvartinaḥ || 46 ||
tgt: 44-49. She saw the Three-eyed Lord in the centre of the assembly stationed there, in an extremely wonderful seat, and surrounded by all his Gaṇas (attendants) beginning with Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, Bāṇa, Bhṛṅgin, Nandin of great power of penance, the son of Śilāda, Mahākāla, Mahācaṇḍa. Mahāmuṇḍa, Mahāśiras, Dhūmrākṣa, Dhūmraketu and Dhūmrapāda—these and many other Gaṇas, the followers of Rudra, (were present there). Some were hideous and terrifying. Others were mere headless trunks. Some had no eyes. Others were devoid of chests. There were hundreds like these. All of them had elephant-hides for their clothes. Clusters of matted hair were their ornaments. All were adorned with Rudrākṣa beads. They were devoid of attachment, They had conquered their sense-organs. They, were antagonistic to objects of sensual pleasure. Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, was seen by her surrounded by all these.

src: ākṣiptacittā sahasā jagāma śivasaṃnidhim | śivena sthāpitā svāṃke prītiyuktena vallabhā || 50 || premṇoditā vacobhiḥ sā bahumānapuraḥsaram | kimāgamanakāryaṃme vada śīghraṃ sumadhyame || 51 ||
tgt: 50-52. Bewildered in her mind, she suddenly went to Śiva’s presence. The beloved wife was placed in his lap by Śiva who was pleased. She was addressed with loving words with due respect: “O lady of excellent waistline, what is the purpose of your arrival? Tell me quickly.”

src: evamuktā tadā tena uvācāsitalocanā || 52 ||
tgt: On being spoken thus by him, the dark-eyed lady said:

src: satyuvāca | piturmama mahāyajñe kasmāttava na rocate | gamanaṃ devadevaśa tatsarvaṃ kathaya prabho || 53 ||
tgt: Satī said: 53. O lord, O lord of the chiefs of Devas, how is it that going to the great sacrifice of my father is not approved of by you? Tell (me) everything.

src: suhṛdāmeṣa vai dharmaḥ suhṛdbhiḥ saha saṃgatim | kurvaṃti yanmahādeva suhṛdāṃ prītivardhinīm || 54 || tasamātsarvaprayatnena anāhūto'pi gaccha bhoḥ | yajñavāṭaṃ piturme'dya vacanānme sadāśiva || 55 ||
tgt: 54-55. This is the duty of friends, O Mahādeva, that they (regularly) associate with their friends, thereby increasing the pleasure and love of their friends. Hence make all efforts (to be present there). Oh, go there even if you have not been invited. Go to the sacrificial enclosure of my father today at my request, O Sadāśiva.

src: tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā ba bhāṣe sūnṛtaṃ vacaḥ | tvayā bhadre na gaṃtavyaṃ dakṣasya yajanaṃ prati || 56 ||
tgt: 56-57. On hearing her words (Śiva) spoke these kind and sincere words:

src: tasya ye māninaḥ sarve sasurāsukiṃnarāḥ | te sreva yajanaṃ prāptāḥ pitustava na saṃśayaḥ || 57 ||
tgt: “O gentle lady, you must not go to the sacrifice of Dakṣa. All those persons who honour Dakṣa, including Suras, Asuras and Kinnaras, have undoubtedly gone to the sacrifice of your father.

src: anāhūtāśca ye subhru gacchaṃti paramandiram | apamānaṃ prāpnuvanti maraṇādadhikaṃ tataḥ || 58 || pareṣāṃ maṃdiraṃ prāpta iṃdropi laghutāṃ vrajet | tasmāttvāyā na gaṃtavyaṃ dakṣasya yajanaṃ śubhe || 59 ||
tgt: 58-59. O lady of fine eyebrows, those who go to others’ mansions without being invited, meet with insult which is more (painful) than death. Even Indra who goes to the abode of others meets with contempt and disrespect. Hence, O splendid lady, you must not go to Dakṣa’s sacrifice.”

src: evamuktā satī tena maheśena mahātmanā | uvāca roṣasaṃyuktaṃ vākyaṃ vākyavidāṃ varā || 60 ||
tgt: 60. On being told thus by the noble-souled Śiva, Satī, the most excellent one among those who are conversant with modes of expression, spoke these words full of anger:

src: yajño hi satyaṃ loke tvaṃ sa tvaṃ devavareśvara | anāhūto'si tenādya pitrā me dṛṣṭacāriṇā | tatsarvaṃ jñātumicchāmi tasya bhāvaṃ durātmanaḥ || 61 ||
tgt: 61. “It is true that you are (the real) Yajña in this world, O most excellent lord of Devas. (How is it) that you have not been invited by my father of evil conduct today? Hence I wish to know thoroughly the attitude of that evil-minded one.

src: tasmāccādyaiva gacchāmi yajñavāḍaṃ piturmmama | anujñāṃ dehi me nātha devadeva jagatpate || 62 ||
tgt: 62. Hence I shall go to the sacrificial enclosure of my father today itself. Grant me permission, O my lord, lord of the universe, lord of Devas.”

src: ityukto bhagavānrudrastayā devyā śivaḥ svayam | vijñātākhiladṛgdraṣṭā bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ || 63 ||
tgt: 63-65a. On being told thus by that goddess, Lord Śiva himself, who has knowledge and vision of everything, the lord who is the sanctifier of all living beings, the lord of Devas, Maheśa, the bestower of all Siddhis said to her:

src: sa tāmuvāca deveśo maheśaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ | gaccha devi tvarāyuktā vacanānmama suvrate || 64 ||
tgt: “Go quickly, O gentle lady of holy rites, at my instance, riding on this Nandin and accompanied by various kinds of Gaṇas.”

src: etaṃ naṃdinamāruhya nānāvidhagaṇānvitā | gaṇāḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi jagmūraudrāḥ śivajñayā || 65 || tairgaṇaiḥ saṃvṛtā devī jagāma pitṛmaṃdiram | nirīkṣya tadbalaṃ sarvaṃ mahādevotivismitaḥ || 66 || bhūṣaṇāni mahārhāṇi tebhyo devyai paraṃtapaḥ | preṣayāmāsa cāvyagro mahādevo'nu pṛṣṭhataḥ || 67 ||
tgt: 65b-68. At the bidding of Śiva, sixty thousand of the terrifying Gaṇas went (along with her). Surrounded by those Gaṇas, the goddess went to the abode of her father. Observing the entire army, Mahādeva became excessively surprised. Mahādeva, the unperturbed scorcher of enemies, sent very valuable ornaments to her through his attendants. He sent them immediately after her.

src: devyā gataṃ vai svapiturgṛhaṃ tadā vimṛśya sarvaṃ bhagavānmaheśaḥ | dākṣāyaṇī pitravamānitā satī na yāsyatīti svapuraṃ punarjagau || 68 ||
tgt: Pondering over the departure of the goddess to her father’s abode, Lord Maheśa exclaimed: “On being insulted by her father, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, will never come back to her city again.”

src: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kedārakhaṃḍe dakṣayajñaṃ prati satīdevyāgamanavarṇanaṃnāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ || 2 ||
tgt: Kanakhala—A village two miles to the east of Haridwar (U.P.), at the junction of Gaṅgā and Nīladhārā.

src: lomaśa uvāca | dākṣāyaṇī gatā tatra yatra yajño mahānabhūt | tatpituḥ sadanaṃ gatvā nā nāścaryasamanvitam || 1 || dvāri sthitā tadā devā avatīrya nijāsanāt | naṃdino hi mahābhāgā devalokaṃ nirīkṣya ca || 2 || mātaraṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhi vāṃdhavān | abhivādyaiva pirataṃ mātaraṃ ca mudānvitā || 3 ||
tgt: 1-4a. Dākṣāyaṇī went to the place where the great sacrifice was being performed. After going to the abode of her father, the abode which was full of various wonderful things, she stood at the entrance. The Devas of exalted fortune became delighted. They got down from their seats. After seeing the congregation of the Devas, her parents, friends, relatives and kinsmen, she made obeisance to her father and mother with delight. Then the goddess spoke these words in a manner suitable to the occasion:

src: śaṃbhunā hi vinā tāta kathaṃ yajñaḥ pravartate | ete kathaṃ samāyātā brahmaṇā sahitāḥ pitaḥ || 7 || he bhṛgo tvaṃ na jānāsi he kaśyapa mahāmate | atre viśiṣṭha ekastvaṃ śakra kiṃ kṛtamadyate || 8 || he viṣṇo tvaṃ mahādevaṃ jānāsi parameśvaram | brahmankiṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi mahādevasya vikramam || 9 ||
tgt: 4b-9. “Why was Śaṃbḥu, the extremely splendid (lord), not invited by you? (He is the lord) by whom this entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings has been sanctified. He is Yajña (incarnate), an (important) part of Yajña, the sacrificial gift offered therein, the material offered therein, the Mantras etc., the Havya and Kavya—he is identical with all these things. He is the most excellent one among those who are expert in performing Yajñas. Everything performed without him will become impure. How can a sacrifice function (at all), O dear father, without Śaṃbhu? How did these come here, O father, along with Brahmā? Don’t you know? O Bhṛgu, O Kaśyapa of great intellect, O Atri, O Vasiṣṭha? You are alone, O Śakra, what has been done by you today? O Viṣṇu, you do know the supreme lord Mahādeva. O Brahmā, don’t you know the valour of Mahādeva?

src: purā paṃcamukho bhūtvā garvitosi sadāśivam | kṛtaścaturmukhastena vismṛto'si tadadbhutam || 10 ||
tgt: 10. Formerly you happened to be five-faced. You (spoke) arrogantly to Sadāśiva and you were made four-faced. It is surprising that you have forgotten that miracle.

src: bhikṣāṭanaṃ kṛtaṃ yena purā dāruvane vibhuḥ | śaptoyaṃ bhikṣuko rudro bhavadbhiḥ sakhibhistadā || 11 ||
tgt: 11. He is the lord Rudra who formerly begged for alms in the forest of Dāruvana,[1] when this mendicant was cursed by you (and) your friends.

src: śaptenāpi ca rudreṇa bhavadbhirvismṛtaṃ katham | yasyāvayavamātreṇa pūritaṃ sacarācaram || 12 || liṃgabhūtaṃ jagatsarvaṃ jātaṃ tatkṣaṇameva hi | layānālliṃgamityāhuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ || 13 || sarve devāśca saṃbhūtā yato devasya śūlinaḥ | so'sau vedāṃtago devastvayā jñātuṃ na pāryate || 14 ||
tgt: 12-14. Even after cursing Rudra, how was (this incident) forgotten by you? He is the lord by whose limb alone the universe including the mobile and immobile beings, has been filled up. The entire universe became the Liṅga at that very instant. They call it Liṅga because of the dissolution (of the universe in it).[2] All the Devas along with Vāsava (Indra) are born of the Trident-bearing Lord. Such a lord who is to be realized through the Vedāntas, cannot be comprehended by you.”

src: tasyā vacanamākarṇya dakṣaḥ kruddho'bravīdvacaḥ | kiṃ tvayā bahunoktena kāryaṃ nāstīha sāṃpratam || 15 ||
tgt: 15-19a. On hearing her words, Dakṣa became angry and spoke these words:

src: gaccha vā tiṣṭhavā bhadre kasmāttvaṃ hi samāgatā | amaṃgalo hi bhartā te aśivosau sumadhyame || 16 ||
tgt: “Of what avail is your verbal prolixity. It has no relevance to the present occasion. O gentle lady, (you may) go or stay. Why did you come at all? Your husband is an inauspicious fellow, not conducive to propitiousness, O lady of good waistline.

src: akulīno vedabāhyo bhūtapretapiśācarāṭ | tasmānnākārito bhadre yajñārthaṃ cārubhāṣiṇi || 17 ||
tgt: He is ignoble, excluded from the Vedas. He is the king of goblins, ghosts and vampires. Hence he was not invited to the sacrifice, O gentle lady of sweet speech.

src: mayā dattāsi suśroṇi pāpinā maṃdabuddhinā | rudrāyāviditārthāya uddhatāya durātmane || 18 || tasmātkāyaṃ parityajya svasthā bhava śucismite | dakṣeṇoktā tadā putrī sā satī lokapūjitā || 19 ||
tgt: O lady of excellent loins, it is to Rudra who is haughty and evil-minded and of unknown antecedents that you had been given in marriage by me, a dull-witted sinner. Hence, abandon this body (of yours), O lady of pure smiles, and be happy.” 19b-23. It was thus that his own daughter Satī who was worshipped by all the worlds, was addressed by Dakṣa then.

src: niṃdāyuktaṃ svapitaraṃ vilokya ruṣitā bhṛśam | ciṃtayaṃtī tadā devī kathaṃ yāsyāmi maṃdire || 20 || śaṃkaraṃ draṣṭukāmāṃha kiṃ vakṣye tena pṛcchitā | yo niṃdati mahādevaṃ niṃdyamānaṃ śrṛṇoti yaḥ | tāvubhau narake yāto yāvaccandradivākarau || 21 || tasmāttayakṣyāmyahaṃ dehaṃ pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam || 22 ||
tgt: On seeing her own father full of contempt (for Śiva), Satī became excessively furious. Then the goddess thought thus: ‘Though I am desirous of seeing Śaṅkara, how can I go back to our mansion? What will I say if I am asked (about this incident) by him? He who censures Mahādeva and he who listens when Mahādeva is being censured—both of them go to hell and remain there as long as the moon and the sun (shine). Hence I will abandon this body and enter fire.’ Pondering thus and being overwhelmed by insult, she entered fire[3] uttering the words “O Rudra, O Śiva”.

src: hāhākāreṇa mahatā vyāptamāsīddigaṃtaram | sarve te maṃcamārūḍhāḥ śastrairvyāptā niraṃtarāḥ || 24 || śastraiḥ svairjadhnurātmānaṃ svāni dehāni cicchiduḥ | kecitkaratale gṛhya śirāṃsi svāni cotsukāḥ || 25 ||
tgt: 24-30. The entire quarters became pervaded with the great uproar of “Alas! Alas!”. All those (who had come with Satī) climbed on to the platform. Laden with weapons they crowded the place without any gap. They hit and struck themselves with their weapons. They cut off their own bodies. Some of them cut off their heads and eagerly performed the Nīrājana (waving of the lights in circles) rites with them. Immediately they were reduced to ash. Then everyone said thus: “Twenty thousand of the Gaṇas roared terrifically. Those dreadful ones cut off their limbs by means of weapons. Thus they all perished there along with Dākṣāyaṇī.”[4]

src: gaṇāstatrāyūte dve ca tadadbhutamivābhavat | te sarva ṛṣayo devā iṃdrādyāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ || 28 || viśve'śvanau lokapālāstūṣṇīṃbūtāstadābhavan | viṣṇuṃ vareṇyaṃ kecicca prārthayaṃtaḥ samaṃtataḥ || 29 || evaṃ bhūtastadā yajño jātastasya durātmanaḥ | dakṣasya brahmabaṃdhośca ṛṣayo bhayamāgatāḥ || 30 ||
tgt: That was a great miracle. All sages, the Devas beginning with Indra, along with the groups of Maruts, Viśvedevas, Aśvins and the Guardians of the Quarters—all these became silent then.
