Some of them (walked) round requesting Viṣṇu, the most excellent one. This was the end of the Yajña of that evil-minded one. The Yajña of the unworthy Brāhmaṇa Dakṣa (was ruined) and the sages became afraid.

src: etasminnaṃtare viprā nāradena mahātmanā | kathitaṃ sarvamevaitaddakṣasya ca viceṣṭitam || 31 ||
tgt: 31. In the meantime, O Brāhmaṇas, all these activities and behaviour of Dakṣa were communicated to Rudra by the noble-minded Nārada.

src: tadākarṇyeśvaro vākyaṃ nāradasya mukhodgatam | cukopa paramaṃ kruddha āsanādutpatanniva || 32 ||
tgt: 32. On hearing Nārada’s report the supreme Lord Śiva became extremely infuriated. In his anger he as if jumped up from his seat.

src: uddhṛtya ca jaṭāṃ rudro lokasaṃhārakārakaḥ | āsphoṭayāmāsa ruṣā parvatasya śiropari || 33 ||
tgt: 33. Uprooting a plait of hair from his (matted hair), Rudra, the cause of the annihilation of all the worlds, angrily dashed it on the top of the mountain.

src: tāḍanācca samudbhūto vīrabhadro mahāyaśāḥ | tathā kālī samutpannā bhūtakoṭibhirāvṛtā || 34 ||
tgt: 34. As a result of this dashing, Vīrabhadra of great fame rose up. So also did Kālī surrounded by crores of spirits and goblins.

src: kopānniḥśvasitenaiva rudrasya ca mahātmanaḥ | jātaṃ jvarāṇāṃ ca śataṃ sannipātāstrayodaśa || 35 ||
tgt: 35. Through the wrathful breath of the noble-minded Rudra a hundred (types of) Fevers and thirteen Sannipātas (combined derangement of all the three humours causing deadly varieties of fevers) rose up.

src: vijñapto vīrabhadreṇa rudro raudraparākramaḥ | kiṃ kāryaṃ bhavataḥ kāryaṃ śīghrameva vada prabho || 36 ||
tgt: 36. Rudra of fierce and dreadful exploits was entreated by Vīrabhadra “O Lord! what task of Your Lordship is to be carried out? Tell me quickly.”

src: ityukto bhagavānrudraḥ preṣayāmāsa satvaram | gaccha vīra mahā bāho dakṣayajñaṃ vināśaya || 37 ||
tgt: 37. On being requested thus, lord Rudra hurriedly commissioned him, “Destroy Dakṣa’s Yajña.”

src: śāsanaṃ śirasā dhṛtvā devadevasya śūlinaḥ | kālikā'lihito vīraḥ sarvabhūtaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ | vīrabhadro mahātejā yayau dakṣamakhaṃ prati || 38 ||
tgt: 38. Receiving the behest of the Trident-bearing Lord of Devas with his head (i.e. humbly accepting the order), the heroic Vīrabhadra of excessive refulgence, who was kissed (ā-līḍhā) by Kālikā and was surrounded by all goblins rushed to Dakṣa’s sacrifice.

src: tadānīmeva sahasā durnimittāni cābhavan | rūkṣo vavau tadā vāyuḥ śarkarābhiḥ samāvṛtaḥ || 39 || asṛgvarṣati devaśca timireṇā'vṛtā divaśaḥ | ulkāpātāśca bahavaḥ petururvyāṃ sahasraśaḥ || 40 ||
tgt: 39-40. At that very time, ill-omens occurred suddenly. A rough wind blew carrying with it gravels and sand. The Rain-god showered blood. The quarters were enveloped in darkness. Thousands of meteors fell on the earth.

src: evaṃvidhānyariṣṭāni dadṛśurvibudhādayaḥ | dakṣo'pi bhayamāpanno viṣṇuṃ śaraṇamāyayau || 41 ||
tgt: 41. The Devas and others saw such phenomena foreboding evil. Becoming frightened, Dakṣa sought refuge in Viṣṇu.

src: rakṣarakṣa mahāviṣṇo tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo guruḥ | yajño'si tvaṃ suraśreṣṭha bhayānmāṃ parimocaya || 42 ||
tgt: 42. “Save me, save me, O great Viṣṇu. Indeed you are our greatest preceptor and elderly one. You are (identical with) Yajña, O most excellent one among Suras. Save me from this fearful danger,”

src: dakṣeṇa prārthya māno hi jagāda madhusūdanaḥ | mayā rakṣā vidātavyā bhavato nātra saṃśayaḥ || 43 ||
tgt: 43. On being requested and prayed to by Dakṣa, the slayer of Madhu (Viṣṇu) said: “Protection should be accorded to you by me. There is no doubt about it.

src: apūjyā yatra pūjyaṃte pūjanīyo na pūjyate | trīṇī tatra pravartaṃte durbhikṣaṃ tvayā dharmamajānatāḥ | īśvarāvajñayā sarvaṃ viphalaṃ ca bhaviṣyati || 44 ||
tgt: 44. Disrespect has been shown by you, O Dakṣa, without understanding genuine Dharma (Virtue). Due to the contemptuous disregard of Lord Śiva, everything will become fruitless.

src: apūjyā yatra pūjyaṃ te pūjanīyo na pūjyate | trīṇī tatra pravartaṃte durbhikṣaṃ maraṇaṃ bhayam || 45 ||
tgt: 45. Where those who are not worthy of respect are worshipped, where he who is worthy of being worshipped is not worshipped, three consequences, viz. famine, death and fear, prevail there.

src: tasmātsarvaprayatnena mānanīyo vṛṣadhvajaḥ | amānitānmaheśāttvāṃ mahadbhayamupasthitam || 46 ||
tgt: 46. Hence, the Bull-bannered Lord (Śiva) should be honoured with all efforts. Great fear and danger beset you because the great lord was not honoured.

src: adhunaiva vayaṃ sarve prabhavo na bhavāmahe | bhavato durnnayeneva nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 47 ||
tgt: 47. All of us are not powerful enough now, because of your evil behaviour. There is no need to discuss this matter further.”

src: viṣṇostadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣaściṃtāparo'bhavat | vivirṇavadano bhūtvā tūṣṇīmāsīdbhuvi sthitaḥ || 48 ||
tgt: 48. On hearing those words of Viṣṇu, Dakṣa became lost in (anxious) thoughts. Turning pale in the face, he remained silent and sat on the ground.

src: vīrabhadro mahābāhū rudreṇaiva pracoditaḥ | kālī kātyāyanīśānā cāmuṃḍā muṃḍamarddinī || 49 || bhadrakālī tathā bhadrā tvaritā vaiṣṇavī tathā | navadurgādisahito bhūtānāṃ ca gaṇo mahān || 50 || śākinī ḍākinī caiva bhūtapramathaguhyakāḥ | tathaiva yoginīcakraṃ catuḥ ṣaṣṭyā samanvitam || 51 ||
tgt: 49-51. Expressly commanded by Rudra himself the extremely powerful Vīrabhadra came to the sacrificial enclosure accompanied by the nine Durgās and others.[5] The nine Durgās were Kālī, Kātyāyanī, Īśānā, Cāmuṇḍā, Muṇḍamardinī, Bhadrakālī, Bhadrā, Tvaritā and Vaiṣṇavī. A big multitude of Bhūtas also entered the sacrificial enclosure of great refulgence. Śākinīs, Ḍākinīs, Bhūtas, Pramathas, Guhyakas, a host of Yoginīs (in circular formation) along with the sixty-four (Tantras)[6]—all these entered the sacrificial enclosure suddenly.

src: pārṣadāḥ śaṃkarasyaite sarve rudrasvarūpiṇaḥ | paṃcavaktrā nīlakaṃṭhāḥ sarve te śastrapāṇayaḥ || 53 || chatracāmarasaṃvītāḥ sarve haraparākramāḥ | daśabāhavastrinetrā jaṭilā rudrabhūṣaṇāḥ || 54 || ardhacaṃdradharāḥ sarve sarve caiva mahaujasaḥ | sarve te vṛṣabhārūḍhāḥ sarve te veṣabhūṣaṇāḥ || 55 ||
tgt: 52-55. Hundreds and thousands of Gaṇas who accompanied Vīrabhadra were all the Pārṣadas (attendants) of Śaṅkara. All of them had the form of Rudra. They had five faces and blue throats. All had weapons in their hands. They were duly served with umbrellas and chowries. All were as valorous as Śiva. They had ten arms and three eyes. Their hair was matted. They wore the ornaments of Rudra. Bearing crescent moon (on their heads), all of them had (different kinds of) robes and ornaments.

src: sahasrabāhurbhujagādhipairvṛtastrilocano bhīmabalo bhayāvahaḥ | ebhiḥ sametaśca tadā mahātmā sa vīrabhadro'bhijagāma yajñam || 56 ||
tgt: 56. Accompanied by these, the noble-souled, three-eyed, dreadful Vīrabhadra of terrible might, who had a thousand arms and was entwined by great serpents, marched towards the sacrifice.

src: yugyānāṃ ca sahasreṇa dvipramāṇena syaṃdanam | siṃhānāṃ prayutenaiva vāhyamānaṃ ca tasya tat || 57 ||
tgt: 57. His chariot was drawn by two thousand horses and a million lions.

src: tathaiva daṃśitāḥ siṃhā bahavaḥ pārśvarakṣakāḥ | śārdūlā makarā matsyā gajāścaiva sahasraśaḥ | chatrāṇi vividhānyeva cāmarāṇi tathaiva ca || 58 ||
tgt: 58-59a. The armoured defenders of his sides were many lions, tigers, sharks, fishes and thousands of elephants. He had different kinds of umbrellas and chowries held over the head of everyone everywhere.

src: mūrddhanidhriyamāṇāni sarvatogrāṇi sarvaśaḥ | tato bherīmahānādāḥ śaṃkhāśca vividhasvanāḥ | paṭahā gomukhāścaiva śrṛṃgāṇi vividhāni ca || 59 ||
tgt: 59bc. Then high sounding Bherīs (war-drums), conchs of various (degrees of) sounds, Paṭahas (kettle-drums), musical instruments like Gomukka, different kinds of horns were sounded.

src: tato'vādyaṃta tānyeva ghanāni suṣirāṇi ca | kalagānaparāḥ sarve sarve mṛdaṃgavādinaḥ || 60 ||
tgt: 60. Cymbals, gongs and wind instruments were played. All of them were engaged in singing pleasantly. All of them played on Mṛdaṅgas (special drums).

src: anekalāsyasaṃyuktā vīrabhadrāgratobhavan | raṇavāditranirghoṣairjagarjuramitaujasaḥ || 61 ||
tgt: 61. The Gaṇas proceeded ahead in front of Vīrabhadra indulging in different kinds of dances. Those Gaṇas of unmeasured power and potency roared along with the martial sounds of the musical instruments.

src: tena nādena mahatā nāditaṃ bhuvanatrayam | evaṃ sarve samāyātā gaṇā rudrapraṇoditāḥ || 62 || yajñavāṭaṃ ca dakṣasya vināśārthaṃ prahāriṇaḥ | rajasā cā'vṛtaṃ vyoma tamasā ca vṛtā diśaḥ || 63 ||
tgt: 62-63a. By that great sound the three worlds echoed and reverberated. Thus all those Gaṇas ordered (urged) by Rudra came there to the sacrificial enclosure of Dakṣa and began to smash for the sake of destroying it.

src: saptadvīpavatī pṛthvī cacāla sādrikānanā | te dṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryyaṃ lokakṣayakaraṃ tadā || 64 ||
tgt: 63b-64a. The sky was covered with dust and all the quarters were enveloped in darkness. The earth consisting of the seven islands (continents)[7] shook along with the mountains and forests.

src: uttasthuryugapatsarve devadaityaniśācarāḥ | te vai dadṛśurāyāṃtīṃ rudrasenā bhayāvahām || 65 ||
tgt: 64b-65. Those Devas, Daityas and night-wanderers observed this wonderful spectacle foreboding the ruin of all the worlds. Ail of them stood up simultaneously. They saw the dreadful army of Rudra advancing.

src: idam te na atapaskāya na abhaktāya kadācana na ca aśuśrūṣave vācyam na ca mām yaḥ abhyasūyati
tgt: This confidential knowledge may never be explained to those who are not austere, or devoted, or engaged in devotional service, nor to one who is envious of Me.

src: yaḥ idam paramam guhyam mat bhakteṣu abhidhāsyati bhaktim mayi parām kṛtvā mām eva eṣyati asaṁśayaḥ
tgt: For one who explains this supreme secret to the devotees, pure devotional service is guaranteed, and at the end he will come back to Me.

src: na ca tasmāt manuṣyeṣu kaścit me priya kṛt tamaḥ bhavitā na ca me tasmāt anyaḥ priya taraḥ bhuvi
tgt: There is no servant in this world more dear to Me than he, nor will there ever be one more dear.

src: adhyeṣyate ca yaḥ imam dharmyam saṁvādam āvayoḥ jñāna yajñena tena aham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ
tgt: And I declare that he who studies this sacred conversation of ours worships Me by his intelligence.

src: śraddhā vān anasūyaḥ ca śṛṇuyāt api yaḥ naraḥ saḥ api muktaḥ śubhān lokān prāpnuyāt puṇya karmaṇām
tgt: And one who listens with faith and without envy becomes free from sinful reactions and attains to the auspicious planets where the pious dwell.

src: kaccit etat śrutam pārtha tvayā eka agreṇa cetasā kaccit ajñāna sammohaḥ praṇaṣṭaḥ te dhanam jaya
tgt: O son of Pṛthā, O conqueror of wealth, have you heard this with an attentive mind? And are your ignorance and illusions now dispelled?

src: arjunaḥ uvāca naṣṭaḥ mohaḥ smṛtiḥ labdhā tvat prasādāt mayā acyuta sthitaḥ asmi gata sandehaḥ kariṣye vacanam tava
tgt: Arjuna said: My dear Kṛṣṇa, O infallible one, my illusion is now gone. I have regained my memory by Your mercy. I am now firm and free from doubt and am prepared to act according to Your instructions.

src: sañjayaḥ uvāca iti aham vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahā ātmanaḥ saṁvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutam roma harṣaṇam
tgt: Sañjaya said: Thus have I heard the conversation of two great souls, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna. And so wonderful is that message that my hair is standing on end.

src: vyāsa prasādāt śrutavān etat guhyam aham param yogam yoga īśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt kathayataḥ svayam
tgt: By the mercy of Vyāsa, I have heard these most confidential talks directly from the master of all mysticism, Kṛṣṇa, who was speaking personally to Arjuna.

src: rājan saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya saṁvādam imam adbhutam keśava arjunayoḥ puṇyam hṛṣyāmi ca muhuḥ muhuḥ
tgt: O King, as I repeatedly recall this wondrous and holy dialogue between Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, I take pleasure, being thrilled at every moment.

src: tat ca saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya rūpam ati adbhutam hareḥ vismayaḥ me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
tgt: O King, as I remember the wonderful form of Lord Kṛṣṇa, I am struck with wonder more and more, and I rejoice again and again.

src: yatra yoga īśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ yatra pārthaḥ dhanuḥ dharaḥ tatra śrīḥ vijayaḥ bhūtiḥ dhruvā nītiḥ matiḥ mama
tgt: Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the master of all mystics, and wherever there is Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will also certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary power, and morality. That is my opinion.

src: yad idam ālambanānupalambhaḥ / yaṃ hi nopalabhyate taṃ nālambate /
tgt: It is its nonperception, as one does not objectify a thing that is not perceived.

src: kiṃ ca nopalabhate,
tgt: What does one not perceive?

src: ubhe dṛṣṭī nopalabhate, yad idam ātmadṛṣṭiṃ paradṛṣṭiṃ ca /
tgt: One does not perceive the two views, the view of the self and the view of the other.

src: tad ucyate 'nupalambha iti /
tgt: Therefore, it is called nonperception.

src: evaṃ hi mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvena svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyaṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇopapattiprahāṇāya /
tgt: “Mañjuśrī, thus should a sick bodhisattva control his own mind in order to overcome old age, sickness, death, and birth.

src: evaṃ ca mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvānāṃ bodhir yadi na bhavet,
tgt: Such, Mañjuśrī, is the sickness of the bodhisattva.

src: nirarthako nanu vyāyāmo bhavet /
tgt: If he takes it otherwise, all his efforts will be in vain.

src: yathā pratyarthikanirghātāc churā ity ucyante, evam eva jarāvyādhimaraṇaduḥkhopaśamanād bodhisatvā ity ucyante /
tgt: Just as one is called ‘hero’ when one overcomes all enemies, so, too, one is called ‘bodhisattva’ when one conquers the miseries of aging, sickness, and death.

src: tena bodhisatvena vyādhitenaivaṃ pratyavekṣitavyam /
tgt: “The sick bodhisattva should tell himself

src: yathā mama vyādhir abhūto 'sann evaṃ sarvasatvānām api vyādhir abhūto 'sann iti / tasyaivaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇasya nānuśaṃsādṛṣṭipatitā satveṣu mahākaruṇotpadyate, anyatrāgantukakleśaprahāṇābhiyuktyā satveṣu mahākaruṇotpadyate /
tgt: ‘Just as my sickness is unreal and nonexistent, so the sicknesses of all living beings are unreal and nonexistent.’ Through such considerations, he arouses the great compassion toward all living beings without falling into any sentimental compassion, but instead, arouses great compassion toward all living beings through striving to eliminate the incidental afflictions.

src: anuśaṃsadṛṣṭipatitayaiva hi mahākaruṇayā bodhisatvasya khedo bhavaty upapattiṣu /
tgt: Because great compassion that falls into sentimentally purposive views only exhausts the bodhisattva in his reincarnations.

src: anuśaṃsadṛṣṭiparyutthānavigatayā punar mahākaruṇayā bodhisatvasya khedo na bhavaty upapattiṣu / so 'yam upapadyate, na ca dṛṣṭiparyutthānaparyutthita upapadyate /
tgt: But the great compassion that is free of involvement with sentimentally purposive views does not exhaust the bodhisattva in all his reincarnations. He does not reincarnate through involvement with such views but reincarnates with his mind free of involvement.

src: so 'paryutthitacitta upapadyamāno mukta evotpadyate mukta eva jāyate /
tgt: Hence, even his reincarnation is like a liberation.

src: sa mukta evotpadyamāno mukta eva jāyamāno baddhānāṃ satvānāṃ śaktaḥ pratibalo bandhamokṣāya dharmaṃ deśayitum /
tgt: Being reincarnated as if being liberated, he has the power and ability to teach the Dharma that liberates living beings from their bondage.

src: yathoktaṃ bhagavatā sa tāvad ātmanā baddhaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti nādaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate /
tgt: As the Lord declares ‘It is not possible for one who is himself bound to deliver others from their bondage.

src: yas tv ātmanā muktaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti sthānam etad vidyate tasmān muktena bodhisatvena bhavitavyam, na baddhena /
tgt: But one who is himself liberated is able to liberate others from their bondage.’ Therefore, the bodhisattva should participate in liberation and should not participate in bondage.

src: tatra katamo bandhaḥ,
tgt: “What is bondage?

src: katamo mokṣaḥ /
tgt: And what is liberation?

src: anupāyād bhavagatiparigraho bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ,
tgt: To indulge in liberation from the world without employing liberative art is bondage for the bodhisattva.

src: upāyād bhavagatigamanaṃ mokṣaḥ /
tgt: To engage in life in the world with full employment of liberative art is liberation for the bodhisattva.

src: anupāyād dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ,
tgt: To experience the taste of contemplation, meditation, and concentration without skill in liberative art is bondage.

src: upāyena dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā mokṣaḥ /
tgt: To experience the taste of contemplation and meditation with skill in liberative art is liberation.

src: anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ, upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ /
tgt: Wisdom not integrated with liberative art is bondage, but wisdom integrated with liberative art is liberation.

src: prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhanam, prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
tgt: Liberative art not integrated with wisdom is bondage, but liberative art integrated with wisdom is liberation.

src: tatra katamo 'nupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ,
tgt: “How is wisdom not integrated with liberative art a bondage?

src: yad idaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitanidhyaptiḥ, na ca lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyaptiḥ / iyam anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ /
tgt: Wisdom not integrated with liberative art consists of concentration on voidness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and yet it fails to concentrate on cultivation of the auspicious signs and marks, on the adornment of the buddhafield, and on the work of development of living beingsand it is bondage.

src: tatra katamopāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ,
tgt: “How is wisdom integrated with liberative art a liberation?

src: yad idaṃ lakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyapticittaṃ ca śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitaparijayaś ca / iyam upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ /
tgt: Wisdom integrated with liberative art consists of concentration on cultivation of the auspicious signs and marks, on the adornment of the buddhafield, and on the work of development of living beings, all the while concentrating on deep investigation of voidness, signlessness, and wishlessnessand it is liberation.

src: tatra katamaḥ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ,
tgt: “What is the bondage of liberative art not integrated with wisdom?

src: yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighapratiṣṭhitasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau cāpariṇāmanā / ayaṃ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ /
tgt: The bondage of liberative art not integrated with wisdom consists of the bodhisattva’s planting of the roots of virtue without dedicating them for the sake of enlightenment, while living in the grip of dogmatic convictions, passions, attachments, resentments, and their subconscious instincts.

src: tatra katamaḥ prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ,
tgt: “What is the liberation of liberative art integrated with wisdom?

src: yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighaprahīṇasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau pariṇāmitas tasya cāparāmarśaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisatvasya prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
tgt: The liberation of liberative art integrated with wisdom consists of the bodhisattva’s dedication of his roots of virtue for the sake of enlightenment, without taking any pride therein, while forgoing all convictions, passions, attachments, resentments, and their subconscious instincts.

src: tatra mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvenaivam ime dharmā nidhyapayitavyāḥ /
tgt: “Mañjuśrī, thus should the sick bodhisattva consider things.

src: kāyasya cittasya ca vyādheś cānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmapratyavekṣaṇā, iyam asya prajñā /
tgt: His wisdom is the consideration of body, mind, and sickness as impermanent, miserable, empty, and selfless.

src: yat punaḥ kāyavyādhipariharaṇatayā na khidyate, na pratibadhnāti saṃsāram, satvārthayogam anuyuktaḥ, ayam asyopāyaḥ /
tgt: His liberative art consists of not exhausting himself by trying to avoid all physical sickness, and of applying himself to accomplish the benefit of living beings, without interrupting the cycle of reincarnations.

src: punar aparaṃ yat kāyasya vyādheś cittasya cānyonyaparāparatāṃ na nirnavatāniḥpurāṇatāṃ pratyavekṣate, iyam asya prajñā /
tgt: Furthermore, his wisdom lies in understanding that body, mind, and sickness are neither new nor old, whether considered simultaneously or sequentially.

src: yat punaḥ kāyasya vyādheś cittasya ca nātyantopaśamaṃ nirodham atyayati,
tgt: And his liberative art lies in not seeking pacification or cessation of body, mind, or sicknesses.

src: evaṃ hi mañjuśriḥ glānena bodhisatvena cittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam / na ca tena nidhyaptau vānidhyaptau vā sthātavyam /
tgt: “That, Mañjuśrī, is the way a sick bodhisattva should concentrate his mind he should live neither in control of his mind, nor in indulgence of his mind.

src: yadi hy anidhyaptau tiṣṭhed bāladharma eṣaḥ / atha nidhyaptau tiṣṭhec chrāvakadharma eṣaḥ /
tgt: To live by indulging the mind is proper for fools and to live in control of the mind is proper for the disciples.

src: tasmād bodhisatvena na nidhyaptau sthātavyam /
tgt: Therefore, the bodhisattva should live neither in control nor in indulgence of his mind.

src: yad atrāsthānam ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Not living in either of the two extremes is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yan na pṛthagjanagocaro nāryagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat saṃsāragocaraś ca na ca kleśagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: “Not the domain of the ordinary individual and not the domain of the arhat, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of the world yet not the domain of the afflictions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yan nirvāṇapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na cātyantaparinirvāṇagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Where one understands liberation, yet does not enter final and complete liberation, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yac caturmārasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca sarvamāraviṣayātikrāntagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Where the four māras manifest, yet where all the works of māras are transcended, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat sarvajñajñānaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cākāle jñānaprāptigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Where one seeks the gnosis of omniscience, yet does not attain this gnosis at the wrong time, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yac catuḥsatyajñānagocaraś ca na cākāle satyaprativedhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Where one knows the four noble truths, yet does not realize those truths at the wrong time, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad adhyātmapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: A domain of introspective insight, wherein one does not arrest voluntary reincarnation in the world, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad ajātipratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na ca niyāmāvakrāntigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: A domain where one realizes birthlessness, yet does not become destined for the ultimate, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat pratītyasamutpādagocaraś ca sarvadṛṣṭivigatagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Where one sees relativity without entertaining any convictions, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat sarvasatvasaṃgaṇikāgocaraś ca na ca kleśānuśayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: Where one associates with all beings, yet keeps free of all afflictive instincts, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad vivekagocaraś ca na ca kāyacittakṣayaniśrayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: A domain of solitude with no place for the exhaustion of body and mind, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat traidhātukagocaraś ca na ca dharmadhātusaṃbhedagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the triple world, yet indivisible from the ultimate realm, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yac chūnyatāgocaraś ca sarvākāraguṇaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad ānimittagocaraś ca satvapramocanārambaṇavitarkagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of voidness, yet where one cultivates all types of virtues, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of signlessness, where one keeps in sight the deliverance of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad apraṇihitagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavagatisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of wishlessness, where one voluntarily manifests lives in the world, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad anabhisaṃskāragocaraś ca sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskārāpratiprasrabdhigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: “A domain essentially without undertaking, yet where all the roots of virtue are undertaken without interruption, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat ṣaṭpāramitāgocaraś ca sarvasatvacittacaritapāragamanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the six transcendences, where one attains the transcendence of the thoughts and actions of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat ṣaḍanusmṛtigocaraś ca na ca sarvāsravakṣayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the six superknowledges, wherein defilements are not exhausted, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat saddharmapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca na ca kumārgādhyālambanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of living by the holy Dharma, without even perceiving any evil paths, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yac caturapramāṇagocaraś ca na ca brahmalokopapattisparśanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the four immeasurables, where one does not accept rebirth in the heaven of Brahmā, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad dhyānasamādhisamāpattigocaraś ca na ca samādhisamāpattivaśenopapattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of contemplation, concentration, and absorption, where one does not reincarnate in the formless realms by force of these concentrations and absorptions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat smṛtyupasthānagocaraś ca na ca kāyavedanācittadharmātyarthagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the four foci of mindfulness, where body, sensation, mind, and things are not ultimately of concern, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat samyakprahāṇagocaraś ca na ca kuśalākuśaladvayopalambhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the four right efforts, where the duality of good and evil is not apprehended, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad ṛddhipādābhinirhāragocaraś cānābhogarddhipādavaśavartigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the four bases of magical powers, where they are effortlessly mastered, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat pañcendriyagocaraś ca sarvasatvendriyaparāparajñānagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the five spiritual faculties, where one knows the degrees of the spiritual faculties of living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat pañcabalapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca daśatathāgatabalābhisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of living with the five powers, where one delights in the ten powers of the tathāgata, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yat saptabodhyaṅgapariniṣpattigocaraś ca buddhiprabhedajñānakauśalyagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of perfection of the seven factors of enlightenment, where one is skilled in the knowledge of fine intellectual distinctions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yan mārgapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca kumārgānadhyālambanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac chamathavidarśanāsaṃbhāraparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cātyantaśāntipatanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of living by the eightfold path, without even perceiving any evil paths, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of the cultivation of the aptitude for mental quiescence and transcendental analysis, where one does not fall into extreme quietism, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad anutpādalakṣaṇasarvadharmamīmāṃsanagocaraś ca rūpalakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakāyālaṃkārapariniṣpattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of the realization of the unborn nature of all things, yet of the perfection of the body, the auspicious signs and marks, and the ornaments of the Buddha, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yac chrāvakapratyekabuddhākalpasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca buddhadharmātyajanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of manifesting the attitudes of the disciples and the solitary sages without sacrificing the qualities of the Buddha, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad atyantaviśuddhiprakṛtisamāpannasarvadharmānugamanagocaraś ca yathādhimuktisarvasatveryāpathasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain of conformity to all things utterly pure in nature while manifesting behavior that suits the inclinations of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: yad atyantāsaṃvartavivartākāśasvabhāvasarvabuddhakṣetrapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca nānāvyūhānekavyūhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca,
tgt: A domain where one realizes that all the buddhafields are indestructible and uncreatable, having the nature of infinite space, yet where one manifests the establishment of the qualities of the buddhafields in all their variety and magnitude, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

src: ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad dharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca bodhisatvacaryātyajanagocaraś ca, ayam api bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
tgt: The domain where one turns the wheel of the holy Dharma and manifests the magnificence of ultimate liberation, yet never forsakes the career of the bodhisattva, such is the domain of the bodhisattva!”

src: iha nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne ye mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena sārdham āgatā devaputrās tato 'ṣṭānāṃ devaputrasahasrāṇām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni // //
tgt: When Vimalakīrti had spoken this discourse, eight thousand of the gods in the company of the crown prince Mañjuśrī conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: glānapratisaṃmodanāparivartaś caturthaḥ //
tgt: The Inconceivable Liberation

src: athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat
tgt: Thereupon, the venerable Śāriputra had this thought

src: kutreme bodhisatvā niṣatsyanti, ime ca mahāśrāvakāḥ / neha gṛha āsanāni saṃvidyante /
tgt: “There is not even a single chair in this house. Where are these disciples and bodhisattvas going to sit?”

src: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetovitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram etad avocat
tgt: The Licchavi Vimalakīrti read the thought of the venerable Śāriputra and said, “Reverend Śāriputra, did you come here for the sake of the Dharma?

src: kiṃ bhadantaśāriputro dharmārthika āgata utāsanārthikaḥ / āha dharmārthikā vayam āgatā nāsanārthikāḥ /
tgt: Or did you come here for the sake of a chair?” Śāriputra replied, “I came for the sake of the Dharma, not for the sake of a chair.”

src: āha tena hi bhadantaśāriputra yo dharmarthiko bhavati, nāsau svakāyārthiko bhavati /
tgt: Vimalakīrti continued, “Reverend Śāriputra, he who is interested in the Dharma is not interested even in his own body, much less in a chair.

src: yo bhadantaśāriputra dharmārthiko bhavati, na sa rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānārthiko bhavati,
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, he who is interested in the Dharma has no interest in matter, sensation, intellect, motivation, or consciousness.

src: na skandhadhātvāyatanārthikaḥ /
tgt: He has no interest in these aggregates, or in the elements, or in the sensemedia.

src: yo dharmārthikaḥ, na sa kāmadhāturupadhātvārūpyadhātvarthiko bhavati,
tgt: Interested in the Dharma, he has no interest in the realm of desire, the realm of pure matter, or the immaterial realm.

src: nāsau buddhābhiniveśārthiko bhavati, na dharmasaṃghābhiniveśārthikaḥ /
tgt: Interested in the Dharma, he is not interested in attachment to the Buddha, attachment to the Dharma, or attachment to the Saṅgha.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra yo dharmārthikaḥ, nāsau duḥkhaparijñānārthiko na samudayaprahāṇārthiko na nirodhasākṣātkriyārthiko na mārgabhāvanārthiko bhavati /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, he who is interested in the Dharma is not interested in recognizing suffering, abandoning its origination, realizing its cessation, or practicing the path.

src: aprapañco hi dharmo nirakṣaraḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is ultimately without formulation and without verbalization.

src: tatra yaḥ prapañcayati ḥ duḥkhaṃ parijñāsyāmi samudayaṃ prahāsyāmi nirodhaṃ sākṣātkariṣyāmi mārgaṃ bhāvayiṣyāmīti, nasau dharmārthikaḥ, prapañcārthiko 'sau /
tgt: Who verbalizes ‘Suffering should be recognized, origination should be eliminated, cessation should be realized, the path should be practiced,’ is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in verbalization.

src: dharmo hi bhadantaśāriputra upaśāntaḥ /
tgt: “Reverend Śāriputra, the Dharma is calm and peaceful.

src: tatra ya utpādavyaye caranti, na te dharmārthikā na vivekārthikāḥ, utpādavyayārthikās te /
tgt: Those who are engaged in production and destruction are not interested in the Dharma, are not interested in solitude, but are interested in production and destruction.

src: dharmo hy arajo rajo'pagataḥ / tatra ye kvacid dharme rakṣante 'ntaśo nirvāṇe 'pi, na te dharmārthikāḥ,
tgt: He who is attached to anything, even to liberation, is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in the taint of desire.

src: dharmo hy aviṣayaḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is not an object.

src: ye viṣayasaṃkhyātāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, viṣayārthikās te /
tgt: He who pursues objects is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in objects.

src: dharmo nāyūho niryūhaḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is without acceptance or rejection.

src: ye kecid dharmaṃ gṛhṇanti vā muñcanti vā, na te dharmārthikāḥ, udgrahaniḥsargārthikās te /
tgt: He who holds on to things or lets go of things is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in holding and letting go.

src: dharmo 'nālayaḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is not a secure refuge.

src: ya ālayārāmāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, ālayārthikās te /
tgt: He who enjoys a secure refuge is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in a secure refuge.

src: dharmo nirnimittaḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is without sign.

src: yeṣāṃ nimittānusārivijñānam, na te dharmārthikāḥ, nimittārthikās te /
tgt: He whose consciousness pursues signs is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in signs.

src: dharmo 'saṃvāsaḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is not a society.

src: ye kecid dharmeṇa sārdhaṃ saṃvasanti, na te dharmārthikāḥ, saṃvāsārthikās te /
tgt: He who seeks to associate with the Dharma is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in association.

src: dharmo 'dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātaḥ /
tgt: The Dharma is not a sight, a sound, a category, or an idea.

src: ye dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāteṣu caranti, na te dharmārthikāḥ, dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātārthikās te /
tgt: He who is involved in sights, sounds, categories, and ideas is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in sights, sounds, categories, and ideas.

src: dharmo bhadantaśāriputra asaṃskṛtaḥ saṃskṛtāpagataḥ /
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, the Dharma is free of compounded things and uncompounded things.

src: ye saṃskṛtagocarāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, saṃskṛtodgrahaṇārthikās te /
tgt: He who adheres to compounded things and uncompounded things is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in adhering to compounded things and uncompounded things.

src: tasmād iha bhadantaśāriputra dharmārthikena te bhavitukāmena sarvadharmānarthikena bhavitavyam /
tgt: “Thereupon, reverend Śāriputra, if you are interested in the Dharma, you should take no interest in anything.”

src: iha dharmanirdeśe nirdiśyamāne pañcānāṃ devaputraśatānāṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham /
tgt: When Vimalakīrti had spoken this discourse, five hundred gods obtained the purity of the Dharmaeye in viewing all things.

src: tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ daśasu dikṣv asaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetraśatasahasreṣu buddhakṣetracārikāṃ carasi / tat katarasmin buddhakṣetre tvayā sarvaviśiṣṭāni sarvaguṇopetāni siṃhāsanāni dṛṣṭāni /
tgt: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the crown prince, Mañjuśrī, “Mañjuśrī, you have already been in innumerable hundreds of thousands of buddhafields throughout the universes of the ten directions. In which buddhafield did you see the best lionthrones with the finest qualities?”

src: evam ukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat asti kulaputra pūrve digbhāge ṣaṭtriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya merudhvajā nāma lokadhātuḥ /
tgt: Mañjuśrī replied, “‌Noble sir, if one crosses the buddhafields to the east, which are more numerous than all the grains of sand of thirtytwo Ganges rivers, one will discover a universe called Merudhvaja.

src: tatra merupradīparājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati /
tgt: There dwells a tathāgata called Meru­pradīpa­rāja.

src: tasya tathāgatasya caturaśītiyojanaśatasahasra ātmabhāvaḥ / aṣṭaṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasraṃ tasya bhagavataḥ siṃhāsanam /
tgt: His body measures eightyfour hundred thousand leagues in height, and the height of his throne is sixtyeight hundred thousand leagues.

src: teṣāṃ ca bodhisatvānāṃ catvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasra ātmabhāvaḥ / catustriṃśadyojanaśatasahāsrāni teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ siṃhāsanāni /
tgt: The bodhisattvas there are fortytwo hundred thousand leagues tall and their own thrones are thirtyfour hundred thousand leagues high.

src: merudhvajāyāṃ lokadhātau tasya bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sarvaviśiṣṭāni sarvagunopetāni siṃhāsanāni /
tgt: ‌Noble sir, the finest and most superb thrones exist in that universe Merudhvaja, which is the buddhafield of the Tathāgata Meru­pradīpa­rāja.”

src: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samanvāhāraṃ samanvāharati sma / tādṛśaṃ carddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān, yat tato merudhvajālokadhātor dvātriṃśatsiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi tena bhagavatā merupradīparājena tathāgatena preṣitāni /
tgt: At that moment, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, having focused himself in concentration, performed a miraculous feat such that the Lord Tathāgata Meru­pradīpa­rāja, in the universe Merudhvaja, sent to this universe thirtytwo hundred thousand thrones.

src: tāvad udviddhāni tāvad vistīrṇāni tāvad darśanīyāni yad apūrvāṇi tair bodhisatvais taiś ca mahāśrāvakais taiś ca śakrabrahmalokapālair devaputraiś ca /
tgt: These thrones were so tall, spacious, and beautiful that the bodhisattvas, great disciples, Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, and other gods had never before seen the like.

src: tāny upary antarīkṣeṇāgatya vimalakirter licchaver niveśane pratyatiṣṭhan /
tgt: The thrones descended from the sky and came to rest in the house of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti.

src: yatra tāni dvātriṃśatsiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi vicitrāṇy anutpīḍanatayā /
tgt: The thirtytwo hundred thousand thrones arranged themselves without crowding and the house seemed to enlarge itself accordingly.

src: na ca vaiśālyā mahānagaryā āvaraṇaṃ kṛtam, na jambūdvīpasya, na cāturdvīpikasyāvaraṇam /
tgt: The great city of Vaiśālī did not become obscured neither did the land of Jambudvīpa, nor the world of four continents.

src: sarve te tathaiva saṃdṛśyante yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt /
tgt: Everything else appeared just as it was before.

src: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam etad avocat niṣida tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ siṃhāsane sārdham etair bodhisatvaiḥ /
tgt: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the crown prince Mañjuśrī, “Mañjuśrī, let the bodhisattvas be seated on these thrones, having transformed their bodies to a suitable size!”

src: atha ye 'bhijñāpratilabdhā bodhisatvās te dvācatvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasram ātmabhāvam adhiṣṭhāya teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu nisīdanti sma /
tgt: Then, those bodhisattvas who had attained the superknowledges transformed their bodies to a height of fortytwo hundred thousand leagues and sat upon the thrones.

src: ye cādikarmikā bodhisatvās te na śaknuvanti sma teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu niṣattum /
tgt: But the beginner bodhisattvas were not able to transform themselves to sit upon the thrones.

src: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma niṣīda bhadantaśāriputra siṃhāsane /
tgt: The Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, take your seat upon a throne.”

src: āha na śaknomi satpuruṣa niṣattum uccāni pragṛhitāni cemāni siṃhāsanāni /
tgt: He replied, “Good sir, the thrones are too big and too high, and I cannot sit upon them.”

src: āha tena hi bhadantaśāriputra tasyaiva bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya namaskāraṃ kuru /
tgt: Vimalakīrti said, “Reverend Śāriputra, bow down to the Tathāgata Meru­pradīpa­rāja, and you will be able to take your seat.”

src: atha te mahāśrāvakās tasya bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya namaskāraṃ kurvanti sma /
tgt: Then, the great disciples bowed down to the Tathāgata Merupradīparāja and they were seated upon the thrones.

src: vimalakīrtir āha asti bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ cācintyo nāma vimokṣaḥ, yatrācintyavimokṣe pratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ tāvad uccaṃ tāvat pragṛhītaṃ tāvad udviddhaṃ tāvad vistīrṇaṃ sarṣapaphalakośe praveśayet /
tgt: The Licchavi Vimalakīrti replied, “Reverend Śāriputra, for the tathāgatas and the bodhisattvas, there is a liberation called ‘inconceivable.’ The bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can put the king of mountains, Sumeru, which is so high, so great, so noble, and so vast, into a mustard seed.

src: na ca sarṣapaphalakośaṃ vivardhayet / na ca sumeruṃ hāpayet /
tgt: He can perform this feat without enlarging the mustard seed and without shrinking Mount Sumeru.

src: na cāturmahārājakāyikā devās trayastriṃśato vā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ / anye ca satvā ṛddhivineyā jānīyuḥ paśyeyus taṃ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ sarśapaphalakośapraviṣṭam /
tgt: And the deities of the assembly of the four Mahārājas and of the Trayastriṃśa heavens do not even know where they are. Only those beings who are destined to be disciplined by miracles see and understand the putting of the king of mountains, Sumeru, into the mustard seed.

src: ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra bodhisatvānām acintyasya vimokṣasya viṣayapraveśaḥ /
tgt: That, reverend Śāriputra, is an entrance to the domain of the inconceivable liberation of the bodhisattvas.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo yaś caturṣu mahāsamudreṣv apskandhas tam ekasmin romakūpe prakṣipet na ca matsyakacchapaśiśumāramaṇḍūkānām anyeṣāṃ vaudakānāṃ prāṇināṃ pīḍā bhavet / na ca nāgayakṣagandharvāsurāṇām evaṃ bhavet ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ /
tgt: “Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can pour into a single pore of his skin all the waters of the four great oceans, without injuring the wateranimals such as fish, tortoises, crocodiles, frogs, and other creatures, and without the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and asuras even being aware of where they are.

src: sā ca kriyā prajñāyeta / na ca kaścit satvo vihiṃsito viheṭhito vā bhavet /
tgt: And the whole operation is visible without any injury or disturbance to any of those living beings.

src: imaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhārgavacakram iva parigṛhya dakṣiṇe pāṇāv avabhrāmya gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān lokadhātūn kṣipet na ca satvā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ nītāḥ, kuto vāgatā iti / punar api cānāyya yathāsthānaṃ sthāpayet / na ca gamanāgamanaṃ saṃjānīran /
tgt: “Such a bodhisattva can pick up with his right hand this billionworld galactic universe as if it were a potter’s wheel and, spinning it round, throw it beyond universes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, without the living beings therein knowing their motion or its origin, and he can catch it and put it back in its place, without the living beings suspecting their coming and going and yet the whole operation is visible.

src: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra santi satvā apramāṇasaṃsāravainayikāḥ / santi saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikāḥ /
tgt: “Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, there are beings who become disciplined after an immense period of evolution, and there are also those who are disciplined after a short period of evolution.

src: tatrācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo 'pramāṇasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntam ādarśayet saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntam ādarśayet /
tgt: The bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation, for the sake of disciplining those living beings who are disciplined through immeasurable periods of evolution, can make the passing of a week seem like the passing of an eon, and he can make the passing of an eon seem like the passing of a week for those who are disciplined through a short period of evolution.

src: tatrāpramāṇasaṃsāravineyāḥ satvāḥ saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntaṃ saṃjānīran I saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravineyāḥ satvāḥ kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntaṃ saṃjānīran
tgt: The living beings who are disciplined through an immeasurable period of evolution actually perceive a week to be the passing of an eon, and those disciplined by a short period of evolution actually perceive an eon to be the passing of a week.

src: iti hy acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān ekasmin buddhakṣetre saṃdarśayati /
tgt: “Thus, a bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can manifest all the splendors of the virtues of all the buddhafields within a single buddhafield.

src: sarvasatvān api dakṣiṇe karatale pratiṣṭhāpya cittajāyikayarddhyā kramet / sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu ca saṃdarśanaṃ dadyāt /
tgt: Likewise, he can place all living beings in the palm of his right hand and can show them with the supernatural speed of thought all the buddhafields without ever leaving his own buddhafield.

src: yāvatyaś ca daśasu dikṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā vartante, tāḥ sarvā ekaromakūpa ādarśayet / yāvantaś ca daśasu dikṣu candrasūryās tārārūpāni ca,
tgt: He can display in a single pore all the offerings ever offered to all the buddhas of the ten directions, and the orbs of all the suns, moons, and stars of the ten directions.

src: yāvatyaś ca daśasu dikṣu vātamaṇḍalyaḥ pravānti, tā api sarvā mukhadvāre praveśayet / na cāsya kāyo vikīryeta / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre tṛṇavanaspatayo nameyuḥ /
tgt: He can inhale all the hurricanes of the cosmic windatmospheres of the ten directions into his mouth without harming his own body and without letting the forests and the grasses of the buddhafields be flattened.

src: yāni ca daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrāṇy uddahyante kalpoddāhena, tad api sarvam agniskandhaṃ svamukhe prakṣipet / yac ca tena karma kartavyaṃ bhavet,
tgt: He can take all the masses of fire of all the supernovas that ultimately consume all the universes of all the buddhafields into his stomach without interfering with their functions.

src: yac cāvastād gaṅgānadīvālikākoṭīsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣv atikramya buddhakṣetram, tad abhyutkṣipyordhaṃ digbhāgaṃ gaṅgānadīvālikākoṭīsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tadyathāpi nāma balavān puruṣaḥ sūcyagreṇa badarīpatram utkṣipet /
tgt: Having crossed buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges downward, and having taken up a buddhafield, he can rise up through buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and place it on high, just as a strong man may pick up a jujube leaf on the point of a needle.

src: evam acṃtyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sarvasatvāni cakravartyādirūpāṇy adhitiṣṭhet /
tgt: “Thus, a bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can magically transform any kind of living being into a universal monarch, a Lokapāla, a Śakra, a Brahmā, a disciple, a solitary sage, a bodhisattva, and even into a buddha.

src: yāvantaś ca daśasu dikṣu śabdāvabhāsāḥ śabdaprajñāptayaḥ, tāḥ sarvā hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭānāṃ satvānāṃ sarvabuddhaghoṣarutaracitāny adhitiṣṭhan, tataś ca rutaghoṣād anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmaśabdarutāni niścārayet /
tgt: The bodhisattva can transform miraculously all the cries and noisessuperior, mediocre, and inferior, of all living beings of the ten directions, into the voice of the Buddha, with the words of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, having them proclaim, ‘Impermanent! Selfless!’

src: yāvadbhiś cākāranirdeśair daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayanti, tāṃs tato rutanirghoṣān niścārayet /
tgt: And he can cause them to recite the words and sounds of all the teachings taught by all the buddhas of the ten directions.

src: ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ yatkiṃcinmātro viṣayāvatāranirdeśaḥ /
tgt: “Reverend Śāriputra, I have shown you only a small part of the entrance into the domain of the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation.

src: api tu kalpam ahaṃ bhadantaśāriputra kalpāvaśesaṃ vācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ viṣayānāṃ viṣayāvatāranirdeśaṃ nirdiśeyam,
tgt: Reverend Śāriputra, to explain to you the teaching of the full entrance into the domain of the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation would require more than an eon, and even more than that.”

src: atha khalu sthaviro mahākāśyapa imaṃ bodhisatvānām acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptaḥ sthaviraṃ śāriputram etad avocat tadyathāpi nāma āyuṣmañ śāriputra jātyandhasya puruṣasya purastāt kaścid eva sarvarūpagatāny upadarśayet /
tgt: Then, the patriarch Mahākāśyapa, having heard this teaching of the inconceivable liberation of the bodhisattvas, was amazed, and he said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Venerable Śāriputra, if one were to show a variety of things to a person blind from birth, he would not be able to see a single thing.

src: evam eva āyuṣmañ śāriputra ihācintyavimokṣe nirdiśyamāne sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā iha jātyandhā iva cakṣurvihīnā ekasminn apy acintyakāraṇe na pratyakṣāḥ /
tgt: Likewise, venerable Śāriputra, when this door of the inconceivable liberation is taught, all the disciples and solitary sages are sightless, like the man blind from birth, and cannot comprehend even a single cause of the inconceivable liberation.

src: ko nāma vidvān imam acintyaṃ vimokṣaṃ śrutvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpādayet /
tgt: Who is there among the wise who, hearing about this inconceivable liberation, does not conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?

src: tat kiṃ nu bhūyaḥ kariṣyāmo 'tyantopahatendriyā dagdhavinaṣṭānīva bījāny abhājanībhūtā iha mahāyāne /
tgt: As for us, whose faculties are deteriorated, like a burned and rotten seed, what else can we do if we do not become receptive to this Great Vehicle?

src: sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhair imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā rudadbhis trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur vijñāpayitavyaḥ / sarvabodhisatvaiś ca pramuditair imam acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvā mūrdhnā saṃpratyetavyaḥ, adhimuktibalaṃ ca saṃjanayitavyam /
tgt: We, all the disciples and solitary sages, upon hearing this teaching of the Dharma, should utter a cry of regret that would shake this billionworld galactic universe! And as for the bodhisattvas, when they hear this inconceivable liberation they should be as joyful as a young crown prince when he takes the diadem and is anointed, and they should increase to the utmost their devotion to this inconceivable liberation.

src: yasyaiṣācintyavimokṣādhimuktiḥ sarvamārās tasya kiṃ kariṣyanti /
tgt: Indeed, what could the entire host of māras ever do to one who is devoted to this inconceivable liberation?”

src: imaṃ nirdeśaṃ nirdiśataḥ sthavirasya mahākāśyapasya dvātriṃśatā devaputrasahasrair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni /
tgt: When the patriarch Mahākāśyapa had uttered this discourse, thirtytwo thousand gods conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

src: atha vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ sthaviraṃ mahākāśyapam evam āha yāvanto bhadantamahākāśyapa daśasu dikṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu mārā māratvaṃ kārayanti, sarve te yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā upāyakauśalyena satvaparipācanāya māratvaṃ kārayanti / yāvadbhir bhadantamahākāśyapa daśasu dikṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu bodhisatvā yācanakair
tgt: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the patriarch Mahākāśyapa, “Reverend Mahākāśyapa, the māras who play the devil in the innumerable universes of the ten directions are all bodhisattvas dwelling in the inconceivable liberation, who are playing the devil in order to develop living beings through their skill in liberative art.

src: śirāṃsi vāṅgapratyaṅgāni vā rājyarāṣṭrajanapadān vā bhāryāputraduhitṝr vā dāsadāsīr vā hayagajarathavāhanāni vā suvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍamaṇiratnajātaṃ vānnapānāni rasān vā, vastrāṇi cotpīḍya yācyante, sarve te yācanakā yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā upāyakauśalyenemāṃ dṛḍhādhyāśayatāṃ darśayanti /
tgt: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, all the miserable beggars who come to the bodhisattvas of the innumerable universes of the ten directions to ask for a hand, a foot, an ear, a nose, some blood, muscles, bones, marrow, an eye, a torso, a head, a limb, a member, a throne, a kingdom, a country, a wife, a son, a daughter, a slave, a slavegirl, a horse, an elephant, a chariot, a cart, gold, silver, jewels, pearls, conches, crystal, coral, beryl, treasures, food, drink, elixirs, and clothesthese demanding beggars are usually bodhisattvas living in the inconceivable liberation who, through their skill in liberative art, wish to test and thus demonstrate the firmness of the high resolve of the bodhisattvas.

src: ugratapaso hi bhadantamahākāśyapa bodhisatvās ta evaṃ darśayanti /
tgt: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, the bodhisattvas demonstrate that firmness by means of terrible austerities.

src: nāsti hi prākṛtajanasyāsthānānavakāśakṛtasya bodhisatvam utpīḍayitum /
tgt: Ordinary persons have no power to be thus demanding of bodhisattvas, unless they are granted the opportunity.

src: tadyathāpi nāma bhadantamahākāśyapa na śaktir asti khadyotakasya sūryamaṇḍalaprabhām abhibhavitum / evam eva bhadantamahākāśyapa na śaktir asti prākṛtasya janasya bodhisatvenānavakāśakṛtasyopasaṃkramituṃ yācituṃ vā /
tgt: “Reverend Mahākāśyapa, just as a glowworm cannot eclipse the light of the sun, so, reverend Mahākāśyapa, it is not possible without special allowance that an ordinary person can thus attack and deprive a bodhisattva.

src: tadyathā bhadantamahākāśyapa yo hastināgasya prahāro na sa śakyo gardabhena soḍhum / evam eva bhadantamahākāśyapa na śakyam abodhisatvena bodhisatvasyotpīḍanaṃ soḍhum /
tgt: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, just as a donkey could not muster an attack on a wild elephant, even so, reverend Mahākāśyapa, one who is not himself a bodhisattva cannot harass a bodhisattva.

src: bodhisatva eva bodhisatvotpīḍāṃ sahate /
tgt: Only one who is himself a bodhisattva can harass another bodhisattva, and only a bodhisattva can tolerate the harassment of another bodhisattva.

src: ayaṃ bhadantamahākāśyapa acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānām upāyajñānabalapraveśaḥ // //
tgt: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, such is the introduction to the power of the knowledge of liberative art of the bodhisattvas who live in the inconceivable liberation.”

src: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat
tgt: Thereupon, Mañjuśrī, the crown prince, addressed the Licchavi Vimalakīrti

src: kathaṃ satpuruṣa bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ /
tgt: “Good sir, how should a bodhisattva regard all living beings?”

src: tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ marīcikāyām udakam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ māyākāro māyākāranirmitaṃ puruṣam avekṣeta,
tgt: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, a bodhisattva should regard all living beings as a wise man regards the reflection of the moon in water or as magicians regard men created by magic.

src: evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ /
tgt: “Precisely thus, Mañjuśrī, does a bodhisattva who realizes ultimate selflessness consider all beings.”

src: āha yadi kulaputraivaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ, kathaṃ punar asya mahāmaitrī bhavati sarvasatveṣu /
tgt: Mañjuśrī then asked further, “‌Noble sir, if a bodhisattva considers all living beings in such a way, how does he generate the great love toward them?”

src: āha yadā mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatva evaṃ pratyavekṣate,
tgt: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, when a bodhisattva considers all living beings in this way, he thinks

src: iyaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya mahāmaitrī /
tgt: Such, Mañjuśrī, is the great love of a bodhisattva.”

src: āha katarā punar asya mahākaruṇā /
tgt: What is the great compassion of a bodhisattva?

src: tato 'haṃ śarvavarmā ca jñātavantau krameṇa tām / atrāntare sa ca prāyaḥ paryahīyata vāsaraḥ //
tgt: Then I and Śarvavarman came at last to hear of the king’s condition, and by that time the day was almost at an end.

src: asmin kāle na ca svastho rājety ālocya tatkṣaṇam / āvābhyāṃ rājahaṃsākhya āhūto rājaceṭakaḥ //
tgt: So perceiving that the king was still in an unsatisfactory condition, we immediately summoned a servant of the king named Rājahansa.

src: śarīravārtāṃ bhūpasya sa ca pṛṣṭo 'bravīd idam / nedṛśo durmanāḥ pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭo devaḥ kadācana // viṣṇuśaktiduhitrā ca mithyāpaṇḍitayā tayā / vilakṣīkṛta ityāhurdevyo 'nyāḥ kopanirbharam // etattasya mukhācchrutvā rājaceṭasya durmanāḥ / śarvavarmadvitīyo 'haṃ saṃśayādityacintayam // vyādhiryadi bhavedrājñaḥ praviśeyuścikitsakāḥ / ādhirvā yadi tatrāsya kāraṇaṃ nopalabhyate //
tgt: And he, when asked by us about the state of the king’s health, said this: “I never before in my life saw the king in such a state of depression: and the other queens told me with much indignation that he had been humiliated to-day by that superficial blue-stocking, the daughter of Viṣṇuśakti.” When Śarvavarman and I had heard this from the mouth of the king’s servant, we fell into a state of despondency, and thus reflected in our dilemma: “If the king were afflicted with bodily disease we might introduce the physicians, but if his disease is mental it is impossible to find the cause of it.

src: nāstyeva hi vipakṣo 'sya rājye nihatakaṇṭake / anuraktāḥ prajāścaitā na hāniḥ paridṛśyate //
tgt: For there is no enemy in his country the thorns of which are destroyed, and these subjects are attached to him; no dearth of any kind is to be seen;

src: tatkasmād eṣa khedaḥ syād īdṛśaḥ sahasa prabhoḥ / evaṃ vicintite dhīmāñ śarvavarmedam abravīt // ahaṃ jānāmi rājño 'sya manyurmaurkhyānutāpataḥ / mūrkho 'ham iti pāṇḍityaṃ sadaivāyaṃ hi vāñchati // upalabdho mayā caiṣa pūrvam eva tadāśayaḥ / rājñyāvamānitaś cādya tannimittam iti śrutam // evamanyonyamālocya tāṃ rātrimativāhya ca / prātar āvāma gacchāva vāsaveśma mahīpateḥ //
tgt: so how can this sudden melancholy of the king’s have arisen?” After we had debated to this effect, the wise Śarvavarman said as follows:— “I know the cause: this king is distressed by sorrow for his own ignorance, for he is always expressing a desire for culture, saying, ‘I am a blockhead.’ I long ago detected this desire of his, and we have heard that the occasion of the present fit is his having been humiliated by the queen.” Thus we debated with one another, and after we had passed that night, in the morning we went to the private apartments of the sovereign.

src: tatra sarvasya ruddhe 'pi praveśe kathamapyaham / prāviśaṃ mama paścācca śarvavarmā laghukramam //
tgt: There, though strict orders had been given that no one was to enter, I managed to get in with difficulty, and after me Śarvavarman slipped in quickly.

src: upaviśyātha nikaṭe vijñaptaḥ sa mayā nṛpaḥ / akāraṇaṃ kathaṃ deva vartase vimanā iti // tacchrutvāpi tathaivāsītsa tūṣṇīṃ sātavāhanaḥ / śarvavarmā tataścedamadbhutaṃ vākyamabravīt // śrutaṃ mama syāt kāpīti prāguktaṃ deva me tvayā / tenāhaṃ kṛtavānadyā svapnamāṇavakaṃ niśi // svapne tato mayā dṛṣṭaṃ nabhasaścyutamambujam / tacca divyena kenāpi kumāreṇa vikāsitam //
tgt: I then sat down near the king and asked him this question: “Why, O king, art thou without cause thus despondent?” Though he heard this, Sātavāhana nevertheless remained silent, and then Śarvavarman uttered this extraordinary speech: “King, thou didst long ago say to me, ‘Make me a learned man.’ Thinking upon that, I employed last night a charm to produce a dream.[25] Then I saw in my dream a lotus fallen from heaven, and it was opened by some heavenly youth, and out of it came a divine woman in white garments, and immediately, O king, she entered thy mouth.

src: iyaddṛṣṭvā prabuddho 'smi manye sā ca sarasvatī / devasya vadane sākṣāt saṃpraviṣṭā na saṃśayaḥ // evaṃ niveditasvapne śarvavarmaṇi tatkṣaṇam / māmastamaunaḥ sākūtamavadatsātavāhanaḥ // śikṣamāṇaḥ prayatnenā kālena kiyatā pumān / adhigacchati pāṇḍityametanme kathyatāṃ tvayā //
tgt: When I had seen so much I woke up, and I think without doubt that the woman who visibly entered thy mouth was Sarasvatī.” As soon as Śarvavarman had in these terms described his dream, the king broke his silence and said to me with the utmost earnestness: “In how short a time can a man, who is diligently taught, acquire learning? Tell me this.

src: mama tena vinā hyeṣā lakṣmīrna pratibhāsate / vibhavaiḥ kiṃ nu mūrkhasya kāṣṭhasyābharaṇairiva // tato 'hamavadaṃ rājanvarṣairdvādaśabhiḥ sadā / jñāyate sarvavidyānāṃ mukhaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ naraiḥ //
tgt: For without learning all this regal splendour has no charms for me. What is the use of rank and power to a blockhead? They are like ornaments on a log of wood.” Then I said: “King, it is invariably the case that it takes men twelve years to learn grammar, the gate to all knowledge.

src: ahaṃ tu śikṣayāmi tvāṃ varṣaṣaṭkena tadvibho / śrutvaitatsahasā serṣyaṃ śarvavarmā kilāvadat // sukhocito janaḥ kleśaṃ kathaṃ kuryadiyacciram / tadahaṃ māsaṣaṭkena deva tvāṃ śikṣayāmi tat // śrutvaivaitad asaṃbhāvyaṃ tam avocam ahaṃ ruṣā / ṣaḍbhir māsais tvayā devaḥ śikṣitaś cet tato mayā // saṃskṛtaṃ prākṛtaṃ tadvaddeśabhāṣā ca sarvadā / bhāṣātrayamidaṃ tyaktaṃ yanmanuṣyeṣu saṃbhavet // śarvavarmā tato 'vādīnna cedevaṃ karomyaham / dvādaśābdānvahāmyeṣa śirasā tava pāduke //
tgt: But I, my sovereign, will teach it you in six years.” When he heard that, Śarvavarman suddenly exclaimed, in a fit of jealousy: “How can a man accustomed to enjoyment endure hardship for so long? So I will teach you grammar, my prince, in six months.” When I heard this promise, which it seemed impossible to make good, I said to him in a rage: “If you teach the king in six months, I renounce at once and for ever Sanskrit, Prakrit and the vernacular dialect, these three languages which pass current among men.”[26] Then Śarvavarman said: “And if I do not do this, I, Śarvavarman, will carry your shoes on my head for twelve years.” Having said this, he went out;

src: ityuktvā nirgate tasminnahamapyagamaṃ gṛham / rājāpyubhayataḥ siddhiṃ matvāśvasto babhūva saḥ //
tgt: I too went home; and the king for his part was comforted, expecting that he would attain his object by means of one of us two.

src: vihastaḥ śarvavarmā ca pratijñāṃ tāṃ sadustarām / paśyansānuśayaḥ sarvaṃ svabhāryāyai śaśaṃsa tat // sāpi taṃ duḥkhitāvocatsaṃkaṭe 'smiṃstava prabho / vinā svāmikumāreṇa gatiranyā na dṛśyate //
tgt: Now Śarvavarman being in a dilemma, seeing that his promise was one very difficult to perform, and regretting what he had done, told the whole story to his wife, and she, grieved to hear it, said to him: “My lord, in this difficulty there is no way of escape for you except the favour of the Lord Kārttikeya.”[27] “It is so,” said Śarvavarman, and determined to implore it.

src: tatheti niścayaṃ kṛtvā paścime prahare niśi / śarvavarmā nirāhārastatraiva prasthito 'bhavat //
tgt: Accordingly in the last watch of the night Śarvavarman set out fasting for the shrine of the god.

src: tacca cāramukhādbuddhvā mayā prātarniveditam / rājñe so 'pi tadākarṇya kiṃ bhavedityacintayat //
tgt: Now I came to hear of it by means of my secret emissaries, and in the morning I told the king of it; and he, when he heard it, wondered what would happen.

src: tatastaṃ siṃhaguptākhyo rājaputro hito 'bravīt / tvayi khinne tadā deva nirvedo me mahānabhūt //
tgt: Then a trusty Rājpūt called Siṃhagupta said to him: “When I heard, O king, that thou wast afflicted I was seized with great despondency.

src: maivaṃ kṛthā nṛpasyecchā setsyatyevetyavārayat / vāgantarikṣādatha māṃ tanmanye siddhirasti te //
tgt: Then I went out of this city, and was preparing to cut off my own head before the goddess Durgā in order to ensure thy happiness.

src: ityuktvā nṛpamāmantrya satvaraṃ śarvavarmaṇaḥ / paścāccāradvayaṃ so 'tha siṃhagupto vyasarjayat // so 'pi vātaikabhakṣaḥ san kṛtamaunaḥ suniścayaḥ / prāpa svāmikumārasya śarvavarmāntikaṃ kramāt //
tgt: the king’s wish shall be fulfilled.’ Therefore, I believe, thou art sure of success.” When he had said this, that Siṃhagupta took leave of the king and rapidly dispatched two emissaries after Śarvavarman, who, feeding only on air, observing a vow of silence, steadfast in resolution, reached at last the shrine of the Lord Kārttikeya.

src: śarīranirapekṣeṇa tapasā tatra toṣitaḥ / prasādamakarottasya kārtikeyo yathepsitam //
tgt: There, pleased with his penance that spared not the body, Kārttikeya favoured him according to his desire;

src: āgatyāgre tato rājñe cārābhyāṃ sa niveditaḥ / siṃhaguptavisṛṣṭābhyāmudayaḥ śarvavarmaṇaḥ // tacchrutvā mama rājñaśca viṣādapramadau dvayoḥ / abhūtāṃ mekhamālokya haṃsacātakayoriva // āgatya śarvavarmātha kumāravarasiddhimān / cintitopasthitā rājñe sarvā vidyāḥ pradattavān //
tgt: then the two spies sent by Siṃhagupta came into the king’s presence and reported the minister’s success. On hearing that news the king was delighted and I was despondent, as the chātaka joys, and the swan grieves, on seeing the cloud.[28] Then Śarvavarman arrived, successful by the favour of Kārttikeya, and communicated to the king all the sciences, which presented themselves to him on his thinking of them.

src: prādurāsaṃśca tāstasya sātavāhanabhūpateḥ / tatkṣaṇaṃ kiṃ na kuryāddhi prasādaḥ pārameśvaraḥ // atha tam akhilavidyālābham ākarṇya rājñaḥ pramuditavati rāṣṭre tatra ko 'pyutsavo 'bhūt / api pavanavidhūtāstatkṣaṇollāsyamānāḥ prativasati patākā baddhanṛttā ivāsan //
tgt: And immediately they were revealed to the King Sātavāhana. For what cannot the grace of the Supreme Lord accomplish? Then the kingdom rejoiced on hearing that the king had thus obtained all knowledge, and there was high festival kept throughout it; and that moment banners were flaunted from every house and, being fanned by the wind, seemed to dance.

src: rājārharatnanicayairatha śarvavarmā tenārcito gururiti praṇatena rājñā / svāmīkṛtaśca viṣaye marukacchanāmni kūlopakaṇṭhaviniveśini narmadāyāḥ //
tgt: Then Śarvavarman was honoured with abundance of jewels fit for a king by the sovereign, who bowed humbly before him, calling him his spiritual preceptor; and he was made governor of the territory called Bakakaccha, which lies along the bank of the Narmadā.

src: yo 'gre cāramukhena ṣaṇmukhavaraprāptiṃ samākarṇayat saṃtuṣyātmasamaṃ śriyā narapatistaṃ siṃhaguptaṃ vyadhāt / rājñīṃ tām api viṣṇuśaktitanayāṃ vidyāgame kāraṇaṃ devīnāmupari prasahya kṛtavān prītyābhiṣicya svayam // iti mahākaviśrīsomadevabhaṭṭaviracite kathāsaritsāgare kathāpīṭhalambake ṣaṣṭhas taraṅgaḥ / saptamas taraṅgaḥ / tato gṛhītamauno 'haṃ rājāntikamupāgamam / tara ca ślokamapaṭhaddvijaḥ kaścitsvayaṃ kṛtam //
tgt: The king being highly pleased with that Rājpūt Siṃhagupta, who first heard by the mouth of his spies that the boon had been obtained from the six-faced god,[29] made him equal to himself in splendour and power. And that queen too, the daughter of Viṣṇuśakti, who was the cause of his acquiring learning he exalted at one bound above all the queens, through affection anointing[30] her with his own hand. THEN, having taken a vow of silence, I came into the presence of the sovereign, and there a certain Brāhman recited a śloka he had composed, and the king himself addressed him correctly in the Sanskrit language;

src: taṃ cācaṣṭa svayaṃ rājā samyaksaṃskṛtayā girā / tatrālokya ca tatrastho janaḥ pramudito 'bhavat //
tgt: and the people who were present in Court were delighted when they witnessed that.

src: tataḥ sa śarvavarmāṇaṃ rājā savinayo 'bravīt / svayaṃ kathaya devena kahaṃ te 'nugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ // tacchrutvānugrahaṃ rājñaḥ śarvavarmābhyabhāṣata / ito rājannirāhāro maunastho 'haṃ tadā gataḥ //
tgt: Then the king said deferentially to Śarvavarman: “Tell me thyself after what fashion the god showed thee favour.” Hearing that, Śarvavarman proceeded to relate to the king the whole story of Kārttikeya’s favourable acceptance of him.

src: tato 'dhvani manāk cheṣe jāte tīvratapaḥkṛśaḥ / klāntaḥ patitavān asmi niḥsaṃjño dharaṇītale //
tgt: I went, O king, on that occasion fasting and silent from this place, so when the journey came to an end,[1] being very despondent, and emaciated with my severe austerities, worn out, I fell senseless on the ground.

src: uttiṣṭha putra sarvaṃ te saṃpatsyata iti sphuṭam / śaktihastaḥ pumānetya jāne māmabravīttadā // tenāhamamṛtāsārasaṃsikta iva tatkṣaṇam / prabuddhaḥ kṣutpipāsādihīnaḥ svastha ivābhavam //
tgt: Then, I remember, a man with a spear in his hand came and said to me in distinct accents: “Rise up, my son; everything shall turn out favourably for thee.” By that speech I was, as it were, immediately bedewed with a shower of nectar, and I woke up, and seemed free from hunger and thirst and in good case.

src: atha devasya nikaṭaṃ prāpya bhaktibharākulaḥ / snātvā garbhagṛhaṃ tasya praviṣṭo 'bhūvamunmanāḥ //
tgt: Then I approached the neighbourhood of the god’s temple, overpowered with the weight of my devotion, and after bathing I entered the inner shrine of the god in a state of agitated suspense.

src: tato 'ntaḥ prabhuṇā tena skandena mama darśanam / dattaṃ tataḥ praviṣṭā me mukhe mūrtā sarasvatī //
tgt: Then that Lord Skanda[2] gave me a sight of himself within, and thereupon Sarasvatī in visible shape entered my mouth.

src: tacchrutvaiva manuṣyatvasulabhācāpalādbata / uttaraṃ sūtramabhyūhya svayameva mayoditam //
tgt: So that holy god, manifested before me, recited the sūtra beginning, “the traditional doctrine of letters.” On hearing that I, with the levity which is so natural to mankind, guessed the next sūtra and uttered it myself.

src: athābravītsa devo māṃ nāvadiṣyaḥ svayaṃ yadi / abhaviṣyadidaṃ śāstraṃ pāṇinīyopamardakam //
tgt: Then that god said to me: “If thou hadst not uttered it thyself, this grammatical treatise would have supplanted that of Pāṇini.

src: adhunā svalpatantratvātkātantrākhyaṃ bhaviṣyati / madvāhanakalāpasya nāmnā kālāpakaṃ tathā // ityuktvā śabdaśāstraṃ tatprakāśyābhinavaṃ laghu / sākṣādeva sa māṃ devaḥ punarevamabhāṣata // yuṣmadīyaḥ sa rājāpi pūrvajanmanyabhūdṛṣiḥ / bharadvājamuneḥ śiṣyaḥ kṛṣṇasaṃjño mahātapāḥ // tulyābhilāṣām ālokya sa caikāṃ munikanyakām / yayāv akasmāt puṣpeṣuśaraghātarasajñatām //
tgt: As it is, on account of its conciseness, it shall be called Kātantra, and Kālāpaka, from the tail (kalāpa) of the peacock on which I ride.” Having said this, that god himself in visible form revealed to me that new and short grammar,[3] and then added this besides: “That king of thine in a former birth was himself a holy sage, a pupil of the hermit Bharadvāja, named Kṛṣṇa, great in austerity, and he, having beheld a hermit’s daughter who loved him in return, suddenly felt the smart of the wound which the shaft of the flowery-arrowed god inflicts.

src: ataḥ sa śapto munibhiravatīrṇa ihādhunā / sā cāvatīrṇā devītve tasyaiva munikanyakā //
tgt: So, having been cursed by the hermits, he has now become incarnate here, and that hermit’s daughter has become incarnate as his queen.

src: itthamṛṣyavatāro 'yaṃ nṛpatiḥ sātavāhanaḥ / dṛṣṭe tvayyakhilā vidyā prāpsyatyeva tvadicchayā //
tgt: So this King Sātavāhana, being an incarnation of a holy sage,[4] when he beholds thee will attain a knowledge of all the sciences according to thy wish.

src: akleśalabhyā hi bhavantyuttamārthā mahātmanām / janmāntarārjitāḥ sphārasaṃskārākṣiptasiddhayaḥ // ityuktvāntarhite deve niragacchamahaṃ bahiḥ / taṇḍulā me pradattāśca tatra devopajīvibhiḥ //
tgt: For the highest matters are easily acquired by great-souled ones, having been learnt in a former birth, the real truth of them being recalled by their powerful memories.”[5] When the god had said this he disappeared, and I went out, and there grains of rice were presented me by the god’s servants.

src: tato 'ham āgato rājaṃs taṇḍulās te ca me pathi / citraṃ tāvanta evāsan bhujyamānā dine dine //
tgt: Then I proceeded to return, O king, and wonderful to say, though I consumed those grains on my journey day after day, they remained as numerous as ever.

src: evamuktvā svavṛttāntaṃ virate śarvavarmaṇi / udatiṣṭhannṛpaḥ snātuṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ sātavāhanaḥ //
tgt: When he had related his adventure, Śarvavarman ceased speaking, and King Sātavāhana in cheerful mood rose up and went to bathe.

src: tato 'haṃ kṛtamaunatvādvyavahārabahiṣkṛtaḥ / anicchantaṃ tamāmantrya praṇāmenaiva bhūpatim // nirgatya nagarāttasmācchiṣyadvayasamanvitaḥ / tapase niścito draṣṭumāgato vindhyavāsinīm // svapnādeśena devyā ca tayaiva preṣitastataḥ / vindhyāṭavīṃ praviṣṭo 'haṃ tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ bhīṣaṇāmimām //
tgt: Then I, being excluded from business by my vow of silence, took leave, with a low bow only, of that king, who was very averse to part with me, and went out of that town, accompanied by only two disciples, and, with my mind bent on the performance of austerities, came to visit the shrine of the dweller in the Vindhya hills, and having been directed by the goddess in a dream to visit thee, I entered for that purpose this terrible Vindhya forest.

src: pulindavākyād āsādya sārthaṃ daivātkathaṃcana / iha prāpto 'hamadrākṣaṃ piśācānsubahūnamūn // anyonyālāpameteṣāṃ dūrādākarṇya śikṣitā / mayā piśācabhāṣeyaṃ maunamokṣasya kāraṇam //
tgt: A hint given by a Pulinda enabled me to find a caravan, and so somehow or other, by the special favour of destiny, I managed to arrive here, and beheld this host of Piśācas, and by hearing from a distance their conversation with one another, I have contrived to learn this Paiśācha language,[6] which has enabled me to break my vow of silence.

src: upagamya tataścaitāṃ tvāṃ śrutvojjayinīgatam / pratipālitavānasmi yāvadabhyāgato bhavān //
tgt: I then made use of it to ask after you, and hearing that you had gone to Ujjayinī, I waited here until your return;

src: dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ svāgataṃ kṛtvā caturthyā bhūtabhāṣayā / mayā jātiḥ smṛtetyeṣa vṛttānto me 'tra janmani //
tgt: on beholding you I welcomed you in the fourth language (the speech of the Piśācas), and then I called to mind my origin. This is the story of my adventure in this birth.

src: evamukte guṇāḍhyena kāṇabhūtiruvāca tam / tvadāgamo mayā jñāto yathādya niśi tacchṛṇu //
tgt: [M] (main story line continued) When Guṇāḍhya had said this, Kāṇabhūti said to him: “Hear how your arrival was made known to me last night.

src: rākṣaso bhūtivarmākhyo divyadṛṣṭiḥ sakhāsti me / gatavānasmi codyānamujjayinyāṃ tadāspadam //
tgt: I have a friend, a Rākṣasa of the name of Bhūtivarman, who possesses heavenly insight, and I went to a garden in Ujjayinī, where he resides.

src: tatrāsau nijaśāpāntaṃ prati pṛṣṭo mayābravīt / divā nāsti prabhāvo nāstiṣṭha rātrau vadāmyataḥ //
tgt: On my asking him when my own curse would come to an end, he said: ‘We have no power in the day;

src: tatheti cāhaṃ tatrasthaḥ prāptāyāṃ niśi valgatām / tamapṛcchaṃ prasaṅgena bhūtānāṃ harṣakāraṇam //
tgt: wait, and I will tell you at night.’ I consented, and when night came on I asked him earnestly the reason why goblins[7] delighted in disporting themselves, as they were doing.

src: purā viriñcasaṃvāde yaduktaṃ śaṃkareṇa tat / śṛṇu vacmīti māmuktvā bhūtivarmātha so 'bravīt //
tgt: Then Bhūtivarman said to me: ‘Listen; I will relate what I heard Śiva say in a conversation with Brahmā.

src: divā naiṣāṃ prabhāvo 'sti dhvastānāmarkatejasā / yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācānāṃ tena hṛṣyantyamī niśī // na pūjyante surā yatra na ca viprā yathocitam / bhujyate 'vidhinā vāpi tatraite prabhavanti ca //
tgt: Rākṣasas, Yakṣas, and Piśācas have no power in the day, being dazed with the brightness of the sun, therefore they delight in the night.[8] And where the gods are not worshipped, and the Brāhmans, in due form, and where men eat contrary to the holy law, there also they have power.

src: amāṃsabhakṣaḥ sādhvī vā yatra tatra na yāntyamī / śucīñ śūrān prabuddhāṃś ca nākrāmanti kadācana //
tgt: Where there is a man who abstains from flesh, or a virtuous woman, there they do not go.

src: ityuktvā me sa tatkālaṃ bhūtivarmābravītpunaḥ / gacchāgato guṇāḍhyaste śāpamokṣasya kāraṇam // śrutvaitadāgataścāsmi tvaṃ ca dṛṣṭo mayā prabho / kathayāmyadhunā tāṃ te puṣpadantoditāṃ kathām //
tgt: They never attack chaste men, heroes, and men awake.’[9] When he said this on that occasion Bhūtivarman continued: ‘Go, for Guṇāḍhya has arrived, the destined means of thy release from the curse.’ So hearing this, I have come, and I have seen thee, my lord. Now I will relate to thee that tale which Puṣpadanta told;

src: kiṃ tvekaṃ kautukaṃ me 'sti kathyatāṃ kena hetunā / sa puṣpadantas tvaṃ cāpi mālyavān iti viśrutaḥ // kāṇabhūteriti śrutvā guṇāḍhyastamabhāṣata / gaṅgātīre 'grahāro 'sti nāmnā bahusuvarṇakaḥ // tatra govindadattākhyo brāhmaṇo 'bhūdbahuśrutaḥ / tasya bhāryāgnidattā ca babhūva patidevatā //
tgt: but I feel curiosity on one point: tell me why he was called Puṣpadanta and thou Mālyavān.” Hearing this question from Kāṇabhūti, Guṇāḍhya said to him: On the bank of the Ganges there is a royal district granted to Brāhmans by royal charter, named Bahusuvarṇaka, and there lived there a very learned Brāhman named Govindadatta, and he had a wife, Agnidattā, who was devoted to her husband.

src: sa kālena dvijastasyāṃ pañca putrānajījanat / te ca mūrkhāḥ surūpāśca babhūvurabhimāninaḥ //
tgt: In course of time that Brāhman had five sons by her. And they, being handsome but stupid, grew up insolent fellows.

src: atha govindadattasya gṛhānatithirāyayau / vipro vaiśvānaro nāma vaiśvānara ivāparaḥ // govindadatte tatkālaṃ gṛhādapi bahiḥ sthite / tatputrāṇāmupāgatya kṛtaṃ tenābhivādanam //
tgt: Then a guest came to the house of Govindadatta, a Brāhman, Vaiśvānara by name, like a second god of fire.[10] As Govindadatta was away from home when he arrived, he came and saluted his sons, and they only responded to his salute with a laugh;

src: hāsamātraṃ ca taistasya kṛtaṃ pratyabhivādanam / tataḥ sa kopān nirgantuṃ prārebhe tadgṛhād dvijaḥ //
tgt: then that Brāhman in a rage prepared to depart from his house.

src: āgatenātha govindadattena sa tathāvidhaḥ / kruddhaḥ pṛṣṭo 'nunīto 'pi jagādaivaṃ dvijottamaḥ //
tgt: While he was in this state of wrath Govindadatta came, and asked the cause, and did his best to appease him;

src: putrāste patitā mūrkhāstatsaṃparkādbhavānapi / tasmānna bhokṣye tvadgehe prāyaścittaṃ nu me bhavet //
tgt: but the excellent Brāhman nevertheless spoke as follows:— “Your sons have become outcasts, as being blockheads, and you have lost caste by associating with them, therefore I will not eat in your house;

src: atha govindadattastamuvāca śapathottaram / na spṛśāmyapi jātvetānahaṃ kutanayāniti //
tgt: if I did so I should not be able to purify myself by any expiatory ceremony.” Then Govindadatta said to him with an oath: “I will never even touch these wicked sons of mine.” His hospitable wife also came and said the same to her guest;

src: tadbhāryāpi tathaivaitya tamuvācātithipriyā / tataḥ kathaṃcid ātithyaṃ tatra vaiśvānaro 'grahīt //
