tgt: then Vaiśvānara was with difficulty induced to accept their hospitality.

src: taddṛṣṭvā devadattākhyastasyaikastanayastadā / abhūdrovindadattasya nairghṛṇyenānutāpavān // vyarthaṃ jīvitamālokya pitṛbhyāmatha dūṣitam / sanirvedaḥ sa tapase toṣayiṣyannumāpatim //
tgt: One of Govindadatta’s sons, named Devadatta, when he saw that, was grieved at his father’s sternness, and, thinking a life of no value which was thus branded by his parents, went in a state of despondency to the hermitage of Badarikā to perform penance;

src: tataḥ parṇāśanaḥ pūrvaṃ dhūmapaś cāpy anantaram / tasthau cirāya tapase toṣayiṣyann umāpatim // dadau ca darśanaṃ tasya śaṃbhustīvrataporjitaḥ / tasyaivānucaratvaṃ ca sa vavre varamīśvarāt //
tgt: there he first ate leaves, and afterwards he fed only on smoke, persevering in a long course of austerities[11] in order to propitiate the husband of Umā.[12] So Śambhu,[12] won over by his severe austerities, manifested himself to him, and he craved a boon from the god, that he might ever attend upon him.

src: vidyāḥ prāpnuhi bhogāṃśca bhuvi bhuṅkṣva tatastava / bhavitābhimataṃ sarvamiti śaṃbhustamādiśat // tataḥ sa gatvā vidyārthī puraṃ pāṭaliputrakam / siṣeve vedakumbhākhyamupādhyāyaṃ yathāvidhi //
tgt: Śambhu thus commanded him: “Acquire learning, and enjoy pleasures on the earth, and after that thou shalt attain all thy desire.” Then he, eager for learning, went to the city of Pāṭaliputra, and according to custom waited on an instructor named Vedakumbha.

src: tatrasthaṃ tamupādhyāyapatnī jātu smarāturā / haṭhādvrave bata strīṇāṃ cañcalāścittavṛttayaḥ //
tgt: When he was there, the wife of his preceptor, distracted by passion, which had arisen in her heart, made violent love to him. Alas! the fancies of women are ever inconstant.

src: tena saṃtyajya taṃ deśamanaṅgakṛtaviplavaḥ / sa devadattaḥ prayayau pratiṣṭhānamatadritaḥ //
tgt: Accordingly Devadatta left that place, as his studies had been thus interfered with by the God of Love, and went to Pratiṣṭhāna with unwearied zeal.

src: tatra vṛddhamupādhyāyaṃ vṛddhayā bhāryayānvitam / mantrasvāmyākhyamabhyarthya vidyāḥ samyagadhītavān //
tgt: There he repaired to an old preceptor named Mantrasvāmin, with an old wife, and acquired a perfect knowledge of the sciences.

src: kṛtavidyaṃ ca taṃ tatra dadarśa nṛpateḥ sutā / suśarmākhyasya subhagaṃ śrīrnāma śrīr ivācyutam //
tgt: And after he had acquired learning the daughter of the King Suśarman, Śrī by name, cast eyes upon the handsome youth, as the goddess Śrī upon Viṣṇu.

src: so 'pi tāṃ dṛṣṭavān kanyāṃ sthitāṃ vātayanopari / viharantīṃ vimānena candrasyevādhidevatām //
tgt: He also beheld that maiden at a window, looking like the presiding goddess of the moon, roaming through the air in a magic chariot.

src: baddhāviva tayānyonyaṃ māraśṛṅkhalayā dṛśā / nāpasartuṃ samarthau tau babhūvaturubhāvapi //
tgt: Those two were, as it were, fastened together by that look which was the chain of love, and were unable to separate.

src: sātha tasyaikayāṅgulyā mūrtayeva smarājñayā / ito nikaṭamehīti saṃjñāṃ cakre nṛpātmajā //
tgt: The king’s daughter made him a sign to come near with one finger, looking like love’s command in fleshly form.

src: tataḥ samīpaṃ tasyāśca yayāvantaḥpurācca saḥ / sā ca cikṣepa dantena puṣpamādāya taṃ prati //
tgt: Then he came near her, and she came out of the women’s apartments, and took with her teeth a flower and threw it down to him.

src: saṃjñāmetāmajānāno gūḍhāṃ rājasutākṛtām / sa kartavyavimūḍhaḥ sann upādhyāyagṛhaṃ yayau //
tgt: He, not understanding this mysterious sign [also see notes on sign-language] made by the princess, puzzled as to what he ought to do, went home to his preceptor.

src: luloṭha tatra dharaṇau na kiṃcidvaktumīśvaraḥ / tāpena dahyamāno 'ntarmūkaḥ prabhuṣito yathā //
tgt: There he rolled on the ground unable to utter a word, being consumed within with burning pain, like one dumb and distracted;

src: vitarkya kāmajaiścihnairupādhyāyena dhīmatā / yuktyā pṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃcicca yathāvṛttaṃ śaśaṃsa saḥ //
tgt: his wise preceptor guessing what was the matter by these love symptoms, artfully questioned him, and at last he was with difficulty persuaded to tell the whole story.

src: tadbuddhvā tamupādhyāyo vidagdho vākyamabravīt / dantena puṣpaṃ muñcantyā tayā saṃjñā kṛtā tava // yadetatpuṣpadantākhyaṃ puṣpāḍhyaṃ suramandiram / tatrāgatya pratīkṣethāḥ sāṃprataṃ gamyatāmiti //
tgt: Then the clever preceptor guessed the riddle, and said to him[13]: “By letting drop a flower with her tooth she made a sign to you that you were to go to this temple rich in flowers, called Puṣpadanta, and wait there;

src: śrutveti jñānasaṃjñārthaḥ sa tatyāja śucaṃ yuvā / tato devagṛhasyāntastasya gatvā sthito 'bhavat //
tgt: so you had better go now.” When he heard this and knew the meaning of the sign, the youth forgot his grief. Then he went into that temple and remained there.

src: sāpyaṣṭamīṃ samuddiśya tatra rājasutā yayau / ekaiva devaṃ draṣṭuṃ ca garbhāgāramathāviśat //
tgt: The princess on her part also went there, giving as an excuse that it was the eighth day of the month, and then entered the inner shrine in order to present herself alone before the god;

src: dṛṣṭo 'tra dvārapaṭṭasya paścātso 'tha priyastayā / gṛhītānena cotthāya sā kaṇṭhe sahasā tataḥ //
tgt: then she touched her lover, who was behind the panel of the door, and he suddenly springing up threw his arms round her neck. She exclaimed: “This is strange;

src: citraṃ tvayā kathaṃ jñātā sā saṃjñetyudite tayā / upādhyāyena sā jñātā na mayeti jagāda saḥ // muñca māmavidagdhastvamityuktvā tatkṣaṇātkrudhā / mantrabhedabhayātsātha rājakanyā tato yayau //
tgt: how did you guess the meaning of that sign of mine?” He replied: “It was my preceptor that found it out, not I.” Then the princess flew into a passion and said, “Let me go; you are a dolt,” and immediately rushed out of the temple, fearing her secret would be discovered.

src: so 'pi gatvā vivikte tāṃ dṛṣṭanaṣṭāṃ smaran priyām / devadatto viyogāgnivigalajjīvito 'bhavat //
tgt: Devadatta on his part went away, and thinking in solitude on his beloved, who was no sooner seen than lost to his eyes, was in such a state that the taper of his life was well-nigh melted away in the fire of bereavement.

src: dṛṣṭvā taṃ tādṛśaṃ śaṃbhuḥ prākprasannaḥ kilādiśat / gaṇaṃ pañcaśikhaṃ nāma tasyābhīpsitasiddhaye //
tgt: Śiva, who had been before propitiated by him, commanded an attendant of his, of the name of Pañcaśikha, to procure for him the desire of his heart.

src: sa cagatya samāśvāsya strīveṣaṃ taṃ gaṇottamaḥ / akārayatsvayaṃ cābhūdvṛddhabrāhmaṇarūpadhṛt //
tgt: That excellent Gaṇa thereupon came and consoled him, and caused him to assume the dress of a woman, and he himself wore the semblance of an aged Brāhman.

src: tatastena samaṃ gatvā taṃ suśarmamahīpatim / janakaṃ sudṛśastasyāḥ sa jagāda gaṇāgraṇīḥ //
tgt: Then that worthy Gaṇa went with him to King Suśarman, the father of that bright-eyed one, and said to him: “My son has been sent away somewhere,[14] I go to seek him;

src: putro me proṣitaḥ kvāpi tamanveṣṭuṃ vrajāmyaham / tanme snuṣeyaṃ niḥkṣepo rājansaṃprati rakṣyatām // tacchrutvā śāpabhītena tenādāya suśarmaṇā / svakanyāntaḥpure gupte strīti saṃsthāpite yuvā //
tgt: accordingly I deposit with thee this daughter-in-law of mine; keep her safely, O king.” Hearing that, King Suśarman, afraid of a Brāhman’s curse, took the young man and placed him in his daughter’s guarded seraglio, supposing him to be a woman.

src: tataḥ pañcaśikhe yāte svapriyāntaḥpure vasan / strīveṣaḥ sa dvijastasyāvisrambhāspadatāṃ yayau //
tgt: Then after the departure of Pañcaśikha the Brāhman dwelt in woman’s clothes in the seraglio of his beloved, and became her trusted confidant.

src: ekadā cotsukā rātrau tenātmānaṃ prakāśya sā / guptaṃ gāndharvavidhinā pariṇītā nṛpāmajā // tasyāṃ ca dhṛtagarbhāyāṃ taṃ dvijaṃ sa gaṇottamaḥ / smṛtamātrāgato rātrau tato 'naiṣīdalakṣitam //
tgt: Once on a time the princess was full of regretful longing at night, so he discovered himself to her and secretly married her by the gāndharva form of marriage.[15] And when she became pregnant that excellent Gaṇa came on his thinking of him only, and carried him away at night without its being perceived.

src: tatastasya samutsārya yūnaḥ strīveṣamāśu tam / prātaḥ pañcaśikhaḥ so 'bhūtpūrvavadbrāhmaṇākṛtiḥ //
tgt: Then he quickly rent off from the young man his woman’s dress, and in the morning Pañcaśikha resumed the semblance of a Brāhman;

src: tenaiva saha gatvā ca suśarmanṛpam abhyadhāt / adya prāpto mayā rājan putras tad dehi me snuṣām //
tgt: and going with the young man to the King Suśarman he said: “O king, I have this day found my son;

src: tataḥ sa rājā tāṃ buddhvā rātrau kvāpi palāyitām / tacchāpabhayasaṃbhrānto mantribhya idamabravīt //
tgt: so give me back my daughter-in-law.” Then the king, supposing that she had fled somewhere at night, alarmed at the prospect of being cursed by the Brāhman, said this to his ministers: “This is no Brāhman;

src: na vipro 'yamayaṃ ko'pi devo madvañcanāgataḥ / evaṃprāyā bhavantīha vṛttāntāḥ satataṃ yataḥ //
tgt: this is some god come to deceive me, for such things often happen in this world.

src: tathā ca pūrvaṃ rājābhūttapasvī karuṇāparaḥ / dātā dhīraḥ śibirnāma sarvasattvābhayapradaḥ //
tgt: “So in former times there was a king named Śivi, self-denying, compassionate, generous, resolute, the protector of all creatures;

src: taṃ vañcayitumindro 'tha kṛtvā śyenavapuḥ svayam / māyākapotavapuṣaṃ dharmam anvapatad drutam //
tgt: and in order to beguile him Indra assumed the shape of a hawk, and swiftly pursued Dharma,[16] who by magic had transformed himself into a dove.

src: kapotaśca bhayādgatvā śiberaṅkamaśiśriyat / manuṣyavācā śyeno 'tha sa taṃ rājānamabravīt //
tgt: The dove in terror went and took refuge in the bosom of Śivi. Then the hawk addressed the king with a human voice: ‘O king, this is my natural food;

src: rājan bhakṣyam idaṃ muñca kapotaṃ kṣudhitasya me / anyathā māṃ mṛtaṃ viddhi kas te dharmas tato bhavet // tataḥ śibiruvācainameṣa me śaraṇāgataḥ / atyājyastaddadāmyanyanmāṃsametatsamaṃ tava // śyeno jagāda yadyevamātmamāṃsaṃ prayaccha me / tateti tatprahṛṣṭaḥ sansa rājā pratyapadyata //
tgt: surrender the dove to me, for I am hungry. Know that my death will immediately follow if you refuse my prayer; in that case where will be your righteousness?’ Then Śivi said to the god: ‘This creature has fled to me for protection, and I cannot abandon it, therefore I will give you an equal weight of some other kind of flesh.’ The hawk said: ‘If this be so, then give me your own flesh.’ The king, delighted, consented to do so.

src: yathā yathā ca māṃsaṃ svamutkṛtyāropayannṛpaḥ / tathā tathā tulāyāṃ sa kapoto 'bhyadhiko 'bhavat //
tgt: But as fast as he cut off his flesh and threw it on the scale, the dove seemed to weigh more and more in the balance.

src: tataḥ śarīraṃ sakalaṃ tulāṃ rājādhyaropayat / sādhu sādhu śamaṃ tvetaddivyā vāgudabhūttataḥ // indradharmau tatastyaktvā rūpaṃ śyenakapotayoḥ / tuṣṭāvakṣatadehaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ cakratuḥ śibim //
tgt: Then the king threw his whole body on to the scale, and thereupon a celestial voice was heard: ‘Well done! This is equal in weight to the dove.’ Then Indra and Dharma abandoned the form of hawk and dove and, being highly pleased, restored the body of King Śivi whole as before, and after bestowing on him many other blessings they both disappeared.

src: dattvā cāsmai varānanyāṃstāvantardhānamīyatuḥ / evaṃ māmapi ko 'pyeṣa devo jijñāsurāgataḥ // ityuktvā sacivānsvairaṃ sa suśarmā mahīpatiḥ / tamuvāca bhayaprahvo viprarūpaṃ gaṇottamam //
tgt: In the same way this Brāhman is some god that has come to prove me.”[17] Having said this to his ministers, that King Suśarman of his own motion said to that excellent Gaṇa that had assumed the form of a Brāhman, prostrating himself before him in fear: “Spare me.

src: abhayaṃ dehi sādyaiva snuṣā te hāritā niśi / māyayaiva gatā kvāpi rakṣyamāṇāpyaharniśam // kṛcchrātsa dayayevātha viprarūpo gaṇo 'bravīt / tarhi putrāya rājanme dehi svāṃ tanayāmiti // tacchrutvā śāpabhītena rājñā tasmai nijā sutā / sā dattā devadattāya tataḥ pañcaśikho yayau //
tgt: She has been taken somewhere or other by magic arts, though guarded night and day.” Then the Gaṇa, who had assumed the Brāhman’s semblance, pretending to be with difficulty won over to pity him, said: “If this be so, king, give thy daughter in marriage to my son.” When he heard this, the king, afraid of being cursed, gave his own daughter to Devadatta; then Pañcaśikha departed.

src: devadatto 'pi tāṃ bhūyaḥ prakāśaṃ prāpya vallabhām / jajṛmbhe 'nanyaputrasya śvaśurasya vibhūtiṣu //
tgt: Then Devadatta having recovered his beloved, and that in an open manner, flourished in the power and splendour of his father-in-law, who had no son but him.

src: kālena tasya putraṃ ca dauhitramabiṣicya saḥ / rājye mahīdharaṃ nāma suśarmā śiśriye vanam //
tgt: And in course of time Suśarman anointed the son of his daughter by Devadatta, Mahīdhara by name, as successor in his room, and retired to the forest.
